title: Design Philosophy

body: - **Determinism under a seed** — the timeline engine runs on a `current_thread` tokio runtime with zero work-stealing, so the same scenario + seed always produces the same emission stream shape; reproducibility is a property the architecture enforces in the runtime flavor, not a convention bolted on later.

- **Headless-drivable core, thin shell** — all engine logic lives in runtime-agnostic library crates that `scripts/agent-run.sh` (the source of truth) drives through `conductor-cli`; the CLI/headless path is the release gate (the Tauri GUI shell retired 2026-10-11, intent R1). A scenario declaring the real-model L4 posture (2026-09-22) is evaluated by `conductor run` alone under its declared posture, while `conductor suite` keeps the deterministic gate and records it `Blocked` (§Standard Contracts — Readiness gate).

- **Compiler-enforced module seams** — the modular monolith is realized as a crate-per-seam Cargo workspace where `Cargo.toml` dependency edges *are* the architecture and a forbidden cross-seam dependency simply will not compile.

- **Outcomes are values, errors are harness faults** — verification verdicts (`Pass`/`Fail`/`CalibrationRegion`) and report states (`Pass`/`Fail`/`ManualCheck`/`KnownResidual`/`Blocked`) are typed return values; `Result::Err` is reserved strictly for Conductor's own failures (config parse, transport down, MCP unreachable), so the report can correctly classify a model-backed SUT's behavior by matching on types rather than catching exceptions.

- **Journal-relative ground truth** — every SLO is measured as `read_back_observed_at − journal_emitted_at` against an on-disk JSONL emission journal, never wall-clock-from-test-start; file artifacts are the agent-parseable ground truth and the embedded SQLite index is a thin convenience layer over them.

title: Stack and Technologies

body: | Layer | Technology | Role |
| Language / runtime | Rust 2024 (cargo 1.85, MSRV 1.94.1) | Primary implementation language; Pulse-consistency mandate |
| Async runtime | tokio 1.52.3 (`current_thread` flavor) | Deterministic single-threaded scheduler for the timeline engine; core-owned runtime |

| Determinism RNG | rand_chacha 0.9 (`ChaCha8Rng`) + rand_core 0.9 (`SeedableRng`) | Seedable, platform-stable PRNG owning the timeline scheduler's non-determinism (seeded per-gap jitter); `seed_from_u64` for cross-platform/version-stable reproducibility |
| Backend framework | N/A — no web framework | Conductor exposes no HTTP/network service of its own (gRPC client + MCP client only) |

| OTLP emission | opentelemetry-proto 0.32.0 (`default-features = false` at the workspace entry; `gen-tonic` + `trace`/`logs`) | Raw hand-built OTLP message structs (`ExportTraceServiceRequest`/`ResourceSpans`/`Span`/`Status`) for byte-level fault control |
| gRPC transport | tonic 0.14.6 + tonic-prost 0.14.6 + prost 0.14 | Ships generated `TraceServiceClient`/`LogsServiceClient` over loopback gRPC |

| MCP read-back client | hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC over tokio child stdio | Direct JSON-RPC client (no SDK; rmcp removed 2026-06-27) — `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`, version negotiation read from the `initialize` result, RAW `serde_json::Value` tool results (Pulse's sidecar is non-MCP-compliant for `tools/call`) |

| Hashing / digest | blake3 1.8.6 (pinned `blake3 = "1"` in `[workspace.dependencies]`) | Exception-fingerprint derivation in `conductor-emit` — a NORMAL (non-dev) dep, because a test-scoped dep cannot back a shipped signature. Version-matched to the SUT's own pin (`andromeda-pulse Cargo.toml:`) under the Pulse-consistency mandate: Conductor recomputes Pulse's derivation, so the algorithm is the SUT's choice, not Conductor's. Conductor's first hashing dependency (pulls `arrayref` / `arrayvec` / `constant_time_eq` / `cpufeatures`), and still its only SHIPPED one: `sha2 0.10` (0.10.9, locked by this dev edge itself since 2026-10-11) is a TEST-only `conductor-run` dev-dependency for the real-model harvest's sha256 digest pins over committed capture evidence (2026-09-30) |
| Database | rusqlite 0.38.0 + libsqlite3-sys 0.36.0 (`bundled` → SQLite 3.50.4, JSON1) | Synchronous, append-mostly embedded index (`runs.db`), deliberately off the async runtime |
| ORM / migrations | None — raw SQL in the storage seam | Right altitude for a small fixed set of hand-written run-metadata tables |
| Message broker | N/A | Single-process; inter-module flow is in-process Rust calls / `tokio::sync::mpsc` at most |
| Mobile framework | N/A | Desktop-only, host-bound (holds `:4317`, reads local git workspace) |
| AI/ML serving | N/A | Conductor is the test driver; model behavior lives in Pulse (the system under test) |

| Validation | serde 1.0.x + garde 0.22.1 | `#[derive(Validate)]` range rules + `#[garde(custom)]` field validators + the garde-expressible cross-field invariants for scenario config; a SIBLING-spanning invariant ships instead as a load-path `Scenario::check_*()` called from `from_toml_str` (§Established Decisions [Validation Library]) |
| Serialization (JSON) | serde_json 1.0 | Canonical-name (de)serialization for the run-report envelope + per-run JSONL journal (serde companion; report-seam runtime dep) |

| Scenario config (TOML) | toml 0.9 | Declarative scenario config (de)serialization from `scenarios/*.toml` via serde (`Scenario::from_toml_str`); hand-author-ergonomic format chosen over JSON (P4 decision); audit/deny-clean |
| Error handling | thiserror 2.0.18 + anyhow 1.0.104 | Typed per-seam error enums in library crates; type-erased `Result` at binary edges |

| CLI argument parsing | clap 4 (`derive`) | Declarative verb surface over the `current_thread` bootstrap (`conductor-cli`) — the verbs are whichever `Commands` (`cli.rs`) declares, never a literal list here; layout-templates §Surface: cli Primary screens is the enumerating home. `derive` macros for the `Cli`/`Commands` structs |

| Terminal output rendering | owo-colors 4 + indicatif 0.18 + comfy-table 7 + inquire 0.9 | `conductor-cli` presentation layer (Epoch 8): tty-gated status-line color (never color-alone), run/suite progress spinner, results + capability-coverage tables (the manifest's accepted set) + the `conductor scenarios` catalogue table, isatty-gated interactive operator-pause prompts (inquire confirm; headless never blocks) |
| Self-observation | tracing 0.1.44 + tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 | Structured JSON self-observation logs; NOT an OTel SDK (OTLP is the PRODUCT emission); detail in obs-plan §3 |
| Build / packaging | Cargo workspace, `cargo build --release` | Local release binary (source of truth) |

| CI/CD | GitHub Actions (`cargo fmt --all --check` / `cargo build` / nextest / clippy + the static gates (over committed data · repository hygiene)) | Formatting, build + test gating, the static gates each asserting a committed artifact against the production source it is derived from (coverage-completeness 2026-09-06 · scenario-assertion audit 2026-09-16) and the repository-hygiene gates (secret scan · workflow env-context, 2026-09-24); dynamic scenario proof REQUIRING A LIVE PULSE remains a local operator gate |
| Code quality | clippy + cargo-nextest (optional: cargo-modules, cargo-rail) | Linting, test running, and module-graph auditing |

| Operator instruments (host runtime) | Host Python 3 — resolved by no lockfile, pinned by no toolchain file | Runs the repo's committed operator-local instruments: the code-graph pipeline (`scripts/code-graph.py` + `scripts/scip_pb2.py` + `scripts/requirements.txt`, since 2026-06-18) and the mutation-tally gate (`scripts/mutation-gate.py` + `scripts/mutation-roster.toml`, since 2026-09-13 — every roster row carries a required `tally` of `missed` or `timeout`; since 2026-09-30 a stdlib-only `selftest [--fixtures DIR]` verb grades the committed fixture tree `scripts/fixtures/mutation-gate/`, spawning no process and running no `cargo mutants`) and the architecture-registry check (`scripts/arch-registry-check.py`, stdlib only, since 2026-09-24 — sizes §Established Decisions / §Occupied Resources against 60 % of the Read cap and proves a drafted compaction lossless). None is invoked by any CI step, and none adds a sixth `agent-run.{sh,ps1}` command — the 5-command harness surface is unchanged |

title: Established Decisions

body: - **[Language / Runtime] Rust 2024 + tokio 1.52.3:** Pinned by brief for Pulse-consistency; tonic/prost require a tokio reactor and the deterministic phase scheduler maps cleanly to `tokio::time` for exact gap/silence/ramp timing.

- **[Async Runtime Flavor] tokio `current_thread`, core-owned:** Zero work-stealing makes emission ordering a deterministic function of the seed; throughput headroom is irrelevant because load-testing is an explicit non-goal (Pulse prior art saturated ~10k spans/s). `#[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]` on the CLI path.

- **[Determinism RNG] rand_chacha `ChaCha8Rng` seeded via `seed_from_u64`:** The timeline scheduler's sole source of non-determinism is a seedable `ChaCha8Rng` (rand_chacha 0.9 + rand_core 0.9), seeded `seed_from_u64(scenario.seed)`; ChaCha8's algorithm is stable across platforms and crate versions, so the same seed reproduces the same emission-stream shape on any host — `StdRng` (no cross-version stability guarantee) was rejected for exactly this reason. The seed materially shapes timing (bounded per-gap jitter), and a transition's `elapsed_ms` is a deterministic cumulative sum of effective gaps, never a clock read.

- **[OTLP Emission Strategy] opentelemetry-proto 0.32.0 raw types over the SDK exporter:** The `opentelemetry-otlp` exporter is a near-deal-breaker — it offers no control over fingerprint identity, severity boundaries, or root-vs-child error placement and spawns its own batch tasks on the runtime. Raw message structs give byte-level control, which fault injection requires; this is the single most consequential fork in the build.

- **[Backend Framework] None (no web framework):** Conductor is a gRPC client + MCP client, not a server; it exposes no HTTP/network surface of its own, so Axum/Actix and REST/GraphQL/tRPC are all out of scope.

- **[Database] rusqlite 0.38.0 with `bundled` SQLite, synchronous:** Quiz I pinned file artifacts + a thin SQLite index; rusqlite keeps the storage seam synchronous (no async-runtime entanglement) and `bundled` yields a self-contained cross-platform build with JSON1 for indexing fingerprint arrays. sqlx (async-first) and SeaORM (ORM over-scope) were rejected.

- **[ORM] None — raw SQL:** `runs.db` is a small fixed set of hand-written tables of run metadata (`runs`, the scenario-grained run index; `run_envelope`, the run-level envelope standing; `run_check`, the per-check index keyed `(run_id, scenario, check_index)`), each added additively under `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`; an ORM's entity/migration machinery is weight with no payoff for hand-written append + a handful of cross-run SELECTs + one run-scoped teardown. That teardown is `RunsDb::delete_run` (2026-09-06) — three LITERAL `DELETE … WHERE run_id = ?1` statements over `runs` / `run_check` / `run_envelope` in one transaction, rusqlite bound parameters, idempotent, and never `format!`-assembled even over a hard-coded table list (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Input). The seam is its sole implementation: the `conductor cleanup <run_id>` verb is the only caller and the harness shells issue no SQL of their own.

- **[MCP Read-Back Client] hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC (rmcp removed 2026-06-27):** The read-back client (`conductor-verify/src/jsonrpc.rs` + `client.rs`) speaks JSON-RPC directly over the sidecar's stdio — `initialize` (capturing the server's `protocolVersion` for negotiation) + `tools/list` + `tools/call` — returning the **raw `serde_json::Value` result**. rmcp 1.7.0 was the original choice (typed SDK + version negotiation) but was **removed** when proven against the live sidecar: Pulse's MCP *server* is itself hand-rolled JSON-RPC (`crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`) and **non-MCP-compliant for `tools/call`** — it returns the raw tool payload as the JSON-RPC `result` (no `{content:[…]}` envelope), which rmcp's typed `call_tool` deserializes into `ServerResult` and rejects as `UnexpectedResponse` on *every* live call (rmcp exposes no raw-result escape). A hand-rolled client is therefore the faithful match to Pulse's actual wire format; version negotiation reduces to reading the `initialize` result's `protocolVersion`, the contract manifest still pins `2024-11-05`, and the preflight gate still guards a strict-newer mismatch.

- **[Validation Library] serde 1.0.x + garde 0.22.1:** garde (the modern rewrite of `validator`) expresses scenario bounds declaratively next to the serde structs — `range` rules for simple bounds (a bounded error fraction, shipped as `EmissionShape::Error { error_percent: u32 }` ∈ 0..=100 — an integer percent, not an f64, so `PhaseSpec`/`Scenario` keep `Eq`; non-negative durations, sane ramp factors) and `#[garde(custom)]` field validators for the rest; cross-field invariants spanning distinct fields (p50≤p95≤p99 ordering, severity-mix sums, the fault ⇒ `occurrences = 0` silence rule `fault_phases_are_silent`) use garde's `Context` pattern or a field-level `custom` one altitude up (the fault rule sits on `Scenario::phases`, like `no_duplicate_pids` on `p_ids`), since garde 0.22.1's `custom` is field-level only (no container-level custom) — with no async or web-framework coupling. **A THIRD route exists, and its boundary is structural:** the one-altitude-up `custom` covers only an invariant CONTAINED WITHIN the lifted field (`fault_phases_are_silent` needs `phases` alone), because a field-level `custom` receives `(&field, &())` and can see no SIBLING field. An invariant spanning a field and its sibling therefore cannot be a garde validator at all under 0.22.1 — it ships as a plain load-path method invoked from `Scenario::from_toml_str`, the shape `Scenario::check_capabilities` already uses, `Scenario::check_budgets` (`budget_ms` ≤ its scenario's own `slo_tier` deadline) joined, and `Scenario::check_checklist` (a declared `[[checklist]]` may not sit beside a non-empty `expected` — the checklist renders only on the operator-checklist path a checks-bearing scenario never takes) now joins. **A nested spec field must `dive`, never `skip`** — a `skip`ped nested struct deserializes unvalidated because garde never descends into it. **Pinned 0.22.1**, not the originally-chosen 0.23.0: its `garde_derive 0.23.0` proved absent from the registry, so 0.23.0 + the `derive` feature is unbuildable. validator (predecessor) and serde_valid (JSON-Schema niche) were rejected.

- **[Scenario Config Format] TOML on disk via the `toml` crate (0.9):** scenario config files under `scenarios/` are declarative TOML, serde-deserialized and bounds-checked with garde at load. The load-error mapping is **three-way**: `Scenario::from_toml_str` → `CoreError::Config` on a parse failure OR on a non-garde load-path check failure (`check_budgets`, `check_capabilities`, `check_checklist`), and `CoreError::Validation` only on a garde failure — because `Validation` is pinned `#[from] garde::Report` and structurally cannot carry a hand-written message. All three are harness faults on the `Result::Err` side of the verdict/error wall. TOML was chosen over JSON (the only other candidate; serde_json was already present) for hand-author ergonomics + inline comments across the per-P-ID scenario files — a P4 user decision. The `toml` crate is audit/deny-clean; serde_json remains the run-report-envelope / JSONL-journal serializer.

- **[Accepted Capability Set] a versioned SUT capability manifest, not a compile-time constant:** which Pulse P-IDs a scenario may name is **data** — `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`, read and bounds-checked at load (same `toml` + serde stack, no new dependency). Validation is two-layered: garde's `pid_format` asserts the `P-NNN` **shape** only, and `Scenario::check_capabilities` asserts **membership** against the manifest, applied by `Scenario::from_toml_str_with(&str, &CapabilityManifest)` at every load site that takes a `&CapabilityManifest` — the binary edge (`conductor-cli::paths`) and the `conductor-core` catalog loaders that carry the manifest through (`list_scenarios(dir, &manifest)` for identity-only summaries, `load_catalog(dir, &manifest)` for the whole `Scenario` where a gate needs the phases a summary drops); the set is whatever takes that parameter, never a count. A malformed / absent / unparseable manifest is a **harness fault** (`CoreError`, `Result::Err`) carrying a named reason — never `Blocked` (a blocked row needs `run_id`/`seed`/`scenario`/`p_ids`/`slo_tier`, none of which exist at manifest-load time) and never a silent widening. The **accepted set** is data; the **coverage classification** stays code-native (`coverage_matrix()` in `conductor-core`, a no-runtime-IO `static`), and `check_sut_drift` asserts set-equality between the two — deliberately a two-source comparison, which sourcing the classification from the manifest would collapse into a self-check. So re-aiming at a newer Pulse release is a manifest edit **plus** a matching classification row: an accepted id with no row (or a classified id the manifest no longer accepts) is a `CoreError::SutDrift`, never a silent gap. **A second integrity gate sits beside it on a different axis:** `check_sut_drift` asks whether every accepted capability is *classified*, while `check_scenario_backing` asks whether every capability classified `Auto` — the mode that claims Conductor both drives the stimulus and asserts the reaction — actually has a scenario naming it. A capability can pass the first and fail the second, because classification is a statement of intent and a scenario is what makes it true. The `UNBACKED_AUTO` pin records the `Auto` claims no scenario yet backs, held to exact-set equality against the committed catalog (a new unbacked claim, a pin a scenario now covers, or a pin that lost its `Auto` classification are each a `CoreError::UnbackedCoverage`), so the ledger can only shrink under compulsion. Only `Auto` participates — `DriveObserve` is operator-confirmed by definition, and `StaticOnly` / `NotConductors` are deliberately not Conductor's to drive. `Scenario::from_toml_str(&str)` and `PId`'s shape are unchanged — garde's `dive` propagates `Context`, so threading the accepted set through garde would have forced a context onto `PId`/`PhaseSpec`/`EmissionSpec`/`ExpectedCheck` and changed `PId`'s public API.

- **[Error Handling] thiserror 2.0.18 in seam crates + anyhow 1.0.104 at edges, plus a type-level verdict/error wall:** The report's states require *matching on error variants* — "MCP tool absent" → `Blocked`, "transport refused" → harness error, "wrong incident" → `Fail` — so verification outcomes are VALUES (`Verdict`/`ReportState`), never Rust errors; `Result::Err` is reserved for harness failures only. `tonic::Status` codes and MCP error responses are first-class verification inputs. anyhow lives only at the `conductor-cli` edge.

- **[Module Boundaries] Crate-per-seam Cargo workspace:** In Rust, crates are compiler-enforced visibility boundaries; one workspace with a runtime-agnostic `conductor-core` plus the seam crates `conductor-timeline`/`conductor-emit`/`conductor-faults`/`conductor-verify`/`conductor-report` (+ the `conductor-cli` bin) makes a forbidden cross-seam dependency fail to compile, gives per-seam `cargo test -p` (and, with the qualifier below, `cargo build -p`), ships a single deployable, and mirrors Pulse's `crates/…` layout. The compiler enforces; cargo-modules/cargo-rail only audit. **The forbidden-edge property is compiler-enforced and unqualified; the standalone per-seam BUILD now holds for every member, measured rather than gate-enforced.** Workspace feature unification can mask a feature a crate uses but declares only in `[dev-dependencies]`, so a crate compiles in the workspace and in `cargo test -p` while failing alone. The standalone sweep takes the eight members each on its OWN targets — `--lib` for the seven library crates, `--bins` for `conductor-cli`, which has no lib target and would false-red under a uniform `--lib` — every one exit 0 (as measured at the `2026-10-11-conductors-window-retired` gate). `--all-targets` is deliberately NOT the sweep form: it re-unifies dev-dependencies, which is the exact masking the sweep exists to catch. The caveat: no CI job builds a member standalone, so the property is measured-at-a-chunk rather than gate-enforced, and a future dev-only feature declaration could reintroduce it unnoticed.

- **[Workspace / Core Structure] Runtime-agnostic core library + one CLI bin:** This is the structural decision that makes "headless-drivable" real — engine logic lives in a runtime-agnostic core that `agent-run` drives through `conductor-cli`, enforcing the headless/CLI split at compile time. The Tauri GUI bin it also served retired 2026-10-11 (intent R1, ratified at that chunk's wrap).
- **[Real-time Strategy] Retired 2026-10-11:** the Tauri 2 IPC `Channel` for in-app live updates left with the window (intent R1); no live-update surface remains.

- **[Message Broker] N/A:** Single-process modular monolith; inter-module flow is in-process Rust calls / `tokio::sync::mpsc` channels at most — no Kafka/NATS/Redis. The only queue-like surface is the OTLP gRPC stream to Pulse, which is the SUT, not Conductor's infrastructure.

- **[Deployment] Local `cargo build --release` + `scripts/agent-run.sh`:** Headless is the source of truth, co-located with Pulse (which binds loopback `:4317` only, ruling out remote/containerized execution). No cloud / container / serverless.

- **[CI/CD] GitHub Actions, fmt + build + test + the static gates (over committed data · repository hygiene):** the `rust` job also carries a static gate per committed artifact that a production source derives — the `Coverage-completeness gate` (2026-09-06) and the `Scenario-assertion audit gate` (2026-09-16) — and two repository-hygiene gates (2026-09-24): the `Secret-scan gate` (no secret-shaped string or file name in `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`) and the `Workflow env-context gate` (every `env.X` expression read names a declared or `GITHUB_ENV`-written key, an admission a `GITHUB_ENV context probe` step pair re-measures each run). Each is its own named step with no `continue-on-error` and no `if:`, each opening its `run` with a presence guard on its subject that emits a `::error::` annotation and exits 1 so an absent subject fails loudly rather than passing vacuously, then invoking the specific nextest target (`-p conductor-report --test coverage_gate` · `-p conductor-core --test scenario_audit_gate` / `secret_scan_gate` / `workflow_env_gate`). Re-listing a gate's assertion in shell would be a second copy that drifts, so the gate IS the Rust test and the step is its presence-guarded invocation. The `rust` job opens with `cargo fmt --all --check` as its own named step (`Formatting gate (cargo fmt)`, step index 2, immediately after the toolchain install and before the cache restore, no `continue-on-error` and no `if:` — rustfmt is a `rust-toolchain.toml` component, so the gate adds no dependency and no lockfile delta; `--all` rather than the bare form because the workspace declares no `default-members`, making the two equivalent today and divergent the moment one is added); then `cargo build` / nextest / clippy on the dev OS target verify the harness compiles and unit/golden tests pass. The `rust` job is the only job: the `frontend` and `a11y` jobs, the msedgedriver pin gate and the routine webview a11y leg left with the window on 2026-10-11 (intent R1, ratified at that chunk's wrap), and with them the leg's hosted-runner and dev-host verdicts — removed, not re-measured; their text is last at `321dc8f`. What stays an operator/local gate is end-to-end dynamic scenario proof REQUIRING A LIVE PULSE (`mcp-server` feature + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`), because CI has no Pulse instance.

- **[Timing-Tolerance Model] Hybrid journal-relative deadline + tier-scaled bounded slack:** Latency is always `read_back_observed_at − journal_emitted_at` (never wall-clock-from-test-start); deterministic/hard SLOs get a tolerance band scaled to hardware-profile-aware tiers (<5s / <20s / <90s), while sample-count floors (50-sample latency / 10-span error-rate) and model-interpretive timings route to the calibration-region bucket instead of hard-failing. **The tier deadline is a CEILING, not necessarily the deadline itself:** an `[[expected]]` check may declare its own sub-tier `budget_ms` and is then graded against a per-check EFFECTIVE deadline (`ExpectedCheck::effective_deadline_ms(tier)` — the budget when declared, else the tier's), so `evaluate_slo` takes an effective `deadline_ms` and `SloOutcome` carries it. Every expected check persists its own `latency_ms`/`deadline_ms`/`verdict` rather than only the run's shared whole-loop value — and because the corpus is observed ONCE per scenario, the per-check latencies are equal by construction and the DEADLINE is what separates two checks' timing verdicts. This reconciles determinism-under-seed with the reality that Pulse runs in real time as a black box.

- **[Read-Back Dependency Posture] Version-pinned MCP contract + preflight gate (protocol `2024-11-05` · tool presence · data-dir canary) + per-scenario explicit degrade:** At suite start, MCP `initialize` asserts the negotiated protocol version — **pinned at `2024-11-05`, Pulse's actual hand-rolled server version, read from the `initialize` result (no client-library default to drift from)** — plus presence of each required tool (`query_incident_list` · `retrieve_report` with `degraded_mode` · `retrieve_telemetry_slice` · `mark_incident_resolved` · `retrieve_incident_events`) against a pinned manifest; the gate then attempts a **canary round-trip** — Conductor emits a unique fingerprint-storm (three, 90 s apart, under real-model L4) and asserts Pulse opened an incident **AFTER the storm's emission instant** — to prove the data-dir/workspace wiring before any scenario trusts read-back, and to attribute the incident to THIS run rather than to corpus residue. The gate reaches `ready:true` live (`canary_round_trip: "ok"`, exit 0). Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-16-canary-fingerprint-derivation-aligned/evidence/leg-verdict.md`.

**Freshness is the canary's carrier BY CHOICE.** The model's `evidence_refs` — which the deterministic-L4 fixture fills with a constant `det-*` triple (`det-span-…` / `det-template-0007` / `det-fingerprint-…`) — are non-empty but payload-INVARIANT. From SUT HEAD `83d4060` an incident's `retrieve_telemetry_slice.fingerprint_refs` are the model's refs ∪ the triggering cue's full-hex fingerprint (`grounded_fingerprint_hashes`), written at creation only — a dedupe never updates it; at Pulse S `03ec944` Conductor's emitted fingerprint is a member (4 refs, 3 `det-*`) and its `retrieve_report` reads `degraded_mode: false`, as measured at `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-02-p-075-assert-round-against-pulse/evidence/round-ledger.md`. Ten committed live envelopes of 2026-09-10 carry such a 32-hex value, and the canary's differs run to run because its storm is unique per run. Freshness stays the canary's carrier because it is sufficient and unchanged, not because nothing else varies; the real-model capture attributes by the cue fingerprint AND freshness. Conductor stamps the emission instant from `std::time` and compares against `opened_at_unix_nano`, which Pulse sources from the corpus row's own `created_unix_nano` (`mcp-server/tools.rs:412`, surfaced at `:348-354`). **Honest limit, narrowed:** freshness proves causation-in-time; the one read-back value that varies with the emitted payload is the grounded cue fingerprint, while every L4-authored field (`title` / `severity` / `fingerprint` / `evidence_refs`) remains a fixture constant under deterministic L4. `incident_events` — the corpus table persisting created/resolved lifecycle events, and the one table whose content is NOT L4-authored — reached no MCP tool at Pulse HEAD `83d4060`; at S2 `cdb6c1e` `retrieve_incident_events` reads it by id (oldest first, `resolved` stamped inside the `mark_incident_resolved` call), a pinned required tool since 2026-10-03.

Payload fidelity is PARTIAL at `83d4060` — one read-back value, the grounded cue fingerprint, varies with what Conductor emitted (above); **runtime-STATE fidelity** needs no L4-authored field at all, and is live-proven: Conductor writes through `mark_incident_resolved` and observes the consequence through `query_incident_list`. It survives deterministic L4 precisely because it depends on no L4-authored field — it varies with what Conductor DID, not with what it EMITTED. Measured 2026-09-01: incident 6 resolved and gone from the active set with `idle_seconds_at_resolve = 0.0`, against Pulse's 120s auto-resolve idle threshold, so the resolver is excluded by construction and Conductor's write is the only remaining cause — `conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs`.

**Two mechanisms measured the same day bound how that attribution can be built.** (1) **At most ONE incident is active per DEDUPE TUPLE:** Pulse's producer dedupes a new incident against an OPEN incident carrying the same `(kind, scope, scope_id)` tuple — the workspace scopes the CANDIDATE SET, the tuple is the key, **as measured at `andromeda-pulse pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:811`** (HEAD `83d4060`). The originating leg's storms all shared one tuple, which is why it observed the effect at workspace grain. So a spared-control design is unattainable WITHIN a tuple, and the freshness caveat "a concurrent unrelated incident inside the poll window would satisfy it" cannot arise within one — attribution rides LIVENESS instead (an incident refreshed seconds ago cannot be the idle-resolver's). Across DIFFERENT scopes both remain possible: a cross-scope two-incident control is a weighable route option, untested, **not** a retirement. (2) **The DECLINED write arm is unreachable through MCP:** Pulse guards on `UPDATE … WHERE id = ?5 AND updated_unix_nano <= ?2` returning `DeclinedStale` on zero rows (`crates/corpus/src/contract.rs:652-659`), and its dispatch stamps `now` fresh per call, so the predicate fails only against a future-stamped row. That arm is stub-proven and permanently so.

**Conductor's fingerprint now IS Pulse's derivation**, recomputed over the same preimage the wire carries: blake3 over `exception_type` + `\0` + `normalize_stacktrace(render_stacktrace(spec))`, truncated to `FINGERPRINT_BYTES = 16` and rendered as **32 lowercase hex chars** (`conductor-emit/src/exception.rs`), transcribed from `andromeda-pulse crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs` (`compute_exception_fingerprint`) at HEAD `efabe8e`. Pulse's 8-char prefix (`fingerprint_to_hex_prefix`) is a logging convenience, not a wire identity. It is no longer the gate's carrier — its value is that Conductor's expectation now predicts how Pulse actually GROUPS exceptions (P-017/P-018 and the storm live proof). ONE identity narrowing comes with it, deliberate: only the first `NORMALIZED_FRAMES = 3` normalized lines contribute. **Normalization is TOKEN-LEADING** — `is_absolute_path_start` is guarded by `is_token_boundary`, so a path token counts as absolute only at position 0 or after a non-path byte. A RELATIVE path is therefore preserved in FULL and is identity-significant at EVERY depth (`src/worker.rs`, `src/anything/else.rs` and `other/worker.rs` are three DISTINCT identities), while a TOKEN-LEADING absolute path is stripped to nothing (`at handler(/usr/lib/thing.rs:10)` → `at handler()`), which differs from every surviving relative path — so no path variation can preserve identity for a relative-path base. The insensitive axes are LINE (`:line(:col)` suffixes) and HEX ADDRESSES (`0x…`). Measured 2026-08-17 and byte-verified against `andromeda-pulse crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs` at HEAD `efabe8e`; pinned by `exception.rs::relative_paths_are_significant_at_every_depth` + `::token_leading_absolute_paths_normalize_to_the_same_empty_form`. **Caveat (verified live 2026-06-27): Pulse's incident creation is NON-DETERMINISTIC + LLM-in-the-loop**: the write-path is OTLP → L1 → L2 RetryStorm cue (deterministic; ≥5 same fingerprint / 30s raises a **Suggested** cue, ≥10 the **Autonomous** cue Tier-1 requires — clearing the ≥5 floor alone forms no incident) → L3 digest (20-60s cadence) → **L4 llama.cpp inference decides Dismiss/Severity** → incident — an incident forms only if the L4 model surfaces it (behind a degraded-mode backoff; never cleanly reproduced even in Pulse's own dev), so deterministic incident-readback verification against the real LLM is impossible. **How Conductor deterministically verifies an LLM-in-the-loop SUT is SETTLED** — the leading option landed Pulse-side: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true` swaps a canned `L4Output` for the inference, which is what makes the live legs reproducible. **Its cost is a recorded deferral, not a silence:** under deterministic L4 every live leg exercises the plumbing and never the interpretation, so **"Conductor green" does not mean Pulse's interpretation is trustworthy** — it means the pipeline carried a canned answer end to end. Verifying the real thing (deterministic mode OFF, a known root cause injected, the top hypothesis asserted to identify it) needs both real per-check read-back extraction and a non-deterministic live leg that can never be a CI gate; it is **owned by a conductor-0.3.0 entry** and pinned machine-readably in `.andromeda/residuals.md`. **That leg now SHIPS, driven only as the pre-stated series its posture contract fixes before the first drive — and once, on 2026-10-07, as its pre-registered capture run, which states no verdict:** `agent-run run --live real-model` (a `--live` selector, not a sixth command) drives `scenarios/real-model-interpretation.toml` under the real-model L4 posture and grades each counted drive against a rule committed before it fires. The 2026-09-23 drive blocked MODEL-SIDE at the one-storm canary (`NoAttributableIncident → Blocked`); the 2026-09-29 series cleared that with the three-storm canary (Readiness gate) and graded one drive `NotIdentified`, its model input carrying the workspace key as `[redacted: credit_card]` (Pulse's scrubber matched the dir name; as measured at that chunk's `evidence/rm-capture-b2.txt`). The 2026-10-07 sixth series then met `v3-09` on three drives, read no wider, and "Conductor green" still does not mean Pulse's interpretation is trustworthy. The four diagnostic-quality capabilities it covers are backed since 2026-09-29 (named by the scenario, each graded by its own harvest arm, out of `UNBACKED_AUTO`) — backing is not verifying. On absence / version-mismatch / empty-canary, dependent auto scenarios report as **blocked** (a distinct state, never silently downgraded to pass/fail/manual-check) with the named precondition. The two remaining report states are triggered as follows: **ManualCheck** is the terminal "awaits a human go/no-go" state, reached two ways — a visual/operator-checklist claim with no programmatic MCP read-back (the operator-checklist path, which cannot be auto-verified), OR an auto-measured model-interpretive (calibration-region) check routed there by the default `Verdict → ReportState` mapping (see §Probabilistic-Assertion Policy); **KnownResidual** is the state for a check whose deviation matches a pre-accepted residual (e.g. a `retrieve_report` result returned under `degraded_mode`, or a fingerprint flagged as an accepted known-residual), distinguishing an accepted residual from a real `Fail` in the run report. **A SECOND route reaches it (2026-08-20):** after a GREEN preflight — whose canary already proved this run reaches the corpus — a scenario read-back returning an EMPTY active list routes a **declare-only** scenario (zero `[[expected]]`) to the same pre-accepted residual (`KnownResidual` / `verdict: null`) rather than `Blocked`, because an emptied active list is Pulse's own auto-resolve lifecycle (120s idle / 30s resolver ticks) and a scenario that grades nothing cannot pass falsely on an empty observation. The carve-out is confined by construction: a scenario carrying ANY `[[expected]]` check does not receive THIS route — an empty active list leaves it `Blocked` with the named precondition — and every read-back call failure lands `Blocked` unconditionally. **That confinement binds this route ALONE.** The OTHER route to `KnownResidual` — the degraded read-back — is NOT gated on declare-only (measured 2026-08-21, leg D: a then checks-bearing `findings-counter-refresh` landed `KnownResidual` on a degraded read-back; a sample floor never hard-fails). **`degraded` is a PER-READ-BACK property, never a mode-wide guarantee.** Deterministic L4 has now been measured BOTH ways: `findings-counter-refresh` degraded (2026-08-21), while `degraded-mode-report` read back an OPEN, non-degraded incident and took the graded route to `manual_record` → `ManualCheck` — as measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite/evidence/live-suite-verdict.md`, where `state_for` (`conductor-run/src/execute.rs`) returns `KnownResidual` iff `observation.degraded`, so a `ManualCheck` row proves `degraded == false`. The mechanism is CREATION-time: Pulse attaches the parsed interpretation when it creates the incident (`andromeda-pulse pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:884`, commit `b2e4cb3`, read at HEAD `83d4060`), so a single-storm incident can read back non-degraded — which is also why a real-model leg needs no multi-digest emission profile to have a hypothesis to grade (§Occupied Resources, the posture-doc entry). The degraded read-back remains one of the two routes to `KnownResidual` and remains ungated on declare-only. So "checks-bearing ⇒ `Blocked`" is true of the auto-resolve route and of read-back FAILURES, never as a global guarantee. Shipped as `route_read_back` / `ReadBack {Graded, AutoResolved, Blocked}` (crate-private, `conductor-run`), unit-pinned on all three arms, and **first fired LIVE on 2026-08-21** (leg E, `ack-cooldown`): a scenario that forms no incident of its own leaves only the preflight canary's, whose cues are `curious` — and the Tier-1 coordinator accepts Autonomous alone, so nothing refreshed it — letting it auto-resolve on schedule before read-back. **That firing condition is UPTIME-BOUND, and the bound is the window IN FORCE AT BOOT, not a fixed hour.** The one-hour figure is `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_SECONDS = 3_600`'s DEFAULT (`andromeda-pulse crates/triage/src/baseline/activity_floor.rs:36`, evaluator per emit cycle at `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs:186`, HEAD `83d4060`); `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` overrides it once at Pulse's boot (§Occupied Resources — Environment variables), so a stretched boot-wide window disarms the silence evaluator for a whole suite. **That removes cause (a) and is NOT sufficient — cause (b) is untouched by the posture, and it is what still decides the leg.** With the evaluator disarmed (`silence_cues_emitted: 0`, `services_in_bootstrap: 2`), the arm is reached only when the window's last incident forms early enough to clear the 120s idle + 30s tick before read-back — as measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven/evidence/hue-verdict.md`, where two runs of the identical tree under the identical posture graded `KnownResidual` and `ManualCheck`. So the posture makes the arm REACHABLE rather than RELIABLE, and this leg stays not-run-stable under it. Under the DEFAULT window the mechanism below is unchanged: "nothing refreshed it" holds only while Pulse is inside the emitting service's one-hour bootstrap window; past it, the silence evaluator raises `service_went_silent` cues for exactly the quiet the arm depends on, and those cues reach the Autonomous band and create NEW incidents during the silent phase — so the active set is never empty and the arm is unreachable at any window length. Inside the window the arm is reachable but still bounded by the 120s idle + 30s tick measured from the LAST preflight incident, which can be more than one. The canary's own error-rate cues keep the list non-empty only while a cue-bearing digest refreshes an incident of the SAME identity, which a `curious` cue never triggers.

- **[Probabilistic-Assertion Policy] Two-state split (hard-fail / calibration-region):** Deterministic claims (hard signals, baseline math, suppression/bypass logic, lifecycle timing) are hard pass/fail; model-interpretive claims (severity choice, hypothesis quality, P-008 root-vs-deep weighting) are calibration-region + report-for-human and never hard-failed on exact values — because exact-match assertions cannot fairly judge a model-backed detector. The default `Verdict → ReportState` mapping is `Pass→Pass` / `Fail→Fail` / `CalibrationRegion→ManualCheck` (`Verdict::default_report_state`); `verdict` and `state` stay independent (a producer may set a context-specific state), and the run-report lamp is chosen **verdict-first**, so a calibration row renders HOLD, not Manual. **A pre-committed-rule arm (2026-09-22):** a model-interpretive claim graded against a rule committed BEFORE the drive may `Pass` on a match (`Identified → (Pass, Pass)`), a miss is `CalibrationRegion → ManualCheck` — never `Fail` — and an outcome with nothing to grade (no ranked hypothesis, no attributable incident, a failed read-back) is `(null, Blocked)`. It ships at test tier, in `conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs`'s `row()`; `conductor-verify`'s `classify()` is unchanged, and no `Verdict` / `ReportState` variant or envelope key was added.

- **[Run-History Persistence] File artifacts + embedded SQLite index:** Per-run JSONL emission journal + Markdown run report stay on disk as agent-parseable ground truth; a thin `runs.db` indexes run_id · seed · scenario · P-IDs · verdict · fingerprints · timestamps for cross-run/seed-to-seed queries and for P-036 cross-incident fingerprint recurrence, kept synchronous and append-mostly off the async runtime.

title: Conventions

body: **Interface surfaces (three pinned, no network API of Conductor's own):**

- **Outbound emission:** OTLP over gRPC to `127.0.0.1:4317` via tonic 0.14.6 / tonic-prost 0.14.6; OTLP wire format built from opentelemetry-proto raw types. OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions are the shared vocabulary (`service.name`, span `Status.Code=ERROR`, exception span events with `exception.type`/`message`/`stacktrace`, log `SeverityNumber` at boundaries); W3C Trace Context propagates across emulated service edges.

- **Inbound verification:** MCP read-back via a hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC client over the sidecar's stdio (rmcp removed — Pulse's `tools/call` is non-MCP-compliant); a version-pinned contract manifest + `initialize` preflight gate, with the **blocked** report state on mismatch.

**Error handling:** Typed `thiserror` enums per seam crate (e.g. `EmitError`, `VerifyError`, `ContractMismatch`, `ConfigError`); `anyhow` only at the `conductor-cli` edge. A type-level verdict/error wall separates verification outcomes from harness failures: `enum Verdict { Pass, Fail, CalibrationRegion }` and `enum ReportState { Pass, Fail, ManualCheck, KnownResidual, Blocked }` are returned as `Ok(...)`; `Result::Err` means a harness fault (config parse, transport down, MCP unreachable). Read-back transport/decode/JSON-RPC errors fan out into `VerifyError` variants (`Transport`/`Protocol`/`Decode`/`JsonRpc` — blocked/fail/harness-error); garde's validation `Report` becomes a `ConfigError` harness-failure class via `#[from]`. `tonic::Status` codes and MCP error responses are first-class verification inputs, not panics.

**Naming patterns:** snake_case Rust source files and identifiers (per Rust convention); crates named `conductor-<seam>` (kebab-case crate names, snake_case module paths); scenarios keyed by Pulse capability P-ID, drawn from the SUT capability manifest's accepted set — "no scenario without a P-ID". On-disk artifacts use kebab-case Markdown filenames (e.g. `coverage-matrix.md`, run report) and per-run JSONL journals.

**Config conventions:** Declarative scenario config (no scenario DSL) deserialized with serde and bounds-checked with garde at load; validation co-located with the serde structs in their owning seam crates, diving into nested spec structs rather than skipping them. Durations are non-negative; an error fraction is bounded (shipped as an integer `error_percent` ∈ 0..=100); ramp factors validated sane; latency targets enforce p50≤p95≤p99 ordering and severity-mix sums. A phase's emission shape is declared data — `EmissionSpec { signal, occurrences, shape }`, where `occurrences: 0` is a deliberate silence window and the shape selects its emit-primitive family. A phase may also declare a FAULT for its window — the optional `[phases.fault]` table (`PhaseSpec.fault: Option<FaultSpec>`, serde default absent, garde `dive`) carrying the closed `FaultKindSpec::PortOccupier` kind (an unknown kind is a parse error, never an inferred default), under the scenario-level invariant that a fault-declaring phase is a silence window (`fault_phases_are_silent`: fault ⇒ `occurrences = 0` — during a port-occupier hold nothing real listens on the egress target). An `[[expected]]` check may additionally declare `budget_ms` — optional integer milliseconds (`#[serde(default)]`, garde `range(min = 1, max = MAX_BUDGET_MS)`, the ceiling DERIVED from `SloTier::Tier90s.deadline_ms()` rather than re-pinned as a literal) — the sub-tier deadline that check is graded against; absent means it inherits its scenario's tier. Because the rule spans `expected` and its sibling `slo_tier`, it is checked at load by `Scenario::check_budgets()` rather than by garde (§Established Decisions [Validation Library]). No committed scenario TOML declares one. A scenario may additionally declare `[[checklist]]` — an array-of-tables of `ChecklistItem { induced, observation }` (`#[serde(default)]`, garde `dive`, both halves `length(min = 1, max = MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT)` with `MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT = 200`, a length bound on untrusted scenario-authored text the CLI's interactive hold prints, each half on its own indented `induced:` / `observe:` line) carrying the operator-checklist rows a hold renders; `HoldPoint` carries the same vector so the hold projects them to the CLI's interactive hold (the headless path prints none). Because that rule spans `checklist` and its sibling `expected`, it too is checked at load — by `Scenario::check_checklist()`, which rejects a `[[checklist]]` declared beside a non-empty `expected` (the checklist renders only on the operator-checklist path, which a checks-bearing scenario never takes). Exactly two committed scenarios declare it: `halo-hue-encoding` and `halo-breathing-encoding`.

**Data model conventions (SQLite / `runs.db`):** Raw SQL, no migration framework; primary index keyed by `run_id` (with `seed`/`scenario`) per the Run-History decision — no synthetic UUID/serial PK is introduced. Timestamps are stored as journal-relative values whose source of truth is the JSONL journal; wall-clock stamps for the journal come from `std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant` (never tokio's virtual clock, which would break journal-relative SLO math). Column types are fixed on first write (no migration framework to coerce later): on `runs`, `latency_ms` is INTEGER milliseconds (NULL for blocked rows); `journal_emitted_at`/`read_back_observed_at` are stored as TEXT RFC-3339 (the JSONL envelope's wire form), while the integer-millisecond value the SLO math consumes is the separate `latency_ms` INTEGER column; `slo_tier` is a closed TEXT enum over exactly `<5s`/`<20s`/`<90s`. Nullability is qualified PER TABLE: on `run_check` both `latency_ms` and `deadline_ms` are INTEGER **NOT NULL** — a blocked or declare-only check emits no row at all rather than a NULL one — and `budget_ms` is INTEGER NULL when the check inherits its scenario's tier. Fingerprint arrays are stored as a JSON1 TEXT array of fingerprint strings and indexed via SQLite JSON1.

title: Standard Contracts

body: Conductor exposes no HTTP service, so it has no `/health` or `/ready` HTTP endpoints. The equivalent contracts every scenario/module must follow are the **MCP preflight readiness gate** and the **run report artifact envelope** — these are the shared shapes scopes depend on.

**Readiness gate (MCP `initialize` preflight + data-dir canary, run once at suite start).** Asserts the negotiated protocol version (pinned at `2024-11-05` — Pulse's hand-rolled server version, `jsonrpc.rs:`) and required-tool presence against the pinned contract manifest, then attempts a **canary round-trip** — emit a unique fingerprint-storm, assert an incident opened AFTER the storm's emission instant — to prove the data-dir/workspace wiring end-to-end (tool presence alone does not prove read-back sees the live Pulse's corpus) and to attribute that incident to this run rather than to residue. Under the real-model L4 posture the canary is `REAL_MODEL_CANARY_STORMS = 3` distinct storms of `CANARY_STORM_COUNT` 12, `REAL_MODEL_CANARY_STORM_GAP = 90 s` apart, the freshness stamp taken before the first, because the real model's surface/dismiss decision is nondeterministic per decision (as measured at the 2026-09-29 series: `k_A = 2`, confirmed `k_B = 2`); the deterministic canary (`boot` and every deterministic leg) stays one storm, byte-identical. **The gate reached `ready:true` for the first time on 2026-08-16.** The carrier is freshness BY CHOICE — sufficient and unchanged — not because payload identity is out of reach: at HEAD `83d4060` an incident's `fingerprint_refs` carries the triggering cue's full-hex fingerprint beside the L4 model's `evidence_refs` (a constant `det-*` triple under deterministic L4), and that value varies with what Conductor emitted (measured 2026-09-10). Titles stay scrubbed, the `span_events` fingerprint column stays unread by any MCP tool, and `incident_events` — the non-L4-authored lifecycle table — reached no MCP tool at HEAD `83d4060` (measured 2026-09-01) and is read by `retrieve_incident_events` at Pulse S2 `cdb6c1e` (read live 2026-10-03). **Runtime-STATE fidelity** is the other live-proven axis — the `mark_incident_resolved` write plus `query_incident_list` active-set membership vary with what Conductor DID, and are live-proven. See §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture]. Read a staleness block accordingly: it says the corpus is reachable and non-empty but this run's storm raised nothing, NOT that the wiring is broken. **NOTE (verified live 2026-06-27):** the round-trip can complete only when Pulse's non-deterministic LLM pipeline (L2 cue → L3 digest → L4 inference) surfaces an incident (see [Read-Back Dependency Posture] + `architecture-amendments.md`); the live read-back surface is **9 tools** at Pulse S2 `cdb6c1e` (4 live-buffer: `query_traces`/`query_metrics`/`query_logs`/`generate_snapshot` + the 5 corpus tools; 8 at `83d4060`), and only the **persistent-corpus tools** work cross-process from a Conductor-spawned sidecar — the in-memory-buffer tools return empty (the sidecar shares no memory with pulse-app). Conceptual readiness result shape (in-memory / serialized into the run report):

```json
{
  "ready": false,
  "negotiated_protocol_version": "2024-11-05",
  "expected_protocol_version": "2024-11-05",
  "required_tools": {
    "query_incident_list":     "present",
    "retrieve_report":         "present",
    "retrieve_telemetry_slice":"absent",
    "mark_incident_resolved":  "present",
    "retrieve_incident_events":"present"
  },
  "data_dir": "<ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR — must equal the live Pulse's>",
  "canary_round_trip": "ok",
  "blocked_precondition": "mcp-server cargo feature + ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED + ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR == live Pulse's data-dir",
  "checked_at": "2026-06-12T21:59:37Z"
}
```

When `ready` is false, every dependent auto scenario is emitted into the report with `state: "blocked"` and the named precondition — never pass/fail/manual-check. **The gate's named preconditions are FIVE:** protocol version-mismatch · required-tool absence · no incident opened after the canary storm was emitted (every incident in the corpus predates it, so Pulse raised none for this run) · **app/sidecar workspace-key agreement** · and **unmet run-contract terms** (`contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml`, §Occupied Resources). **Which terms bind is POSTURE-selected (2026-09-22):** the gate evaluates under one L4 posture — `preflight_for(manifest, posture)` grades the contract through `RunContract::evaluate_for`, where a term tagged with a posture binds only under it and an untagged term under every posture. `conductor run` passes the scenario's declared `l4_posture`; `preflight()` delegates to the deterministic posture and remains what `conductor suite` and `drive_run` call; `readiness()` (the `boot` verb) stays deterministic. A scenario whose declared posture differs from the posture its run's gate evaluated is recorded `Blocked` at SCENARIO level, before the ready check, with a message-borne log line naming both postures — never a sixth gate precondition. The last composes ONE string naming each unmet term individually — its condition and its candidate causes — and its arm sits after the tool checks but BEFORE the canary arms, because an unmet launch condition *explains* a failed canary: surfacing the canary symptom first sends the operator to the wrong cause, and with the contract's raised poll floor it would also spend the whole budget to do so. That arm skips the canary poll rather than paying it. The last is emitted when `query_incident_list` returns zero incidents — byte-identical on the wire to a workspace-key divergence, which returns zero rows forever. **The divergence mechanism changed SUT-side and is now the FALLBACK case (measured 2026-09-01, HEAD `83d4060`):** `pulse-app` PUBLISHES the key it stamps to `{data_dir}/run/workspace-key`, and the sidecar reads it (`workspace_detector::contract::read_published_workspace_key`), falling back to `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` only when that file is absent, unreadable, or fails its bounds/control-character check. So a divergence now requires the publication to fail; on the 2026-09-01 leg the published key matched the incidents' stamped `workspace` byte-for-byte (`\\?\…` extended-length form, the app's detected root) and no divergence occurred. That string therefore names the key agreement AND "Pulse raised no incident" as the two candidate causes rather than claiming a measurement Conductor cannot make (read-back exposes no second workspace key: `query_incident_list` takes no arguments). Every precondition string is host-path-free — `data_dir` is redacted in the readiness result. A blocked row populates only the identity fields (`run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `slo_tier`); `verdict`, `journal_emitted_at`, `read_back_observed_at`, `latency_ms`, and `fingerprints` are emitted as JSON `null` (and stored NULL in `runs.db`) because the scenario was never measured. Cross-run latency/percentile and P-036 fingerprint queries MUST exclude NULL-measurement rows so blocked scenarios never contribute phantom values. **Corpus access (corrected — verified live 2026-06-27):** Pulse's `corpus.db` is **plaintext SQLite**, NOT encrypted-at-rest — the prior P-049 "encrypted at rest / `OsKeychainBackend` / keychain read-while-write" assumption is WRONG, so the keychain-failure canary mode does not apply. The sidecar opens `{data_dir}/corpus/corpus.db` directly; incidents are filtered by the `workspace` column (not `workspace_root`). Conductor still treats `corpus.db` as out-of-scope SUT-owned data (never persists/exfiltrates it — save ONE ratified, scoped exception since 2026-09-23: scrubbed real-model capture evidence in a chunk's `evidence/` tree, security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection, which records the 2026-09-29 breach — series pins in test source, outside that tree — as REMEDIED on 2026-09-30: every capture sha256 digest-pinned and graded from its file, no capture text in test source, the graded 2026-09-23 copy elided; both stated residuals — the frozen 2026-09-22 file's prefix and the graded 2026-10-01 d3 capture's all-digit prefix — were fixed 2026-10-02 under the founder's ruling, the frozen file elided in place).

**Liveness equivalent (OTLP egress check).** The `127.0.0.1:4317` connectability check has TWO production callers, with deliberately different dispositions. Before emission, the timeline engine confirms the gRPC channel is connectable; a refused transport surfaces there as a harness error (`Result::Err`), not a verification verdict. The scheduling-time precondition probe (`conductor_run::observe_preconditions`) reuses the same connect-and-drop primitive — no bind, no OTLP written, `:4318` untouched — but a refusal there is a REPORTED unmet precondition and a non-zero exit, never an `Err` and never a verdict: it runs before any scenario exists to carry one. **The probe grades THREE subjects — `egress-reachable` · `sidecar-resolvable` · `handles-declared` — each graded by the KIND of value its handle carries, so all three are meetable.** `observe_preconditions` builds the `declared` set PER HANDLE through `conductor_core::handle_declared`: the PATH-valued `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` is declared when present and non-empty after trim, while every other name delegates to the value-only `conductor_core::flag_declared` and keeps the `"true"`/`"1"` truthy gate — the DETERMINISTIC posture's grading, which every pre-existing scenario and the flagless probe take. Under the real-model posture (2026-09-22), selected by `conductor preconditions --for <scenario>` naming a scenario that declares it, `observe_preconditions_for` grades through `conductor_core::handle_declared_for`, which differs only for `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`: that handle must be ABSENT or falsy, read under the union of both sides' truthiness rules (Conductor's `true`/`1` ∪ Pulse's `1`/`true`/`yes`, trimmed and ASCII-lowercased — `conductor_core::flag_declared_on_either_side`), so its declaration is the unmet subject; exit 0 was measured under the real-model launch environment on 2026-09-23. A non-zero exit therefore names a genuinely unmet subject again. As measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence/report.md` (2026-09-04T17:07Z, full operator env: `conductor preconditions` exit 0, printing `[PRECONDITION] every live-Pulse precondition is satisfied`), and `agent-run boot`'s leading arm now short-circuits only on an actually-unmet subject — it reached `conductor preflight --json` and emitted `ReadyState` JSON in BOTH shipped shells (`scripts/agent-run.sh` 17:07:17→17:08:04Z · `scripts/agent-run.ps1` 17:11:16→17:12:03Z, both exit 0, zero `skipped preflight` lines, neither script edited). The env read is covered by `observe_preconditions_grades_each_handle_from_its_own_environment`, which exercises the read→grade path rather than constructing the `declared` set directly. This SUPERSEDES the 2026-09-04T06:41Z reading (the `sr-findings-remediation` measurement), which recorded the pre-fix state where one truthy-only `declares()` graded all three names and the PATH handle could never declare.
**Run report envelope (per scenario check).** Every check classifies into the canonical states; the Markdown report + `runs.db` row share this shape:

```json
{
  "run_id": "2026-06-12T21-59-37-...",
  "seed": 424242,
  "scenario": "error-baseline-spike",
  "p_ids": ["P-009", "P-010"],
  "verdict": "Pass",
  "state": "Pass",
  "journal_emitted_at": "...",
  "read_back_observed_at": "...",
  "latency_ms": 1840,
  "slo_tier": "<90s",
  "fingerprints": ["..."]
}
```

`verdict ∈ {Pass, Fail, CalibrationRegion}`; `state ∈ {Pass, Fail, ManualCheck, KnownResidual, Blocked}`. The sample's Pass/Pass is illustrative of the envelope SHAPE; NINE families now ship declare-only — the durable anchor is the COMPLEMENT, which shrinks rather than grows: as measured 2026-09-15 and again 2026-09-23 exactly TWO committed scenarios still declare live `[[expected]]` checks, `root-span-error-scope` and `span-status-error-detection` (`grep -l '^\[\[expected\]\]' scenarios/*.toml` → 2 of 37 at 2026-09-23 — the escaped form; the unescaped `'^[[expected]]'` this passage carried until then is a bracket expression and returns 0), so declare-only is the corpus's default shape and the list below records HOW each family reached it — `fingerprint-storm` (retired 2026-08-16), `error-baseline-spike` + `latency-regression` (2026-08-18), `restart-suppression` (2026-08-18), `pii-scrub` (2026-08-19), the connection family (`receiver-lifecycle-state` · `receiver-failed-port-conflict` · `last-span-ago-tracking` · `orthogonal-health-domains`, 2026-08-19), the delegated-timing family (`halo-hue-encoding` · `service-constellation-discovery` · `report-render-surface`, 2026-08-21, joined by `findings-counter-refresh` 2026-09-15), the severity-lifecycle family (`incident-auto-resolution` · `severity-tier-autonomous` · `severity-tier-suggested` · `severity-tier-curious` · `ack-cooldown`, 2026-08-21) and the structurally-dead-assertion class (`constellation-severity-live-wiring` · `pulse-run-contract` · `cross-incident-recurrence`, 2026-09-15, joined the same day by `activity-floor` · `service-went-silent` · `high-severity-log-capture` · `exception-event-capture` · `threshold-hot-reload` — the class was taken in two passes over one twelve-block population, not decomposed) — zero `[[expected]]` checks each (no read-back surface can carry them under deterministic L4), so their live rows land `verdict: null` / `state: "KnownResidual"` by EITHER of the two routes to that state — the degraded read-back, or (2026-08-20) the auto-resolve residual when a post-green-preflight read-back finds an empty active list — with the live claims graded at the harvest tier. `real-model-interpretation` (2026-09-22) is declare-only FROM BIRTH and is not a tenth family: it grades nothing through the envelope — its interpretation claim is graded at the harvest tier against a rule committed before the drive — and its success row, a non-degraded read-back, lands `ManualCheck`, not `KnownResidual`. Every read-back call failure still lands `Blocked` unconditionally; a checks-bearing scenario is excluded from the AUTO-RESOLVE route only, and can still reach `KnownResidual` through the degraded read-back (measured 2026-08-21, leg D — see §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture]).

**Per-check record (the second shared artifact shape).** Beside the eleven-field run envelope, a graded check serializes as a nine-key `CheckRecord` — `run_id` · `scenario` · `check_index` (its ordinal in the scenario's `expected` list, the stable key since an `ExpectedCheck` carries no name) · `kind` · `verdict` · `state` · `latency_ms` · `deadline_ms` · `budget_ms` (null when the check inherits its scenario's tier). It rides three surfaces: the per-run JSONL journal beside the envelope rows, the `run_check` table (§Occupied Resources), and an indented per-check detail line under each scenario block of the Markdown report. It exists because the run seam grades EVERY check but the envelope row carries only the worst — the per-check grain is where the others land, with the deadline each was actually judged against. The envelope's own eleven-field shape is byte-unchanged, and a blocked or declare-only scenario emits ZERO check records.

**Timestamp formats.** `run_id` uses a filesystem-safe hyphen-delimited stamp (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-<suffix>`) because it is the `runs.db` primary key and the stem of `<run_id>.jsonl` / the run report — colons are illegal in filenames on the Windows dev host. In-payload instant fields use colon-delimited RFC-3339 (`2026-06-12T21:59:37Z`): `checked_at` in the readiness result, and the human-facing run-report serialization of `journal_emitted_at`/`read_back_observed_at` (whose `runs.db` columns are TEXT RFC-3339 per the Data model conventions; the integer-millisecond value the SLO math consumes is the separate `latency_ms` INTEGER column). The encodings denote the same instant; only `run_id` is constrained to the hyphen form.

title: Occupied Resources

body: **Ports:**

- `127.0.0.1:4317` — OTLP/gRPC **egress target** (Pulse's loopback ingest). Conductor is the client; the port is owned by Pulse, but Conductor must be co-located with it. The port-occupier fault scenario also binds `:4317` to exercise Pulse's reaction.
- `:4318` (OTLP/HTTP) — not used; gRPC-only loopback is the pinned path.

- No non-loopback egress: the CI-job-scoped `https://msedgedriver.microsoft.com` fetch retired 2026-10-11 with the `a11y` job, so the loopback-only client model holds for every shipped binary, harness leg and CI job (count 1 → 0).
- No inbound listener of Conductor's own **in the shipped binaries** (no API port, no DB port — SQLite is embedded/in-process).
**Interface routes / surfaces (no HTTP routes):**
- MCP tools consumed: `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report` (with `degraded_mode`), `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved`, `retrieve_incident_events`.
- Route prefixes: none — Conductor exposes no HTTP surface; the consumed MCP tool names are the complete route-equivalent set, and the `conductor-*` crate-name prefix is the reserved namespace.
**Service / process names:**
- `conductor-cli` (the `agent-run` binary) — headless source of truth.

- Launched child process: Pulse MCP server (`andromeda-pulse-mcp`), spawned over PIPED stdio from a `tokio::process::Command` built by `conductor-verify/src/spawn.rs::build_command` and handed to `ReadbackClient::connect_command`. Gated on its `mcp-server` feature, **spawned with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` set to the live Pulse's data-dir** so it reads the same corpus (the established `.env(...)` spawn pattern in Pulse's `tests/sidecar_subprocess.rs`). **On Windows the command carries the `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` creation flag** (`spawn::console_suppressing_flags()`, `#[cfg(windows)]`), so a launched sidecar raises no console pane and publishes no absolute exe path (evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-sidecar-spawn-without-a-console-window/evidence/nvda-pass.json`). The program is a fixed NAME resolved through the inherited `PATH` (never operator-chosen), so **`PATH` is a spawn-resolution input**: where the sidecar binary is not on it, preflight returns BLOCKED in ~2ms with every tool `absent` — at row level indistinguishable from a genuine SUT-side gate failure — so every operator-driven live leg's firing form carries a `PATH` prefix resolving it (measured 2026-09-01).

- Emitted OTLP service identities (the PRODUCT stream's `service.name` values): `conductor` (`DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME` — the scenario dispatcher's identity) and `conductor-canary` (`CANARY_SERVICE_NAME`, `conductor-run` — the preflight canary's warm-up + storm). Split deliberately (2026-08-18): the preflight runs inside every scenario leg, and Pulse keys per-service sample counts (`persistence_seconds` = cumulative samples, `crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs:55` at HEAD `efabe8e`) and error-rate EWMAs per service — a shared identity would age every scenario's young-sample suppression window and inflate its baseline denominator before phase 1 emits.

**Crate names (workspace members):** `conductor-core` (the runtime-agnostic engine library the other members depend on — `conductor-emit` EXCEPTED; the dependent set is whatever the members' `Cargo.toml` files declare, never a universal), `conductor-timeline`, `conductor-emit`, `conductor-faults`, `conductor-verify`, `conductor-report`, `conductor-run` (the run composition root library — preflight + scenario execution + `persist` + the suite driver `drive_run` (the composition `conductor suite` drives: a per-scenario progress callback, a stop flag polled before each scenario and set by the suite's Ctrl-C handler, one persist that keeps every finished record) + the fault-phase guard that binds/releases the port-occupier for a fault-declared phase's window, RAII release = the scheduler's boundary drop; carries the `conductor-run → conductor-faults` dependency edge — sitting above the seams and below the `conductor-cli` bin), and `conductor-cli`.
**On-disk artifacts / database:**

- `runs.db` — embedded SQLite index, **three tables**: `runs`, the scenario-grained run index keyed `(run_id, scenario)` (run_id · seed · scenario · P-IDs · verdict · fingerprints · timestamps); `run_envelope`, the run-level SUT-load-envelope standing keyed `run_id` (`classification` · `cause`); and `run_check`, the genuine **per-check index** keyed `(run_id, scenario, check_index)` (`kind` · `verdict` · `state` · `latency_ms` · `deadline_ms` NOT NULL, `budget_ms` NULL when the check inherits its scenario's tier). Each of the latter two is deliberately a separate table rather than a column on `runs`, on the same reasoning at a different grain: the envelope qualifier is run-scoped and the check qualifier is check-scoped, so `runs` keeps its eleven columns and `state` stays the closed five-variant set (§Standard Contracts). A blocked or declare-only scenario writes ZERO `run_check` rows — the per-check grain never synthesizes a value for something never measured.
- Per-run JSONL emission journal + per-run Markdown run report.

- `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` — the self-observation `tracing` JSON stream in agent mode (`--agent-mode`); a SEPARATE artifact + schema from the per-run emission journal, written as a sibling of the runs dir (moves with `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`), truncated per invocation (the `-latest` name).

- `runs/live-suite/{leg}.jsonl` — the per-leg frozen copies of `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` the operator-gated `run --live` suite writes before each next leg starts. They exist because that sink truncates per invocation. Harness-owned by `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` with NO `CONDUCTOR_*` handle of its own (the path is `$RUNS_DIR/live-suite`, so it moves with `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`) — git-ignored, LEG-stemmed and cleared at suite start by a non-recursive `rm -f …/*.jsonl` (the `cleanup` verb's idiom; the harness ships no recursive delete), so an aborted run's stale leg file is never read as current. The real-model arm (`run --live real-model`) writes three files there, cleared non-recursively before its leg: `rm.jsonl` (its frozen self-obs), `rm-capture.txt` (the grading rule's record, then the scrubbed capture) and `rm-capture.err`. Per-run `<run_id>.jsonl` journals and `runs.db` rows are unaffected.

- `runs/span-landing/span-{a,b}.jsonl` — the span-landing pass's drive journals: no `CONDUCTOR_*` handle, git-ignored, cleared by name (`rm -f`) before drive A, read by `span_landing_live` via `capture_paths`, a stale pair refused.
- `coverage-matrix.md` — every capability in the SUT capability manifest classified.
- Pinned MCP contract manifest file (`contracts/mcp-contract.toml`).

- `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` — the versioned SUT capability manifest: the accepted Pulse capability set (`sut_version` · `captured_at` · `capabilities[]`), the single source of which P-IDs a scenario may name. Runtime-read and bounds-checked at load; resolved from a fixed `CapabilityManifest::default_path()` through `resolve_under` with deliberately NO `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle (unlike `CONDUCTOR_CONTRACT_MANIFEST`). Re-aiming Conductor at a newer Pulse release is an edit to this file plus a matching row in the code-native coverage classification, which `check_sut_drift` holds to set-equality (§Established Decisions [Accepted Capability Set]).

- `contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml` — the pinned SUT load envelope: the proven-good storm bounds a scenario must stay inside (`sut_version` · `captured_at` · `provenance` · an `[envelope]` table · an `[[exempt]]` ledger of `{scenario, reason}`). Its terms are a **transcribed SUT record, never a Conductor measurement**, which the `provenance` field states so a reader can tell how far to trust them. Runtime-read and bounds-checked at load; resolved from a fixed `LoadEnvelope::default_path()` through `resolve_under` with deliberately NO `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle (the capability-manifest precedent). The **two sustained terms are the asserted ones**, judged PER EMITTING PHASE: no phase declaring occurrences may run longer than `max_sustained_storm_ms` nor emit faster than `max_sustained_rate_spans_per_s`. **The rate term counts WIRE RECORDS, and is an upper BOUND:** `phase_rate_exceeds` judges `occurrences × EmissionSpec::max_spans_per_dispatch() × 1000 > max_rate × gap_ms` (`conductor-core/src/load_envelope.rs`), exact integer math with no division. The per-dispatch count is measured PER `EmissionShape` arm against the dispatcher's own arm — `Ramp`/`Breathing` emit `sum(window_counts)`, `Latency` its `samples`, `Error` `depth + 1`, `Pii` 2 spans on traces or one record per category on logs, `Topology` one span per service, every other shape 1. It is a BOUND rather than an exact count because the rate curves' per-window counts carry seeded jitter (`conductor-emit/src/rate.rs`, ±15 %) while the static catalog gate has no seed, and a ceiling is the conservative direction for a load bound. Under the shipped mapping the catalog's worst case is `halo-breathing-encoding` at ~232 records/s, ≈43× under `max_sustained_rate_spans_per_s = 10000`. The term keeps its name and its value because it transcribes a SUT record about wire load. `max_scenario_duration_ms` is **recorded but no longer asserted** — elapsed time is not storm time. `check_load_envelope` (the static catalog gate) and `LoadEnvelope::classify` (the per-run judgment behind the `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` caption) read ONE shared basis BY CONSTRUCTION — `phase_rate_exceeds` has exactly one caller, `phase_breach`, whose only two callers they are — so the gate and the caption cannot mean different things. The `[[exempt]]` ledger — held at exact-set equality in both directions, so it can only shrink under compulsion — is **empty**: every catalog scenario passes the asserted terms unaided. The storm term bounds the longest single emitting window, never the SUMMED emitting-phase duration: summing disjoint bursts separated by quiet is not *sustained*.

- `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml` — the pinned Pulse run contract: the launch conditions under which a live Pulse can be verified at all (`sut_version` · `captured_at` · `provenance` · an `[incident_formation]` table of the harness's own obligations · a `[[term]]` list of `{id, statement, check, env?, posture?, causes}`). Its SUT-side terms are a **transcribed SUT record, never a Conductor measurement**, which the `provenance` field states. Runtime-read and bounds-checked at load; resolved from a fixed `RunContract::default_path()` through `resolve_under` with deliberately NO `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle (the capability-manifest precedent). Each term declares HOW it is checked, and that is a statement about what Conductor can honestly know: `shell-declaration` (observable as a declaration in Conductor's OWN environment — the shell that also launches `pulse-app` — unmet iff undeclared), `shell-absence` (the same observation, unmet iff DECLARED, the declaration read under the union of Conductor's and Pulse's truthiness rules; with `shell-declaration` the only kinds that can block, each naming its `env`), `asserted` (satisfied by construction, or reaching the gate proves it), `declared-not-observable` (true or false entirely on the SUT's side with no read-back surface exposing it — recorded so an operator can satisfy it, never blocking, because a block would claim a measurement Conductor cannot make). Of its SEVEN `[[term]]`s, `l4-deterministic` carries `posture = "deterministic"` and `l4-real-model` (`check = "shell-absence"` on `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`, `posture = "real-model"`) is a CONDUCTOR posture term, as the header's PROVENANCE line states, not a transcribed SUT record. A term's optional `posture` comes from the closed `L4Posture` set: a tagged term binds only under that posture, an untagged one under every posture (`RunContract::evaluate_for`; `evaluate` delegates to the deterministic posture, so its result is unchanged). The OBSERVED shell handle set stays TWO — `observed_env()` yields each var once, and two terms name the L4 handle. `sidecar-built` stays `asserted` although its rationale is measurably FALSE — a `PATH` miss short-circuits to `[BLOCKED]` in ~0s UPSTREAM of term evaluation (as measured at `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md:`), so it cannot catch its own falsity — because re-classifying moves what the preflight gate can block on (operator-selected at `2026-09-03-live-pulse-preconditions-probed`). `[incident_formation]` carries a warm-up pre-roll and the canary poll floor that outlasts the L3 digest cadence. The warm-up is harmless and its stated purpose measured FALSE on two axes: the **baseline-derived cue families** gate on `BootstrapState::Ready` (`crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs:164`) — `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_SECONDS = 3_600` per service, wall-clock (`crates/triage/src/baseline/activity_floor.rs:33`, the DEFAULT), with `baseline_state` at **0 rows** — which `warmup_ms = 45000` misses by **80×**, unfixable by its own knobs and uncatchable by its `asserted` term — and the canary's RetryStorm path consults no baseline at all (`crates/triage/src/pattern/storm.rs:245-285`; incidents form with `baseline_state` at 0 rows, `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/chunks/2026-08-15-tier-1-incident-path-investigation/evidence/premise-check.md`). What gates the canary is a **tier band on Conductor's own side**: the storm must clear `DEFAULT_AUTONOMOUS_THRESHOLD = 10` (`crates/triage/src/pattern/storm.rs:78`, compared with `>=` at `:245`) because Pulse's Tier-1 coordinator accepts Autonomous cues alone (`crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs:390`), which the shipped `CANARY_STORM_COUNT` of 12 clears. Every span `ok_span` builds carries a seeded per-call identity (disjoint warm-up/storm seed ranges), because Pulse's `spans` table is `PRIMARY KEY (trace_id, span_id)` (`andromeda-pulse crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:36`) and a replay rejects the whole batch. `tracked_fingerprints_count` is a **60s-windowed gauge over DISTINCT fingerprints, sampled at a 15s tick AFTER eviction** — a working storm reads `1` and a late sample 0 — so never read it as evidence of absence; the cumulative `storms_detected_total` and `fingerprints_evicted_total` are immune to the window. Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-14-canary-fingerprint-feed-capture/fingerprint-feed-verdict.md` · `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-15-canary-spans-pulse-fingerprints/evidence/leg-verdict.md`.

- `contracts/scenario-audit-ledger.toml` — the committed scenario-assertion audit ledger: the exact-set record `check_scenario_audit` grades the catalog against on two axes (`sut_version` · `sut_head` · `captured_at` · `provenance` header, an `[[live_assertion]]` array of `{scenario, ground, discriminates, weakness}` and an `[[over_tier]]` array of `{scenario, reason}`). Both arrays are graded in BOTH directions — a measured member absent from the ledger is `unpinned`, a pinned member the measurement no longer finds is `rotted`, a pin naming no catalog scenario is `lost_subject` — and every one surfaces as `CoreError::ScenarioAudit`, never a verdict. Its grounds are transcribed readings of `andromeda-pulse` at its own `sut_head`, so a SUT rendering change rots them visibly.
