## 2026-09-24-architecture-registries-compacted-under-the-read-cap — §Established Decisions [CI/CD]: passages moved out of the body

**Section:** §Established Decisions — [CI/CD]
**Change:** compacted under the read cap; the passages below left the body verbatim.
**Why:** the body holds only current truth; history lives here + in git (this sidecar's preamble).

- then `cargo build` / nextest / clippy on the dev OS target verify the harness compiles and unit/golden tests pass, and a third job (`a11y`, `runs-on: windows-2022` since 2026-09-17, moved from `windows-2025` on the measured configuration) runs the routine webview a11y leg — `scripts/agent-run.ps1 run --e2e` under `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT`, invoked since 2026-09-17 through the leg's entry point `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` DIRECTLY, at the hosted step's native HIGH integrity (its captured console and token witness printed by the step afterwards);
- the `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` launch that stood here from 2026-09-16 is retired from this step and survives only on the job's driver-alone diagnostics, the asserting step still carrying no `continue-on-error` and no `if:`.
- The job's WebView2 provisioning is likewise replaced:
- the `Install WebView2 Evergreen runtime 152+ (gate)` step and its `≥ 152` runtime floor are retired outright in favour of driver/runtime COHERENCE — a `Pin msedgedriver to the image's WebView2 runtime (gate)` step reads the runtime from the two `EdgeUpdate` client keys, fetches the driver for THAT version, Authenticode-gates it, asserts driver major == runtime major and publishes `EDGEWEBDRIVER`, carrying no `continue-on-error` and no `if:` — then the reused `journal_conformance` gate over `runs/a11y`, then the violation-record artifact upload (2026-09-07).
- **The a11y job ran RED on GitHub's hosted `windows-2025` image at runtime 152/153, as measured at runs 34157101273 · 34158355397 · 34160378753 · 34162118841 (2026-09-07, from a since-deleted `ci-probe/` ref) — a reading bound to THAT image and runtime pair, superseded as the arm's verdict by the green below.** It resolves the driver from the image and its RED wdio output reaches the job log — both fixed at `2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed` and proven in CI — then fails at WebView2 session creation, before the `journal_conformance` gate or the record upload is reached.
- The leg also RUNS on the Windows dev host through tauri-driver, and its tally there is now a green too:
- 12 passing / 2 skipped at runtime 152 (2026-09-10);
- 10 passing / 2 failing / 2 skipped re-measured 2026-09-16 after the host floated to Evergreen 153.0.4234.32 unprompted;
- and 12 passing / 0 failing / 2 skipped on 2026-09-17 once the two regressions were fixed.
- Those regressions were the hold-free Operable pair (SC 2.1.1 reachability · SC 2.4.3 focus order) and NOT session creation, and both were ASSERTION defects rather than a platform property — one walk waiting on a `BODY` sentinel this webview's focus cycle need not contain — so the pair is now environment-independent, measured green on two configurations differing in runtime major, driver major and coherence.
- Hosted-runner runnability is MEASURED and PROVEN for the configuration named above, and unproven elsewhere — the configuration that achieved it is no longer probe-scoped:
- it is the shipped arrangement as of 2026-09-17 (operator ruling at the chunk's P4, re-ruled at P5 to ratify the driver pin).
- **Since 2026-09-17 the job pins the DRIVER to the runtime the image already carries, replacing the in-job WebView2 runtime provisioning it ran from 2026-09-08 (conditionally from 2026-09-12)** — ahead of the routine arm it reads the runtime from the `EdgeUpdate` client keys and fetches msedgedriver for THAT version (§Occupied Resources — Ports), admitted by a pre-execution `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` gate (status `Valid` AND an `O=Microsoft Corporation` signer, non-zero exit on either arm), then asserts driver major == runtime major;
- The `≥ 152` runtime floor is RETIRED and no longer exists in code:
- it was not necessary (a coherent 131/131 pair runs the arm green), not sufficient (a coherent 152/152 pair fails, run `34654076633`), and destructive on the working configuration (run `35185153012` installed 153 over a native 131).
- Whether a 152+ runtime actually opens the remote-debugging endpoint is now **measured, and the answer is no** — as measured at CI run `34280136892` (2026-09-08), the run that followed the commit shipping the probe:
- the gate installed Evergreen 152.0.4191.66 (Authenticode `Valid`, `O=Microsoft Corporation`, re-read by the diagnostics step seven minutes later) and probe (a) still reported `DevToolsActivePort first seen: never within 90s` with the app alive (`HasExited=False`) and three `msedgewebview2` children resident.
- The runtime-major hypothesis is therefore FALSIFIED;
- the cause stayed OPEN until 2026-09-12, when it was established as elevation (below).
- **Both halves of the former leading candidate pair — a hosted-image policy, and a session property — are now MEASURED and neither holds**, as measured at CI run `34586959536` (`conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed/evidence/reading.md`, step `WebView2 cause probes (diagnostic)`, against a same-script dev-host control):
- all five probed Edge / EdgeUpdate / EdgeWebView policy keys are ABSENT in both the machine and user hives on the hosted runner AND on the dev host, so no policy difference exists to explain a behavioural one;
- and the runner is `SessionId 2` with `UserInteractive: True` — not session 0 and not a service context — corroborated by the isolation step's own `tasklist` showing the app and its webview children on Console session 2.
- **The cause is now ESTABLISHED as elevation, and two further candidates are retired** (2026-09-12, `2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed`).
- The third candidate's reading WAS taken:
- moving the module section inside the `WebView2 session isolation (diagnostic)` step's live window — the placement, not a longer timeout, was the whole defect — read `msedgewebview2 : 6 live process(es)` with its loaded module versions on the hosted runner beside a same-script dev-host control (as measured at CI run `34645345201`;
- Driver/runtime major SKEW is RETIRED as a cause by direct variation with a control:
- ELEVATION was then VARIED on the known-good host:
- an elevated leg on the Windows dev host reproduces `session not created: DevToolsActivePort file doesn't exist` where the non-elevated control is a recorded green, the pair differing on `IsElevatedAdmin` alone (as measured 2026-09-12, `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed/evidence/reading.md`).
- **Elevation is NOT the whole discriminator, and "the app must not run elevated" is RETIRED as a general remedy** — the shipped asserting step runs at the hosted runner's native HIGH integrity and creates a session (run 35208593666).
- What the 2026-09-12 variation established still stands on its own scope:
- the Medium-integrity drop helped at runtime 153 on the dev host and BREAKS the session on `windows-2022` at 131, which is why the asserting step no longer takes it, and the remedy CLASS named here — a limited-token launch, then a re-measurement — is now itself MEASURED INSUFFICIENT (2026-09-16):
- both mechanisms shipped, a scheduled task and then `runas /trustlevel` replacing it in the same chunk, are correct and structurally unable to lower the MANDATORY INTEGRITY LABEL, which three dev-host legs established as the discriminator (admin+High no session · non-admin+High no session · non-admin+Medium session created) — `RunLevel Limited` cannot, because the runner's job account is the built-in Administrator with `FilterAdministratorToken` off and therefore has no filtered token;
- `runas /trustlevel` cannot, because it strips the Administrators group and leaves the label.
- The remainder — an explicit medium-integrity launch **[measured-insufficient 2026-09-17:
- the explicit medium-integrity launch WAS built and measured — it lowers the label as designed (parent `S-1-16-12288` → child `S-1-16-8192` on the runner, confirmed from inside the leg) and did NOT open the endpoint.
- The one CI run that opened a session invoked the leg DIRECTLY at High integrity.
- The remainder is no longer 'a medium-integrity launch'.]** — is owned by the successor route entry, `v3-02` having returned to the pool.

## 2026-09-24-architecture-registries-compacted-under-the-read-cap — §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture]: passages moved out of the body

**Section:** §Established Decisions — [Read-Back Dependency Posture]
**Change:** compacted under the read cap; the passages below left the body verbatim.
**Why:** the body holds only current truth; history lives here + in git (this sidecar's preamble).

- **The gate reached `ready:true` for the first time on 2026-08-16** (`canary_round_trip: "ok"`, `blocked_precondition: null`, exit 0).
- titles are scrubbed, and `retrieve_telemetry_slice.fingerprint_refs` — the former carrier — was populated from the **L4 model's `evidence_refs`** alone (`andromeda-pulse pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:684-701`), which the deterministic-L4 fixture fills with a constant `det-*` triple (`det-span-…` / `det-template-0007` / `det-fingerprint-…`):
- the chain is `deterministic_inference.rs → interpretation/markdown.rs → mcp-server/tools.rs:436`.
- Pulse's own computed fingerprint lands in the `span_events.fingerprint` column, which no MCP tool reads — so at `efabe8e` it reached no read-back surface, and the old assertion could never have passed however the derivations were aligned.
- **At HEAD `83d4060` it reaches `fingerprint_refs` by another route:** an incident's refs are the model's refs ∪ the triggering cue's full-hex fingerprint (`grounded_fingerprint_hashes`, `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs`, read at `83d4060` by `2026-09-22-interpretation-proven-live`) — as measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle/evidence/leg1-2026-09-10T19-32-57-092.jsonl`, whose envelope `fingerprints` carries `0bddf438a748f326f07436169ea20a6a` beside the `det-*` triple, the value that run's own self-obs line `canary fingerprint computed …` states (its `.selfobs.jsonl` twin).
- **A SECOND axis was measured 2026-09-01 (Pulse HEAD `83d4060`) and closes the same way:** `incident_events` — the corpus table persisting created/resolved lifecycle events, and the one table whose content is NOT L4-authored — is written by `crates/triage/src/incident/persistence.rs::save_incident_event` and read only corpus-side (`crates/corpus/src/disposition.rs` + a `contract.rs` test helper), with ZERO references in `crates/mcp-server`;
- **But "no stronger claim exists" is RETIRED — a stronger one does, on a different axis.** Payload fidelity was unattainable at `efabe8e` and is PARTIAL at `83d4060` — one read-back value, the grounded cue fingerprint, varies with what Conductor emitted (above);
- incident 6 resolved and gone from the active set with `idle_seconds_at_resolve = 0.0`, against Pulse's 120s auto-resolve idle threshold (its corpus records the incident active 16:42:38→16:43:23, a 45s life), so the resolver is excluded by construction and Conductor's write is the only remaining cause — `conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs`.
- **Two mechanisms measured the same day bound how that attribution can be built.** (1) **At most ONE incident is active per DEDUPE TUPLE:** Pulse's producer dedupes a new incident against an OPEN incident carrying the same `(kind, scope, scope_id)` tuple — the workspace scopes the CANDIDATE SET, the tuple is the key, **as measured at `andromeda-pulse pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:811`** (`.find(|inc| inc.kind == kind && inc.scope == scope && inc.scope_id == scope_id)` over `registry.list_active(&digest.workspace)`, HEAD `83d4060`).
- The originating leg's storms all shared one tuple, which is why it observed the effect at workspace grain (`created=false deduped=true` observed while one was open;
- every `created=true` occurred with the active set empty;
- a new incident formed the same second the prior was resolved) — **the leg evidence stands;
- This SUPERSEDES the leading-path-segment narrowing recorded 2026-08-16:
- the SUT changed its normalization, and until Conductor transcribed the guard its `fingerprint()` returned a DIFFERENT value than Pulse's for every slash-bearing path — a live derivation drift no Conductor-vs-Conductor gate could see.
- as measured 2026-08-21 (leg D), `findings-counter-refresh` CARRIED one `[[expected]]` at that time and still landed `KnownResidual`, because ITS read-back came back degraded, and its unmet `CountAtLeast` floor graded `CalibrationRegion` rather than failing (a sample floor never hard-fails).
- That measurement stands as the evidence for the route;
- the scenario itself has been declare-only since 2026-09-15, when that floor was retired as structurally dead, so it is no longer a LIVE example of a checks-bearing scenario taking this route.
- **`degraded` is a PER-READ-BACK property, never a mode-wide guarantee — the universal "under deterministic L4 every read-back returns `degraded_mode`" is RETIRED, measured false 2026-09-06.** Deterministic L4 has now been measured BOTH ways:
- `findings-counter-refresh` degraded (2026-08-21), while `degraded-mode-report` read back an OPEN, non-degraded incident and took the graded route to `manual_record` → `ManualCheck` (`latency_ms 6045`, run `2026-09-06T09-11-09-325`, leg B1 of `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite`) — as measured at that chunk's `evidence/b1.jsonl` + `evidence/live-suite-verdict.md`, where `state_for` (`conductor-run/src/execute.rs`) returns `KnownResidual` iff `observation.degraded`, so a `ManualCheck` row proves `degraded == false`.
- only the universal is withdrawn.
- **That firing condition is UPTIME-BOUND, and the bound was invisible until 2026-09-06 — but the bound is the window IN FORCE AT BOOT, not a fixed hour.** The one-hour figure is `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_SECONDS = 3_600`'s DEFAULT;
- **That removes cause (a) and is NOT sufficient — cause (b) is untouched by the posture, and it is what still decides the leg.** As measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven/evidence/hue-verdict.md`, two runs of the identical tree under the identical posture on 2026-09-07 graded differently:

- As measured at `pulse-legs/a11y-20260906-110201/logs/agent-latest.jsonl.2026-09-06` (`2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite` and its 0-pending adaptation):
- the day's FIRST emitted silence cue fired 10:11:09.723Z, one hour after the canary service's first span (~09:11Z), and thereafter incidents formed mid-silence at 11:00:33 and 11:02:02 after cues of magnitude 3.0 → 5.0 → 7.03 — against `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_SECONDS = 3_600` (`andromeda-pulse crates/triage/src/baseline/activity_floor.rs:36`, evaluator per emit cycle at `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs:186`, HEAD `83d4060`).
- This qualifies the leg-E narrative rather than retiring it:
- leg E reached the arm because it ran inside that window, not because a `curious` cue can never be refreshed.
- This RETIRES the 2026-08-20 reading that the canary's own error-rate cues necessarily keep the list non-empty:

**Change:** compacted under the read cap; the passages below left the body verbatim.
**Why:** the body holds only current truth; history lives here + in git (this sidecar's preamble).

- no phase declaring occurrences may run longer than `max_sustained_storm_ms` nor emit faster than `max_sustained_rate_spans_per_s` (`EmissionSpec::occurrences` is what made both computable).
- **The rate term counts WIRE RECORDS, and is an upper BOUND (shipped 2026-09-06, superseding the DISPATCHES reading measured 2026-08-20):** `phase_rate_exceeds` judges `occurrences × EmissionSpec::max_spans_per_dispatch() × 1000 > max_rate × gap_ms` (`conductor-core/src/load_envelope.rs`), exact integer math with no division.
- The per-dispatch count is measured PER `EmissionShape` arm against the dispatcher's own arm — `Ramp`/`Breathing` emit `sum(window_counts)`, `Latency` its `samples`, `Error` `depth + 1`, `Pii` 2 spans on traces or one record per category on logs, `Topology` one span per service, every other shape 1 — so the retired `samples` / `windows` reading held for `Latency` alone and understated a rate curve by its own rate.
- Under the shipped mapping the catalog's worst case is `halo-breathing-encoding` at ~232 records/s (a ramp bounded at 1160 records per dispatch over a 5 s window), ≈43× under `max_sustained_rate_spans_per_s = 10000` — **superseding the "~200× under the bound" figure, which held only for the `samples` reading** — so no verdict moves and the `[[exempt]]` ledger stays empty.
- The contract file itself is unchanged:
- the term keeps its name and its value, because it transcribes a SUT record about wire load and the fix brings the code to the name rather than the name to the code.
- This retires the SURFACED-not-authored disposition — the fix is AUTHORED by `2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate`, and it is neither of the two the prior record predicted (it is not `occurrences × samples`, and the term was not renamed).
- `phase_rate_exceeds` has exactly one caller, `phase_breach`, whose only two callers are `check_load_envelope` (the static gate) and `LoadEnvelope::classify` (the per-run caption), so the two cannot diverge.
- `check_load_envelope` (the static catalog gate) and `LoadEnvelope::classify` (the per-run judgment behind the `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` caption) read ONE shared basis, so the gate and the caption cannot mean different things, and the `[[exempt]]` ledger — still held at exact-set equality in both directions, so it can only shrink under compulsion — is now **empty**:
- The artifact had predicted a different landing (that asserting SUMMED emitting-phase duration would retire the exemptions);
- measurement falsified it — summing disjoint bursts separated by quiet is not *sustained*, and both prior exemptions stay over a summed ceiling — so the shipped term bounds the longest single emitting window instead.

## 2026-09-24-architecture-registries-compacted-under-the-read-cap — §Occupied Resources On-disk artifacts / database: `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml`: passages moved out of the body

**Section:** §Occupied Resources — On-disk artifacts / database: `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml`
**Change:** compacted under the read cap; the passages below left the body verbatim.
**Why:** the body holds only current truth; history lives here + in git (this sidecar's preamble).

- The `[[term]]` list carried SIX terms as of 2026-09-03, when it gained `mcp-enabled` (`check = "shell-declaration"`, `env = "ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED"`), the same class as the shipped `l4-deterministic` and needing no new machinery.
- It carries SEVEN as of 2026-09-22 (`grep -c '^\[\[term\]\]'` → 7):
- `l4-real-model` (`check = "shell-absence"` on `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`, `posture = "real-model"`) — a CONDUCTOR posture term, as the header's PROVENANCE line states, not a transcribed SUT record — beside `l4-deterministic`, now tagged `posture = "deterministic"`.
- **A second term's `asserted` rationale is measurably FALSE, and the shape is the `warmup_ms` one:** `sidecar-built` reads "an unbuilt sidecar fails connect and surfaces the read-back-unreachable precondition upstream of this gate, so reaching term evaluation at all proves it" — but a `PATH` miss short-circuits to `[BLOCKED]` in ~0s UPSTREAM of term evaluation (as measured at `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md:54`, 2026-08-20;
- consistent with the ~2ms all-tools-absent reading in §Occupied Resources — Service/process names), so the term is satisfied-by-construction exactly when it is false and cannot catch its own falsity.
- It was deliberately NOT re-classified at `2026-09-03-live-pulse-preconditions-probed` (operator-selected):
- re-classifying moves what the preflight gate can block on, which is a larger change than probing preconditions.
- it does not carry the canary service out of Pulse's baseline bootstrap, and no pre-roll measured in seconds can.** Pulse gates the **baseline-derived cue families** on `BootstrapState::Ready` (`crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs:164` — the ONLY such gate in `crates/triage/`, sitting inside `evaluate_service_went_silent`, the P-014-class silence cue), which requires `now − first_observed_unix_nanos ≥ BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_SECONDS = 3_600` **per service, wall-clock** (`crates/triage/src/baseline/activity_floor.rs:33`, `:173-183`;
- that constant is the DEFAULT — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` overrides it once at Pulse's boot, §Occupied Resources — Environment variables — which changes nothing about the disproof below, since no seconds-scale warm-up clears any window of that order), and the `baseline_state` corpus table holds **0 rows**, so every `pulse-app` launch resets the anchor to zero.
- The shipped `warmup_ms = 45000` is 45s against a 3,600s gate — short by **80×** and unfixable by any value of its own knobs, which is why the term's `check = "asserted"` (satisfied by construction) cannot catch its own falsity.
- **That diagnosis is TRUE only of the baseline-derived families, and the canary does not ride one (measured 2026-08-15).** The RetryStorm path consults no baseline at all (`crates/triage/src/pattern/storm.rs:245-285` keys solely on count-in-window against the thresholds and the `last_emitted` tier ladder), so "without a baseline the L2 cue evaluator never considers it" holds for service-went-silent and never bound the canary storm;
- Pulse forms incidents for a sustained storm with `baseline_state` at 0 rows, measured twice on two fresh data dirs (`andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/chunks/2026-08-15-tier-1-incident-path-investigation/evidence/premise-check.md`).
- The warm-up's stated purpose is therefore disproved on a second axis — it aims at a gate this path never crosses — but it is harmless.
- **The claim that reaching a live incident requires a Pulse-side change (a test-mode bootstrap override, or populating `baseline_state`) is likewise measured FALSE and is retired**:
- no such change exists, `baseline_state` still holds 0 rows, and incidents form anyway.
- What actually gated the canary was a **tier band on Conductor's own side**:
- the storm must clear `DEFAULT_AUTONOMOUS_THRESHOLD = 10` (`crates/triage/src/pattern/storm.rs:78`, compared with `>=` at `:245`) because Pulse's Tier-1 coordinator accepts Autonomous cues alone (`crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs:390`), and the shipped `CANARY_STORM_COUNT = 6` sat in `5 <= 6 < 10` — cue floor cleared, Autonomous band missed, no incident possible.
- `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-10-workspace-key-divergence-probe/two-launch-verdict.md` §Re-run — 2026-08-13.
- **A SECOND gap sat beside it on the canary's own path (measured 2026-08-14/15) and is now CLOSED (2026-08-16) — its cause was CONDUCTOR-side, not Pulse-side.** The symptom:
- Conductor's storm reached the wire with its `exception` events intact and Pulse counted every span (the ingest heartbeat's `span_count` is a cumulative `fetch_add`, reading `15` = 3 warm-up + 12 storm at the 2026-08-15 leg), yet the `buffer.tick` trio read `span_events_seen: 0` · `observer_invocations: 0` · `fingerprints_computed: 0` with `rows_ingested: 1` — the fingerprint observer never invoked, and the loss localized between OTLP ingest receipt and the buffer's span-event enumeration.
- **The cause was a span-identity collision against a primary key.** Pulse's `spans` table is `PRIMARY KEY (trace_id, span_id)` (`andromeda-pulse crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:38`), while Conductor's `ok_span` stamped a CONSTANT identity — `vec![1; 16]` / `vec![1; 8]` — on every call, so every warm-up span after the first violated the key and was logged-and-skipped by `run_consumer`.
- That is exactly the producer-dependence observed:
- `inject_demo` derives `trace_id(seq)` / `span_id(seq)` per sequence and never collides.
- Fixed by `2026-08-15-canary-spans-pulse-fingerprints` (seeded per-call identity, disjoint warm-up/storm seed ranges);
- **One honest limit on the closure:** why the storm's 12 DISTINCT-id spans also appended zero rows on the prior leg was never directly observed — that leg captured no `duckdb.append` lines and its data dir no longer exists — so the appender-poisoning reading is **inferred, consistent with both measurements, and not proven**.
- Read the storm-detector telemetry accordingly:
- `tracked_fingerprints_count` is a **60s-windowed gauge over DISTINCT fingerprints, sampled at a 15s tick AFTER eviction**, so a working identical-fingerprint storm reads `1` regardless of its occurrence count — never the count itself (never 6 at the retired size, never 12 at the shipped `CANARY_STORM_COUNT`) — and a late sample reads 0 on a healthy path;
- That reading is what the 2026-08-16 leg confirmed from both directions:
- on the broken path both cumulative counters held 0 across 31 tick lines spanning three arms (twelve inside the retention window), while on the fixed path they read `2` and `1` with `tracked_fingerprints_count` still sampling `0` — a healthy storm, 77s past its 60s window.
- Never read that gauge as evidence of absence.

- **A FOURTH handle class, and its control model is none of the other three:** it is FLAG-valued (affirmative `"true"` / `"1"`, mirroring `conductor_core::flag_declared`), never a path — so the `std::fs::canonicalize` rule has nothing to canonicalize and the wdio-edge `isFile` + shell-metacharacter guard has nothing to guard.
- Unset or falsy, the leg keeps its documented skip-at-exit-0 so an unconfigured dev host is never read as a defect;
- affirmatively declared, an unresolved `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` / `CONDUCTOR_NVDA` exits NON-ZERO, which is what stops the CI a11y gate from reporting success by skipping.

title: Infrastructure Patterns
body:
## Infrastructure Patterns

**Build system:** `.gitattributes` pins LF at checkout repo-wide (`* text=auto eol=lf`, added 2026-09-13), and beneath it keeps `coverage-matrix.md text eol=lf` (added 2026-09-06) as the NAMED gate-correctness control, not cosmetics: the coverage-completeness gate byte-compares the committed `coverage-matrix.md` against `CoverageMatrix::render()`, which is `writeln!`-built (LF) and written verbatim, so the equality holds only where checkout preserves LF — `core.autocrlf=true` is the norm on the Windows dev host and every CI job runs on a Windows runner — the two original jobs on `windows-latest` and the `a11y` job on the explicit `windows-2022` label (moved 2026-09-17 from `windows-2025`), pinned rather than floating so a `-latest` move cannot change the WebView2 runtime the leg resolves from the image. **The image no longer decides the driver — the job does:** since 2026-09-17 a `Pin msedgedriver to the image's WebView2 runtime (gate)` step reads the runtime from the `EdgeUpdate` client keys, fetches msedgedriver for THAT version, Authenticode-gates it, asserts driver major == runtime major and publishes `EDGEWEBDRIVER`. The `≥ 152` runtime FLOOR and the conditional in-job Evergreen install it guarded are both RETIRED: the floor was not necessary (a coherent 131/131 pair runs the arm green), not sufficient (a coherent 152/152 pair fails, run `34654076633`) and destructive on the working configuration (run `35185153012` raised a native 131 image to 153). The measured subject is driver/runtime COHERENCE, which this gate MAKES rather than asserts — the earlier always-latest install's rationale was already EXHAUSTED for the same reason, resting on the runtime major as the discriminator, falsified at run `34280136892`. **The 2026-09-08 exit condition — pin once the `a11y` job actually GATES — is now MET**, by the route that exists: the job gates on the measured configuration (run 35208593666, a11y job `success`) and it is the DRIVER that is pinned, to the runtime already present. The versioned Standalone Installer that disposition originally named could never have served it — that installer installs Evergreen and takes no version argument. The wildcard IS the repo-wide policy; the named rule keeps that one path's guarantee independent of any later narrowing of it. The pin renormalizes nothing — `git ls-files --eol` measured 3031 `i/lf` · 13 `i/none` · 4 `i/-text`, no `i/crlf` and no `i/mixed`, against a system-gitconfig `core.autocrlf=true`, and git's "LF will be replaced by CRLF" warning went from firing on every touched file to 0 (as measured 2026-09-13 at `2026-09-13-audit-debt-retired-before-epoch-1-closes`). Cargo (cargo 1.85, Rust 2024 edition, MSRV 1.94.1). Lint with `cargo clippy`; test with `cargo nextest` — the pinned runner, driven through a zero-retry `ci` profile in `.config/nextest.toml` (no retries mask flakes — the determinism invariant) plus `cargo test --doc` for the doctests nextest skips — over the dev-test stack rstest/proptest/insta/assert_cmd/assert_fs/predicates/regex/sha2 (`regex` a `conductor-core` dev-dependency edge for the secret-scan and workflow env-context gates, `sha2` a `conductor-run` one for the real-model harvest's digest pins, each already locked transitively — no new package); line coverage via `cargo-llvm-cov` (requires the `llvm-tools-preview` toolchain component). Exact tool/dep versions live in test-plan §4. `bundled` SQLite compiles SQLite C from source (longer cold builds, fully self-contained). tonic 0.14 moved prost codegen to `tonic-prost-build` — build scripts use that crate (budget a small adjustment when mining Pulse's prior-art injectors that predate the split). Optional `cargo-modules` / `cargo-rail` audit the dependency graph. The `conductor-tauri` GUI bin uses `tauri-build` (build-dep): its `tauri::generate_context!` resolves `build.frontendDist` (`ui/dist`) at COMPILE time, so the webview bundle MUST be built (`npm run build`) before any workspace `cargo build`/`nextest`/`clippy` that compiles `conductor-tauri` — wired as an `ensure_frontend` step into `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` (the `run` verb) and the CI Rust job (a bare `cargo build` does NOT run `beforeBuildCommand` — only the Tauri CLI does). **`npm run build` is necessary but NOT sufficient, and the PROFILE does not decide it:** whether the binary loads the embedded bundle or `devUrl` turns on the **`custom-protocol` feature** — `tauri` 2.11.3's `build.rs` computes `let dev = !custom_protocol` and emits `cargo:dev`, which `tauri-build` 2.6.0 reads back through `DEP_TAURI_DEV` (`is_dev()`), **as measured 2026-09-01** (a bare `cargo build --release -p conductor-tauri` emitted `cargo:rustc-cfg=dev` and opened on `http://localhost:5173`; the same build with `--features tauri/custom-protocol` opened on `http://tauri.localhost/` — that measurement was taken on the Windows host, and the custom-protocol origin is per-OS: `tauri` 2.11.3's `tauri_protocol_url` is `http://tauri.localhost` on Windows/Android and `tauri://localhost` on Linux/macOS, as measured on the Linux dev host at `2026-10-04-host-portable-tauri-ipc-tests`). A binary that must serve the bundle is therefore built `cargo build --release -p conductor-tauri --features tauri/custom-protocol`, which is what both harness shells do for `--e2e`. The Tauri tree adds many `unmaintained`-but-non-vulnerable transitive advisories (gtk-rs Linux-webview path · `unic-*` via `urlpattern` · `proc-macro-error`) + the `MPL-2.0` / `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception` licenses — all justified in `deny.toml`. That license policy also covers the workspace's OWN `conductor-*` crates — `deny.toml` carries no `private` exemption — and each passes as `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, inherited from `[workspace.package]` (`license.workspace = true` in every member), so a member without an allowed license fails `cargo deny check licenses`; `publish = false` exempts nothing. The accepted set is no longer Tauri-only: `BSD-2-Clause` was added for `arrayref` (via `conductor-emit`→`blake3`), the first cargo-side exception from outside that tree. Each entry names its crate and dependency path inline; BOTH supply-chain runners are green over the un-drifted lock — `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` exit 0 and `cargo audit` exit 0 (1239 advisories loaded, 562 packages scanned, 17 allowed warnings: 16 `unmaintained` + 1 `unsound`, every one `deny.toml`-adjudicated — `RUSTSEC-2025-0119` left the ignore list at 2026-09-07 when its subject `number_prefix` left the tree with the indicatif 0.18 bump, taking `deny.toml`'s ignore entries 17 → 16), as measured 2026-09-05 against advisory-db HEAD `5a0ebedf` with `git status --porcelain` empty. The long-standing red was a LOCAL host-checkout artifact, never an external advisory-DB fault: an untracked `crates/gettext-sys/RUSTSEC-2026-0244.md` left in this host's advisory-db clone after upstream moved that file to `crates/gettext-rs/` on 2026-08-09 (`e12b689b`), which a fetch into the existing copy never removes — so the checkout's `status --porcelain` is read BEFORE any parse failure is classified external (security-plan §Dependency Security).

**Deployment model:** Local-only — `cargo build --release` produces the `conductor-cli` binary run beside Pulse via `scripts/agent-run.sh`; the Tauri 2 bundler produces the optional GUI installer set. The bundler is a HOST dev-tool (`tauri-cli` / `tauri-bundler`), absent from `Cargo.lock` — the tree resolves no bundler version at all, and the `2.11.3` this line long carried mirrored the `tauri` CRATE version, which is a different artifact and still correct. Its floor is met by the installed CLI, `tauri-cli` 2.11.4 on first install, and its output is the Windows installer set that `bundle.targets = "all"` yields on this host — **as measured 2026-09-10**: nsis 4.21 MB · msi 5.87 MB, both under gitignored `target/`. The MB scale is the durable fact and the byte count is not: two builds of the same source that day emitted nsis 4 418 544 B and then 4 414 280 B (msi 6 152 192 B both times), so a byte-exact installer size states more than this toolchain reproduces. The roster floor lives in test-plan §4. No Docker / Compose / Kubernetes / serverless — Pulse binds loopback `:4317`, so execution is necessarily co-located on the dev host.

**Directory structure (crate-per-seam Cargo workspace):**

```
conductor/
├─ Cargo.toml                 # workspace manifest (members + shared deps)
├─ Cargo.lock
├─ rust-toolchain.toml        # pin Rust 2024 / MSRV 1.94.1
├─ rustfmt.toml               # workspace fmt config — one key: edition = "2024"
├─ .gitattributes             # repo-wide LF pin (* text=auto eol=lf) + the named coverage-matrix.md control
├─ LICENSE-MIT · LICENSE-APACHE # the dual license — every Cargo + npm manifest declares `MIT OR Apache-2.0`
├─ scripts/
│  ├─ agent-run.sh            # headless source-of-truth entrypoint
│  ├─ webview2-cause-probe.ps1 # CI-only read-only diagnostic; invoked solely by ci.yml's a11y job, wired into neither harness shell, adds no 6th command
│  ├─ a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1 # CI-only limited-token launcher for the a11y job's DRIVER-ALONE DIAGNOSTIC steps (runas /trustlevel); left the asserting step 2026-09-17; same qualifier — solely ci.yml's a11y job, neither harness shell, no 6th command
│  ├─ a11y-token-witness.ps1   # CI-only entry point of the launched leg; witnesses the token it actually got before wdio starts; same qualifier
│  ├─ mutation-gate.py        # operator-local mutation-tally gate (`<unit>` | `selftest`); invoked by no CI step, wired into neither harness shell, no 6th command
│  ├─ mutation-roster.toml    # the gate's expected `missed` / `timeout` multisets per unit
│  └─ fixtures/mutation-gate/ # the committed `selftest` fixture tree (roster.toml · roster-bad.toml · arms.toml · arms/{name}/)
├─ crates/
│  ├─ conductor-core/         # runtime-agnostic engine library (usable outside Tauri)
│  ├─ conductor-timeline/     # deterministic seeded phase scheduler (tokio::time)
│  ├─ conductor-emit/         # OTLP raw-type emission primitives + exception events / fingerprint primitive (opentelemetry-proto + tonic)
│  ├─ conductor-faults/       # fault helpers (ramps, silence, port-occupier, fingerprint-storm)
│  ├─ conductor-verify/       # MCP read-back client (hand-rolled JSON-RPC), preflight gate, verdict logic
│  ├─ conductor-report/       # JSONL journal + Markdown report + runs.db (rusqlite) storage seam
│  ├─ conductor-run/          # run composition root lib (preflight + execute_scenario + persist + live-counter drive_run + the fault-phase occupier guard; → conductor-faults) — shared by both bins
│  ├─ conductor-cli/          # `agent-run` bin (#[tokio::main(flavor="current_thread")] + anyhow)
│  └─ conductor-tauri/        # Tauri 2 GUI bin (commands + Channel; owns its own runtime)
├─ scenarios/                 # declarative scenario config (serde + garde), each naming its P-IDs — a P-ID may be named by several
├─ contracts/                 # pinned MCP contract manifest + the SUT capability manifest + the SUT load envelope + the SUT run contract + the scenario-assertion audit ledger + the P-025 measurement contract + the real-model leg posture (the two members no Rust code reads)
├─ runs/                      # per-run artifacts: the <run_id>.jsonl journal + <run_id>.md report are run_id-stemmed, never overwritten
│  └─ live-suite/             # `run --live` per-leg self-obs captures + the real-model arm's rm-capture.{txt,err} — leg-stemmed, each set cleared per invocation of its own arm (the one exception to the line above)
│  └─ span-landing/           # the span-landing operator pass's span-{a,b}.jsonl — the two named files cleared non-recursively before drive A; read by span_landing_live, a stale pair refused
│  └─ runs.db                 # embedded SQLite cross-run index
├─ coverage-matrix.md         # every manifest capability classified (definition of done)
└─ .github/workflows/         # GitHub Actions: fmt + build + test + clippy + the static gates (over committed data · repository hygiene) + the a11y webview e2e gate
```

**CI/CD approach:** GitHub Actions on the dev OS target runs `cargo fmt --all --check` (the `rust` job's early unconditional formatting gate, 2026-09-09 — not part of the lint stage), `cargo build`, `cargo nextest`/`cargo test` (incl. golden tests), and `cargo clippy`, plus the static gates over committed data — each its own named `rust`-job step asserting a committed artifact against the production source it derives from: the coverage-completeness gate (2026-09-06) and the scenario-assertion audit gate (2026-09-16, guarded by a presence check on its ledger so an absent subject fails loudly rather than passing vacuously) — and two repository-hygiene gates of the same step shape (2026-09-24): the secret-scan gate (no secret-shaped string or file name in git's cached + untracked-not-ignored listing) and the workflow env-context gate (every `env.X` expression read names a declared or `GITHUB_ENV`-written key, beside the `GITHUB_ENV context probe` pair) — plus the `a11y` job's Pulse-free routine webview leg (`agent-run.ps1 run --e2e`, invoked since 2026-09-17 through the leg's entry point `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` DIRECTLY at the hosted step's native High integrity + the `journal_conformance` gate over `runs/a11y` + the violation-record upload, 2026-09-07). All three stages now EXECUTE in CI on the measured configuration: hosted `windows-2022` at a coherent 131.0.2903.86 driver/runtime pair, where the leg ran 12 passing / 0 failing / 2 skipped, the conformance gate ran (`8 tests run: 8 passed`) and the record uploaded — as measured at run 35208593666. The earlier reading, that the job reached only the first stage and failed at WebView2 session creation, was measured at run 34162118841 on the hosted `windows-2025` image at runtime 152/153 and stands as that configuration's fact, not the arm's verdict; owner the route entry *Hosted-runner WebView2 session*. Dynamic end-to-end scenario proof (error-baseline-spike, fingerprint-storm, restart-suppression) requires a live Pulse with the `mcp-server` feature + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` and is an explicit operator/local gate, not a CI gate — the exclusion is the live-Pulse dependency, not the end-to-end tier.

title: Threat Model Summary

body: _[ALL tiers — VERBATIM copy from threat-assessment.md]_

**Security tier:** `Minimal (0)`
_Justification: Every signal points to a minimal-tier local utility — a single-developer, local-only, no-cloud, no-multi-tenancy tool with no user accounts (auth "none"), where the only persisted data is self-generated synthetic test telemetry and run-metadata in an embedded SQLite index (`runs.db`) plus on-disk JSONL/Markdown artifacts (no PII/payment/health/credentials owned by Conductor), and there is zero network exposure — Conductor is a loopback gRPC/MCP client with no inbound listener of its own. With no compliance triggers, the residual risk classes that remain are exactly those Minimal tier covers: dependency/supply-chain audit (notably `bundled` SQLite compiled from C source and the OTLP/gRPC/MCP dependency tree), input validation on operator-supplied scenario config and `CONDUCTOR_*` env-var path overrides, and error sanitization at the `anyhow` binary edges and in run-report artifacts._
**Data classification:**

- **Type:** config — declarative scenario config (serde + garde, no DSL)
  - **Where:** `scenarios/` directory, deserialized into the owning seam crates; `contracts/` pinned MCP contract manifest (Conventions: Config conventions; Occupied Resources: On-disk artifacts)
  - **Volume:** aggregate (one config file per Pulse P-ID, over the SUT capability manifest's accepted set), transient at load

- **Type:** test-telemetry / run-metadata (synthetic, not user data) — emission journals, run reports, and the `runs.db` index (run_id · seed · scenario · P-IDs · verdict · fingerprints · timestamps)
  - **Where:** `runs/` directory (per-run `<run_id>.jsonl` journal + `<run_id>.md` report) and embedded SQLite `runs.db` (Occupied Resources: On-disk artifacts; Established Decisions: Run-History Persistence)
  - **Volume:** aggregate, persisted on disk (append-mostly); content is self-generated synthetic OTLP fault data (spans/metrics/logs Conductor emits), not user-derived

- **Type:** credential — **none owned by Conductor.** A keychain reference appears (`OsKeychainBackend("com.andromeda.pulse")`, Standard Contracts readiness gate), but it belongs to Pulse (the system under test): the sidecar opens Pulse's `corpus.db` (plaintext SQLite — the P-049 encrypted-at-rest assumption proved wrong when verified live 2026-06-27; the `OsKeychainBackend` reference is Pulse-side and not exercised for corpus access) as the *same OS user*. Conductor does not store, generate, or manage any secret; the architecture states explicitly "No secrets, no `DATABASE_URL`, no cloud credentials" (Cross-cutting Patterns: Trust boundary; Occupied Resources: Environment variables — "no secrets/cloud env vars (local-only tool)")
  - **Where:** N/A for Conductor (OS keychain access is Pulse-side, exercised via the spawned sidecar's canary)
  - **Volume:** N/A

- **Type:** PII — **none.** Project Intent: "Personal — solo developer, local dev host, no cloud, no multi-tenancy." No user accounts, no user-supplied content. The only identities are synthetic incident/fingerprint data Conductor itself emits.
- **Type:** payment — **none.** Stack lists no payment/billing SDK (no Stripe etc.); Project Intent describes no transactions.
- **Type:** health — **none.** No medical data in Stack or Intent.

Note: `corpus.db` (Pulse's incident corpus — **plaintext SQLite**, NOT encrypted-at-rest; the P-049 encryption assumption proved wrong live 2026-06-27) is **out of scope** — owned by Pulse (the SUT); Conductor reaches it through the MCP TOOL SURFACE only — read-back **plus the `mark_incident_resolved` lifecycle write** (first production caller 2026-08-31, `conductor_run::probe_resolve_lifecycle`) — never the file, and never persists/exfiltrates its content (Standard Contracts readiness gate), with ONE ratified, scoped exception: scrubbed real-model capture evidence (§Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection; ratified 2026-09-23).
**Attack surface:**

- **Vector:** CLI input — seed/scenario flags, the `run_id`-class POSITIONAL argument on the `report` and `cleanup` verbs, and env-var overrides on the `agent-run` / `conductor-cli` path (the `cleanup` run_id's only sink is a rusqlite `?1` bound parameter, never a path join)
  - **Entry point:** `conductor-cli` binary args + `CONDUCTOR_*` env namespace (`CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`, `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR`, `CONDUCTOR_CONTRACT_MANIFEST`, and `CONDUCTOR_SEED`) (Occupied Resources: Environment variables; Cross-cutting Patterns: Config management)
  - **Trust boundary:** operator-supplied on the local host; CLI flag precedence over env; no untrusted/remote source

- **Vector:** config files (local file parsing) — scenario config + pinned MCP contract manifest read from disk
  - **Entry point:** `scenarios/` (serde deserialize) and `contracts/` manifest; `anyhow` at the CLI edge, `ConfigError` harness-fault class via garde `#[from]`
  - **Trust boundary:** garde validation at load (`range` rules: a bounded error fraction — the shipped `error_percent` ∈ 0..=100 — non-negative durations, sane ramp factors, bounded per-phase occurrences; `#[garde(custom)]` cross-field: p50≤p95≤p99, severity-mix sums, the per-shape emission rules, the `[phases.fault]` closed `kind` enum + the scenario-level fault ⇒ `occurrences = 0` silence rule; plus the load-path `Scenario::check_*()` arm for sibling-spanning rules garde cannot express — `check_capabilities`; `check_budgets` for `budget_ms` bounded `1..=MAX_BUDGET_MS` and cross-checked against the scenario's own `slo_tier`; and `check_checklist`, which rejects a `[[checklist]]` declared beside a non-empty `expected`, all faulting as `CoreError::Config`), diving into nested spec structs rather than skipping them (Conventions: Config conventions, Error handling). Source is operator-authored local files, not external input.

- **Vector:** MCP read-back child-process stdout — Conductor spawns the Pulse MCP server (`andromeda-pulse-mcp`) over piped stdio from `conductor-verify`'s own `spawn::build_command` (`tokio::process::Command`; rmcp and its `TokioChildProcess` were removed 2026-06-27) and **trusts that child's stdout as the read-back source**
  - **Entry point:** hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC client over stdio (rmcp removed 2026-06-27); version-pinned contract manifest + `initialize` preflight gate (Conventions: Inbound verification; Cross-cutting Patterns: Trust boundary)
  - **Trust boundary:** preflight readiness gate — negotiated protocol pinned at `2024-11-05`, required-tool presence vs. manifest, data-dir canary round-trip; mismatch/empty ⇒ **blocked** state. The child is a locally-spawned, co-located process under the same OS user (not a remote/untrusted peer); `tonic::Status` codes and MCP error responses are first-class typed verification inputs, not panics.

- **Vector:** OTLP/gRPC egress — outbound only to `127.0.0.1:4317` (Pulse's loopback ingest)
  - **Entry point:** tonic client; Conductor is the client, port owned by Pulse (Occupied Resources: Ports; Conventions: Outbound emission)
  - **Trust boundary:** loopback-only egress; a refused transport surfaces as `Result::Err` (harness fault), not a verdict

- **Vector (single deliberate exception):** port bind `:4317` — the port-occupier fault scenario intentionally binds `:4317` to exercise Pulse's reaction
  - **Entry point:** `conductor-faults` seam (Cross-cutting Patterns: Trust boundary; Occupied Resources: Ports)
  - **Trust boundary:** loopback only; the *sole* case where a SHIPPED Conductor binary opens a port, and it is an intentional in-host fault, not a network listener accepting external input.

- **Vector:** public API / file upload / OAuth / WebSocket / UGC / webhook — **none.** No web framework (Stack: "Backend Framework: None"), no HTTP surface (`:4318` unused, no `/health` or `/ready` HTTP endpoints), no SSE/WebSocket/polling, local-only deployment (Infrastructure Patterns: Deployment model — "No Docker/Compose/Kubernetes/serverless… execution is necessarily co-located on the dev host"). No external/internet exposure exists.
**Auth model:**
- **Approach:** none
- **Provider:** N/A
- **Scope:** N/A

**Reason:** Project Intent records "Personal — solo developer, local dev host, no cloud, no multi-tenancy" with no user accounts and no API consumers. Conductor exposes no network service (Stack: "Backend Framework: None"; Occupied Resources: "No inbound listener of Conductor's own"), so there is no authenticated surface to protect. Development Style is **agent-driven** — the headless `scripts/agent-run.sh` path is the source of truth and release gate (Cross-cutting Patterns: Development Style), which implies no interactive login UX. The only env flag is `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`, which Conductor explicitly asserts it does **not** set itself (it is a Pulse-side operator gate). It must nonetheless be present in **Conductor's own process environment**, where the operator exports it and the spawned sidecar receives it by environment **inheritance** — Since 2026-09-03 an absent declaration is ALSO observed UPSTREAM — as a `[PRECONDITION]` subject of `conductor preconditions` and as the run contract's `mcp-enabled` `shell-declaration` term — so it is named before any spawn, rather than only downstream as the sidecar starting and immediately exiting with every read-back measuring the unreachable path. Conductor still never SETS the flag, and inheritance remains the sole channel to the child: `spawn.rs` passes only `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` through the `.env(...)` builder, so inheritance is the sole channel for this flag. Absent it, the sidecar starts and immediately exits (`env_var_mcp_enabled: false` with `feature_flag_enabled: true`) and every read-back measures the unreachable path — verified live 2026-08-13. Defaulting to JWT/session/OAuth here would contradict the single-user local model.
**Infrastructure:**

- **Hosting:** local-only — `cargo build --release` produces the `conductor-cli` binary run beside Pulse via `scripts/agent-run.sh`. Explicitly "No Docker/Compose/Kubernetes/serverless" (Infrastructure Patterns: Deployment model; Established Decisions: Deployment)

- **Database:** embedded — rusqlite 0.38.0 with `bundled` SQLite 3.50.4 (JSON1, via libsqlite3-sys 0.36.0), synchronous raw SQL, in-process `runs.db`; no DB port, no `DATABASE_URL` (Stack: Database; Occupied Resources: Ports + Environment variables)

- **Networking:** local only — egress is loopback OTLP/gRPC to `127.0.0.1:4317` (`:4318` unused) and a stdio child-process MCP session; no inbound listener, and no public networking from any SHIPPED binary or dev-host harness leg. No non-loopback egress remains in the project: the CI-only msedgedriver fetch retired 2026-10-11 with the `a11y` job (count 1 → 0). Co-location is forced because Pulse binds loopback `:4317` (Cross-cutting Patterns: Trust boundary; Infrastructure Patterns: Deployment model)

- **CI/CD:** GitHub Actions runs one job, `rust` — `cargo fmt --all --check` (the early formatting gate, 2026-09-09) / `cargo build` / cargo-nextest (incl. golden tests) / `cargo clippy` / the secret-scan and workflow env-context gates (2026-09-24 — in-repo test targets, no fetched tool) / the `cargo audit` + `cargo deny` supply-chain steps / coverage; the `frontend` and `a11y` jobs, with the npm audit and the fetched-binary surface, left with the window on 2026-10-11. Dynamic end-to-end scenario proof requires a live Pulse and is an explicit operator/local gate, not a CI gate (Infrastructure Patterns: CI/CD approach; Established Decisions: CI/CD)

**Compliance triggers:**
None — no compliance-regulated data detected. No payment data → no PCI DSS; no EU personal data / no user accounts → no GDPR; no health/medical data → no HIPAA; no children's data → no COPPA. The only persisted data is self-generated synthetic test telemetry and run metadata (`runs.db`, JSONL journals); Pulse's `corpus.db` (plaintext SQLite, P-049 encryption not active live) is out of scope and owned by the SUT.

This tier is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how much security rigor downstream
skills (security-pass per phase + cross-cutting reads from design / tests /
obs / a11y) should apply.

title: Input Validation

body: _[ALL tiers]_

**Boundary:** validate at ALL system boundaries — wherever untrusted data
enters the system. For Conductor every boundary is operator-supplied on the
local host (CLI args, env-var path handles, on-disk config, trusted-child
stdout); the controls below are the trust boundaries the architecture already
names (Conventions: Config conventions, Inbound verification; Cross-cutting
Patterns: Trust boundary).
| Boundary | What to validate | How (stack-specific) |

| Scenario config files (`scenarios/`, serde deserialize) | a bounded error fraction (shipped as an integer `error_percent` ∈ 0..=100); non-negative durations; sane ramp factors; cross-field p50≤p95≤p99; severity-mix sums. **The `[phases.emission]` block:** its `kind` shape discriminator is REQUIRED whenever the table exists (no inferred default), `occurrences` is bounded by `MAX_OCCURRENCES` (`0` = a declared silence window), and each shape carries its own cross-field rules — percentile ordering, severity numbers ∈ 1..=24, the breathing amplitude < center sign guard, ≥2 distinct topology services, non-empty variant/category sets. **The `[[expected]]` block's `budget_ms`** (optional — `Option<u32>`, `#[serde(default)]`): garde `range(min = 1, max = MAX_BUDGET_MS)` where the ceiling is DERIVED from `SloTier::Tier90s.deadline_ms()`, plus the sibling-spanning load-path rule that it not exceed the scenario's own `slo_tier` deadline. **The `[phases.fault]` block** (optional — `PhaseSpec.fault: Option<FaultSpec>`, serde default absent, `dive` never `skip`): its `kind` is the CLOSED `FaultKindSpec` enum (`port_occupier`; an unknown kind is a deserialize error, never an inferred default), the scenario-level `fault_phases_are_silent` requires `occurrences = 0` on any fault-declaring phase, and the occupier PORT is deliberately NOT a config field (a private builder parameter — no operator-steerable bind target). **The `[[checklist]]` block** (optional — `Scenario.checklist: Vec<ChecklistItem>`, `#[serde(default)]`, `dive` never `skip`): each `ChecklistItem { induced, observation }` has BOTH halves bounded `length(min = 1, max = MAX_CHECKLIST_TEXT)` (ceiling `200` — a length bound on untrusted scenario-authored text the CLI's interactive hold prints, each half on its own indented `induced:` / `observe:` line; length only — no newline or control-character rule), and the sibling-spanning load-path rule rejects a declared checklist beside a non-empty `expected`; the load path is pinned by `a_checklist_half_at_the_bound_loads`, `an_out_of_bound_checklist_half_is_a_validation_fault` (201 chars / empty → `CoreError::Validation`) and `a_checklist_beside_expected_checks_is_a_config_fault` (→ `CoreError::Config`). `HoldPoint.checklist` carries the same dived vector to the CLI's interactive hold (`PromptResolver`); the headless path prints none. **The top-level `l4_posture` key** (optional, 2026-09-22 — `Scenario.l4_posture: L4Posture`, `#[serde(default)]` → `deterministic`): the CLOSED `L4Posture` unit enum (`deterministic` · `real-model`, no catch-all variant); an unknown value is a load-time `CoreError::Config`, never an inferred default. Its `#[garde(skip)]` is the closed-unit-enum form — the parse IS the validation — not the nested-spec `skip` this row bans | garde 0.22.1 `#[derive(Validate)]` `range` rules + `#[garde(custom)]` cross-field, co-located with the serde structs in their owning seam crate; failed `Report` → `ConfigError` via `#[from]` (harness fault, not a verdict). **A rule that must read a SIBLING field is a second, co-equal mechanism, not a garde validator:** garde 0.22.1's field-level `custom` receives `(&field, &())` and structurally cannot see a sibling, so such rules ship as an explicit `Scenario::check_*()` invoked from `from_toml_str` (`check_capabilities`; `check_budgets` for `budget_ms` ≤ its scenario's own `slo_tier` deadline; `check_checklist` for a `[[checklist]]` declared beside a non-empty `expected`) and raise `CoreError::Config` — a harness fault at load, never a verdict — because the `#[from] garde::Report` variant `CoreError::Validation` cannot carry a hand-written message. **Every nested spec field must `dive`, never `skip`** — a `skip`ped nested struct (as `PhaseSpec.emission` was until the emission dispatcher) deserializes entirely unvalidated, because garde never descends into it and its rules therefore never execute |

| Pinned MCP contract manifest (`contracts/`) | expected protocol version `2024-11-05`; required-tool name set (`query_incident_list` · `retrieve_report` · `retrieve_telemetry_slice` · `mark_incident_resolved` · `retrieve_incident_events`, the fifth pinned 2026-10-03 on the founder's live ratification) — a sidecar lacking any one blocks on the EXISTING `required tool(s) absent` precondition, so the gate's named preconditions stay five | serde deserialize of the manifest; assert against the `initialize` result's `protocolVersion` in the preflight gate (`conductor-verify`) — mismatch ⇒ `blocked`, never silent downgrade |

| Committed SUT-facing manifests read at a fixed path (`contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` · `contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml` · `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml` · `contracts/scenario-audit-ledger.toml`) | **capabilities:** non-empty `sut_version`/`captured_at`/set, `P-NNN` shape per id, no duplicates. **load envelope:** non-empty `sut_version`/`captured_at`/`provenance`, strictly positive `[envelope]` terms, no duplicate or reason-less `[[exempt]]` entry. **run contract:** non-empty `sut_version`/`captured_at`/`provenance`, non-empty `[[term]]` list, unique term ids, every term carrying both a statement and its causes, a non-zero `min_canary_poll_seconds`, no warm-up window with zero emissions, and every SHELL term — `shell-declaration`, and since 2026-09-22 `shell-absence` — naming the env var it observes; a term's optional `posture` must be a member of the closed `L4Posture` set (`deterministic` · `real-model`), an unknown value being a hard parse fault. All three: absent/malformed is a hard harness fault, **never defaulted and never silently widened** | serde deserialize + an explicit `validate()` in `conductor-core` (`CapabilityManifest::load` / `LoadEnvelope::load` / `RunContract::load`); resolved by every SHIPPED reader from a fixed `default_path()` through `resolve_under`, with deliberately **no `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle** (unlike `CONDUCTOR_CONTRACT_MANIFEST`) so the path is not operator-steerable; read faults carry `e.kind()` only, never the path (artifact hygiene). **`pulse-capabilities.toml` additionally has a TEST-BINARY reader outside `conductor-core` (2026-09-06):** `conductor-report --test coverage_gate` loads it through the same bounds-checking `CapabilityManifest::load`, but resolves the conventional repo path from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` rather than `default_path()` — a cargo test binary's CWD is its own package root, where no `contracts/` exists, so the CWD-relative default cannot resolve there. It introduces no `CONDUCTOR_*` handle and reads nothing operator-supplied, so the not-operator-steerable property holds by a different resolution; the duty binds per READER, and this reader is recorded rather than assumed. **`scenario-audit-ledger.toml` is the SECOND artifact of that test-binary-reader shape, and the first with NO shipped reader at all (2026-09-16):** `conductor-core --test scenario_audit_gate` loads it through `ScenarioAuditLedger::load`, resolving the workspace root from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` for the same CWD reason. Its validation is a serde typed parse with a hard `CoreError` on absent or malformed — never defaulted, never a silent widen — and its resolution differs from the three manifests above: `default_path()` is a hard-coded relative constant and `load()` takes an ALREADY-RESOLVED path, so `conductor-core` never calls `resolve_under` for it and there is deliberately no `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle. garde does not apply (it is not a scenario-config struct). Read faults carry `e.kind()` only, never the path. The not-operator-steerable property therefore holds by the hard-coded constant rather than by `resolve_under`, and — the duty binding per READER — this reader is recorded too: a committed artifact parsed at runtime earns its row whether or not a shipped binary is the one parsing it. **`pulse-run-contract.toml` additionally has readers OUTSIDE `conductor-core`:** `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` parse `warmup_ms` + `min_canary_poll_seconds` to derive the `boot` wall-clock budget, and carry the same never-defaulted rule — a missing term is a hard exit 2, and a lowered `CONDUCTOR_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT` clamps up to the contract floor rather than down, so the budget comes from the validated fixed-path contract rather than an operator-steerable env handle. **`contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` is NOT a member of this row, and its one reader is recorded here rather than assumed (2026-10-08):** no shipped code reads it; since the 2026-09-30 series a `conductor-run` test helper (`pre_registered`, in the real-model harvest) holds each dated section by a sha256 pin — root from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, no `CONDUCTOR_*` handle, read faults by error kind, nothing parsed from the file. A digest hold is not the runtime read that contract's own `## Regime` notice names, so this row's duties do not attach to it — the founder's ruling by dialog, 2026-10-08, relayed by the pc overseer, his pick verbatim: «Нет, исправить фразу (Recommended)». The notice stands for a real runtime read: were shipped code to read or parse the file, the duties attach in full. The record widens nothing — no new crossing, input class or write |

| the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` declaration-only READ SET (read, never written) — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, enumerated by `conductor_core::OBSERVED_HANDLES` | nothing to validate — a declaration-only read: Conductor tests only whether its OWN environment declares each — affirmatively, or, for `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` under the real-model posture (2026-09-22), NOT — and no value ever becomes a path, an argv element, or a log value on this read (the probe renders handle NAMES only; the data-dir handle's separate test-binary VALUE readers (the real-model capture and the `span_landing_live` witness) are recorded at the capture-ingest rows and the spawn row below) | `conductor_core::handle_declared` — per-name dispatch: the PATH-valued `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` graded by PRESENCE-after-trim, every other name delegating to the value-only `conductor_core::flag_declared` — called per handle by `conductor_run::observe_preconditions`, the deterministic posture's grading. Under the real-model posture `observe_preconditions_for` grades through `conductor_core::handle_declared_for`, which differs only for the L4 handle: it must be ABSENT or falsy, read under the union of both sides' truthiness rules (`conductor_core::flag_declared_on_either_side` — Conductor's `true`/`1` ∪ Pulse's `1`/`true`/`yes`, trimmed and ASCII-lowercased, transcribed from Pulse's own rule), a union that can only widen what BLOCKS. The run-contract path reads a `shell-declaration` term's var through the value-only `flag_declared` and the `shell-absence` term's var through that value-only union. **All three handles are gradable and `handles-declared` is SATISFIABLE** (as measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence/report.md`: `conductor preconditions` exit 0, 2026-09-04T17:07Z, full operator env). The non-widening witness holds — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=false` declares (it is a path) while `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=false` does not — because the run-contract path routes only to value-only tests (`flag_declared`, and the union for the `shell-absence` term) and structurally cannot reach the presence arm. "Nothing to validate" still holds: handle NAMES only, no value becoming a path, an argv element or a log value (a distinctive data-dir value appeared 0 times across the probe, `--json` and both live `boot` artifacts; the gate's own `data_dir` renders `<redacted>`). Under the deterministic posture an absent declaration of either boolean surfaces as an unmet contract term and/or a named `[PRECONDITION]` subject; under the real-model posture a PRESENT L4 declaration does, named by handle only — each naming both candidate causes, **never as a claimed measurement of `pulse-app`** — Conductor launches no Pulse process and cannot inspect one |

| Env-var path handles (`CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` / `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR` / `CONDUCTOR_CONTRACT_MANIFEST`) | path exists / is a directory or file as expected; **canonicalize** and bounds-check at the CLI edge (these sit OUTSIDE garde's struct validation per security-research.md serde+garde finding). The duty binds per READER: `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` also has FOUR test-binary readers — `conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs` (since 2026-09-06, set by the CI journal-conformance step, a no-op when unset) and the three operator-gated `live-pulse` readers `conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs` (2026-09-22), `conductor-run/tests/live_suite.rs` (2026-09-06) and `conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs` (2026-10-01). Since `2026-09-23-real-model-capture-path-handles-guarded-and-stale-read-back-texts-corrected` (the span-landing witness from birth) all four resolve the handle through the shared test module `conductor-run/tests/capture_paths` (`runs_dir_from` → `conductor_core::resolve_under`) BEFORE any read, so an absolute or `..`-escaping value is REJECTED rather than replacing the workspace root, and every rejection is a path-free `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR rejected: {fixed reason}`; `live_suite.rs`'s three failure texts name the file name and the error kind, never a resolved path — as measured at `crates/conductor-run/tests/capture_paths_guard.rs` (8 cases, green under nextest and `cargo test`). This SUPERSEDES the unguarded-join residual recorded here 2026-09-06 / 2026-09-23 and discharges its route CARRY | `std::fs::canonicalize` + explicit type/existence check in `conductor-cli`; reject before any `runs.db`/journal write or manifest read |

| Real-model capture ingest (`conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs`, `live-pulse` feature, run ONLY by `agent-run run --live real-model` — never CI — into the committed per-chunk `evidence/rm-capture.txt`, one `evidence/rm-capture-{drive}.txt` per pre-registered drive since 2026-09-29 (a series' drive, or the 2026-10-07 capture run's); 2026-09-22) | untrusted SUT output from two sources: (1) the attributed incident re-read over MCP — since 2026-09-29 its report body printed verbatim from its first `## ` line — bounded (a 600 s poll at 10 s; an id sweep of at most 64 ids from the highest id seen minus 63, floor 1, that stops after 3 misses) and (2) Pulse's own newest `agent-latest.jsonl.*` under `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`'s `logs/` — a TEST-binary reader turning that handle's VALUE into a path — since `2026-09-23-real-model-capture-path-handles-guarded-and-stale-read-back-texts-corrected` through `capture_paths::pulse_logs_dir_from`, which canonicalizes it and requires a directory before joining `logs/`, every failure a path-free reason (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR unset` / `rejected: {io::ErrorKind}` / `rejected: not a directory`) surfaced as `pulse-log: none ({reason})` through the scrub below (the no-canonicalize residual of 2026-09-22 is retired). Since 2026-09-29 it also prints Pulse's `creating digest corpus retrieval rows:` line, the `canary:` lines and `scenario_storm=` on storm lines; since 2026-10-01, Pulse's `interpretation.incident.skipped` lines fields-only (`skip_reason`, `decision`, `severity`, `digest_kind` — closed enums Pulse's code writes, allowlisted on its side) and, on each `canary:` line, its inference's `skip_reason` as a trailing field. Every printed line passes `mask_workspace_key` FIRST, then `redact_value`, then `mask_host_paths` (its named roots are `/home/`, `/Users/`, `%APPDATA%` and, since 2026-10-06, `/tmp/` and `/var/tmp/`, all with the same match semantics — `redact_value` names neither temp root, so a temp-rooted workspace path kept its parent through the chain, as measured at `a_posix_path_valued_workspace_leaks_neither_its_key_nor_its_path` and `the_mask_covers_the_named_roots`, each red before the extension; no committed capture holds a temp-rooted path, so no digest pin moved), then `elide_fingerprints` (two rules since 2026-10-02 — KEYED: the alphanumeric value after every `fingerprint_hex=` prints `<fingerprint>` whatever its class, all-digit included, an existing `<fingerprint>` or an empty keyed value left as it is, the shape of the `workspace=` rule; UNKEYED: a fingerprint-shaped token — eight or more lowercase hex digits holding at least one letter — prints as `<fingerprint>`, while an unkeyed all-digit run, a nanosecond stamp or a seed, passes; the harvest walks every committed `rm-capture*.txt` under `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/*/evidence/`, workspace-root anchored from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` with no handle, and holds each at zero un-elided keyed values and a fixed point of the elision, the population pinned by count beside an inverse control; envelope `fingerprints` stay elided to counts). The workspace-key mask (since 2026-09-30) prints `<workspace-key>` for the value of every `workspace=` line whatever it holds — the raw key, a scrubber rendering such as the `[redacted: credit_card]` measured at the 2026-09-29 b2 drive, anything else — and for every occurrence of the key bounded outside `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` (each `## Previously Seen` entry's `({workspace})` suffix); the key is the data dir's basename, taken once from the guarded `capture_paths::pulse_logs_dir_from` path's parent, never from a raw read of the handle (absent or rejected ⇒ no key, the `workspace=` lines masked regardless). Pulse stamps the key as a PATH — its detected workspace root, else the data dir (andromeda-pulse `crates/workspace-detector/src/contract.rs` `workspace_key`, at `fcc31b2`, unchanged at `a2addb3`, at `5f77859`, at `f70be92` and at `9bfefb8`) — so the leaf matches only under a launch whose detection falls back to the data dir, as the 2026-09-30, 2026-10-01, 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07 series' did, and the 2026-10-07 capture run's (the 2026-10-07 series' `pulse-app` by digest and its launch shape; Pulse's boot line read the data dir's leaf as the workspace basename), and the 2026-10-07 sixth series' (Pulse's boot line again read the leaf as the workspace basename). Pulse's witnesses are read fields-only and the capture itself never prints the workspace basename; the report's rendering of it is witnessed by one class-only line, `pulse-report workspace rendering: {verbatim|scrubbed|absent|unknown-key}` (`verbatim` = the value or its last path component is the key), never the value — as measured at the 2026-09-30, 2026-10-01, 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07 series and at the 2026-10-07 capture run (a pre-registered run that is not a series), whose leaves occur 0 times across their three captures each (on the 2026-10-06 series, the first on the Linux dev host with a home-rooted data dir, on the 2026-10-07 series and on the 2026-10-07 capture run, each `## Previously Seen` suffix is a POSIX path and prints `<redacted>`, taken whole by `redact_value` after the key mask) — and as measured at the 2026-10-07 sixth series (Pulse `9bfefb8`), whose leaf occurs 0 times across its three captures, whose rendering witness reads `verbatim` on all three and whose `## Previously Seen` suffixes each print `<redacted>` (that chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`); the output is buffered and written ONCE. Corpus-rendered model text may enter the committed copy only under the ratified Data Protection exception (§Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection) | the capture's own scrub path, its MCP re-read going through the hardened `ReadbackClient::connect`; its reader `real_model_harvest` loads each committed capture from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` + a hard-coded path (no `CONDUCTOR_*` handle), checks it against its sha256 digest pin over the LF-normalized content, and grades the file only after the digest matches — no capture text sits in test source (since 2026-09-30); the chunk's host-path hygiene gates over the capture and the harvest |

| Span-landing witness ingest (`conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs`, `live-pulse` feature, operator-gated, never CI; 2026-10-01) | untrusted SUT output: every `agent-latest.jsonl*` under `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`'s `logs/` (a TEST-binary reader turning that handle's VALUE into a path), plus the two frozen Conductor self-obs journals `runs/span-landing/span-{a,b}.jsonl` under `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` (the firing form clears those two named files, non-recursively, before drive A) | both handles through the shared `conductor-run/tests/capture_paths` guards (`pulse_logs_dir_from`: canonicalize + is-dir before `logs/` is joined; `runs_dir_from` → `resolve_under`), every rejection and read failure a path-free reason (`e.kind()` only); one bounded `serde_json` decode per line, an undecodable line skipped; a STALE pair is refused before any grading (`pair_is_current`: drive A at or after the live Pulse log's first line, drive B at or before its last, A before B), so a pair left from an earlier pass is never graded against the current log; it prints exactly ONE integers-only `span-landing: PASS|FAIL …` line — never a Pulse line, a path, a workspace key or a fingerprint — so nothing it emits needs the capture scrub chain and nothing from the ingest is committed beyond those integers |

| `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` — **the SPAWN-propagation use specifically** (the handle also has a non-spawn DECLARATION reader in the row above — it grades this handle on PRESENCE via `conductor_core::handle_declared`, so a real path DOES satisfy that subject; it still carries no value anywhere and neither relaxes nor satisfies this duty — and TEST-binary VALUE readers: since 2026-09-22 the real-model capture and since 2026-10-01 the `span_landing_live` witness each join it with `logs/` to read Pulse's own log, canonicalized and required to be a directory first (`conductor-run/tests/capture_paths`, since `2026-09-23-real-model-capture-path-handles-guarded-and-stale-read-back-texts-corrected`, retiring the 2026-09-22 no-canonicalize residual) — which likewise neither relaxes nor satisfies this duty; the capture's own sidecar spawn goes through the hardened `ReadbackClient::connect`, and the witness spawns no sidecar) | reject argument-injection metacharacters before spawn; treat strictly as an env value passed via the `.env(...)` builder, NEVER interpolated into argv or a shell (MCP-sidecar STDIO command/argument-injection class, CVE-2026-30623 / OX advisory) | validate the path string in `conductor-verify` before the `spawn::build_command` / `tokio::process::Command` stdio spawn; resolve the platform default (`%APPDATA%\andromeda-pulse` on Windows · `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`~/.andromeda-pulse` on Linux) if Pulse leaves it unset |

| CLI arguments / stdin (`conductor-cli` seed/scenario flags + the `run` target (a scenario name or a P-ID) + the `run_id` positional + the `preconditions --for` scenario name) | `CONDUCTOR_SEED` parses to the seed integer type; scenario key maps to a known P-ID ("no scenario without a P-ID"); CLI flag precedence over env. `conductor preconditions --for <SCENARIO>` (2026-09-22) takes a scenario NAME resolved through the validated scenario load; a `P-NNN`-shaped value is refused at argument parsing (a clap usage error, exit 2), because a P-ID can name several scenarios; without the flag the probe is unchanged. The `run` target (and the harness's `SCENARIO=`, passed straight through) refuses a P-ID that several scenarios name BEFORE any scenario load — an `anyhow` harness fault naming the P-ID, the count and the matching scenario file stems (never a path), rendered `error:` + `hint:` at exit 1; a single-owner P-ID still resolves (2026-09-30; it took the first `read_dir` match before). The harness's `run --live [real-model]` selector is a closed `case` allowlist — the `.ps1` binds the token by position count — and an unknown token prints usage and exits 2 before any probe, never reaching an argv or a path. The `run_id`-class POSITIONAL argument (`report` / `cleanup`, the latter added 2026-09-06) is NOT path-handle class: on `cleanup` its only sink is a rusqlite `?1` bound parameter and it is never joined into a path, so the canonicalize duty above does not attach to it; the harness shells additionally reject it upstream (`valid_run_id` / `Test-RunId`) before the spawn. `conductor scenarios` (2026-10-12) takes no argument: it loads the catalogue through the validated `list_scenarios` load and the capability manifest's fixed `default_path()` → `resolve_under` route (an absent or malformed manifest is a harness fault, `error:` + `hint:`, exit 1, path-free). `conductor suite`'s operator stop (2026-10-12) is an in-process OS signal registration (`tokio::signal::ctrl_c`, installed after preflight) that carries no value — the first Ctrl-C sets the stop flag, the second exits 130 — so neither adds an input class | the CLI arg parser in `conductor-cli`; `anyhow` at the binary edge for type-erased parse failures |

| MCP child stdout (trusted-child boundary — read-back AND the `mark_incident_resolved` lifecycle write, which shares the same `call_tool` path and controls; its applied response `{resolved, incident_id}` and its DECLINED arm, a JSON-RPC `ToolDispatchFailed` from Pulse's `IncidentWriteOutcome::DeclinedStale`, both arrive here; and the `retrieve_incident_events` by-id READ on the same path — its response `{incident_id, events[{event_kind, occurred_unix_nano}], total, truncated}` and its unknown-id arm, a JSON-RPC error carrying `incident not found` that lands as a typed `VerifyError::JsonRpc`, never `Ok` and never a panic) | bounded line-delimited JSON-RPC decoding (serde_json is recursion-limited against decode-bomb depth; a soft per-line size bound on the child's stdout — no unbounded read); a JSON-RPC error or empty canary round-trip ⇒ `blocked`, never false pass | hand-rolled JSON-RPC client (`conductor-verify/src/jsonrpc.rs`) parses each response line to `serde_json::Value`; the verdict/error wall maps JSON-RPC errors / decode faults to typed inputs (`VerifyError::{JsonRpc,Decode,Transport}`), never panics; canary asserts `query_incident_list` reports an incident opened AFTER the storm's emission stamp (`extract::opened_at_unix_nanos` vs `CanaryMarker.emitted_at_unix_nano`) — an absent or unparseable stamp contributes nothing and reads as NOT-fresh ⇒ `blocked`, never a false pass |

| `runs.db` writes (rusqlite raw SQL, no ORM) | use **bound parameters** for `run_id`/`seed`/fingerprint-JSON1 writes — never string-formatted SQL (despite near-nil injection exposure because content is self-generated synthetic data, per security-research.md rusqlite finding) | rusqlite 0.38.0 parameterized statements in the `conductor-report` storage seam; fingerprint arrays written as a JSON1 TEXT array |
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Input for input-validation bans.)
