The obs service-identity env-handles `CONDUCTOR_SERVICE_NAME` / `CONDUCTOR_ENV` (obs-plan §3) are **non-path string labels** stamped into self-observation JSON log *values* (JSON-escaped by serde_json; no path / SQL / argv exposure), and `CONDUCTOR_AGENT_MODE` is a **non-path boolean trigger** (only its presence is read — `agent_mode = --agent-mode flag || env-set`; the value is unused, never stamped into a log or interpolated into a path); all three require **no validation**, unlike the `CONDUCTOR_*` *path* handles in the table above. (The agent-mode log path `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` is itself derived from `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` through the same `resolve_under` traversal guard as the other artifact handles — not from `CONDUCTOR_AGENT_MODE`.)

title: Data Protection

body:
_[Light for Minimal — adapted: Conductor has no HTTPS surface and stores no
sensitive data]_

**No sensitive data stored.** Conductor owns no credentials, PII, payment, or
health data (Threat Model Summary § Data classification — all "none"). The only
persisted data is self-generated synthetic OTLP test telemetry and run-metadata
(`runs.db` + per-run JSONL journals + Markdown reports under `runs/`), which is
not user-derived and carries no confidentiality requirement.

**No HTTPS/TLS surface to enforce.** Conductor exposes no inbound listener and
runs no HTTP server (Threat Model Summary § Attack surface; Stack: "Backend
Framework: None"). Its only network egress is **loopback** OTLP/gRPC to
`127.0.0.1:4317` plus a stdio child-process MCP session — neither crosses a host
boundary, so TLS / HSTS / certificate pinning are N/A (adding them would
contradict the loopback-only Minimal model).

**Encryption at rest is out of scope for Conductor.** Pulse's `corpus.db` is
**plaintext SQLite** — the P-049 "encrypted at rest via `OsKeychainBackend`"
assumption proved WRONG when verified live (2026-06-27), so the keychain-failure
canary mode does not apply. Conductor reaches the corpus through the MCP tool
surface only — read-back to prove wiring, plus the `mark_incident_resolved`
lifecycle write — never the file, and never persists or exfiltrates its content
(Standard Contracts: Readiness gate), except the ratified, scrubbed real-model
capture evidence (§Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection).

_Per template: for Minimal tier the At-rest / Key-management / Data-lifecycle
subsections are omitted — no sensitive data is stored and there is no key
material under Conductor's control._

title: Dependency Security

body: _[ALL tiers]_

This is the primary residual-risk class for Conductor's Minimal tier
(Threat Model Summary § tier justification: "dependency/supply-chain audit,
notably `bundled` SQLite compiled from C source and the OTLP/gRPC/MCP
dependency tree").

**Audit tool:** `cargo-audit` **≥ 0.22** (RustSec; installed 0.22.2) — the ecosystem-standard scanner and minimum bar; audits `Cargo.lock` against the RustSec advisory DB and uniquely flags unmaintained crates (covers the `bundled`-SQLite C version via the `libsqlite3-sys` crate advisory, plus the tonic/prost tree). Strongly recommended companion: `cargo-deny` **≥ 0.19** (Embark; installed 0.19.4) — superset that additionally gates banned crates, duplicate versions, untrusted sources, and license policy via a single `deny.toml`; the 2026 practice is `cargo-audit` report-only first, then `cargo-deny` with advisory blocking on high/critical. (Both from security-research.md § Dependency Audit Tools.) These are external CLI tools, **not `Cargo.lock`-pinnable dependencies** — the stated versions are **minimum floors**; the actual security signal is the RustSec advisory DB fetched fresh on each run plus the committed lock, so any tool at or above the floor running green satisfies the gate.
**Two distinct external-decay faults, two distinct remedies (do not conflate them):**

- A **TOOL fault** — the installed scanner is too old, or carries a bug a newer release fixes. Remedy: **raise the floor** to the fixed release (these tools are unlockable, so a floor is the only pin available).

- An **advisory-DATABASE fault** — the RustSec DB itself will not parse or fetch, so *no* released tool version can read it. A floor raise is **unexecutable** here and would look like compliance while changing nothing. Remedy: a **bounded wait** — re-check each chunk, and keep coverage meanwhile via the deliberate audit↔deny **overlap**, verifying `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` actually ran green rather than assuming it. Never a `deny.toml` ignore (that suppresses a real signal class for a transient external fault), never a CI edit, never a silent accept.
  *Established empirically 2026-08-09* (`2026-08-09-interpretation-correctness-posture`): `duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244` failed byte-identically on the installed 0.22.1 **and** on the latest published 0.22.2, so no floor raise existed — the tool was never the fault. **Re-adjudicated 2026-09-05 (`2026-09-05-audit-corrective`): the fault was LOCAL, not an advisory-DATABASE fault.** The duplicate was an untracked `crates/gettext-sys/RUSTSEC-2026-0244.md` in this host's `${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/advisory-db` checkout; upstream had moved that file to `crates/gettext-rs/` on 2026-08-09 (`e12b689b`) — the deferral's first day — and a fetch INTO an existing clone never deletes untracked files, so every reading measured the cache rather than the world. Post-clean the probe measures green: HEAD `5a0ebedf`, `git status --porcelain` empty, `cargo audit` exit 0 over 1239 advisories / 564 crates with 18 `deny.toml`-adjudicated allowed warnings, `cargo deny` exit 0 — closing the standing deferral. **So the porcelain check on the DB checkout PRECEDES classifying any parse failure as external** (a fetch cannot clear residue; a CI run's clean checkout, or a fresh clone under `--db`, is the second witness). Distinguishing the cases is what keeps a red gate honest instead of papered over.
  **Admitting a NEW dependency under a red audit (2026-08-16; regime CLOSED 2026-09-05 — the audit measures green, so a delta now lands under a green `cargo audit` over the committed lock, and this conditional re-arms only if a future audit goes red on a fault verified external by the porcelain check above):** the wait was originally justified partly by the tree being static — a zero-delta chunk cannot have caused an external failure. That no longer holds once a dependency lands, so the condition is explicit: **a dependency delta MAY land under a red audit, but only on a `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` VERIFIED green over the NEW `Cargo.lock`** — verified, never assumed, because the deny overlap is then the sole coverage for the added packages, and any new license/advisory it surfaces takes the justified-exception mechanism above. State the changed basis when re-pinning the deferral: "no dependency delta" stops being available as a reason. First applied when `blake3` (+ `arrayref`/`arrayvec`/`constant_time_eq`/`cpufeatures`) landed at `2026-08-16-canary-fingerprint-derivation-aligned` against the 22nd consecutive red audit.
**Pinning:** `Cargo.lock` committed (makes the audit deterministic — security-research.md cargo-audit + tar-rs findings). Toolchain pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` to **≥ 1.94.1** — **done** (channel `1.95.0`, workspace `rust-version = 1.94.1`), clearing the tar-rs symlink-chmod CVE-2026-33056 / RUSTSEC-2026-0033 in the `cargo build` extraction path.
**Update policy:** manual review for a single-developer tool; bump versions flagged by `cargo-audit`/`cargo-deny`. The `tauri` ≥ 2.10.3 floor (CVE-2026-42184) and its bundler host-tool floor retired 2026-10-11 with the window: no `tauri` package remains in `Cargo.lock`. Keep `libsqlite3-sys` current so SQLite patch bumps flow in. (rmcp removed 2026-06-27 — the read-back client is now hand-rolled JSON-RPC; the former rmcp ≥ 1.4.0 / GHSA-89vp-x53w-74fx stdio-client note no longer applies.)
**Accepted exceptions (deny.toml, each with a justifying comment):** as of 2026-10-11 the set is **0 `[advisories] ignore` entries + 8 `[licenses] allow` entries**, reconciled against `deny.toml` at `2026-10-11-conductors-window-retired` (the 16 Tauri-tree ignores and the `MPL-2.0` allow left with their subject; `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception` stays for its current holders — `blake3`, `rustix`/`linux-raw-sys`, the `wasi`/`wit-bindgen`/`wasm-*` tree). The license allows include `Zlib` (`foldhash` via `rusqlite`→`hashbrown`) and `BSD-2-Clause` (`arrayref` via `conductor-emit`→`blake3`) — both OSI-approved + FSF Free/Libre, permissive. This is the documented mechanism for non-actionable advisories / permissive-license additions, with the deny gate staying green (no unresolved CVE). `deny.toml` itself remains the authority on the full set; the counts here are a reconciliation stamp, not a second source. The workspace's own `conductor-*` crates are NOT exempt: `deny.toml` carries no `private` exemption, so `cargo deny check licenses` checks them like any dependency, and they pass as `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, inherited from `[workspace.package]` — a member without an allowed license fails the gate, and `publish = false` exempts nothing. The allow set needed no entry for them (`MIT` and `Apache-2.0` are already allowed); the 0 + 8 counts above are the 2026-10-11 reading.

**Retired 2026-09-07:** the `number_prefix` ignore (RUSTSEC-2025-0119) is gone. `indicatif` 0.18 replaced `number_prefix` with `unit-prefix`, so the crate left `Cargo.lock` entirely and the entry's own justifying comment — which named the `via indicatif 0.17` dependency path — no longer described anything in the tree. The authority for removing it is **`deny.toml:`'s own requirement** that every accepted advisory be listed *with* a justifying comment; **no rule of this plan compelled it**, and the 2026-06-23 sidecar's Follow-up ("a future `indicatif` 0.18 bump may drop `number_prefix`") anticipated the retirement without obliging it.
**The third dependency class — RETIRED 2026-10-11 (0 members):** the CI-time-fetched third-party binary the `a11y` job acquired (since 2026-09-17 the version-pinned msedgedriver, admitted by a pre-execution Authenticode gate) left with that job, so the audited surface is again the Rust crate graph alone (`Cargo.lock`, scanned by `cargo-audit` + `cargo-deny`); its registration, version disposition and measurements are last at `321dc8f`. A job-time-fetched program re-opens the class only as an escalated, operator-ratified boundary widening.

**CI integration:** add a `cargo install cargo-audit` + `cargo audit` step (and optionally `cargo deny check advisories bans sources licenses`) to the existing `.github/workflows/` that already runs `cargo build` / nextest / clippy (Infrastructure Patterns: CI/CD approach). Build fails on advisory hit.
**Critical CVE response SLA:** for a single-developer local tool — patch within ~1 week of disclosure for actionable advisories against the dependency tree; immediate bump for any advisory that touches the `cargo build` extraction path (tar-rs class), since that is the live build boundary.

**Frontend (npm) supply chain — RETIRED 2026-10-11:** no npm tree remains (`crates/conductor-tauri/ui/package-lock.json` left whole with the window; `git ls-files '*package.json'` → 0), and the `npm audit --omit=dev` gate left with the `frontend` job; Cargo is the one audited ecosystem.

_Supply chain integrity subsection — artifacts Conductor PRODUCES (release signing / SBOM / base-image scanning):
**SKIP** — Standard + Hardened only; Conductor is Minimal tier with no
container/cloud deployment. The SKIP is scoped to PRODUCED artifacts:
and no consumption-side signature control remains
(the fetched-binary class and its Authenticode gate retired 2026-10-11). Optional additive note only: `cargo-auditable` 0.7.4
(security-research.md) can wrap the release build as `cargo auditable build
--release` to embed the dependency list into the shipped `conductor-cli` binary
for later `cargo audit bin <binary>` when the binary is run beside Pulse on
another dev host — low priority, purely additive, not a gate._
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Code Patterns for supply-chain bans.)

title: Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project)

body:
_[ALL tiers — explicit derivation hint for downstream consumers per D26 chain.
Adapted for Minimal tier: auth and supply-chain-signing phases are dropped.]_

The downstream skills derive the following bootstrap phases from the contract
above. Listed for explicitness — route may reorder / combine, setup-project may
add stack-specific intermediate steps.

- **input-validation-library-install:** confirm `garde` 0.22.1 + `serde` 1.0.x are wired with `#[derive(Validate)]` `range` + `dive` on every scenario-config boundary struct in its owning seam crate, AND that every sibling-reading cross-field rule ships as a `Scenario::check_*()` invoked from `from_toml_str` with a test pinning that the load path actually invokes it (Input Validation above). Add the separate `std::fs::canonicalize` + bounds-check at the `conductor-cli` edge for the RUST-READ `CONDUCTOR_*` path handles (outside garde's struct validation). Scope this phase's canonicalize work per READER rather than per handle (2026-09-06): `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` reaches Rust in test binaries too — `conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs` reads it, as do the three operator-gated `live-pulse` readers `live_suite.rs`, `real_model_live.rs` and `span_landing_live.rs` (2026-10-01) — so what this phase installs covers exactly the readers a SHIPPED binary provides. Those four `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` test readers carry no residual: since `2026-09-23-real-model-capture-path-handles-guarded-and-stale-read-back-texts-corrected` (the span-landing witness from birth) they resolve through `conductor-run/tests/capture_paths` → `resolve_under` (Input Validation, path-handle row).

- **dep-audit-tooling-install:** install `cargo-audit` ≥ 0.22 (installed 0.22.2) (+ recommended `cargo-deny` ≥ 0.19 (installed 0.19.4) with `deny.toml`) per Dependency Security above; toolchain `rust-toolchain.toml` ≥ 1.94.1 (done — 1.95.0). _Realized in 2026-06-15-dependency-audit-gate; the tool versions are floors, not lockable pins._

- **secret-management-init:** minimal — Conductor owns no secrets (Threat Model Summary § Data classification: credential "none"). No dotenv/secret-manager wiring; only the non-secret `CONDUCTOR_*` / Pulse-side `ANDROMEDA_*` env handles per Secret Management below. Effectively a no-op beyond asserting "no secrets introduced."

- **secret-scanning-ci-gate:** REALIZED 2026-09-24. The `rust` job's `Secret-scan gate` runs `crates/conductor-core/tests/secret_scan_gate.rs` — content rules plus a secret-file-name class over git's cached + untracked-not-ignored listing, an exact-set allowlist, and a hit that names `path:line` and never echoes its match — so no secret is ever introduced into the `conductor-*` workspace unnoticed. `.gitignore` ignores `.env*` and the key / certificate / SSH-key file classes the gate detects (`*.pem` `*.p12` `*.pfx` `*.key` `*.cer` `*.crt` `*.jks` `*.keystore` `id_*`), none of which is expected (Secret Management; bans in `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Secrets). The scanner is an in-repo Rust static gate, operator-selected (§Secret Management → Secret-scan gate shape).

- **error-sanitization-wire:** wire boundary error sanitization per Error Handling above — module-internal `thiserror` 2.0.18 typed enums (`EmitError`, `VerifyError`, `ContractMismatch`, `ConfigError`) collapse to type-erased `anyhow` only at the `conductor-cli` edge; run-report artifacts (`<run_id>.md`, `runs.db` rows) must not leak absolute paths / internal struct names.

- **dep-security-ci-gate:** wire `cargo-audit` (+ optional `cargo-deny` advisories/bans/sources/licenses) + `Cargo.lock` drift verification into the existing GitHub Actions pipeline (build + nextest + clippy); build fails on advisory hit per the SLA stated.

_Phases dropped for Minimal tier: **auth-scaffolding-baseline** (auth approach =
none — single-user local tool), **logging-redaction-wire** (Logging & Monitoring
section SKIP at Minimal; redaction guidance instead folded into the Logging
anti-patterns + Error Handling as forward-guardrails), **supply-chain-signing-init**
(Standard + Hardened only)._

route uses this list to plan phase ordering (typically:
input-validation-library-install → dep-audit-tooling-install →
secret-management-init → secret-scanning-ci-gate → error-sanitization-wire →
dep-security-ci-gate). setup-project uses this list to materialize each phase's
bootstrap script + dependency list + CI workflow snippet.

title: Secret Management

body: _[ALL tiers; expand for Hardened]_

**Conductor owns no secrets** (Threat Model Summary § Data classification:
credential "none"; architecture Cross-cutting Patterns: Trust boundary — "There
are no secrets, no `DATABASE_URL`, and no cloud credentials"). This section
therefore documents the *absence* and the env-handle discipline rather than a
storage/rotation regime.
**Storage:**
- **Production:** N/A — no secrets to store. Local-only tool; no cloud secret manager, no `.env` secret file.

- **Development:** N/A — no dev secrets. Only non-secret configuration handles exist under the reserved `CONDUCTOR_*` env namespace (`CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`, `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR`, `CONDUCTOR_CONTRACT_MANIFEST`, `CONDUCTOR_SEED`) and the Pulse-side `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` flags.
- **Production / dev separation:** N/A — no secret values exist in either.

**Never in code:** no credentials exist to hardcode; the OS keychain reference (`OsKeychainBackend("com.andromeda.pulse")`) is Pulse-side and accessed by the spawned sidecar as the same OS user — Conductor never reads, stores, or embeds keychain material.

**Secret scanning in CI:** defense-in-depth that holds the no-secrets invariant over time — the `rust` job's `Secret-scan gate` fails the build on any secret-shaped string or file name in the `conductor-*` workspace (§Bootstrap phases `secret-scanning-ci-gate`). The scanner is an in-repo Rust static gate, operator-selected over a job-time-fetched tool, which would re-open the now-empty third dependency class and add a CI non-loopback egress where none remains (Secret-scan gate shape, below); do not adopt an unvetted tool.

**Secret-scan gate shape:** the gate is the `conductor-core` test target `crates/conductor-core/tests/secret_scan_gate.rs`, built on `regex` — a `conductor-core` dev-dependency edge on an already-locked package, so the gate admits no new package. The `rust` job's `Secret-scan gate` step is only its presence-guarded invocation (it fails when git lists no tracked files, so the gate never passes over an empty subject), and `agent-run run`'s workspace nextest runs the same target locally. Where the workspace root holds no `.git` entry at all (a VCS-less copy, such as cargo-mutants' default copy) the gate skips with one path-free stderr line and passes — decided by `Path::exists` before any spawn, so a `.git` FILE (a worktree, a submodule) counts as a repository and no spawn, argv element or env var is added — while a `git ls-files` failure inside a repository still fails it ("the gate has no subject"); CI always runs over a checkout, behind the unchanged presence guard. The gate carries in-suite negative arms that prove it can fail — every rule fires on a runtime-built sample. Its accepted trade-off is a small rule set Conductor maintains itself, with no entropy scoring; the alternative, a job-time-fetched scanner (a marketplace action or a downloaded binary), stays rejected because it would re-open the now-empty third dependency class (§Dependency Security) and add a CI non-loopback egress where none remains.
**Rotation cadence:** N/A — no API keys, DB passwords, JWT signing keys, or TLS certificates under Conductor's control (`runs.db` is an unencrypted local file of synthetic data; no `DATABASE_URL`).
**Access auditing:** N/A — no secret store to audit.

**What counts as secret (for the scanning gate's invariant):** API keys, DB passwords, JWT signing keys, OAuth client secrets, encryption keys, signing keys, webhook secrets, third-party tokens — **none of which Conductor should ever contain.** The OS keychain material that backs Pulse's `corpus.db` is explicitly Pulse's, not Conductor's.
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Secrets for secret-handling bans.)

title: Error Handling

body: _[ALL tiers]_

**External responses (to the operator):** sanitized — no stack
traces, file paths, internal hostnames, or library versions exposed. Conductor's
"external" surface is the `conductor-cli` stderr alone; the type-erased `anyhow` edge must not
surface absolute filesystem paths (e.g. canonicalized `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`) or
internal seam-crate struct names to those surfaces.

**Internal logging (for debugging):** full typed error detail stays inside the
seam crates as `thiserror` 2.0.18 enums (`EmitError`, `VerifyError`,
`ContractMismatch`, `ConfigError`); the verdict/error wall keeps `Result::Err`
strictly for harness faults (config parse, transport down, MCP unreachable) and
keeps verification outcomes as typed VALUES (`Verdict { Pass, Fail,
CalibrationRegion }` / `ReportState { Pass, Fail, ManualCheck, KnownResidual,
Blocked }`) returned as `Ok(...)`.

**Error format:** stack-native — `thiserror` typed enums per seam crate collapsed
to `anyhow` only at the `conductor-cli` boundary
(architecture Conventions: Error handling). RFC 7807 / GraphQL error extensions
are N/A (no HTTP/GraphQL surface). `tonic::Status` codes and MCP error responses
are first-class typed verification inputs, never panics.

**Run-report artifact sanitization:** the `<run_id>.md` report and `runs.db`
rows are agent-parseable ground truth — they must record verdict/state/identity
fields (`run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `slo_tier`, `latency_ms`,
`fingerprints`) WITHOUT leaking absolute host paths (the canonicalized
`CONDUCTOR_*` directories, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`) or internal struct/field
names from the seam crates. A `blocked` row populates only identity fields with
the named precondition string; measurement fields are JSON `null`.
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Logging for error-disclosure bans.)

title: Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)

body: _[ALL tiers — single source of truth for all security bans]_

title: Authentication

body:
_Conductor has no live auth surface today (auth approach = none — single-user
local tool). These are forward-guardrails: IF any auth/recovery surface is ever
added (e.g. a remote-controllable mode), these bans apply._
- NEVER reveal whether an account exists in a recovery/login flow (account enumeration) — applies the instant any identity surface is introduced.
- NEVER use weak recovery questions ("mother's maiden name") as a sole recovery factor.
- NEVER skip rate limiting on auth endpoints (brute-force) — if Conductor ever grows an authenticated control surface beyond local IPC, gate it.

- NEVER add interactive login to the headless `scripts/agent-run.sh` source-of-truth path — it is agent-driven by design (Cross-cutting Patterns: Development Style); an auth prompt there would silently break the release gate.

title: Input

body: - NEVER use the `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` / `CONDUCTOR_SCENARIOS_DIR` / `CONDUCTOR_CONTRACT_MANIFEST` env path handles without `std::fs::canonicalize` + bounds-check at the `conductor-cli` edge (path traversal) — these sit OUTSIDE garde's struct validation (security-research.md serde+garde finding). **The duty binds by READER, not by handle** (restated 2026-09-06): a handle in the shipped-binary set may ALSO have an unguarded test-only reader, and `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` has Rust test-binary readers — `conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs` reads it (set by the CI journal-conformance step, a no-op when unset), as do the three operator-gated `live-pulse` readers `conductor-run/tests/live_suite.rs`, `conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs` and `conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs` (2026-10-01). NEVER let such a reader join the handle under the workspace root unguarded: since `2026-09-23-real-model-capture-path-handles-guarded-and-stale-read-back-texts-corrected` (the span-landing witness from birth) all four resolve it through `conductor-run/tests/capture_paths` → `resolve_under`, rejecting an absolute or `..` value with a path-free reason (§Input Validation, path-handle row). The canonicalize duty above still binds every SHIPPED reader of every handle — for `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` that duty remains discharged at the `conductor-cli` edge.

- NEVER interpolate `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` (or any operator-supplied value) into the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` argv or a shell string — pass it strictly via the `.env(...)` builder and reject argument-injection metacharacters first (MCP-sidecar STDIO command/argument-injection class, CVE-2026-30623 / OX advisory; e.g. the `npx -c` allowlist bypass).

- NEVER spawn the MCP sidecar from an operator-chosen command — spawn `andromeda-pulse-mcp` as a fixed, hard-coded program NAME resolved through the inherited `PATH` (never a config-derived or operator-supplied command string) (MCP-sidecar STDIO design flaw). `PATH` is therefore BOTH a spawn-resolution input AND, since 2026-09-03, the subject of a second NON-SPAWNING resolution of the same const: `conductor_verify::sidecar_resolves_on_path()` walks `std::env::split_paths(PATH)` + `PATHEXT` for `PULSE_MCP_PROGRAM`, constructs no `Command`, and returns a boolean-grade fact — the resolved path is never returned, logged or rendered, and never becomes the spawn program. On the `agent-run` path SET `{boot, run --live}` (the second added 2026-09-06) a `PATH` miss is now named upstream as the `sidecar-resolvable` `[PRECONDITION]` subject instead of only surfacing as the ~0s `[BLOCKED]` row measured 2026-08-20 — on `run --live` it refuses the suite before any leg spawns a sidecar. The original rule stands: `PATH` is a spawn-resolution input: the environment selects WHICH binary the fixed name resolves to. Measured 2026-08-20 — a `PATH` entry split on a drive-letter colon resolved the sidecar nowhere and the run reported `[BLOCKED]` in ~0s, indistinguishable at row level from a genuine SUT-side gate failure.

- NEVER use string concatenation / `format!` to build SQL for `runs.db` — use rusqlite 0.38.0 **bound parameters** for `run_id`/`seed`/fingerprint-JSON1 writes (raw SQL, no ORM — security-research.md rusqlite finding), even though content is self-generated synthetic data.

- NEVER deserialize scenario config without validation at load — garde's `range` + `#[garde(custom)]` rules AND the load-path `Scenario::check_*()` cross-field checks called from `from_toml_str` TOGETHER are the trust boundary (`budget_ms` ≤ its scenario's own `slo_tier` deadline is one such rule); NEVER write a SIBLING-reading invariant as `#[garde(custom)]` — in garde 0.22.1 it receives `(&field, &())`, sees no sibling, and would look enforced while never testing the invariant (a bounded error fraction, shipped as `error_percent` ∈ 0..=100; p50≤p95≤p99; the `[phases.fault]` closed `kind` enum + fault ⇒ `occurrences = 0`); an unvalidated `serde` deserialize bypasses it. NEVER mark a nested spec field `#[garde(skip)]` — garde does not descend into it, so its rules never run and the boundary is silently bypassed even though the rules exist; `dive` is the only correct annotation (`PhaseSpec.emission` carried the historical `skip`; `PhaseSpec.fault` dives from birth).

- NEVER decode prost/protobuf from the child's stdout without bounded recursion on the read-back path (protobuf-decode DoS lineage RUSTSEC-2020-0002 / RUSTSEC-2024-0437); an empty canary round-trip MUST become `blocked`, never a false pass-as-empty.

title: Data Protection

body: - NEVER use deprecated crypto algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4, ECB mode) — the ban is now ACTIVE, not hypothetical: `conductor_emit::exception::fingerprint` ships a **blake3** derivation (first 16 bytes / 32 hex), replacing the retired non-cryptographic FNV-1a. Note the run-report `fingerprints[]` column is fed from read-back `Observation#fingerprints`, never from that derivation — the two never meet.

- NEVER have Conductor's production code directly open, copy, or exfiltrate Pulse's `corpus.db` (plaintext SQLite — P-049 encryption not active live; corpus access is via the MCP TOOL SURFACE only — read-back plus the `mark_incident_resolved` lifecycle write — never the file) — it is owned by Pulse (the SUT); never persist its content into Conductor artifacts (Standard Contracts: Readiness gate) — with ONE ratified, scoped exception (the operator's P4 decision, ratified at the `2026-09-22-interpretation-proven-live` wrap on 2026-09-23): corpus-rendered model text the real-model capture re-reads over MCP (the attributed incident's `retrieve_report` sections) may enter a chunk's committed `evidence/` tree, and only through `mask_workspace_key` + `redact_value` + `mask_host_paths` + `elide_fingerprints`, every `fingerprint_hex=` value elided whatever its class, and every unkeyed fingerprint-shaped token — an unkeyed all-digit run is a stamp or a seed and passes (§Input Validation — the real-model capture ingest row); anywhere else the ban binds unchanged. The 2026-09-23 capture carries none — no report was read; the 2026-09-29 series' b2 capture carries one report body; the 2026-09-30 series read none; the 2026-10-01 series' d1 and d3 captures carry one report body each, d2 none; the 2026-10-06 series' d1, d2 and d3 captures carry one report body each; so do the 2026-10-07 series' d1, d2 and d3 captures, the 2026-10-07 capture run's d1, d2 and d3 captures, and the 2026-10-07 sixth series' d1, d2 and d3 captures. On that capture run an operator-owned recording of the model's argv ran beside the leg, outside this repository: no Conductor artifact holds or reads it, the chunk's attempt ledger names the operator's three files by sha256 and byte count and copies none, and no fact derived from a recorded prompt entered a committed file — the exception stays scoped to the scrubbed capture evidence (as measured at the `2026-10-07-a-capture-run-records-the-prompt-the-model-received-in-each-drive` chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). **The 2026-09-29 BREACH is REMEDIED (2026-09-30), never ratified:** it had put that report body in test source, as byte-equal string literals in `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_series/mod.rs`, outside the `evidence/` tree this exception names. Every committed capture is now held by a sha256 digest pin per evidence file and graded from the file after its digest matches, with no committed capture text in test source — held by the harvest's `no_committed_capture_text_sits_in_test_source` arm, as measured at its inverse control (a planted report line red, removed green); the graded 2026-09-23 capture is an elided copy under `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-30-interpretation-re-proven-on-a-clean-named-data-dir/evidence/`, its storm `fingerprint_hex` tokens printed `<fingerprint>`. Both formerly stated residuals were FIXED on 2026-10-02 under the founder's ruling, never ratified: the frozen 2026-09-22 file was elided in place on its two keyed lines — a recorded exception to "frozen evidence is never edited" — and is byte-identical to the graded copy; the graded 2026-10-01 `rm-capture-d3.txt` was re-elided on its two keyed lines and its digest pin moved, and `the_2026_10_01_captures_carry_no_fingerprint_and_no_workspace_key` asserts zero all-digit keyed values for every drive; every committed real-model capture carries zero un-elided `fingerprint_hex` values (`every_committed_capture_carries_no_un_elided_fingerprint_value`), and no committed quote of either value remains in the tree (git history keeps the originals and was not rewritten). The ban is on FILE access, not on the sanctioned write tool: staging a corpus row directly to induce a SUT state (e.g. Pulse's `DeclinedStale`) is the banned route, and is why that arm is stub-proven instead.
- NEVER persist real secrets or credentials into the unencrypted `runs.db` / JSONL journals — they store only self-generated synthetic telemetry; treat them as world-readable local files.

- NEVER disable TLS verification or downgrade to plaintext on any surface that is ever promoted beyond loopback — today egress is `127.0.0.1:4317` loopback-only, but a non-loopback target must not silently skip transport verification.

title: API

body:
_Conductor exposes no network API today (no inbound listener; Backend Framework =
none). These are forward-guardrails: IF a network surface is ever added, these
bans apply._

- NEVER expose internal error details (stack traces, file paths, library versions, internal struct names) in any response — the `anyhow` edge and run-report artifacts must stay sanitized (Error Handling above).
- NEVER skip request size limits (DoS via large payloads) — if Conductor ever adds a network surface beyond loopback/IPC, it MUST enforce request size limits and bounded decoding before parsing.
- NEVER trust `X-Forwarded-For` (or any client-supplied origin/IP header) without verifying the proxy chain — relevant only if a network listener is ever introduced.

- NEVER promote the port-occupier fault bind on `:4317` (the single deliberate `conductor-faults` port bind) into a general-purpose inbound listener accepting external input — it is an intentional in-host fault, not an API surface.

title: Secrets

body: - NEVER commit `.env` files or any secret-shaped string to the `conductor-*` workspace — Conductor owns no secrets and that invariant must hold (enforced by the secret-scanning CI gate; see Secret Management).
- NEVER hardcode credentials in source code — there are none to hardcode; the OS keychain reference is Pulse-side, accessed by the spawned sidecar, never embedded in Conductor.
- NEVER put credentials in URL query strings or argv — use the `.env(...)` builder for the sidecar's `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` (which is a non-secret path handle, not a credential).
- NEVER introduce a `DATABASE_URL` or cloud-credential env var — the SQLite path is a local file and the tool is local-only (Occupied Resources: Environment variables — "no secrets/cloud env vars").
- NEVER skip the secret-scanning CI gate — it is the only thing that enforces the "no secrets ever" invariant over time for this workspace.

title: Logging

body: - NEVER log secrets, tokens, or `Authorization` headers — there are none in Conductor, and this ban keeps it that way if any future integration introduces them.
- NEVER expose stack traces, absolute file paths, or internal struct/field names to the operator via `conductor-cli` stderr — sanitize at the `anyhow` edge (Error Handling above).

- NEVER let run-report artifacts (`<run_id>.md`, `runs.db` rows, JSONL journals) or committed evidence records (the per-chunk `evidence/` tree) leak absolute host paths (canonicalized `CONDUCTOR_*` directories, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`) or internal seam-crate struct names — they are agent-parseable ground truth shared across hosts, so they must carry verdict/state/identity fields only.

- NEVER write the journal/report wall-clock stamps from tokio's virtual clock — use `std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant` so journal-relative SLO math stays correct (Cross-cutting Patterns: Determinism discipline); a wrong clock source corrupts the ground-truth artifact.

title: Code Patterns

body: - NEVER spawn a child via a shell / `eval`-equivalent with operator-supplied input. Two rules, by spawn class: **(a) the MCP sidecar** — fixed hard-coded program NAME resolved through the inherited `PATH` + `.env(...)`, no config-into-argv — the same const also has a NON-SPAWNING sibling resolution (`sidecar_resolves_on_path`, a directory walk returning a boolean-grade fact whose resolved path is never returned, logged, rendered, or used as a spawn program — it answers presence with no process at all) (MCP-sidecar STDIO design flaw, CVE-2026-30623) — AND the spawn must suppress the child's console window (a `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`-class creation flag on Windows). **SHIPPED 2026-09-04:** `build_command` applies `.creation_flags(console_suppressing_flags())` under `#[cfg(windows)]` (`conductor-verify/src/spawn.rs`), held by a `#[cfg(windows)]` unit test (`spawn.rs::the_sidecar_spawn_suppresses_the_child_console`), so the spawn raises no terminal pane and discloses no absolute exe path. As measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-sidecar-spawn-without-a-console-window/evidence/nvda-pass.json`: SR row S1-01's `heard` lost `<host-path>`, `<host-path> terminal blank` and `pane`, and the committed record carries 0 `security_finding` rows and 0 `<host-path>` placeholders. This SUPERSEDES the 2026-09-02 reading (NVDA spoke the pane's title at SR pass row S1-01), which measured the pre-fix state and stands as the dated history that motivated the duty. The applied flag is not assertable at the unit tier — `std::process::Command` exposes no creation-flags getter — so the flag VALUE is unit-held and its APPLICATION was evidenced by the operator-local SR leg until that leg retired with the window (2026-10-11; test-plan §1 untestable zones). **(b) any HARNESS spawn** on the ROUTINE `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` path — ONE governed form since 2026-10-11, never a shell string and never an `eval`-equivalent: the fifth, the TEARDOWN spawn, where the shells invoke the repo-built `conductor` binary as a fixed program with a fixed verb and the operator-supplied `<run_id>` as a SEPARATE argv word (`conductor cleanup <run_id>`), admitted only after each shell's own run-id rejection (`valid_run_id` / `Test-RunId`), never assembled into a shell string and never as the program (operator-ratified 2026-09-06 as a deliberate, net-reducing boundary widening that replaced a `sqlite3`-CLI spawn). Forms 1–4 and 8 (the dev-only driver stack's `wdio.conf.ts` spawns and `send-keys.ps1`) and form 7 (`scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1`) retired 2026-10-11 with their files, the sixth retired 2026-09-17, and no ordinal is reused: the driver-stack and CI-workflow loci hold no governed form, and the network-arriving-PROGRAM property has no carrier (ratified by the operator on the founder's ruling R1 at that chunk's wrap; the retired registrations are last at `321dc8f`). A NINTH form escalates like every one before it and never becomes routine. An operator-supplied VALUE appears only as a separate element of an **array-form argv**, after rejection, never inside a shell string and never as the program. A spawn from a cargo TEST binary sits outside rule (b) — recorded 2026-09-24 for `crates/conductor-core/tests/secret_scan_gate.rs`'s `git -C <repo root> ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard`, a fixed PATH-resolved program with a fixed argv and no operator-supplied value; like the test binaries' `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*` spawns it composes nothing and adds no governed form.

- NEVER pin the read-back client to a strict newer protocol default — it MUST READ the `initialize` result's `protocolVersion` (Pulse's hand-rolled server version) and HOLD it against the manifest-pinned `2024-11-05`, surfacing a difference as the distinct `Blocked` precondition, and tolerate minimal capabilities. The hand-rolled client does not negotiate a version down from a default of its own — it reads what the server reports and asserts against the pin; a strict-newer default is the silent-mismatch class the preflight exists to prevent (Established Decisions: MCP Read-Back Client).

- NEVER follow symlinks when changing permissions during crate extraction on a pre-1.94.1 toolchain — bump `rust-toolchain.toml` to ≥ 1.94.1 to clear the tar-rs symlink-chmod flaw in the `cargo build` extraction path (CVE-2026-33056 / RUSTSEC-2026-0033) and keep `Cargo.lock` committed.

title: Universal

body: - NEVER run `cargo build --release` (the release gate) or merge to the dev OS target without `cargo-audit` (and recommended `cargo-deny`) green — the dependency/supply-chain audit IS the Minimal-tier residual-risk control for the `bundled`-SQLite-from-C + OTLP/gRPC/MCP tree (Threat Model Summary § tier justification).

- NEVER let `Cargo.lock` drift or go uncommitted — it makes the `cargo-audit`/`cargo-deny` scan non-deterministic and lets the `bundled` SQLite C version float past advisory tracking (security-research.md cargo-audit + rusqlite findings).

- NEVER add a scenario without a Pulse P-ID, and NEVER introduce an inbound network listener of Conductor's own **into the shipped binaries** — both violate the architecture's scope law / trust boundary and silently widen the attack surface beyond the loopback-client model (Cross-cutting Patterns: Scope law, Trust boundary).

- NEVER let a malformed child/transport input panic — `tonic::Status` codes and MCP error responses are first-class typed verification inputs routed through the verdict/error wall (`Ok(Verdict/ReportState)` vs `Result::Err` for harness faults only); a panic on the read-back path corrupts run classification.

- The ban below scopes to a preflight that is INVOKED. `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` run `conductor preconditions` as a leading arm and short-circuit on non-zero on the path SET `{boot, run --live}` (the second added 2026-09-06), SKIPPING the preflight entirely — so on either path an unmet precondition mints no `ReadyState`, no `Verdict`/`ReportState` and no `blocked` row. On `run --live` the short-circuit is a REFUSAL at exit 1 that names each unsatisfied subject and fires no leg, so the sidecar is never spawned rather than the run degrading to a ~0s `[BLOCKED]` row; the `run --live real-model` arm (2026-09-22) leads with `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation`, graded under that scenario's real-model posture, and refuses the same way. The probe's own properties are unaffected and stand: it is non-mutating (client-only `:4317` connect, no spawn, no env write) and exits non-zero naming every unsatisfied subject. **The "not a downgrade" reading HOLDS again as shipped, and the withdrawal is retired:** the probe grades the PATH-valued `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` by presence through `conductor_core::handle_declared` (the two flag handles keeping the truthy gate via the value-only `flag_declared` under the deterministic posture; under the real-model posture the L4 handle must instead be absent or falsy), so `handles-declared` is satisfiable, the short-circuit fires only on a genuinely unmet subject, and `boot` reaches the MCP readiness gate. As measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence/report.md`: `conductor preconditions` exit 0 (2026-09-04T17:07Z), then `ReadyState` emitted with `ready: true` / `canary_round_trip: "ok"` / `blocked_precondition: null` / 4-of-4 tools / `data_dir: "<redacted>"` in BOTH harness shells (bash 17:07:17→17:08:04Z · pwsh 17:11:16→17:12:03Z), zero `skipped preflight` lines in either, with no edit to `scripts/agent-run.sh` or `.ps1`. This SUPERSEDES the 2026-09-04T06:41Z `sr-findings-remediation` reading, which measured the pre-fix state.

- NEVER silently downgrade a failed preflight to pass/fail/manual-check — each of the gate's FIVE named preconditions (version mismatch / missing tool / no incident opened after the canary storm was emitted / app-sidecar workspace-key agreement / unmet run-contract terms) MUST surface as the distinct `blocked` state with its own named precondition string, never a false pass and never the generic corpus-empty string (Standard Contracts: Readiness gate). The run-contract arm composes ONE string naming each unmet term individually, carrying the condition AND its candidate causes — a term whose truth lives on the SUT's side is recorded `declared-not-observable` and never blocks, because blocking on it would assert a measurement Conductor cannot make. The keychain read-while-write fault is NOT among them — the P-049 encrypted-at-rest assumption was disproved live (`corpus.db` is plaintext SQLite), so that canary mode does not apply.

- NEVER add `unsafe` across the OTLP/gRPC/SQLite FFI boundary without review — safe Rust + `current_thread` tokio give memory/data-race safety for free, but the `bundled`-SQLite C and raw-protobuf/tonic codegen are the FFI surface the language cannot check (use `cargo-geiger` 0.13.0 ad-hoc to map `unsafe`; keep `libsqlite3-sys` current — security-research.md Rust/tokio + cargo-geiger findings).

- NEVER skip bumping a pinned dependency flagged by research — the toolchain ≥ 1.94.1 (tar-rs) is the standing FLOOR, and it is met (pinned ≥ 1.94.1). The `tauri` ≥ 2.10.3 floor retired 2026-10-11 with the crate: no `tauri` package is in `Cargo.lock`.

**Why:** D-security-deps (escalate) fired on the new a11y harness devDeps → `npm audit` = 20 (19 mod + 1 high), ALL dev-only + transitive (`@opentelemetry/core <2.8.0` via lighthouse→@sentry/node; `serialize-javascript <=7.0.4` via @wdio/mocha-framework→mocha), none fixable non-breaking; `npm audit --omit=dev` = 0. Resolved WITH the user (2026-06-27 — implement AskUserQuestion "Dev-aware gate (wrap amends)" + wrap mechanism AskUserQuestion "`npm audit --omit=dev`"): the dev tree is non-shipping test tooling, so gate production deps strictly + accept dev-only advisories at dev-tree grain — the npm analogue of the established deny.toml justified-exceptions discipline (a category-grain accept, vs cargo's per-advisory ignore, chosen for a Minimal-tier local tool to avoid adding an audit-suppression tool). A new playbook rule was added so this no longer escalates. Cascaded to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Frontend gate `npm audit` → `npm audit --omit=dev`) + `.claude/rules/security.md` + `.claude/docs/security-summary.md`; the arch §Inherited Defaults / §Stack one-liners updated in lockstep (architecture-amendments). The arch devDep-registration proposal was dismissed as over-reach (a11y-plan §3.5 + stack.md already name the harness tooling).

**Section:** §Threat Model (attack-surface entry point) · §Input Validation (MCP contract-manifest + MCP-read-back-child-stdout rows) · §Anti-Patterns (STDIO injection wording + negotiate-down) · §Dependency Security (audit tree + Update policy) · §Key decision

**Why:** mirrors the arch [MCP Read-Back Client] reversal (rmcp removed — Pulse's `tools/call` is non-MCP-compliant). **Every security INVARIANT is preserved** (the report demonstrates it): the hardened spawn (fixed path + `.env(...)` + metachar-reject) is unchanged (D-security-subprocess clean), the read-back decode is bounded + non-panicking through the verdict/error wall (D-security-input — the boundary is still validated, JSON not protobuf), no new dependency was added (D-security-deps clean — rmcp removed, tokio/serde_json already deps, `cargo audit` exit 0 / `cargo deny check` ok, Cargo.lock un-drifted). Routine wording→sound-impl reconcile (the 2026-06-15 rule) where the invariant holds; the decision reversal itself user-confirmed at the wrap escalation (2026-06-27). **Section:** §Security Anti-Patterns → Input (+ its restatement in → Code Patterns)
**Change:** Re-worded the sidecar-spawn ban from "a fixed, hard-coded program path only" to "a fixed, hard-coded program NAME resolved through the inherited `PATH` (never a config-derived or operator-supplied command string)", and named `PATH` as a spawn-resolution input — the environment selects WHICH binary the fixed name resolves to. **Why:** `crates/conductor-verify/src/spawn.rs` pins `PULSE_MCP_PROGRAM = "andromeda-pulse-mcp"` — a program NAME whose own doc comment says "resolved from `PATH`" — so the ban's wording overstated the control while its INTENT (never operator-chosen; a compile-time constant) held and is preserved. **Why:** Unlike the 2026-06-23 dismissals under playbook rule @58, this chunk genuinely ADDS an external-input boundary and a spawn, so that rule's precondition was unmet and the escalate-severity detectors fired correctly. Both ban qualifications were escalated and operator-ratified at this wrap: left unqualified, the plan would forbid a leg the harness now ships, so a reader checking a green chunk would read a violation that is not one. body:
## 2026-09-04-sidecar-spawn-without-a-console-window — the console-suppression duty stops being owed and starts being held
**Section:** §Security Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns rule (a) — console-window clause (primary) · rule (a) — `sidecar_resolves_on_path` sibling clause · §Input Validation — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` SPAWN-propagation row · §Threat Model Summary — MCP read-back child-process stdout vector
**Change:** (1) Rule (a)'s console clause is retired from "recorded as a routed product defect, not yet shipped" to SHIPPED and live-verified — `build_command` applies `.creation_flags(console_suppressing_flags())` under `#[cfg(windows)]`, held by a `#[cfg(windows)]` unit test — with the 2026-09-02 pane measurement kept as the dated history that motivated the duty, explicitly marked SUPERSEDED. (2) The `sidecar_resolves_on_path` sibling clause stops arguing from "constructs no `Command`, therefore opens no console window and adds no absolute-exe-path disclosure channel of the class named below" — a contrast the shipped fix dissolves — and states its remaining distinct property instead (a boolean-grade directory walk whose resolved path is never returned, logged, rendered, or used as a spawn program). (3)+(4) Both restatements of the retired `TokioChildProcess` spawn mechanism are corrected to `spawn::build_command` / `tokio::process::Command`; every substantive control (fixed program NAME through the inherited `PATH`, `.env(...)`-only data dir, injection-metacharacter reject, nothing operator-supplied in argv, no shell in the vector) is preserved verbatim and unchanged.
**Why:** This plan's own body named the fix as route-owned and not shipped; the chunk discharged it. As measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-sidecar-spawn-without-a-console-window/evidence/nvda-pass.json`: SR row S1-01's `heard` lost `<host-path>`, `<host-path> terminal blank` and `pane`, with 0 `security_finding` rows and 0 `<host-path>` placeholders where the prior record carried both, and 0 host paths inside any `Speaking [...]` line of the raw speech log. Validated ROUTINE under playbook `:134` ("a chunk SHIPS the fix that a spec master's own body already names as route-owned-not-shipped … including at escalate severity"), whose mandatory precedence check was performed: rule `:124` (Boundary widening, never-routine) does NOT match — the flag SUPPRESSES a window and admits nothing new across the boundary; the change narrows a disclosure channel rather than widening a crossing. The applied flag's unit-tier unassertability (`std::process::Command` has no creation-flags getter) is recorded in the body rather than left implicit, so a later reader does not mistake the missing unit assertion for missing coverage. **Search performed:** grep of security-plan.md for `not yet shipped`, `route-owned`, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, `console window`, `pane`, `spawn.rs:80`, `TokioChildProcess`, plus rule (a) read in full for the mechanism however worded — 4 sites carried it, all 4 amended. Post-edit re-grep: `recorded as a routed product defect, not yet shipped` = 0, `therefore opens no console window` = 0, `TokioChildProcess` = 1 (the historical "were removed 2026-06-27" note this amendment authored, not a live claim). Cross-master sweep for the same retired claims is recorded in the architecture and obs-plan sidecars. **One further site corrected in the same pass (§Input Validation — screen-reader speech-log ingest row):** the ingest parser was cited at the repo-root-relative `test/a11y/screen-reader/parse-nvda-log.ts`, which resolves to nothing; the file is at `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/test/a11y/screen-reader/parse-nvda-log.ts` (verified on disk). Same defect class as the a11y-plan pass-spec path corrected this wrap — a sibling file under the same non-resolving prefix — found by the cascade's closure sweep rather than by a detector, and fixed here so a single-site apply does not leave the duplicate standing. Post-edit: `grep -rn 'test/a11y/screen-reader'` across the seven masters returns only `crates/…`-prefixed paths (excluding sidecar entries, which quote the old form to explain the correction).

## 2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite — the leading preconditions probe now covers two harness paths

**Change:** Both sites state the path SET `{boot, run --live}` rather than `boot` alone: the leading `conductor preconditions` arm short-circuits on either, minting no `ReadyState`, no `Verdict`/`ReportState` and no `blocked` row, and on `run --live` the short-circuit is a REFUSAL at exit 1 naming each unsatisfied subject with no leg fired — so the sidecar is never spawned rather than the run degrading to a ~0s `[BLOCKED]` row. The `PATH`-miss sentence likewise names the SET and the `sidecar-resolvable` subject. The probe's own properties (non-mutating, client-only `:4317` connect, no spawn, no env write, fires no canary) are unchanged.
**Why:** `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite` added a second harness path that runs the same probe as its leading arm (report §Harness / gate surface); measured on the refusal arm — exit 1 with `sidecar-resolvable` and `handles-declared` both named, 0 host paths, no capture dir created (report §Outcome). Routine under playbook.md:28 (spec wording reconciled to the shipped implementation): the invariant is unchanged, only the set of paths realising it grew. **Escalation resolved, not applied — the three OTHER security proposals this pass raised are withdrawn at the source.** The detector correctly found the harness's first recursive delete (`rm -rf "$RUNS_DIR/live-suite"`, a path derived from an operator-supplied `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` with no canonicalize, no `--`, no non-empty assertion, and executing BEFORE any Rust-side `resolve_under` rejection) and proposed recording it as a documented residual plus widening two bans to accommodate it. Escalated to the operator per the never-routine security-boundary rule; the operator chose to FIX THE CODE instead. Both shells now clear the capture dir with the file's own non-recursive `cleanup` idiom (`rm -f …/*.jsonl` · `Remove-Item '…/*.jsonl'`), the harness ships NO recursive delete, and the two ban-widening amendments have no subject. §Input Validation, §Anti-Patterns → Input's canonicalize-duty scope and §Anti-Patterns → Code Patterns clause (b)'s "In every form" universal are therefore all UNCHANGED — no security ban was weakened this pass.

**Section:** Input Validation (env-var path handles row, CLI arguments row) + Threat Model Summary (Vector: CLI input) + Bootstrap phases (input-validation-library-install) + Security Anti-Patterns - Input (canonicalize taxonomy) + Security Anti-Patterns - Code Patterns (child-spawn rule (b))

## 2026-09-07-a11y-ci-gate — `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT` registered as a FOURTH handle class
**Section:** §Input Validation (boundary table) · §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface → Vector: CLI input · §Secret Management → Storage → Development
**Change:** Added the `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT` boundary row and widened the two namespace-wide enumerations from three dev-harness shapes to four. The row records why its control model is NEITHER shipped shape: it is FLAG-valued, not path-valued, so the `std::fs::canonicalize` rule has nothing to canonicalize and the wdio-edge `isFile` + shell-metacharacter guard has nothing to guard; the only test is affirmative truthiness mirroring `conductor_core::flag_declared`; the value never becomes a path, argv element, spawn program or log value. Its sole effect is to INVERT what an already-unresolved host-tool handle costs — lax keeps the skip at exit 0, strict exits non-zero — and the existing guards are byte-unchanged, an ADDED arm rather than a relaxation. Mandated coverage recorded as the e2e tier's two measured arms.
**Why:** ESCALATED at this wrap because NO playbook rule governs the class. Rule `:115` (host-tool handle) requires a PATH-valued handle read SOLELY by `wdio.conf.ts`, behind the `isFile`/metacharacter guard, used in an array-form spawn — all four false. Rule `:121` (harness-owned constant) requires the handle be SET by `wdio.conf.ts` and READ by a `conductor-run` test binary — both false; that rule's own note warns against stretching `:115` for a class failing its clauses. The operator ratified it as a fourth class, mirroring how `CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` was ratified as the third on 2026-09-02, and a playbook rule was minted. `:210` and `:314` were deliberately NOT widened: both enumerate PATH handles, and a flag handle is outside their subject. (2) §Dependency Security gains a THIRD dependency class beside the Rust crate graph and the npm tree: a CI-time-fetched third-party binary that appears in NO lockfile and that `cargo audit` / `cargo deny` / `npm audit` are structurally blind to, because they scan committed manifests and this dependency is acquired at job time. **Why:** D-security-subprocess (1) + D-security-deps (3, two `dependent-of`), all `escalate`, all routed to `playbook.md:124` and operator-ratified at this wrap — the precedent is exact: the 4 → 5 widening at `2026-09-06-run-report-envelope-conformance-gate` was ratified with NO routine rule minted, so a sixth crossing escalates again, and this one did. The `≥ 152` floor is retired as falsified on its own terms — not necessary (a coherent 131/131 pair runs the arm green), not sufficient (a coherent 152/152 pair fails, run `34654076633`), destructive on the working configuration (run `35185153012`). The float's stated EXIT CONDITION is rewritten because the mechanism it named does not exist: the Standalone Installer installs Evergreen and takes no version argument, and Fixed Version cannot supply 131; the float retires instead by pinning the DRIVER to the runtime. §Networking re-registers the sole non-loopback egress as the unconditional but version-derived `msedgedriver.microsoft.com` fetch (count one before, one after), and §CI/CD records that the fetching step verifies and stops while the LEG executes the fetched binary. The `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` row's producer sentence is corrected: `EDGEWEBDRIVER` is now written by the pin gate through `GITHUB_ENV`, not read from the runner image; the `Test-Path` precondition and `wdio.conf.ts`'s sole-reader `isFile` + metacharacter guard stay byte-unchanged. **Spawn rule (b), both ESCALATED and operator-resolved 2026-09-17:** the SIXTH form is RETIRED with its step and its ordinal is not reused, but its distinguishing property — a governed form whose PROGRAM arrives from the network at job time — TRANSFERS to the dev-only driver-stack spawn, because the binary at `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` is now the fetched driver; the SEVENTH form is RETAINED with its SCOPE corrected to the job's driver-alone diagnostic steps (four `ci.yml` call sites, down from five), never the asserting step, which invokes the leg's entry point directly at native High integrity. A clarifying clause was added where coherence is introduced, distinguishing it from the separately-retired skew cause.

**Why:** Report `Spec claims disproved by measurement` 1, 2 and 4, and the `Dependencies` / `Symbols — Ports/egress` / `Harness / gate surface` bullets. Rule (b)'s class escalates rather than going routine however often it recurs, so both forms were put to the operator rather than applied as drift. Both resolutions were ratified 2026-09-17 with their reasons recorded: a registry silent about a spawn a committed workflow still performs fails in the same way as one describing a spawn it no longer performs (the seventh), and retiring the network-program property outright would orphan the Authenticode control's stated justification while the job still executes a network-fetched binary (the sixth). The egress ratification rests on a measured NET NARROWING — the fwlink carried no version selector, this URL's version derives from the image — re-derived independently at this wrap: `ci.yml` contains exactly two network calls, the driver fetch and `127.0.0.1:9515`, the latter loopback.
