title: Security Decisions Log
body:
## Security Decisions Log

_Records key decisions during plan generation + manual additions between phase loops._

**Initial entry:**

`2026-06-14` — Initial security plan generated by `/andromeda-security`
- **Tier:** Minimal (0) — justified by: single-developer, local-only, no-cloud, no-multi-tenancy tool with no user accounts (auth "none"), no PII/payment/health/credentials owned by Conductor (only self-generated synthetic test telemetry + run-metadata in `runs.db`/JSONL), zero network exposure (loopback gRPC/MCP client, no inbound listener), and no compliance triggers. Residual risk classes are exactly Minimal-tier: dependency/supply-chain audit (`bundled` SQLite from C + OTLP/gRPC/MCP tree), input validation on operator-supplied scenario config and `CONDUCTOR_*` path handles, and error sanitization at the `anyhow` edges + run-report artifacts.
- **Key decision:** Subprocess-spawn hardening for the MCP stdio sidecar child is the single most architecture-relevant control (security-research.md MCP-sidecar STDIO command/argument-injection finding, CVE-2026-30623): spawn `andromeda-pulse-mcp` as a fixed hard-coded program path, pass `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` strictly via `.env(...)`, never interpolate operator input into argv/shell, and reject argument-injection metacharacters before spawn. Paired with `cargo-audit` 0.22.2 (+ recommended `cargo-deny` 0.19.8) in CI as the supply-chain control, and two required dependency bumps: toolchain ≥ 1.94.1 (tar-rs symlink-chmod CVE-2026-33056) and `tauri` ≥ 2.10.3 (origin-confusion CVE-2026-42184).
- **Open questions:** (1) Whether the optional `conductor-tauri` GUI will use any Tauri plugin beyond the IPC commands + `Channel` — if the `shell-open` plugin is ever added it MUST be explicitly scoped (CVE-2025-31477); flagged so a downstream Tauri scope can decide. (2) `cargo-deny` adoption (over `cargo-audit` alone) is recommended-not-required for a single-developer tool — left to setup-project / operator preference; `cargo-audit` is the firm minimum bar. (3) No secret-scanning tool was researched in Phase 2 — secret scanning was not a researched category because Conductor owns no secrets (Threat Model Summary § Data classification: credential "none"). The optional defense-in-depth secret-scanning CI gate (Secret Management + Bootstrap phases) therefore names no specific tool; no maintained option was researched for this category, so selection is deferred to setup-project / operator. Revisit only if Conductor ever acquires secret material (it has none today).

**Subsequent entry format (for manual additions or re-runs):**

`{YYYY-MM-DD}` — {short title of decision}
- **Decision:** {what was decided}
- **Rationale:** {why — reference threat model / research / org constraint}
- **Impact:** {which sections affected; downstream skills affected}
- **By:** {`/andromeda-security` re-run / manual edit by {who}}

(Append new entries at the bottom; do not modify historical entries.)

`2026-09-24` — Secret-scanning tool selected: an in-repo Rust static gate (closes Initial entry open question 3)
- **Decision:** the secret-scanning CI gate is `crates/conductor-core/tests/secret_scan_gate.rs` — a `conductor-core` test target using `regex` (a dev-dependency edge, already locked; no new package) — run by the `rust` job's presence-guarded `Secret-scan gate` step and locally by `agent-run run`'s workspace nextest. Its subject is git's cached + untracked-not-ignored listing; its allowlist is an exact set, EMPTY at selection (0 hits over the tracked tree, with every rule firing on a runtime-built sample).
- **Rationale:** a job-time-fetched scanner (a marketplace action or a downloaded binary, gitleaks being the one considered) would have been a second member of the third dependency class (§Dependency Security) and a second CI non-loopback egress — a boundary widening. The in-repo gate adds neither, and it carries in-suite negative arms proving it can fail. Its trade-off is recorded: a small rule set Conductor maintains itself, with no entropy scoring.
- **Impact:** §Bootstrap phases `secret-scanning-ci-gate` and §Secret Management "Secret scanning in CI" now describe a realized gate; §Threat Model Summary CI/CD lists it; §Security Anti-Patterns → Secrets names the gate as enforcing. No egress, spawn-form or dependency-class count moves.
- **By:** manual edit by the operator's P4 selection (`2026-09-24-secret-scanning-ci-gate`), recorded at that chunk's wrap.

title: design-system
Design System — Conductor

body: **Conductor has no interface.** Its window — the `desktop-webview` surface — was retired 2026-10-11 (`2026-10-11-conductors-window-retired`, intent R1); the cli surface below is all it renders.

title: Brand Identity

body: **Personality:** Mission-control patience — armed, nominal, go/no-go: a single-operator console that stays calm and resolute under load, terse status callouts with no alarm in the tone even when a verdict comes back Fail.

**Domain anchors:** Mission-control console (single-station, not a war-room dashboard) · Count / heartbeat (the run's single live mono tick) · Operator-pause / go-no-go hold (the staged "hold before you commit the next timeline step") · Verdict / report states (`Verdict: Pass / Fail / CalibrationRegion`; the 5-valued `ReportState: Pass / Fail / ManualCheck / KnownResidual / Blocked`) · Coverage matrix (the dense single-row-per-P-ID wall over the manifest's accepted capability set).

**Signature element:** The **Paused-count hold-point** — the frozen heartbeat at the operator-pause. A single prominent mono count (run-elapsed / step index) ticks in place at the top of the console tinted nominal-green; when an operator-pause go/no-go prompt fires before a committed timeline step, the count does NOT blank and does NOT keep running — it **freezes at the exact hold value**, the phase line beside it flips to "HOLD — operator pause", and the count tints green → hold-amber for the duration of the hold. On proceed it resumes from the frozen value; on abort it stops and dims to blocked slate-violet. **The absence of motion is the signature** — "paused count shows where it stopped" (NASA Open MCT). The verdict lamp (in-place per-P-ID status light) is retained as a *supporting* status convention, not the signature.
**Expression level:** `0.3` — governs animation intensity, layout freedom, and interaction complexity across the entire project.
- `0.0-0.2`: static, grid-locked, zero animation, dense
- `0.3-0.4`: subtle hover states, fade transitions, quiet focus rings
- `0.5-0.6`: smooth transitions, micro-interactions, loading skeletons
- `0.7-0.8`: staggered entrances, parallax, spring physics
- `0.9-1.0`: scroll-driven, 3D, particles, canvas/WebGL

This number is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how much motion and visual dynamism downstream phases should implement. At `0.3`, Conductor gets honest progress feedback only — never `framer-motion`, spring physics, parallax, or staggered reveals. Per-surface expression: cli `0.3`.

**Design direction:**
The cool, blue-cast calm of a single-operator mission-control console watching one live instrument: a near-black Tokyo-Night slate ground (`#1A1B26`) where the only color is functional status — a green / amber / red / slate-violet tier that reads as *Verdict / ReportState*, never as mood. Elevation is flat inset-border seams (`#2A2E42`) with zero drop shadows — Linear's "instrument-panel density" rather than a Grafana tile wall, the Coverage matrix a dense single-row-per-P-ID list. Color, motion, and a reserved mono ID-cyan typographic tier all carry operational meaning; the held silence of the frozen count is the loudest thing on screen. "A control surface, not a dashboard" — terminal density, dark-default, calm under load, no alarm.

title: Color Palette

body: **Rationale:** Every hex derives from the exploration's Color World — the "k9s cluster watch on a Warp terminal" cool blue-cast dev-tool world the user chose over the retro Apollo firing-room palette (Q3 override). The functional status triad (nominal green / hold amber / fail red) + blocked slate-violet is Conductor's specialization of the generic "dark syntax theme": color reads as run state, not decoration. Auto mode is mandatory — every entry carries a **dark (default)** value and a **light variant** (the off-white console under room light) carried verbatim from the Color World's light variants. Mono ID cyan is a fourth *typographic-color* tier reserved strictly for the monospace status face (count / P-IDs / run_id / SLO timings / fingerprints), never used as a generic brand accent.

title: Core Colors

body: | Role | Value (dark default) | Light variant | Usage | Domain anchor |

| Primary | `#7DCFFF` (mono ID cyan) | `#0969DA` | Focus rings, active control highlight, the reserved mono status-tier color (count / P-IDs / run_id / SLO timings / fingerprints) | Linear's "monospace-as-a-typographic-tier" made a color — the Coverage matrix + Fingerprint identity; "blue focus" mapped to the ID-cyan tier (industry-rules) |

| Secondary | `#A9B1D6` (journal line-text) | `#343B58` | UI prose, phase-line label text, run-report body rows, dimmed metadata | The Tokyo-Night foreground grey-lavender — the readable-but-recessive Emission journal / Run report artifact text tier |

| Accent | `#7EE787` (nominal green) | `#1A7F37` | The count/heartbeat tint while on-timeline, the `Pass` verdict lamp | The k9s "healthy" status tier — Count / heartbeat alive + Verdict `Pass`; accent-as-status, never accent-as-brand |

title: Surface Scale (elevation hierarchy)

body: | Level | Value (dark default) | Light variant | Usage |
| Base | `#1A1B26` | `#F4F5F8` | Console app background + frameless titlebar ground (the Mission-control console surface) |
| Raised-1 | `#1F2130` | `#FFFFFF` | Phase-line / count panel, run-report card, coverage-matrix container (+lightness over base, NO shadow) |
| Raised-2 | `#24273A` | `#FBFBFD` | Picker dropdown, popover, tooltip (flat, border-defined) |
| Raised-3 | `#2A2D42` | `#FFFFFF` | Operator-pause go/no-go dialog, modal surface |
| Inset | `#15161F` | `#E9EBF2` | Scenario/seed input fields, the JSONL journal code block (darker than parent) |

title: Text Hierarchy

body: | Level | Value (dark default) | Light variant | Usage |
| Primary | `#C8D0F0` | `#1A1B26` | Phase-line headline, primary labels (lifted from journal-grey for headline contrast) |
| Secondary | `#A9B1D6` | `#343B58` | Run-report body, descriptions, supporting prose (journal line-text) |

| Tertiary | `#838EBA` | `#565F89` | Metadata, `journal_emitted_at` timestamps, captions. Dark lifted from `#717AA0` so it clears 4.5:1 on every surface it renders on — `--color-raised-2` (coverage thead) and `--color-raised-1` (rows), not only `--color-base` (as measured 2026-09-01: one axe `color-contrast` violation, 18 nodes, all this token) |

| Muted | `#727EB5` | `#636882` | Disabled labels, placeholders, dimmed-on-abort text. Both themes moved to clear 4.5:1 against `--color-inset`, in OPPOSITE directions (dark lifted from `#565F89`, light darkened from `#6E7491`); it is its own recessive text tier and no longer shares a hex with `--count-blocked` |

title: Semantic Colors

body: | State | Background (dark) | Border (dark) | Text (dark) | Light text |
| Success (`Pass` / on-timeline) | `#142A1C` | `#2E5A3C` | `#7EE787` | `#1A7F37` |
| Warning (`CalibrationRegion` / HOLD) | `#332B14` | `#5C4E22` | `#E3B341` | `#9A6700` |
| Error (`Fail` / port-occupier alarm edge) | `#33191A` | `#5C2E2E` | `#F85149` | `#CF222E` |
| Info / Blocked (`ReportState::Blocked` — never measured) | `#21243A` | `#3A4066` | `#565F89` | `#6E7491` |
| Manual (`ReportState::ManualCheck` — awaiting operator) | `#1E2233` | `#3A4160` | `#A9B1D6` | `#565F89` |
| Residual (`ReportState::KnownResidual` — pre-accepted gap) | `#26242E` | `#4A4458` (rendered dashed) | `#9A93A8` | `#6E6478` |

> **Verdict (3) vs ReportState (5) — a report row carries BOTH (per arch's run-report envelope).** The functional **machine-verdict** triad maps green = `Verdict::Pass`, amber = `Verdict::CalibrationRegion` (model-interpretive, report-for-human) / operator-pause HOLD, red = `Verdict::Fail` (held muted, no flashing). The **ReportState** adds three outcomes the machine did NOT pass/fail and which therefore must never collapse into `Fail`: slate-violet **hollow ring** = `ReportState::Blocked` (present-but-greyed — *never measured*); neutral-lavender **checkbox glyph** = `ReportState::ManualCheck` (*no programmatic read-back — awaiting the operator's eyes*; deliberately OUTSIDE the green/amber/red triad because there is no machine verdict — it renders as an operator-checklist); muted **dashed** dot = `ReportState::KnownResidual` (a *measured but pre-accepted* spec-vs-runtime gap — P-032 the first instance — carrying "expected until {named fix}", visually NOT red). Fail red is the reserved alarm edge held muted per "calm under load, no alarm"; `ManualCheck` and `KnownResidual` are distinct treatments precisely so neither silently reads as `Fail` (the same "no surprise failure" discipline already applied to `Blocked`).

title: Border Progression

body: | Intensity | Value (dark default) | Light variant | Usage |
| Subtle | `#2A2E42` (inset-border line) | `#D8DBE6` | Section separators, phase-line/count/coverage-matrix-row seams (the flat inset-border elevation — NO drop shadow) |
| Standard | `#363B57` | `#C4C8D8` | Input borders, P-ID list dividers |
| Emphasis | `#565F89` | `#9AA0BE` | Selected coverage-matrix row, active picker item |
| Focus | `#7DCFFF` (mono ID cyan) | `#0969DA` | Focus rings — accessibility-critical, the same ID-cyan as the mono tier so focus reads as "the operator's cursor on the instrument" |

title: Typography

body: Retired 2026-10-11 with the window (its faces, type scale and font loading are last at `321dc8f`). The cli sets no face: the terminal's own monospace carries all output, brand expressed through ANSI color, the ASCII prefixes and header weight (§Surface: cli).

title: Spacing

body: Retired 2026-10-11 with the window (the 4px spacing scale is last at `321dc8f`). For cli, spacing is never hardcoded — `comfy-table` column alignment (the results and coverage tables sized to their content and never wrapped; the `conductor scenarios` catalogue listing the one table sized to the detected terminal width) and `indicatif` layout.

title: Depth Strategy

body: Retired 2026-10-11 with the window (borders-only elevation is last at `321dc8f`); the cli has no depth.

title: Border Radius

body: Retired 2026-10-11 with the window (the radius tokens are last at `321dc8f`); the cli has none — terminal-controlled.

title: Motion (calibrated to expression level `0.3`)

body: Retired 2026-10-11 with the window (the CSS motion tokens and transitions are last at `321dc8f`). The cli's motion is honest progress only: the `indicatif` spinner appears after ~200ms and STOPS in place, never hides, at an operator hold; no pulse, blink or flashing on any status.

title: Iconography

body: Retired 2026-10-11 with the window (its icon library and SVG lamp glyphs are last at `321dc8f`); the cli's status glyphs are its ASCII prefixes and `✓`/`✗`/`?`/`~`/`•`/`→` (§Surface: cli).

title: Surface: desktop-webview

body: Retired 2026-10-11 (`2026-10-11-conductors-window-retired`, intent R1): Conductor has no window. This surface's tokens, components, navigation and platform notes are last at `321dc8f`.

title: Surface: cli

body: **Platform:** Windows / macOS / Linux terminal — headless `conductor-cli` (`scripts/agent-run.sh`), the source of truth + release gate. Line-oriented (ratatui full-TUI deliberately omitted).

**Toolkit / Framework:** clap 4.5 + `owo-colors` 4.x with `std::io::IsTerminal` (styling, TTY-gated per stream) + `indicatif` 0.18 (live counters / spinner) + `comfy-table` 7 (P-ID SLO tables) + `inquire` 0.9 (operator-pause prompts).

title: Tokens (platform-specific)

body: ANSI 256-color codes mapping the Color World (per the library-shortlist mapping), applied via `owo-colors` behind a `std::io::IsTerminal` check — decided independently for stdout and stderr, each requiring a terminal AND `NO_COLOR` unset AND `TERM != dumb`, so output carries no ANSI when piped:

```
Slate ground   #1A1B26  → ANSI 234/235  (backdrop; rarely set — terminal-owned)
Nominal green  #7EE787  → ANSI 114      (Pass / on-timeline heartbeat)
Hold amber     #E3B341  → ANSI 179      (HOLD / CalibrationRegion)
Fail red       #F85149  → ANSI 203      (Fail — no blink)
Blocked violet #565F89  → ANSI 60       (Blocked — never measured)
Manual lavender#A9B1D6  → ANSI 146      (ManualCheck — awaiting operator; paired with [MANUAL] + ? glyph)
Residual mute  #9A93A8  → ANSI 246      (KnownResidual — pre-accepted gap; paired with [RESIDUAL] + ~ glyph)
                                        ALSO the shared recessive tier for every NON-lamp use — currently
                                        the `hint:` stderr label (Component Pattern 5), the coverage-matrix
                                        out-of-scope Mode cell (`not-conductors`), and the run-level
                                        `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` load-envelope caption and the
                                        `[PRECONDITION]` scheduling caption. None is a lamp
                                        state: the always-rendered text label carries the signal, the tint
                                        only de-emphasizes. Markdown, having no color channel, uses
                                        emphasis (`_not-conductors_`) or the bracket label in a blockquote
                                        as the surface-adapted counterpart.
Mono ID cyan   #7DCFFF  → ANSI 117      (P-IDs / run_id / SLO timings / fingerprints)
Journal text   #A9B1D6  → ANSI 146      (report rows / dimmed metadata)
```

Header style: bold + ANSI 117 (ID-cyan) for section titles; metadata dimmed. Status prefixes are ASCII text + color (never color alone) — the closed per-P-ID set `[PASS]` / `[HOLD]` / `[FAIL]` / `[MANUAL]` / `[RESIDUAL]` / `[BLOCKED]`, plus the run-level non-lamp caption SET — `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` (load-envelope) and `[PRECONDITION]` (the `conductor preconditions` probe), both ANSI 246 and both outside the lamp column, neither a lamp state nor a `ReportState` and `✓`/`✗`/`?`/`~`/`•`/`→` (TTY only — never emoji in machine-parseable piped output; `?` = `ManualCheck` awaiting operator, `~` = `KnownResidual` pre-accepted gap).

title: Component Patterns

body: 1. **Paused-count hold-point (signature, CLI mirror — primary placement).** During a run, an `indicatif` progress/spinner carries the count/heartbeat with a colored phase-line prefix (ANSI 114 green). On the operator-pause go/no-go, the spinner **STOPS in place (not hides)** at the exact value, and a bold ANSI 179 amber `HOLD — operator pause` phase line prints **above** the `inquire` prompt. Spinner appears only after ~200ms (honest progress, not instant churn). The stop — not a hide, not an animate-to-100% — is the signature; it embodies "paused count shows where it stopped." TTY-gated so agent-captured artifacts stay clean.

2. **Operator-pause prompt.** `inquire` proceed/abort confirm, gated behind an `isatty` check. **The headless path is NEVER blocked on an interactive prompt** — when stdin is not a TTY (agent-driven `agent-run.sh`), the prompt is skipped per the configured non-interactive policy and the decision is recorded to the artifact; an interactive operator gets the colored confirm. Proceed/abort decision logged to the run report.

3. **Results / SLO table** (the `run` + `suite` per-check table). `comfy-table` 6 columns: P-ID (ANSI 117 cyan) · scenario · `state` (`[PASS]`/`[HOLD]`/`[FAIL]`/`[BLOCKED]` colored prefix) · `slo_tier` (`<5s`/`<20s`/`<90s`) · `latency_ms` (cyan, right-aligned) · fingerprints. Columns sized to their content — never wrapped, never hardcoded, no terminal-width detection. A `Blocked` row carries the named precondition string; measurement columns render as `—`/null, never a red error. **The coverage matrix is a SEPARATE, narrower table** — `conductor coverage` renders 4 columns (P-ID · Title · Category · Mode) sized to their content, carries no verdict/state column and therefore no bracket prefix, and terminates in a roll-up caption (§cli Primary screens). **The scenario catalogue is a THIRD, static table** — `conductor scenarios` renders 3 columns (Scenario · P-IDs in ANSI 117 cyan behind the stdout TTY gate · SLO), carries no verdict/state column and therefore no bracket prefix, is the one table sized to the detected terminal width, and ends in a plain roll-up line (`1 scenario` / `N scenarios`, counted from the catalogue); an empty catalogue prints `No scenarios found.` (§cli Primary screens).

4. **Verdict / report-state lines.** Per-P-ID result printed in place: `✓ P-009  Pass   1840ms <slo_tier>` (green; the tier cell renders the scenario's declared `slo_tier` from the closed `<5s`/`<20s`/`<90s` set — never a baked per-scenario literal) / `✗ P-014  Fail   …` (ANSI 203 red, no blink) / `? P-035  Manual  halo→burgundy? · no OS toast?` (ANSI 146 lavender — `[MANUAL]`, an operator-checklist item with no machine verdict; TTY: `inquire` y/n, headless: recorded unconfirmed) / `~ P-032  Residual  recent_commits stub → v0.3.0` (ANSI 246 muted — `[RESIDUAL]`, a pre-accepted gap, never red) / `• P-022  Blocked  mcp-server feature + ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED + matching data-dir` (ANSI 60 violet). Color is always paired with the text prefix (`[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[MANUAL]`/`[RESIDUAL]`/`[BLOCKED]`/…) for NO_COLOR + screen-reader friendliness. A run whose profile breaches the SUT load envelope additionally prints the run-level `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` caption once, above these lines — a qualifier on the run, never a seventh lamp or a sixth `ReportState`.

5. **Error output.** To stderr, sanitized (no absolute host paths / internal struct names / stack traces per security plan): `error: <short>` + contextual detail + `hint: <fix>`. The `error:` label reuses Fail red (ANSI 203), `hint:` the Residual mute (ANSI 246) — tty-gated on stderr (its own `IsTerminal` gate, distinct from the stdout gate), never new colors. Never colorized when piped; the ASCII `error:`/`hint:` labels always stand (never color-alone); stack traces only under `--debug`/`-v`.

title: Navigation Pattern

body: Linear, top-to-bottom stdout — no cursor manipulation, no full-screen redraw (ratatui omitted). The operator runs `conductor-cli` / `agent-run.sh`, reads colored headers → live `indicatif` heartbeat → `inquire` operator-pause holds (interactive TTY only) → `comfy-table` coverage/SLO summary → run-report path. Pipe-friendly: raw artifact data parseable, human messages colored on stderr, the headless agent path strips ANSI and never blocks.

title: Platform-Specific Notes

body: - Always respect `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, and piped-stdout ANSI stripping (the shipped per-stream `std::io::IsTerminal` gate). Avoid dark-blue-on-black / dark-red-on-black (ANSI 117 cyan + 114 green chosen for contrast on dark terminals).
- Don't rely on color alone — every status carries an ASCII prefix (`[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[HOLD]`/`[BLOCKED]`).

- Interactive `inquire` prompts ALWAYS check `isatty` first; the agent-driven headless source-of-truth path is never gated on a prompt (an auth/interactive prompt there would silently break the release gate — security plan).

- Size `comfy-table` columns from their content (the results and coverage tables) or from the detected terminal width (the `conductor scenarios` listing alone); never hardcode widths or wrap at arbitrary points.

title: Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)
Universal Bans

body: - NEVER use purple-gradient-on-white as a color scheme — Conductor's ground is cool Tokyo-Night slate `#1A1B26`; the indigo/violet "AI gradient" is an explicit Rejected Default.
- NEVER use cookie-cutter card grids without adapting card internals to content — the Coverage matrix is a dense single-row-per-P-ID list, not a tile wall.
- NEVER use the same layout for different information types — the heartbeat/phase-line, coverage matrix (dense list), and run-report each get purpose-built layout.
- NEVER use color purely for decoration — every color communicates Verdict / ReportState (green=Pass, amber=HOLD/CalibrationRegion, red=Fail, slate-violet=Blocked, ID-cyan=mono status tier).
- NEVER converge on common "safe" choices across generations — anchor to THIS domain (mission-control console, frozen heartbeat).

- NEVER give a credential a styled surface (a password / token / key field, a masked-secret chip, a "copy key" affordance) on either surface — Conductor owns no credentials, so no cli output renders, masks or styles one.

title: Rejected Defaults (from exploration)

body: - **A "dashboard" grid of KPI metric cards with big-number tiles + trend sparklines** — rejected because: every OTLP/telemetry tool in training data is a Grafana/Datadog tile wall; Conductor is a single-station Mission-control console ("a control surface, not a dashboard") — one heartbeat + phase line in the titlebar, the Coverage matrix as a dense single-row-per-P-ID list.

- **A flashing / pulsing red banner or animated alert toast on a Fail verdict** — rejected because: alarm = red + motion is the universal reflex, but the personality is "calm under load, no alarm"; Fail is an in-place, motionless `#F85149` verdict lamp on the P-ID row. Conductor must NOT emit native OS toasts (those are Pulse behavior it observes).

- **A determinate progress bar that hides or animates-to-100% during the operator-pause** — rejected because: the signature is the *frozen* heartbeat — the count freezes at the exact hold value and tints amber (CLI: `indicatif` stops-not-hides), embodying "paused count shows where it stopped." Hiding/animating destroys the signature.

- **Indigo/violet "AI gradient" accent + glassmorphism cards** — rejected because: it is the current statistical-average "smart tooling" aesthetic; Conductor uses the cool slate ground with a strict green/amber/red functional status tier and flat inset-border elevation (`#2A2E42`), color-as-state not mood.

- **Conflating "no result yet" with "failed" (graying both the same, or showing Blocked as a red error)** — rejected because: empty-state and error-state are usually collapsed; `Blocked` is a distinct slate-violet (`#565F89`) state carrying the named precondition string — present-but-greyed, *never measured*, never a silent downgrade to red Fail.

- **A monospace font used everywhere for "techy dev-tool vibes"** — rejected because: mono-everything is lazy shorthand; mono is reserved strictly as a status tier (ID cyan `#7DCFFF`) for the count, P-IDs, run_id, SLO timings, fingerprints — UI sans (IBM Plex Sans) for phase line + prose.

title: Per-Surface Bans

body: - NEVER mix stdout (data) and stderr (messages) without intention; raw artifact data on stdout, human messages on stderr.
- NEVER use emoji in machine-parseable (piped) output; ASCII prefixes only there.
- NEVER wrap text at arbitrary points or hardcode widths — size a table from its content, or from the detected terminal width where its surface says so (the `conductor scenarios` listing).
- NEVER print stack traces in normal mode — only under `--debug`/`-v`.
- NEVER use interactive `inquire` prompts without an `isatty` check; NEVER block the headless agent-driven source-of-truth path on a prompt.
- NEVER colorize without checking `NO_COLOR` / `TERM` / pipe status; NEVER rely on color alone (use `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[HOLD]`/`[BLOCKED]` prefixes).
- NEVER hide the progress spinner or animate it to 100% on the operator-pause — it must STOP in place (signature).

title: Self-Validation Protocol

body: Before presenting ANY UI output, downstream implementation phases (per project's specialist plans) must run these checks:

title: 1. Swap Test

body: Replace your typeface with Inter, your colors with Tailwind defaults, your layout with a standard sidebar+cards. If the design doesn't feel meaningfully different → you defaulted. Redo with intent.

title: 2. Squint Test

body: Blur your eyes at the interface. Can you still perceive hierarchy? Does anything jump out harshly? Good craft whispers — nothing should scream.

title: 3. Signature Test

body: Point to the signature element in your output. Can you find it in at least 3 places? If you can't locate it → it doesn't exist. Inject it.

title: 4. Token Test

body: Read your color/spacing values aloud. Do they trace back to the palette and scale above? Random hex values or magic numbers signal no system.

title: 5. Sameness Test (from Interface Design)

body: If another AI given a similar prompt would produce substantially the same output — you have failed. The interface must emerge from THIS product's domain exploration, not from statistical patterns in training data.

title: 2026-06-15-design-token-typography-bundle — §Tokens illustrative CSS `@theme` → `:root`
body:
## 2026-06-15-design-token-typography-bundle — §Tokens illustrative CSS `@theme` → `:root`
**Section:** §Surface: desktop-webview / Tokens
**Change:** the token block is declared on plain `:root` (was `@theme`), with `@import "tailwindcss"` retained for the engine; the light-mode override is `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { :root { … } }` (was a nested `@theme`). Token NAMES + VALUES unchanged (the 34-token binding contract). A Tailwind-v4 note states the reason.
**Why:** Tailwind v4 `@theme`/`@theme static` tree-shakes non-namespace tokens (only 23/34 emitted — all `--space-*`, three `--radius-*`, `--motion-micro` and `--ease-quiet` dropped) and forbids `@theme` nested inside `@media`; the shipped `tokens.css` declares all 34 on `:root` and all 34 emit (Vite's minifier preserves author custom props). The operator chose the `:root` replacement at escalation. Sets a standing `playbook.md` rule: a spec illustration reconciled to a sound implementation is routine when the report proves the invariant holds.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-06-15T22-05-00-wrap/

title: Design Decisions Log
body:
## Design Decisions Log

_Orchestrator records key decisions here. Manual additions welcome._

2026-06-14: Initial design system generated by /andromeda-design (Phase 4)
- Brand personality: Mission-control patience — armed, nominal, go/no-go (single-operator console, calm + resolute, no alarm) — user Q1 override of the recommended orchestral "Conductor's score".
- Surfaces: desktop-webview (Tauri 2 frameless, React 19 + Tailwind v4.1 design tokens on `:root` + shadcn/ui) + cli (`conductor-cli`: clap + owo-colors + indicatif + comfy-table + inquire, ANSI 256, TTY-gated, line-oriented).
- Signature: Paused-count hold-point — the frozen heartbeat at the operator-pause (the absence of motion is the signature; count freezes at the hold value, tints green→amber, resumes on proceed / dims slate-violet on abort) — user Q5 override of the recommended verdict lamp, which is retained as a supporting status convention.
- Color: cool blue-cast Tokyo-Night slate `#1A1B26` dev-tool world (user Q3 override of the retro Apollo firing-room palette) with the functional status tier (green `#7EE787` / amber `#E3B341` / red `#F85149` / blocked slate-violet `#565F89`), mono ID-cyan `#7DCFFF` status tier; Auto mode — dark default + mandatory light variant per Color World entry.
- Expression: 0.3 flat (base / desktop-webview / cli) — functional motion only, zero animation library, in-place CSS color transitions, `prefers-reduced-motion` honored.
- Key rejection: the Grafana/Datadog KPI-card-grid "dashboard" — replaced by the single-station Mission-control console (heartbeat + phase line in the frameless titlebar; Coverage matrix as a dense single-row-per-P-ID list). "A control surface, not a dashboard."
- Security: honors Minimal-tier Tauri guardrails (deny-by-default capabilities, no `shell-open` with derived strings, no remote-origin iframes, Tauri ≥ 2.10.3) and the agent-driven "never block the headless path on an interactive prompt" rule; no styled credential exposure (Conductor owns no credentials).

title: layout-templates
Layout Templates — Conductor

body: _Generated by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8. Foundation document for downstream implementation. Per-surface wireframes and component-level detail for primary sections._
_Auth UX / security-gated flows intentionally deferred — Conductor owns no credentials (local-only loopback tool); no login/credential layouts exist to template._
**Conductor has no interface.** Its window — the `desktop-webview` surface — was retired 2026-10-11 (`2026-10-11-conductors-window-retired`, intent R1); the cli surface below is all it renders.

title: Surface: desktop-webview

body: Retired 2026-10-11 (`2026-10-11-conductors-window-retired`, intent R1): Conductor has no window. This surface's screens, wireframes, components and IA notes are last at `321dc8f`.

title: Surface: cli

body: **Tooling context:** clap 4.5 (`conductor-cli` / `scripts/agent-run.sh`) + `owo-colors` 4.x with `std::io::IsTerminal` (styling, TTY-gated per stream) + `indicatif` 0.18 (live counters / spinner) + `comfy-table` 7 (P-ID SLO tables) + `inquire` 0.9 (operator-pause prompts). Line-oriented (ratatui full-TUI deliberately omitted).

**Expression level (this surface):** 0.3 — colored headers, dimmed metadata, `indicatif` honest progress (spinner appears only after ~200ms), `comfy-table` SLO tables. No cursor manipulation, no full-screen redraw, no animate-to-100%. Motion is honest progress feedback, never live-redrawn dashboard animation (per design-system Motion).
**Signature placement (Paused-count hold-point, named on ≥2 distinct components):**

1. **`indicatif` heartbeat spinner** (primary mirror) — during a run the spinner carries the count/heartbeat with a colored phase-line prefix (ANSI 114, the `count-nominal` mapping); on the operator-pause it **STOPS in place (not hides, not animate-to-100%)** at the exact value. The stop is the signature — "paused count shows where it stopped."

2. **HOLD phase line above the `inquire` prompt** — a bold amber (ANSI 179, the `count-hold` mapping) `HOLD — operator pause` line printed **above** the proceed/abort confirm, carrying the frozen count value as text so the held number is legible at the decision point, not just in the stopped spinner.

3. **Results / SLO table caption** (reinforcement) — when a run is held, the `comfy-table` summary is captioned with the frozen step-index in the hold-amber mapping, echoing where the count stopped for the agent reading the artifact.

Every status above is **paired with an ASCII text prefix** (`[PASS]` / `[HOLD]` / `[FAIL]` / `[BLOCKED]`, `✓`/`✗`/`→`/`•`) so the signal is never color-alone and survives `NO_COLOR` / piping / screen readers — this is a stated requirement; a11y / NO_COLOR compliance derives from it.

title: Primary screens (commands)

body: - **`conductor run <scenario>`** — drive one scenario: colored phase headers → live `indicatif` heartbeat → `inquire` operator-pause holds (interactive TTY only) → per-P-ID verdict lines → `comfy-table` SLO summary → run-report path.

- **`conductor suite`** — drive the full coverage suite across the manifest’s accepted set, MCP preflight readiness gate first, then the same run flow, ending in the dense coverage table. **The operator stop** (2026-10-12): after preflight, before driving, the suite takes Ctrl-C — the first prints the stop-requested line on stderr and the suite stops before its next scenario: the spinner is abandoned in place, the envelope caption and results table print over the kept records, `suite stopped: {kept} of {total} scenarios kept` prints on stderr, and the exit is 130. A second Ctrl-C exits 130 at once. A completed suite still exits on the hard-Fail rule.

- **`conductor report <run_id>`** — re-print a stored run as a colored `comfy-table` results view (reads the per-run JSONL journal; the on-disk `<run_id>.md` artifact stays Markdown), pipe-friendly. After the `Run report <id>` line and a blank line it prints the stored run's `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` load-envelope caption once when that run's stored standing is suspect (2026-10-12; no flag, no new lamp, label or column), then the unchanged six-column table.

- **`conductor preflight [--json]`** — the MCP readiness gate (no longer boot's FIRST act — the probe below leads, and short-circuits past this gate only when a subject is genuinely unmet): emits the `ReadyState` JSON (or a `[PASS]`/`[BLOCKED]` line) and exits 0 iff `ready:true`, non-zero on a Blocked precondition. **`agent-run boot` REACHES it** — the leading probe runs first and short-circuits only on a genuinely unmet subject; on exit 0 boot proceeds here and emits the `ReadyState` JSON, measured in the full shipped shell SET (`scripts/agent-run.sh` 2026-09-04T17:07:17→17:08:04Z · `scripts/agent-run.ps1` 17:11:16→17:12:03Z, both exit 0 with `ready: true`, zero `skipped preflight` lines, neither script edited; `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence/report.md`). Invoking this verb directly remains a valid entry point, not a forced workaround.

- **`conductor preconditions [--for <SCENARIO>] [--json]`** — the non-mutating live-Pulse probe run BEFORE a leg is scheduled: `:4317` reachability as a connect-and-drop client, `andromeda-pulse-mcp` resolved over the inherited `PATH` without spawning, and the three `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` handles read for an affirmative declaration under the deterministic posture — the flagless default. `--for` (2026-09-22) takes a scenario NAME — a `P-NNN`-shaped value is refused at argument parsing (a clap usage error, exit 2), because a P-ID can name several scenarios — and grades the handles under that scenario's declared `l4_posture`: under `real-model` the L4 handle is read for ABSENCE instead, its unmet line reading `declared in this environment, but the real-model posture requires it absent or falsy`. Exits 0 iff every subject is satisfied, non-zero otherwise (the documented `preflight` go/no-go exception, not the scenario-verdict rule) — and **exit 0 IS reachable**: each handle is graded by its own KIND, the PATH-valued member by presence-after-trim and the flag-valued members by an affirmative `"true"`/`"1"`, so `handles-declared` is satisfiable (as measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence/report.md`, 2026-09-04T17:07Z) — and under a `--for` real-model scenario the L4 flag is unmet when EITHER side's truthiness rule declares it (Conductor's `true`/`1` ∪ Pulse's `1`/`true`/`yes`, trimmed and ASCII-lowercased), every other handle graded as before; exit 0 was measured reachable under that posture too (2026-09-23). Both arms of the `[PRECONDITION]` caption are shipped, measured behaviour: ANSI 246, one line per unmet subject naming its statement and candidate causes when any subject is unmet, and the single satisfied line (`[PRECONDITION] every live-Pulse precondition is satisfied`) when none is — so a reader keying on the bracket label must not read it as failure-only. Mints no `Verdict`, no `ReportState` and no per-P-ID row. It fires no canary, so it primes none of the SUT state a preflight would.

- **`conductor coverage [--write]`** — render the static capability-coverage matrix over the manifest's accepted set (`coverage_matrix()` — P-ID / title / category / mode, the definition-of-done classification) as a **4-column** `comfy-table` (P-ID · Title · Category · Mode — no verdict/state column, so no bracket prefix; distinct from the 6-column results/SLO table below); `--write` regenerates `coverage-matrix.md` at the repo root. The table terminates in a **roll-up caption** naming the in-scope denominator beside the full row count — `82 capabilities · 66 in scope (43 auto (N unbacked) · 16 drive+observe · 7 static-only) · 16 not-conductors` — every number manifest-derived (never a literal), the per-mode counts still summing to the row count. The `(N unbacked)` parenthetical **qualifies the auto term only** — `Auto`-classified capabilities no scenario yet names (`conductor_core::UNBACKED_AUTO`, held to the catalog by `check_scenario_backing`). It is a qualifier, **never a fifth summand**: those rows are still classified auto, so counting them separately would break the sum. Plain text, no new token / ANSI / colour, and it is omitted entirely when the count is zero. Rendered identically on both surfaces (the Markdown artifact and the cli), and the out-of-scope token carrying the recessive `status-residual` ↔ ANSI 246 tint over its always-printed label. The same roll-up shape renders on both surfaces (Markdown artifact · cli).

- **`conductor scenarios`** — the scenario catalogue listing (2026-10-12): every scenario loaded through `list_scenarios` and checked against the capability manifest, rendered as a **3-column** `comfy-table` (Scenario · P-IDs · SLO — P-IDs in the ID-cyan mapping behind the stdout TTY gate; no verdict/state column, so no bracket prefix; the one table sized to the terminal width), then a plain roll-up line — `1 scenario` for one, `N scenarios` otherwise, counted from the catalogue, never a literal. An empty catalogue prints `No scenarios found.`; exit 0. An absent or malformed capability manifest is a harness fault (`error:` + `hint:`, exit 1). It takes no argument and mints no token, bracket label or ANSI entry.

- **`conductor cleanup <run_id>`** — the teardown verb (2026-09-06): removes one stored run's rows from all three `runs.db` tables in a single transaction (`RunsDb::delete_run`), printing a plain confirmation line carrying the removed row count with the run id in the ID-cyan mapping. Idempotent — a second call removes nothing and is not an error. Mints NO bracket label, no lamp, no `ReportState` and no new token or ANSI entry; it never prompts, so the headless path stays unblocked. The `run_id` binds as a SQL `?1` parameter only and is never joined into a path (unlike `report`). This is the mechanism `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} cleanup` now invokes behind its existing run-id guard — the shells issue no SQL of their own.

- **`scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`** (both shells ship at identical semantics — test-plan §3; a property of the SCRIPTS together with the invoking environment, since a caller preempting native-command exits diverges the `.ps1` leg with zero script delta — measured 2026-09-07) — the headless, agent-driven source-of-truth path (the 5-command `boot`/`run`/`status`/`cleanup`/`logs` harness; `run` takes `--unit`/`--integration`/`--live` stage flags, default = the full bundled gate). **`--live` is the operator-gated live-Pulse suite** (2026-09-06) — a sibling stage flag, never a sixth command, reachable from no default or CI path. It leads with the non-priming `conductor preconditions` probe: an unmet subject REFUSES the suite at exit 1, printing one host-path-free `[PRECONDITION]` line per unsatisfied subject with its candidate causes, and no leg fires. A third-token selector (2026-09-22) picks the other shape: **`--live real-model`** runs the ONE operator-gated real-model leg (`real-model-interpretation`) instead of the suite, leading with `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation` and refusing the same way; an unknown selector prints `usage: <script> run --live [real-model]` and exits 2 before any probe, in both shells — a selector of `--live`, neither a sixth command nor a new stage flag. `--unit`/`--integration` and the bundled default are same-engine cli legs, TTY-gated so artifacts stay clean and the operator-pause is **never** blocked on an interactive prompt. The `--e2e` webview stage left with the window (2026-10-11); the token now falls to the unknown-token `usage:` exit 2 in both shells.

title: Component — Header / banner

body: The header is printed once per command (never an always-on banner — that wastes terminal real-estate): `CONDUCTOR` + the verb + the scenario/suite + `seed <n>`. Section title is **bold + ANSI 117** (the `color-id-cyan` mapping); the `seed` / metadata is dimmed (ANSI 146, the journal-text mapping). The MCP preflight readiness line follows — protocol version, tool count, canary result — with the negotiated identifiers in ANSI 117 and an `[OK]` / `[BLOCKED]` prefix so the gate reads without color. All styling routes through `owo-colors` gated by `std::io::IsTerminal`, decided independently for stdout and stderr, so output auto-strips ANSI when piped and honors `NO_COLOR` / `TERM=dumb` (a stated requirement; NO_COLOR compliance derives from it).

title: Component — Primary navigation (verb structure)

body: Linear, top-to-bottom stdout — no cursor manipulation, no full-screen redraw (ratatui omitted). Verb-noun via clap: `conductor {verb} {arg}`, flat, one level deep — the verb SET is whichever `Commands` (`crates/conductor-cli/src/cli.rs`) declares, enumerated in §Primary screens below and never baked as a sample here. Help is verb-prefixed (`conductor --help` shows the verb table; `conductor run --help` shows verb flags) — never a separate man page or wiki link; the clap verb table renders flags in the ID-cyan mapping, descriptions in the default foreground. The operator's path is fixed: colored header → live `indicatif` heartbeat → `inquire` operator-pause holds (interactive TTY only) → `comfy-table` coverage/SLO summary → run-report path. Pipe-friendly throughout: raw artifact data is parseable on stdout, human messages route to stderr, and the headless agent path strips ANSI and **never blocks on a prompt** (an interactive gate there would silently break the release gate).

title: Component — Hero / signature output (Paused-count hold-point — CLI mirror)

data.head: ### Component — Hero / signature output (Paused-count hold-point — CLI mirror)

body: The CLI's hero is the decision moment: the operator-pause go/no-go, line-oriented.

- **`indicatif` heartbeat** carries the count + step index + a live counter with a colored phase-line prefix (ANSI 114, the `count-nominal` mapping). The spinner appears only after ~200ms (honest progress, not instant churn).

- **On the operator-pause**, the spinner **STOPS in place at the exact value** — not a hide, not an animate-to-100%. A bold **ANSI 179** (`count-hold` mapping) `HOLD — operator pause` phase line prints **above** the `inquire` proceed/abort confirm, carrying the frozen count as text (signature placement #2). The stop is the signature — it embodies "paused count shows where it stopped."

- **Checklist lines** (2026-10-12): on the interactive hold, each declared `[[checklist]]` item prints two indented plain lines on stderr between the HOLD phase line and the confirm — `  induced: {induced}` / `  observe: {observation}` — no color, no bracket label, while the spinner is suspended; the headless (non-TTY) path prints none.

- **`inquire` confirm** is gated behind an `isatty` check: an interactive operator gets the colored proceed/abort confirm; when stdin is not a TTY (the agent-driven `agent-run.sh`), the prompt is **skipped** per the configured non-interactive policy and the decision is recorded to the artifact — the headless source-of-truth path is never blocked. The proceed/abort decision is logged to the run report.
Expression rationale: the stop — the deliberate halt of an otherwise-honest spinner — is the 0.3-budget signature; the held silence is the event.

title: Component — Primary content block 1 (results / SLO table)

data.head: ### Component — Primary content block 1 (results / SLO table)

body: The **`run` + `suite` per-check table.** `comfy-table` with exactly **6 columns**, sized to their content (never hardcoded, never wrapped at arbitrary points, no terminal-width detection): **P-ID** (ANSI 117, the `color-id-cyan` mapping) · **scenario** · **state** (`[PASS]` / `[HOLD]` / `[FAIL]` / `[BLOCKED]` colored prefix — ANSI 114 / 179 / 203 / 60) · **slo_tier** (`<5s` / `<20s` / `<90s`) · **latency_ms** (ANSI 117, right-aligned) · **fingerprints** (ANSI 117). The header row is dimmed. A **`Blocked` row** carries the named precondition string in its detail; its measurement columns render as `—` / null, **never a red error** (`Blocked` ≠ red — never measured). The summary caption rolls up the tally with each count in its status-color mapping and, while a run is held, echoes the frozen step-index in the hold-amber mapping (signature reinforcement #3). Every state cell pairs its color with the bracket prefix so it survives `NO_COLOR` and piping.

**The coverage matrix is a separate, narrower table** — `conductor coverage` renders **4 columns** (P-ID · Title · Category · Mode), sized to their content, with no verdict/state column and therefore no bracket prefix, terminating in its own roll-up caption (§cli Primary screens). **The scenario catalogue is a third shape** — `conductor scenarios` renders **3 columns** (Scenario · P-IDs · SLO), no state column and no bracket prefix, the one table sized to the terminal width, ending in its `1 scenario` / `N scenarios` roll-up line. None of the three is to be conflated with another: the 6 columns above are the results/SLO shape.

title: Component — Primary content block 2 (verdict / report-state lines)

data.head: ### Component — Primary content block 2 (verdict / report-state lines)

body: Per-P-ID result printed in place, one line each, color always paired with an ASCII prefix:
- `✓ P-009  Pass   1840ms <90s` — `[PASS]`, ANSI 114 (`count-nominal` mapping).
- `⚠ P-008  CalibrationRegion  <20s` — `[HOLD]`, ANSI 179 (`count-hold` mapping) — the calibration-region bucket, never silently a Fail.
- `✗ P-015  Fail  4120ms <slo_tier>` — `[FAIL]`, ANSI 203 (`status-fail` mapping), **no blink** (the tier cell renders the scenario's TOML-declared value from the closed set).

- `? P-035  Manual  halo→burgundy? · no OS toast?` — `[MANUAL]`, ANSI 146 (neutral lavender) — an operator-checklist item (no programmatic read-back; TTY: `inquire` y/n, headless: recorded unconfirmed), never a machine verdict.
- `~ P-032  Residual  recent_commits stub → v0.3.0` — `[RESIDUAL]`, ANSI 246 (muted) — a measured, pre-accepted gap, **never red**.

- `• P-003  Blocked  mcp-server feature + ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED + matching data-dir` — `[BLOCKED]`, ANSI 60 (`count-blocked` mapping), with the named precondition; measurement fields render `—` / null.

Those six are the complete set of **per-P-ID verdict / report-state** bracket labels, and the lamp set is closed at six. Each surface additionally carries a **run-level, non-lamp** qualifier SET, printed outside the lamp column — on cli that is `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` (load-envelope, once per run) and `[PRECONDITION]` (the `conductor preconditions` probe — one line per unmet subject, or the single satisfied line when every subject is met; both arms are reachable, so it is not a failure-only label) (the `not-conductors` Mode-cell precedent in §Primary content block 1) — a SET adapted per surface, never forked: cli stdout's `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` bracket label in ANSI 246 and the Markdown report's banner. It qualifies the run rather than reporting a check, so it is neither a seventh lamp nor a sixth `ReportState`; a parser keying on state labels should read the per-P-ID set plus that non-lamp qualifier SET.

P-IDs, `run_id`, slo_tier, latency_ms, and fingerprints render in the ID-cyan mapping (ANSI 117); report body / dimmed metadata in ANSI 146 (the journal-text mapping). This is the supporting verdict convention, line-oriented.

**Per-check detail region (`runs/<run_id>.md`).** Beneath each P-ID verdict line the Markdown run report carries one INDENTED plain-text line per expected check — that check's ordinal, its comparison kind, its own verdict, its own `latency_ms`, and the deadline it was judged against (its declared budget, or the scenario tier's when it inherits). It is the indented-detail-line precedent (the `Blocked` precondition string, the `KnownResidual` note), applied to the per-check grain: **no new column, no new bracket label — the lamp set stays closed at six — and no new ANSI or token entry.** cli stdout and the 6-column results/SLO table are unchanged; a scenario that graded nothing (blocked, or declare-only) contributes no such line.

title: Component — Footer / terminator + error output

body: - **Terminator:** a single closing line naming the artifact destination — `run report → runs/<run_id>.md` — in the dimmed mapping (ANSI 146), the path left un-colorized when piped. No persistent footer between commands; terminal scroll is the natural footer.

- **Error output** goes to **stderr**, sanitized per the security plan (no absolute host paths / internal struct names / stack traces): `error: <short>` + contextual detail + `hint: <fix>`. Never colorized when piped; stack traces only under `--debug` / `-v`. stdout stays reserved for raw artifact data so a downstream agent parses it cleanly — stdout (data) and stderr (messages) are never mixed without intention.

title: IA notes

body: - **Command model:** verb-noun, flat (one level), help verb-prefixed; output structure is stable across versions because downstream agents parse it — adding a `comfy-table` column without a `--format` flag would be a breaking change.

- **Pipe discipline:** raw artifact data on stdout, human messages on stderr; ANSI auto-stripped when piped; `NO_COLOR` / `TERM=dumb` honored; emoji never used in machine-parseable (piped) output — ASCII prefixes (`[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[HOLD]`/`[BLOCKED]`) only there.

- **Headless invariant:** interactive `inquire` prompts always check `isatty` first; the agent-driven source-of-truth path is **never** gated on a prompt (an interactive gate there would silently break the release gate).
- **Contrast discipline:** ANSI 117 cyan + 114 green chosen for legibility on dark terminals; dark-blue-on-black / dark-red-on-black avoided.

- **Token coordination:** the ANSI codes bind the design-system palette by token name — `count-nominal` → ANSI 114, `count-hold` → ANSI 179, `status-fail` → ANSI 203, `count-blocked` → ANSI 60, `color-id-cyan` → ANSI 117, journal-text → ANSI 146.
- **No URL coupling:** the cli addresses runs by verb and `run_id`, never by URL or deep link.

title: Decisions Log
body:
## Decisions Log

`2026-06-14` — Initial layout templates generated by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8

**Surfaces covered:** desktop-webview (Tauri 2 frameless, React 19 / Tailwind v4.1 design tokens on `:root` / shadcn) + cli (`conductor-cli`: clap / owo-colors / indicatif / comfy-table / inquire, ANSI 256, TTY-gated, line-oriented).

**Key layout choices:**
- **desktop-webview:** single-station console, no router / no breakpoints / no browser nav — the frameless window IS the surface; the "screens" are one window in different run states (`idle` · `live` · `hold` · `aborted`, idle-with-report a sub-state of `idle` — the shipped `RunState` set, 2026-09-02). Coverage matrix is a dense single-row-per-P-ID list (Linear instrument-panel density), explicitly NOT a KPI-card grid. Borders-only depth (`border-subtle` seams, no shadow). "A control surface, not a dashboard."
- **cli:** linear top-to-bottom stdout, verb-noun over the verb set `Commands` declares, no cursor manipulation / no full-screen redraw (ratatui omitted). Two `comfy-table` shapes with terminal-detected width — the 6-column results/SLO table (`run`/`suite`) and the 4-column coverage matrix (`coverage`); every status color paired with an ASCII bracket prefix.

**Cross-surface IA decisions:**
- Same design tokens by name across both surfaces, adapted not forked: desktop CSS vars ↔ cli ANSI codes (`count-nominal` ↔ ANSI 114, `count-hold` ↔ ANSI 179, `status-fail` ↔ ANSI 203, `count-blocked` ↔ ANSI 60, `color-id-cyan` ↔ ANSI 117, journal-text ↔ ANSI 146). The status tier maps 1:1 to typed run outcomes on both — the machine-verdict triad (`Pass` / `CalibrationRegion`-HOLD / `Fail`) plus the three non-verdict ReportStates (`ManualCheck` operator-checklist · `KnownResidual` pre-accepted gap · `Blocked` never-measured), so none silently collapses into `Fail`. No shared URL/deep-link surface — desktop has no routes; cli has no URL coupling.

**Signature placement strategy (Paused-count hold-point):**
- **desktop-webview:** (1) frameless-titlebar count freezes at the hold value `count-nominal` → `count-hold` (primary); (2) operator-pause dialog header echoes the frozen count at the decision point; (3) coverage-matrix header strip echoes the frozen step-index while held. The absence of motion is the signature.
- **cli:** (1) `indicatif` heartbeat spinner STOPS in place at the hold (primary mirror); (2) bold hold-amber HOLD phase line above the `inquire` prompt carries the frozen count as text; (3) `comfy-table` summary caption echoes the frozen step-index while held. The stop — not a hide, not animate-to-100% — is the signature.

**Motion trigger placement:**
- The single design-system High-impact moment (the operator-pause freeze) fires only at the go/no-go hold — desktop: count freeze + `motion-micro` dialog fade + `motion-micro` count-tint color transition (both dropped under reduced-motion preference); cli: `indicatif` stop + hold-amber HOLD line. Verdict lamps (supporting convention) resolve motionless via a `motion-micro` color transition on both surfaces — never flashing. No pulse / blink / glow anywhere; `Fail` is a motionless `status-fail` lamp; `Blocked` (hollow ring), `ManualCheck` (neutral checkbox glyph) and `KnownResidual` (muted dashed dot) are each distinct non-verdict states, none ever red.

**Responsive breakpoints (web/mobile only):**
- N/A — desktop-bound single-station console (no responsive breakpoints, no web/mobile); cli is terminal-width-detected, never hardcoded.

**Notable surface-specific deferrals:**
- No auth/login/credential layouts — Conductor owns no credentials (local-only loopback tool); deferred as nonexistent, not as future work.
- Desktop window-control specifics (Windows/Linux standard buttons vs. macOS traffic-light, double-click-to-maximize) follow OS convention at implementation time.
- cli non-interactive policy specifics (how the headless path records a skipped operator-pause decision to the artifact) are an engine/config concern surfaced here only as the "never block the headless path" layout invariant.

**Notes:**
- Typography referenced by role name only (Display / Heading / Body / Label / Code / Data); color / spacing / radius referenced by token name only (`count-nominal`, `count-hold`, `count-blocked`, `status-fail`, `color-id-cyan`, `color-raised-1/2/3`, `border-subtle`, `border-emphasis`, `space-xs/sm/md/lg/xl`, `radius-sm/md/lg/full`, `motion-micro`, `ease-quiet`) — raw hex / font names / px live in the design-system plan, not here.
- Accessibility behavior is stated as design/behavioral requirements (announce the HOLD flip and verdict changes; accessible names on icon-only controls; visible focus ring in `color-focus`; status never color-alone; honor reduced-motion / `NO_COLOR`); the a11y specialist derives the concrete attributes and conformance downstream.
- Security guardrails honored at the layout level (deny-by-default Tauri capabilities, no remote-origin iframes, no `shell-open` with derived strings, Tauri ≥ 2.10.3; cli stderr sanitization, isatty-gated prompts) — no threat model or compliance content authored here.

title: Test Plan — Conductor

body:
_Generated by `/andromeda-tests`. This file is the single source of truth
for all test strategy + harness contracts + quality gates. Read by
downstream skills (obs / a11y / route / setup-project per D26 cross-
cutting), tests-pass per-phase, combine + `/implement` (via phase loop)._

_Do not edit during phase loop runs (tests-pass / combine / `/implement`).
Manual edits between runs are fine._

_**Agent-driven invariant:** every test layer described in this plan must
be runnable end-to-end by an agent reading exit codes and structured
output. No human-in-the-loop checkpoints, no manual verification, no
visual regression with human review. If a surface cannot be agent-driven,
it is flagged "untestable" in test-scope.md Section 1 and handled via
boundary tests / mocks._

title: 1. Test Scope Summary

body: _[ALL tiers — VERBATIM copy from test-scope.md]_

**Test tier:** `Minimal (0)`
_Justification: The passed `security_tier` is Minimal (0) (single-developer, local-only, no-cloud, no-auth, zero network exposure, only self-generated synthetic data) and the product is effectively a single primary surface (the cli release gate) with no persistent USER data — the lone store (`runs.db` + JSONL) holds only synthetic telemetry classified `low`. These place it below Standard. However, this is Minimal at the upper boundary: the workspace's crate-per-seam members (the set `Cargo.toml [workspace] members` declares) plus several capability surfaces (>5 entities), 7 critical paths, and a Creator-Brief mandate for "production-grade verification rigor" with a determinism hard-bar and an assertion-policy split — so the Minimal baseline is augmented with the Section 5 coverage triggers (security-vector negative-tests, deterministic-replay property/golden tests, MCP contract test, cross-surface parity, bounded fault-injection) without escalating to Comprehensive (which the project disqualifies itself from: NOT a load-tester, no multi-target/distributed, local-only, mobile N/A)._
**Coverage scope (testable entities):**

- **Entity:** `conductor-core` — **Source:** arch Workspace/Modules ("the runtime-agnostic engine library the other members depend on", `conductor-emit` excepted since 2026-09-13 — the dependent set is whatever the members' `Cargo.toml` files declare) — **Testability:** testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** N/A — pure Rust library, `cargo test -p conductor-core` per the per-seam test-isolation convention.

- **Entity:** `conductor-timeline` (deterministic seeded phase scheduler on `tokio::time`) — **Source:** arch Workspace/Modules + Stack ("tokio 1.52.3 `current_thread` flavor — deterministic single-threaded scheduler for the timeline engine") — **Testability:** testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** N/A — determinism is unit-assertable (same seed ⇒ same stream shape per Creator Brief's "Determinism as a hard quality bar"); `current_thread` flavor makes virtual-clock scheduling deterministic in-test.

- **Entity:** `conductor-emit` (OTLP raw-type emission primitives — opentelemetry-proto + tonic) — **Source:** arch Workspace/Modules + Stack ("opentelemetry-proto 0.32.0 ... raw hand-built OTLP message structs for byte-level fault control") — **Testability:** partially-testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** OTLP struct construction and byte-level encoding are unit-testable in isolation; actual gRPC egress to `127.0.0.1:4317` requires a live Pulse ingest listener (arch CI/CD note: "dynamic end-to-end scenario proof requires a live Pulse"). The egress liveness/transport leg is local-gate-only, not CI.

- **Entity:** `conductor-faults` (ramps, silence, port-occupier, fingerprints) — **Source:** arch Workspace/Modules — **Testability:** partially-testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** Ramp/silence/fingerprint generators are unit-testable as pure functions; the `:4317` port-occupier fault (security Vector 6) binds a loopback port — agent-runnable locally via a port-reachability probe but contends with a live Pulse on the same port, so it lives on the local/operator gate.

- **Entity:** `conductor-verify` (MCP read-back client — the hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC stdio client, `jsonrpc.rs` + `client.rs`; preflight gate, verdict logic) — **Source:** arch Workspace/Modules + Stack ("hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC over the sidecar's stdio"; rmcp removed 2026-06-27) + Standard Contracts (preflight readiness gate) — **Testability:** partially-testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** Verdict logic and preflight state mapping (`ready:false ⇒ blocked`, `degraded_mode ⇒ KnownResidual`) are unit-testable against a stub MCP server; the real read-back path needs the spawned `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar with `mcp-server` feature + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` (Creator Brief's MCP read-back prerequisite) — that integration leg is local-gate-only.

- **Entity:** `conductor-report` (JSONL journal + Markdown report + `runs.db` rusqlite storage) — **Source:** arch Workspace/Modules + Stack ("rusqlite 0.38.0 ... embedded run-metadata index `runs.db`") + Standard Contracts (Run report envelope) — **Testability:** testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** N/A — Run-report envelope schema, JSONL journal shape, and `runs.db` rows are golden-testable via cargo-nextest (security data-classification testability hint: "testable ... golden tests via cargo-nextest"); embedded SQLite (`bundled`) needs no external service; DB-row assertions run in-process.

- **Entity:** `conductor-cli` (the `agent-run` binary — headless source of truth) — **Source:** arch Workspace/Modules + Test Harness Commitment ("the headless `scripts/agent-run.sh` path is the source of truth and the release gate") — **Testability:** testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** N/A — binary edge testable via `Command::cargo_bin` subprocess + exit-code/stdout assertions (the agent-driven release gate).

- **Entity:** Scenario-config validation surface (serde + garde — `#[derive(Validate)]` range rules + cross-field invariants) — **Source:** arch Stack ("serde 1.0.x + garde 0.23.0") + Standard Contracts + security Vector 2 + data-classification "config (low)" — **Testability:** testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** N/A — load-time garde validation (a bounded error fraction — the shipped `error_percent` ∈ 0..=100 — non-negative durations, bounded per-phase occurrences, p50≤p95≤p99, severity-mix sums, the per-shape emission rules) is unit-testable with valid/invalid config fixtures; "transient at load" per the data-classification hint.

- **Entity:** Error-handling surface (thiserror typed per-seam enums + anyhow at edges) — **Source:** arch Stack ("thiserror 2.0.18 + anyhow 1.0.102 ... serves the error-handling surface across all seams") — **Testability:** testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** N/A — typed error enums assert per-seam failure mapping; the sanitization invariant (security: "Exposing internal error details ... rejected") is assertable on the `anyhow` edge and report artifacts.

- **Entity:** Scenario catalog (P-ID-keyed over the SUT capability manifest's accepted set — each scenario names its P-IDs, and a P-ID may be named by several scenarios) + `coverage-matrix.md` (every manifest capability classified, zero gaps) — **Source:** arch Project Intent ("its claimed capabilities — the SUT capability manifest's accepted set") + Test-Relevant Conventions ("no scenario without a P-ID") + Creator Brief Must-Work ("`coverage-matrix.md` complete: all 60 P-IDs ... zero gaps") — **Testability:** partially-testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** Matrix completeness/zero-gaps and per-scenario P-ID keying are statically assertable (a missing P-XXX is a defect — Creator Brief). The `auto`-classified scenarios assert via MCP read-back (live Pulse, local gate); `drive+observe` scenarios induce state but the visual confirmation is an operator-checklist item — see untestable zones below.

- **Entity:** `runs.db` SQLite store + per-run JSONL journals + Markdown reports (persistent data store) — **Source:** security data-classification "test-telemetry / run-metadata (synthetic, not user data) (low) — stored in `runs/` ... and embedded SQLite `runs.db`" — **Testability:** testable — **Reason if not fully testable:** N/A — the one persistent store; self-generated synthetic data, append-mostly; fixture strategy is seeded synthetic OTLP via the timeline/emit seams (no developer-seeded DB needed). Golden tests cover artifact shape.
**Untestable zones (flagged here, not given invented drivers):**

- **Untestable:** Live Pulse instance + its `corpus.db` (plaintext SQLite — the P-049 encryption assumption was disproved live 2026-06-27). Source: security (`corpus.db` is owned by Pulse and reached through the MCP tool surface only — never the file) + Creator Brief ("NO Pulse process management — Conductor never starts/stops/restarts Pulse"). Reason: third-party process Conductor cannot start, edit, or reach internally; exercised only via MCP canary round-trip. Pulse-side state is untestable from Conductor.

- **Untestable:** `OsKeychainBackend("com.andromeda.pulse")` credential. Source: security data-classification "credential — none owned by Conductor ... testability hint: untestable in current harness (out of scope)." Reason: Conductor never stores/generates/manages any secret; the keychain is Pulse-side.

- **Untestable (by agent):** `drive+observe` visual/UX confirmation step. Source: Creator Brief coverage classification ("the operator confirms the visual/UX claim via the generated checklist") + Creator Brief anti-pattern ("NO UI automation of Pulse — visual claims are operator checklist items"). Reason: the *checklist rendering* and induced-state context are agent-assertable; the human visual go/no-go judgment is not agent-drivable and is explicitly an operator step.

- **Untestable (at the unit tier):** the APPLIED Windows creation flag on the sidecar spawn. `std::process::Command` exposes exactly five getters (`get_program` / `get_args` / `get_envs` / `get_current_dir` / `get_env_clear`) and none for creation flags, so `build_command`'s `.creation_flags(console_suppressing_flags())` is not assertable through `as_std()` — measured 2026-09-04 (rustc 1.95.0). The flag VALUE is unit-covered (`spawn.rs::the_sidecar_spawn_suppresses_the_child_console`, `#[cfg(windows)]`) and its APPLICATION was evidenced by the operator-local `sr` leg's absence of the console-pane observable until that leg retired with the window (2026-10-11) — no standing leg evidences it now; never by a unit assertion and never by a manual smoke step (§11 → Universal bans one). Flagged here rather than given an invented driver: asserting it would need a Windows window-enumeration dependency to observe a boolean.

- **Untestable (in CI, and in-process):** `conductor suite`'s Ctrl-C stop at the signal itself. The first interrupt is witnessed by the `#[cfg(unix)]` test `the_first_interrupt_sets_the_stop_flag_and_the_process_lives` (a self-sent fixed-argv `kill -INT`, awaited under a bounded `tokio::time::timeout`), which runs on the Linux dev host only until `Linux-only base CI` makes CI Linux; the second Ctrl-C's immediate `std::process::exit(130)` cannot be asserted in-process and stays unwitnessed, with no owner — both accepted by the operator's word (2026-10-12). The stop's outcome stays unit-covered: `suite_exit`'s two tests (a stopped suite exits 130; a completed one exits on the hard-Fail rule) and `drive_run`'s three.

- **Out of scope (no driver):** `static-only` Pulse capabilities. Source: Creator Brief ("static-only ... stays with Pulse's own test matrix — Conductor explicitly does NOT duplicate them"). Reason: no dynamic telemetry dimension; owned by Pulse's suite.
**Surfaces under test:**

- **Surface:** cli (`conductor-cli` / `agent-run` binary) — **Driver:** subprocess + `Command::cargo_bin` (Rust language-native test client / assert_cmd-style), driving `conductor run <scenario>` / `conductor suite` / `conductor report <run_id>` / `scripts/agent-run.sh` — **Signal:** exit code + structured stdout (status text labels `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[HOLD]`/`[BLOCKED]`/`[MANUAL]`/`[RESIDUAL]` per Design System brand anchors, survive `NO_COLOR`/piping — these six are the per-P-ID lamp / report-state label set (closed at six); cli stdout also carries the run-level non-lamp caption SET — `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` (the SUT-load-envelope caption) and `[PRECONDITION]` (the `conductor preconditions` probe caption), both printed outside the lamp column and neither a `ReportState`, so selectors assert the named set plus that non-lamp SET rather than assuming stdout carries only those six) + `runs.db` row check via embedded SQL + per-run `<run_id>.jsonl` journal file existence/content — **Boundary:** cross-surface (drives core → timeline → emit → verify → report; the release-gate path) — **Notes:** Source-of-truth and release gate (arch Test Harness Commitment); headless path "never blocked on an interactive prompt" (Design System cli surface) — TTY-gated interactive `inquire` prompts (operator-pause) must be agent-bypassable on the headless path, a property proven at the UNIT tier (`headless_never_blocks_under_paused_clock`; `resolve_kind_agent_mode_overrides_an_attended_tty`) rather than by this release-gate subprocess leg, whose preflight returns on the Blocked spine before any hold fires. Full dynamic end-to-end (auto scenarios) requires a live Pulse + `mcp-server` feature → local/operator gate, not CI (arch CI/CD note).

- **Surface:** ipc-internal (MCP read-back client — `conductor-verify`'s hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC client over the sidecar's stdio) — **Driver:** language-native IPC test client — the hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp` over stdio + JSON schema assertion on the RAW tool results of the pinned required-tool set (`contracts/mcp-contract.toml` `required_tools` = `READBACK_TOOLS`; the `retrieve_incident_events` read joined it 2026-10-03); against the real `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar on the local gate — **Signal:** IPC response payload check (the `protocolVersion` READ BACK from the `initialize` result == `2024-11-05`, required-tool presence vs. pinned manifest, canary round-trip observing an incident opened after the emission stamp) → maps to verdict/state; `ready:false` ⇒ `blocked`, `degraded_mode` ⇒ `KnownResidual` (arch Standard Contracts) — **Boundary:** cross-surface (preflight gate gates all dependent scenarios) — **Notes:** Real read-back leg requires Creator Brief's documented prerequisite (Pulse `mcp-server` feature + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` + matching `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`); mismatch ⇒ silently-empty read-back, which preflight must catch as `blocked` (security Vector 4). Stub-server leg is fully CI-runnable.

(No web-spa/web-ssr, no api-service with inbound listener, no tui, no mobile, no desktop surface — security excerpt confirms "no web framework, no HTTP surface"; the window retired 2026-10-11, intent R1.)
**Test harness requirements:**

- **5-command requirements:**
  - `boot` — Conductor itself has **no daemon / no inbound listener** (security: "zero network exposure ... no inbound listener of its own"); `boot` is a **precondition probe THEN a preflight readiness gate** (arch Standard Contracts) — the live-Pulse prerequisite is probed and exit-coded ahead of the gate (`:4317` reachability, `andromeda-pulse-mcp` on the inherited `PATH`, the three `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` handles) rather than stated as prose alone, and an unmet subject short-circuits before the gate runs. **The handles subject is met when the environment declares it** — each name is graded by its own KIND via `conductor_core::handle_declared` (the PATH-valued `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` by presence-after-trim, the flag handles by `flag_declared` truthiness), so the short-circuit describes only an actually-unmet invocation and the readiness signal below is reachable through `boot` (see §3). The gate itself that asserts the MCP `initialize` handshake (protocol `2024-11-05`), required-tool presence vs. pinned manifest, and a data-dir canary round-trip. Readiness signal: preflight returns `ready:true`; `ready:false` ⇒ all dependent scenarios report `blocked` (never silently downgraded — security). Precondition: live Pulse + `mcp-server` feature reachable (Creator Brief prerequisite).
  - `run` — invokes the scenario catalog: per-P-ID scenarios (over the manifest’s accepted set) and/or the three named dynamic scenarios (`error-baseline-spike`, `fingerprint-storm`, `restart-suppression`) plus `pii-scrub`, `connection-lifecycle`, `severity-lifecycle` (Creator Brief Must-Work). Exit-code semantics: 0 = all checks Pass; non-zero = at least one hard `Fail`, or — in the bundled default — a red build, doctest or `-D warnings` clippy line, which stops the run at the first such line in both shells (§3 → 5-command implementation); `blocked`/`ManualCheck`/`KnownResidual`/`CalibrationRegion` are reported states, NOT process-failure exits (assertion-policy split: model-interpretive claims are "calibration-region checks + report-for-human, never hard-failed" — Creator Brief Risk Tolerance). Runs `cargo build` + `cargo nextest`/`cargo test` (incl. golden tests) + `cargo clippy` in CI (arch CI/CD).
  - `status` — structured-state query via the Run report envelope (arch Standard Contracts), polled per-check. Fields the agent polls: `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict ∈ {Pass, Fail, CalibrationRegion}`, `state ∈ {Pass, Fail, ManualCheck, KnownResidual, Blocked}`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `journal_emitted_at`, `read_back_observed_at`, `fingerprints`. Mechanism: read the `runs.db` row (embedded SQL) and/or the ENVELOPE line of the per-run JSONL journal — the journal also carries per-check `CheckRecord` lines, so an unqualified or last-line read returns a check record's fields instead (§3 `status`) — no HTTP endpoint exists (no listener).
  - `cleanup` — teardown of per-run on-disk artifacts (`runs/<run_id>.jsonl`, `runs/<run_id>.md`) and `runs.db` rows; must be idempotent (re-running a clean state is a no-op). Conductor must NOT touch Pulse (Creator Brief: "NO Pulse process management"). The `:4317` port-occupier fault (security Vector 6) must release its bind on cleanup. Agent verifies cleanup via file-absence check + `runs.db` row-count query.
  - `logs` — the **emission journal** is ground truth: per-run `<run_id>.jsonl` under `runs/`, wall-clock-stamped via `std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant` (security: "Writing journal/report wall-clock stamps from tokio's virtual clock — rejected") — this is "the left side of every SLO check" (Creator Brief). Plus sanitized stderr (Design System cli "Error output"). Retention: per-`run_id`, append-mostly on disk.

- **Status endpoint shape:** No HTTP/IPC status *endpoint* (no listener). The agent-parseable equivalent is the Run report envelope JSON / `runs.db` row: `{ run_id: string, seed: number, scenario: string, p_ids: string[], verdict: "Pass"|"Fail"|"CalibrationRegion", state: "Pass"|"Fail"|"ManualCheck"|"KnownResidual"|"Blocked", latency_ms: number, slo_tier: string, journal_emitted_at: timestamp, read_back_observed_at: timestamp, fingerprints: ... }` (arch Standard Contracts, Run report envelope). Artifacts must NOT leak absolute host paths or internal struct names (security).

- **Log format:** Structured JSONL — per-run journal is one JSON object per line (arch Test-Relevant Conventions: "per-run JSONL journals stemmed by `run_id`"); agent-parseable with jq / serde. Markdown report (`<run_id>.md`) is the human/agent prose mirror sharing the same envelope fields.

- **PID file location:** N/A — no daemon (security: "no inbound listener of its own"; arch: `conductor-cli` is a one-shot `#[tokio::main(flavor="current_thread")]` binary, not a long-running service).

- **Test data strategy:** Self-bootstrapping via **deterministic seeded synthetic generation** — `conductor-timeline` produces the same stream shape for the same scenario+seed (Creator Brief: "Deterministic under a seed"); no developer-seeded DB. Config fixtures are declarative scenario files (serde + garde) under `scenarios/`, each naming its P-IDs (a P-ID may be named by several) (arch Test-Relevant Conventions). Golden tests assert envelope/journal shape via cargo-nextest (security data-classification hint). Two scenario families (P-032/P-036) require a real git workspace with known recent commits (Creator Brief environment requirement).
**Critical paths:**
