- **Path:** Headless deterministic scenario run with MCP read-back verification (e.g., `error-baseline-spike`) — **Surfaces involved:** cli + ipc-internal (MCP read-back) + persistent-storage (`runs.db` / JSONL) — **Verification signal:** after `conductor run error-baseline-spike --seed <s>`, exit code 0 AND `runs.db` row has `verdict` null + `state=KnownResidual` (the family is declare-only; Pulse's reaction is proven by the harvest-tier cue assertion — `baseline_harvest.rs`) with `latency_ms` recorded against the declared `slo_tier` AND the per-run JSONL journal is written AND MCP read-back (`query_incident_list`/`retrieve_report`) confirms Pulse's reaction; same seed ⇒ same stream shape on re-run. — **Source:** Creator Brief Must-Work ("End-to-end proof against a real Pulse: at minimum `error-baseline-spike` ... produce verified expected outcomes (MCP read-back where applicable)") + arch Critical paths hint.

- **Path:** Fingerprint-storm scenario (fault-injection burst + read-back) — **Surfaces involved:** cli + ipc-internal (MCP read-back) + persistent-storage; exercises `conductor-faults` fingerprints — **Verification signal:** `conductor run fingerprint-storm` exits 0 with per-P-ID `verdict`/`state` rows recorded; the envelope's `fingerprints` field present and SUT-populated under deterministic L4 — the constant `det-*` refs from the fixture's `evidence_refs` (payload-invariant, measured 2026-08-18 at `efabe8e`) and, at Pulse HEAD `83d4060`, each incident's triggering-cue fingerprint, a 32-hex value that varies with what Conductor emitted (measured 2026-09-10; arch §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture]); Pulse's fingerprint reaction proven on the live/operator gate via the test-only storm-log harvest (`cue_kind = "retry_storm"`, the suggested→autonomous tier ladder, exactly one incident), NOT via the `fingerprints` array — no shipped check keys on it — or a read-back token check (§6). — **Source:** arch Critical paths hint (named verbatim) + Creator Brief Must-Work.

- **Path:** Restart-suppression incl. one bypass case (suppression/bypass logic) — **Surfaces involved:** cli + ipc-internal + persistent-storage — **Verification signal:** `conductor run restart-suppression` produces a declare-only row — `verdict` null, `state=KnownResidual` (non-Blocked), `latency_ms` recorded against the declared `slo_tier` (`<90s`) — with journal + `runs.db` asserting the deterministic stream; the suppression/bypass claim grades as hard pass/fail at the HARVEST tier (`crates/conductor-run/tests/restart_harvest.rs`, verbatim leg captures): the proven bypass set is the absolute-rate arm + the neither-condition suppressed case (the relative-magnitude arm is unreachable at shipped SUT constants), and suppression-eligibility is the service's young cumulative-sample window (`persistence_seconds` = samples), not a spike duration. — **Source:** arch Critical paths hint (named verbatim) + Creator Brief Must-Work ("`restart-suppression` (incl. one bypass case)"); re-based 2026-08-18 (the v2-11/v2-12 harvest-tier precedent).

- **Path:** Severity-lifecycle full pass observing auto-resolve — **Surfaces involved:** cli + persistent-storage — **Verification signal:** re-based 2026-08-21 (live proof). The five family scenarios land declare-only (`verdict` null, `state=KnownResidual`, non-Blocked, `latency_ms` against the declared `slo_tier`); the live auto-resolve claim grades HARD at the harvest tier (`conductor-run/tests/severity_harvest.rs`) on the active-set-empties instant plus the same-fingerprint retrigger's `created=true, deduped=false`, and severity choice stays CalibrationRegion at the cue tier (report-for-human, not hard-failed) — Creator Brief assertion-policy split. The resolution-summary half is unreachable under deterministic L4 and is recorded, not asserted. (`mark_incident_resolved` GAINED a production caller on 2026-09-01 — `conductor_run::probe_resolve_lifecycle`, §5 — but it is exercised out-of-band and never inside this path, so this path's grading is unchanged.) — **Source:** Creator Brief Must-Work ("one full `severity-lifecycle` pass observes auto-resolve + resolution summary").

- **Path:** Known-residual classification path (P-032 reports as KnownResidual, not a surprise failure) — **Surfaces involved:** cli + ipc-internal (`retrieve_report` with `degraded_mode`) + persistent-storage; runs inside a real git workspace (P-032 environment requirement) — **Verification signal:** `conductor run` for P-032 produces `state=KnownResidual` (NOT `Fail`); a `degraded_mode` read-back result maps to `KnownResidual` (arch Standard Contracts); run report distinguishes it from pass/fail/manual-check. — **Source:** Creator Brief Must-Work ("P-032 reports as known-residual (not as a surprise failure)") + Creator Brief environment requirement (P-032 git workspace).

- **Path:** Coverage-matrix completeness gate (every manifest capability classified auto / drive+observe / static-only / not-Conductor's, zero gaps) — **Surfaces involved:** cli + persistent-storage (the COMMITTED `coverage-matrix.md` artifact, LF-pinned by `.gitattributes` so its byte comparison is host-independent); shipped since 2026-09-06 as the crate-local `conductor-report --test coverage_gate` target, CI-enforced by the `.github/workflows/ci.yml` "Coverage-completeness gate" step (a loud guard on the artifact's presence, then the target, red on violation) — **Verification signal:** the classification is asserted set-equal to the SUT capability manifest's accepted set — no literal count or P-ID range — with every capability in exactly one of the four modes and zero unclassified entries; a missing P-XXX fails the gate ("A P-XXX missing from the matrix is a defect" — Creator Brief); this is the "0.1.0 done" definition (arch Critical paths hint). — **Source:** Creator Brief Must-Work ("`coverage-matrix.md` complete: all 60 P-IDs ... zero gaps") + arch ("complete `coverage-matrix.md` ... is the definition of done").

- **Path:** In-process ↔ headless parity — every DETERMINISTIC-POSTURE catalog scenario gives the same envelope from the in-process composition and from the headless `conductor run`, deterministic under fixed seed — **Surfaces involved:** cli + in-process core + persistent-storage — **Scope (2026-09-22, operator-ratified 2026-09-23):** a scenario declaring the real-model L4 posture (`real-model-interpretation`) is outside parity BY DESIGN — only the headless `conductor run` evaluates the gate under its declared posture (`preflight_for`); the in-process `{preflight, drive_run}` composition and `conductor suite` keep the deterministic gate and record it `Blocked` at scenario level, and its envelope follows the model, not the seed. — **Verification signal:** a run driven through `conductor_run::{preflight, drive_run}` yields the same `runs.db` envelope (verdict/state/seed) as the headless `conductor run` for the same scenario+seed, with an emission journal written per run from both paths. The Creator Brief's control-panel-LAUNCHED half retired with the window on 2026-10-11 — narrowed by the founder's ruling (intent R1), ratified at that chunk's wrap, and no longer owed. — **Source:** Creator Brief Must-Work ("Every catalog scenario runs from the control panel AND headless; deterministic under a fixed seed; emission journal written per run"), narrowed by R1.

(7 paths — the maximum. `connection-lifecycle` Must-Work scenarios are covered as DECLARE-ONLY instances of Path 1's pattern — no read-back-graded checks, rows landing `verdict` null / `state=KnownResidual` — with the live walk/conflict claims graded at the harvest tier in `crates/conductor-run/tests/connection_harvest.rs`; `pii-scrub` is covered as a DECLARE-ONLY instance of that pattern — no read-back-graded checks, its row landing `verdict` null / `state=KnownResidual` — with the live scrub claim graded at the harvest tier in `crates/conductor-run/tests/pii_harvest.rs`.)
**Coverage triggers:**

- **Trigger type:** security-vector-coverage (negative-test) — **Source:** security plan Vector 1 (CLI input — seed/scenario flags + `CONDUCTOR_*` env path handles) — **Required test type:** per-member by who READS the handle. The Rust-read `CONDUCTOR_*` path handles keep the negative-test asserting `std::fs::canonicalize` + type/existence check rejects path-traversal BEFORE any `runs.db`/journal write or manifest read (path handles sit outside garde). The harness-only host dev-tool handles (`CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER`, `CONDUCTOR_NVDA`) and the `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT` flag lost every reader on 2026-10-11 with the window, so their classes and coverage left this trigger. `CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` lost its one reader on 2026-10-12 (`crates/conductor-run/tests/envelope_fixture.rs`, deleted at `Panel-shaped types retired`), so its class and its seeder NO-OP coverage left this trigger too. A further class joined 2026-09-23: the TEST-binary readers of `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` (`conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs`, and the operator-gated `real_model_live.rs` / `live_suite.rs`) plus the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` VALUE read in `real_model_live.rs` — by `pulse_log`, and since 2026-09-30 by `workspace_key()` (the data dir's basename, taken once from the guarded path's parent, for the capture's workspace-key mask) — never read by a shipped binary, so no CLI-edge test reaches them. Each resolves through the shared `conductor-run/tests/capture_paths` guard (`resolve_under` for the runs dir; canonicalize + is-dir for the Pulse data dir), and its mandated negative test is the default-suite target `capture_paths_guard` (absolute and `..` rejected, unset/relative resolved, missing or non-directory data dir rejected, no failure text echoing its input), green under both nextest and `cargo test`.

- **Trigger type:** security-vector-coverage / property-test — **Source:** security plan Vector 2 (config-file parsing) + anti-pattern "Deserializing scenario config without garde validation at load" — **Required test type:** negative-tests asserting garde rejects out-of-range config (an out-of-range error fraction — `error_percent` > 100 in the shipped integer-percent encoding — negative durations, over-bound occurrences, p50>p95>p99 ordering violations, severity-mix sum violations) at load; property test over the `#[garde(custom)]` cross-field invariants. A nested spec field annotated `skip` rather than `dive` must be caught here — its rules exist but never execute.

- **Trigger type:** security-vector-coverage (negative-test) — **Source:** security plan Vector 4 + anti-patterns (rmcp STDIO command/argument-injection CVE-2026-30623; protobuf-decode DoS RUSTSEC-2020-0002/2024-0437; silent preflight downgrade) — **Required test type:** negative-tests asserting (a) `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` with injection metacharacters is rejected and passed only via `.env(...)` — never into argv; (b) the sidecar program path is fixed/hard-coded, not operator-chosen; (c) an empty/malformed canary round-trip becomes `blocked` (never false pass-as-empty); (d) bounded prost recursion does not panic on malformed child stdout.

- **Trigger type:** security-vector-coverage (negative-test) — **Source:** security plan anti-pattern "String concatenation / `format!` to build SQL for `runs.db`" — **Required test type:** negative/static assertion that all `runs.db` access uses rusqlite bound parameters (no string-built SQL), even for synthetic data.

- **Trigger type:** contract-test (no live SaaS, no vendor sandbox) — **Source:** arch Standard Contracts (Pinned MCP contract manifest — protocol `2024-11-05` + required-tool set) + anti-pattern "Pinning the rmcp client to a strict newer protocol default" — **Required test type:** contract test asserting the preflight gate READS the `protocolVersion` back from the `initialize` result and holds it against the pinned `contracts/` manifest's `2024-11-05` (never a strict-newer client default), and that the required-tool set matches that manifest; mismatch ⇒ `blocked`.

- **Trigger type:** property-test (determinism discipline) — **Source:** Creator Brief Risk Tolerance ("Determinism as a hard quality bar: same scenario + seed ⇒ same stream shape") — **Required test type:** property/golden test asserting a fixed scenario+seed reproduces an identical emission-journal stream shape across runs (the deterministic-replay invariant on `conductor-timeline`).

- **Trigger type:** cross-surface-coordination — **Source:** Creator Brief Must-Work ("Every catalog scenario runs from the control panel AND headless"), narrowed by intent R1 on 2026-10-11 — **Required test type:** cross-surface coordination test asserting the in-process core run (`conductor_run::{preflight, drive_run}`) and the headless `conductor run` produce identical envelope verdict/state for the same deterministic-posture scenario+seed (a real-model-posture scenario is excluded by design — Critical Path 7's scope). The control-panel-LAUNCHED half retired with the window (2026-10-11).

- **Trigger type:** chaos-test (fault-injection — but bounded, NOT load) — **Source:** arch `conductor-faults` (ramps, silence, port-occupier) + security Vector 6 (`:4317` port-occupier) + Creator Brief anti-pattern ("NOT a load-tester ... 50k+ spans/sec saturation regimes are explicitly out") — **Required test type:** fault-injection scenario tests asserting Pulse's reaction to silence/ramp/port-occupier faults within SLO — bounded "typical/high" profiles only (P-060); explicitly NOT a saturation/load test (that is Pulse's `perf_load_profiles.rs`).

- **Trigger type:** supply-chain audit (Minimal-tier residual-risk control) — **Source:** security plan anti-patterns ("Running `cargo build --release` or merging without `cargo-audit` (and `cargo-deny`) green"; "Letting `Cargo.lock` drift"; toolchain ≥ 1.94.1 for tar-rs CVE-2026-33056) — **Required test type:** dependency/supply-chain audit gate (`cargo-audit` + recommended `cargo-deny`) green over the `bundled`-SQLite-from-C + OTLP/gRPC/MCP tree; committed `Cargo.lock`; toolchain pinned ≥ 1.94.1.
(Note: artifact-sanitization discipline folds into the Run-report envelope golden tests in Section 3, asserting artifacts carry verdict/state/identity fields only.)

This tier is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how much test rigor downstream
skills (tests-pass per phase + cross-cutting reads from obs / a11y / route
/ setup-project) should apply.

title: 2. Test Strategy

body: _[ALL tiers — high-level pyramid + agent-runnable invariants]_
**Test pyramid (per tier):**
| Level | Coverage focus | Tier-specific depth |

| Unit | Pure functions, isolated module logic (per-seam `cargo nextest run -p conductor-<seam>` 0.9.137) | Bulk of suite — every seam crate's pure logic: timeline scheduling, fault generators, garde validation, verdict mapping, envelope serialization |

| Integration | Cross-module + IPC (the hand-rolled JSON-RPC stub over stdio) + OTLP-egress loopback gRPC `TraceService` stub (`tokio-stream` `TcpListenerStream` on ephemeral `127.0.0.1:0`) + DB (rusqlite `open_in_memory`) | **Included** (integration boundaries present: OTLP egress, MCP read-back, runs.db) — see Section 5 |
| E2E | Critical paths via the cli (assert_cmd) surface | **Included** — all 7 test-scope Sec 4 critical paths; CI-runnable legs (stub MCP) + local-gate legs (live Pulse) — see Section 6 |

| Property-based | Invariant assertions over random inputs (proptest 1.9.0) | **Included via trigger** — determinism-replay + garde cross-field invariants (test-scope Sec 5 property-test triggers), NOT generic Comprehensive escalation |

| Performance / Load | Budget assertions on perf-critical paths | **Excluded** — no perf-budget trigger; Creator Brief anti-pattern "NOT a load-tester ... 50k+ spans/sec saturation regimes are explicitly out" |

| Chaos / Fault | Bounded failure injection (conductor-faults generators + loopback port probe; optional turmoil transport faults) | **Included via trigger** — bounded "typical/high" profiles only (P-060); NOT saturation — see Section 8 |
**Agent-runnable invariants (apply across all levels):**

- Every test layer produces machine-parseable output — cargo-nextest 0.9.137 stable `NextestExitCode` (100 test-fail / 101 build-fail / 4 NO_TESTS_RUN) + `ci` profile JUnit XML; envelope asserted via `serde_json::from_str::<RunReportEnvelope>` on the envelope LINE, or `jq -e`; a whole-journal parse must discriminate the envelope line from the per-check `CheckRecord` line (§3 Log format).
- No human-in-loop verification, no Percy / Chromatic, no `cargo insta review` interactive accept UI (insta runs in CI/assert mode only); exit-code-readable.

- Deterministic — `#[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread", start_paused = true)]` + `tokio::time::advance` (no real `setTimeout`); no real network beyond the loopback set the suite actually opens — the gRPC/MCP stub (no off-host traffic). The operator-local exceptions run on real wall clock. The composed `agent-run run --live` suite (2026-09-06): real wall clock throughout — per-leg budgets derived from the run contract, a fixed 150 s quiet window between legs, and a live Pulse driving every leg — and so does its `run --live real-model` selector (2026-09-22): one leg against a Pulse whose real model interprets non-deterministically, plus a bounded capture poll, driven only as the pre-stated series of `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` (and once, on 2026-10-07, as that contract's pre-registered capture run, which states no verdict), each counted drive graded against a rule recorded before it fires — and so does the operator-gated `span_landing_live` witness (2026-10-01): two same-seed `conductor run` drives against one live Pulse, a 180 s quiet window between them, graded on Pulse's own log against its two frozen drive journals under `runs/span-landing/` (the two named files cleared before drive A; a pair outside that log's span refused, never graded), printing one integers-only `span-landing: PASS|FAIL …` line and minting no `agent-run` verb or selector — and so does the operator-gated `p075_round_live` leg (2026-10-02): one `canary_spec` storm against one live Pulse, read back through the pinned registered MCP tool set (the incident's lifecycle events read through `retrieve_incident_events` before and after the resolve; the resolve through `probe_resolve_lifecycle_timed`, which the shipped `probe_resolve_lifecycle` delegates to), the emitted fingerprint compared in-process, only integers, booleans, closed words and window-relative nanosecond offsets on stdout, no `agent-run` verb or selector; its grades sit at the harvest tier over digest-pinned evidence (the `p075_round_assertion_*` tests at Pulse `03ec944` and the `p075_reround_assertion_*` tests at Pulse S2 `cdb6c1e`, in `lifecycle_harvest` and `delegated_timing_harvest`). NONE of these is seed-deterministic and all are carried ONLY as the §9/§11 operator-local-gate exceptions — never CI legs; proptest counterexamples persisted to `proptest-regressions/` for deterministic replay.

- Self-bootstrapping fixtures — seeded synthetic generation via `conductor-timeline` (no developer-seeded DB); `rusqlite::Connection::open_in_memory()` per unit test, `assert_fs::TempDir`-backed file `runs.db` per cross-process test THAT WRITES RUN ARTIFACTS (a cross-process test of a verb writing none sets no runs-dir handle — see §3 Per-test isolation).
**Test directory + naming conventions:**

- **Directory pattern:** Per-seam crate-local `src/` `#[cfg(test)]` modules for unit tests + crate-local `tests/` for integration tests (arch Test-Relevant Conventions: "crate-per-seam workspace gives independent `cargo build -p` / `cargo test -p` per seam crate"); declarative scenario config fixtures under `scenarios/`, each naming its P-IDs (a P-ID may be named by several); golden snapshots committed under `<crate>/tests/snapshots/` (insta default) + `proptest-regressions/` per crate.

- **File naming:** snake_case Rust source files (arch: "snake_case Rust source files and identifiers"); on-disk test artifacts kebab-case Markdown (`coverage-matrix.md`) + per-run JSONL stemmed by `run_id` (arch Source/file naming).

- **Test function naming:** snake_case `fn` under `#[cfg(test)]` / `#[test]` / `#[tokio::test]` / rstest `#[rstest]`; the crate's per-seam module path namespaces ownership (e.g. `conductor_verify::preflight` tests).

title: 3. Test Harness Contract

body:
_[ALL tiers — central agent-driven mechanism; Section consumed by
setup-project to materialize scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}]_

Architecture committed to the harness pattern: **agent-driven — the headless `scripts/agent-run.sh` path is the source of truth and the release gate** (the GUI shell retired 2026-10-11) (upstream-context arch Test Harness Commitment). This section specifies the concrete contract. Conductor has **no daemon and no inbound listener** (security: "zero network exposure ... no inbound listener of its own"), so `boot` is a precondition probe plus a preflight readiness gate and `status` reads disk artifacts — there is no HTTP/IPC status endpoint.
Contracts: .andromeda/registries/test-plan-contracts.toml — ask registry.py contracts; read one contracts/test-plan/{key}.md; never whole.

title: 4. Unit Test Strategy

body: _[ALL tiers]_

**Framework:** cargo-nextest 0.9.137 (`cargo nextest run`; `nextest-metadata` 0.12.x for the machine-readable contract) as the primary runner — stable `NextestExitCode` enum + `ci`-profile JUnit XML; `cargo test --doc` (Rust toolchain ≥ 1.94.1) as the doctest fallback nextest does not run. **`cargo test -p <crate>` (full, non-doc) is additionally a standing runner-portability gate** — the suite must be green under BOTH runners, and only the shared-process runner can produce that evidence: a test relying on nextest's per-test process for isolation passes there and fails here, which is a determinism break under §10, not a runner quirk.
**Coverage tool:** cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7 (`cargo llvm-cov nextest --lcov`) — first-class nextest integration, LCOV/Cobertura/JSON output, `--fail-under-lines` exit-code gate.
**Mutation instrument:** cargo-mutants 27.1.0 — an operator/local audit instrument, NOT a CI stage (§9) and NOT a numeric threshold (§10). Run discipline, each item measured rather than assumed: `-f` resolves from the **workspace root**, so always pass the full crate path (`-f crates/<crate>/src/<file>.rs` — a package-relative path under `-p <crate>` silently matches nothing); `--test-tool=nextest` is REQUIRED (the default `cargo test` aborts the run in an unmutated tree wherever a test is not runner-portable); **`Found 0 mutants to test` is a NO-OP, never a pass** — it exits 0 with only a `WARN` and is indistinguishable from a clean run unless the tallies are read; **the exit code carries no verdict in either direction — a NON-zero exit reflects surviving/timeout CLASSES, not run failure** (measured **exit 3** on the 2026-08-20 run that fully met its acceptance — 0 missed, every named survivor killed, the non-zero owed entirely to two pre-existing timeouts), so gate on the tallies read out of `mutants.out/` (`missed.txt` holding EXACTLY the run's accepted-deliberate survivors — empty only when none is accepted, since an accepted-deliberate survivor by construction SURVIVES (§10) — plus every other named survivor present in `caught.txt`), never on the exit code; output goes to a gitignored `mutants.out/` (the audit skill redirects with `--output`, an ad-hoc scoped re-run does not). **Since 2026-09-13 the tally read-out has a COMMITTED executable form** — `python -X utf8 scripts/mutation-gate.py {unit}` runs a unit's tier into a fresh `target/mutation-gate/{unit}-{stamp}/` (gitignored; the leaf generated at invocation, since a pre-existing one is stale by construction and `cargo mutants` rotates it to `.old`) and grades EVERY tally the verdict rests on, exiting on the tally rather than on cargo-mutants' own exit — measured twice at that chunk, where `cargo mutants` exited **2** on both runs while both gates read PASS. Since 2026-09-30 the grade runs, in order: each of `missed.txt` · `caught.txt` · `timeout.txt` · `unviable.txt` present (an absent tally fails closed); each file's parsed line count equal to `outcomes.json`'s own count for its class; `missed + caught + timeout + unviable == total_mutants` (conservation — a truncated tally, an unparsed line or a mutant absent from every tally cannot pass unseen); then `missed.txt` and `timeout.txt` each compared as a MULTISET over `(file, mutation)` against the unit's `scripts/mutation-roster.toml` rows of that required `tally` class (a timeout is detection by hang, rostered so a caught→timeout move is graded rather than silent). `unviable` is graded by counts only and never rostered — it moves on host link contention alone (§10 zero-flakiness). The grading is proven WITHOUT a mutation run by the gate's `selftest` verb, which grades the committed fixture tallies under `scripts/fixtures/mutation-gate/` (one arm per verdict path, each asserted on verdict, named finding, finding count and no absolute path) and validates the real roster's schema. It is operator-local like the instrument it wraps: no CI step invokes it and it adds no sixth `agent-run.{sh,ps1}` command. One further contract item, measured the same day: `--output` creates its LEAF itself but fails with `os error 3` when the parent chain is missing, so the stable parent is created first and the leaf never is. Since 2026-10-04 `conductor-core`'s tier no longer needs `--copy-vcs true`: in the default copy (no `.git` in it) the secret-scan gate skips instead of panicking on `git ls-files` exit 128, which had aborted the unmutated baseline — as measured by a `.git`-less copy of the workspace running the gate green with its skip line (`2026-10-04-real-model-test-surface-corrective`), never by a mutation run; the next epoch-boundary audit confirms it under cargo-mutants.
**Roster member identity and registration:** an accepted-deliberate member is identified by cargo-mutants' own mutation DESCRIPTION — the text after the coordinates on a tally line `{path}:{line}:{col}: {mutation}` — joined to `scripts/mutation-roster.toml` by its `member` key; never by `file:line:col` and never by function + column, both of which re-stale as code moves (a member's column can move while its description stays unique across the survivor set). The executable roster carries no line and no column, and two members may legitimately share one `(file, mutation)` pair (the two `replace == with != in stub_result` entries), which is why the comparison is a MULTISET. The roster is populated PER GATED UNIT, not for the whole citation home: it carries rows for the units a chunk has re-run — `conductor-cli` (`member-5`), `conductor-verify` (`member-4`) and `conductor-emit` (`member-emit-1`) — while `member-1` and `member-3` (and `member-2`, retired with its crate on 2026-10-11) are citation-home numbering with no roster row, gaining one only when the epoch-boundary code audit re-runs the tier over their crate (a roster is a ledger of owed work, and only a re-run can shrink it). REGISTRATION is the `[[unit]]` declaration, never the row count: a `[[unit]]` table — optionally carrying a `files` list, workspace-root-relative, that scopes the tier to those paths via `-f` — registers a unit, so a registered unit whose survivors are all killed carries zero `[[entry]]` rows and PASSES when every graded tally agrees (empty `missed` and `timeout` multisets, each tally's count equal to `outcomes.json`'s, conservation holding); rows alone still register a unit; and because a scoped tier can generate nothing at all, a run producing 0 mutants is an explicit FAIL, never the clean sweep `cargo mutants` reports at exit 0.
**Coverage target:** see Section 10 Quality Gates for the Minimal-tier threshold.

**Tool-version policy:** the external-CLI tool versions named in this section (cargo-nextest, cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-mutants) are reference floors, not exact pins — they live outside `Cargo.lock`, so any install that runs the gate green satisfies it (the same floor logic the security-plan applies to cargo-audit / cargo-deny, §Dependency Security). The crate dev-deps (rstest · proptest · insta · assert_cmd · assert_fs · predicates) are caret-resolved with `Cargo.lock` authoritative; their exact resolved versions drift build-to-build and are not pinned in this prose.
**Conventions** (from upstream-context Test-Relevant Conventions):
- Test file location: crate-local `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` inside each `conductor-<seam>` source file, plus crate-local `tests/` for slower in-crate integration (arch per-seam isolation).
- Test function naming: snake_case `fn` under `#[test]` / `#[tokio::test]` / rstest `#[rstest]`.

- Test grouping: per-seam crate boundary is the primary grouping (`cargo nextest run -p conductor-<seam>`); rstest `#[case]` rows group table-driven variants (P-ID catalog, garde valid/invalid matrix).

**Fixture pattern at unit level:** rstest 0.26.1 — `#[fixture]` for the seeded `conductor-timeline` generator (no developer-seeded DB), `#[rstest]` + `#[case]` for table-driven P-ID and garde-config matrices, `#[once]` for the in-memory `runs.db` schema, and `#[future]` + `#[awt]` for async fixtures matching `#[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread")]` on `conductor-timeline`/`conductor-verify`.
**What unit tests cover** (per testable entity from test-scope Sec 1):
- **conductor-core:** engine logic in isolation (pure library; `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core`).

- **conductor-timeline:** deterministic phase scheduling under `#[tokio::test(flavor="current_thread", start_paused=true)]` + `tokio::time::advance` — same seed ⇒ same stream shape (also the property-test target, Section 7).

- **conductor-emit:** OTLP struct construction + byte-level encoding in isolation (egress liveness is local-gate-only, not unit), and the span-identity re-key primitive `rekey_trace_identity` — a pure function of `(request, salt)` whose masks come from one salt-seeded `ChaCha8Rng` (trace mask, then span mask), unit-tested as a per-salt bijection that preserves parent linkage, keeps an empty id empty and moves no content byte.
- **conductor-faults:** ramp/silence/fingerprint generators as pure seeded functions (same seed ⇒ same shape); the `:4317` port-occupier bind/release is a chaos/integration concern (Section 8).

- **conductor-verify:** verdict logic + preflight state mapping (`ready:false ⇒ blocked`, `degraded_mode ⇒ KnownResidual`, an empty corpus OR a stale one — no incident newer than the canary's emission stamp — ⇒ `blocked`) against the hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp` (`conductor-verify/tests/common/mod.rs`).

- **conductor-report:** Run-report envelope serialization + JSONL journal shape + `runs.db` row mapping (canonical line shape golden-locked via exact-string `assert_eq!` at unit level — matching the `verdict.rs`/`report_state.rs`/`scenario.rs` serialization-golden pattern; insta is the E2E journal-golden mechanism with `run_id`/timestamp redaction, §6/§7).
- **Scenario-config validation surface:** garde `range` + `#[garde(custom)]` cross-field rules with valid/invalid fixtures (also property-tested, Section 7).
- **Error-handling surface:** thiserror typed per-seam enum mapping + the `anyhow` edge sanitization invariant (no internal details leaked).

- **Scenario catalog + coverage-matrix:** static assertion that every catalog scenario carries a P-ID. The coverage-matrix half is no longer unit-tier: since 2026-09-06 the zero-unclassified assertion over the committed `coverage-matrix.md` ships at the crate-local `tests/` tier as `crates/conductor-report/tests/coverage_gate.rs` (`conductor-report`'s first `tests/` directory — it must reach both `conductor_core::check_sut_drift` and `conductor_report::CoverageMatrix::render`, which only that side of the dependency edge can do). Since 2026-09-16 the catalog half has a crate-local `tests/`-tier gate of its own: `crates/conductor-core/tests/scenario_audit_gate.rs` asserts, over the committed `contracts/scenario-audit-ledger.toml` plus the catalog as loaded, that no committed scenario declares an unsatisfiable assertion and that every scenario's declared tier is accounted for — reaching `check_scenario_audit` / `ScenarioAuditLedger` / `load_catalog` / `carries_retired_gloss` through the crate root's explicit re-export list. The set of crate-local static gates over committed data is whatever `tests/` targets assert a committed artifact against the production source it derives from, never a count. Since 2026-09-24 a second kind sits beside it, the crate-local repository-hygiene gates: `crates/conductor-core/tests/secret_scan_gate.rs` asserts that no secret-shaped string or file name survives in git's cached + untracked-not-ignored listing, graded against an exact-set allowlist, and `crates/conductor-core/tests/workflow_env_gate.rs` asserts every `env.X` expression read in `.github/workflows/*` against that file's own declarations and `GITHUB_ENV` writes. That set, too, is named by kind, never by a count. See §6.
- Edge cases + invariant assertions per seam.
**What unit tests do NOT cover** (handled at higher levels):
- Integration boundaries — MCP read-back stub stdio, `runs.db` cross-process (Section 5).
- E2E flows — cli subprocess critical paths (Section 6).
- External services — live Pulse / `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar (mocked via the hand-rolled MCP stub at unit/integration; live leg is local-gate-only).
(See `## 11. Test Anti-Patterns` § Unit for unit-level bans.)

title: 5. Integration Test Strategy

body: _[Included — integration boundaries present: MCP read-back stdio, runs.db, cross-surface parity.]_

**Driver(s):** the hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp` over the sidecar stdio, in-process duplex or spawned child (MCP read-back); rusqlite 0.38.0 `Connection::open_in_memory()` / `assert_fs::TempDir`-backed file DB; assert_cmd 2.1.2 for the CLI subprocess leg of cross-surface parity — the assertion library, with the binary path taken from the declared build-graph edge `assert_cmd::Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_conductor"))` (Cargo sets that var for the OWNING package's test targets), never `Command::cargo_bin`'s runtime `target/debug` fallback, which resolves nothing where the binary is not in that package's build graph (measured at `2026-09-02-mutation-tier-restored-for-conductor-tauri`). `cli_smoke`, inside the same owning package, keeps `Command::cargo_bin`.
**Boundary types covered:**
| Boundary | Test approach | Tools |
| Module ↔ module | direct function calls with shared rstest fixtures across `conductor-<seam>` crates | rstest 0.26.1 + cargo-nextest 0.9.137 |
| Module ↔ DB | in-memory `runs.db` per test; `assert_fs::TempDir` file DB for cross-process | rusqlite 0.38.0 (`open_in_memory` / `bundled` SQLite 3.51.1) + assert_fs 1 |

| Module ↔ external (MCP sidecar) | the hand-rolled JSON-RPC stub MCP server over stdio (in-process duplex for verdict logic; `stub_pulse_mcp` test-binary for the spawn/`.env()` path) + JSON-schema assertion on the RAW tool results | `conductor-verify`'s own `jsonrpc.rs` + `client.rs` paired with `stub_pulse_mcp` |

**Setup / teardown lifecycle:** per-test fresh in-memory `runs.db` (parallel-safe under nextest's per-process model); `assert_fs::TempDir` per cross-process test, dropped (auto-cleaned) at test end; the hand-rolled stub spun per test over the sidecar stdio (in-process duplex) or per child spawn.
**Cross-module patterns covered** (from upstream-context Standard Contracts):

- **MCP `initialize` preflight readiness gate** → contract test: READS the `protocolVersion` back from the `initialize` result and holds it against the pinned `contracts/` manifest's `2024-11-05` (never a strict-newer client default — security anti-pattern), required-tool presence vs. that manifest, canary round-trip; `ready:false ⇒ blocked` (test-scope Sec 5 contract-test trigger + Vector 4).

- **query_incident_list** → the canary round-trip against the stub: an incident opened AFTER the emission stamp ⇒ proceed; empty corpus, a corpus of only older incidents, or a missing/unparseable `opened_at_unix_nano` ⇒ `blocked`, never false-pass-as-empty — Vector 4(c). Covered by the fresh / stale / stamp-absent stub legs. **STUB ITEM-KEY FIDELITY (measured 2026-09-01):** the stub's incident item key MUST be `incident_id`, the key the live sidecar emits. The shared stub emitted `id`, so a reader keyed on `id` extracted an empty active set from a POPULATED live corpus — the silently-empty class this bullet already bans, arriving through the mock instead of the data dir, and green against every stub leg on the way to failing live (three incidents active 131–142s each while the leg logged `[]`). Pinned by `lifecycle_harvest::the_live_item_key_is_incident_id`; readers accept either key.
- **retrieve_telemetry_slice / retrieve_report** → per-check read-back extraction against the stub (the canary no longer calls them; malformed ⇒ readers degrade to empty, never a panic).
- **retrieve_report (with `degraded_mode`)** → `degraded_mode` result maps to `state=KnownResidual` (Critical Path 5 / P-032).

- **mark_incident_resolved** → re-based 2026-09-01 (P-075 live proof). It now HAS a production call site — `conductor_run::probe_resolve_lifecycle`, the first in the workspace, deliberately NOT wired into `execute_scenario` or any run path — and was exercised live against Pulse HEAD `83d4060`. Three tiers: the APPLIED arm (raw `{resolved, incident_id}`, un-MCP-wrapped) and the DECLINED arm (`VerifyError::JsonRpc`, Display renders the code only) are stub-proven at the integration tier via `ReadbackClient::resolve_incident` (`conductor-verify/tests/readback.rs`); the DECLINED arm is stub-ONLY and permanently so, because Pulse's `DeclinedStale` is a monotonic-timestamp guard its own dispatch cannot trip (`crates/corpus/src/contract.rs:652-659`); and the live write grades at the harvest tier on the pinned capture (`conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_harvest.rs`) driven by the feature-gated operator leg (`lifecycle_live.rs`). Verdict PROVEN-BY-LIVENESS — runtime-STATE fidelity (the incident left the active set `0.0s` after its last emission, against Pulse's 120s auto-resolve idle threshold), never payload fidelity. Re-graded 2026-10-02 at Pulse S `03ec944` (the P-075 assert round): `ProvenByLiveness` again, idle 12 ms, through the same unchanged probe and `attribute_by_liveness`, held by `lifecycle_harvest::p075_round_assertion_2_runtime_state_fidelity` over the round's digest-pinned capture. The severity-lifecycle resolution summary stays unreachable under deterministic L4, which is a separate claim (2026-08-21) and unchanged.

- **retrieve_incident_events** → added 2026-10-03 (Pulse S2 `cdb6c1e`): a by-id READ through `ReadbackClient::retrieve_incident_events`, no production caller. Three tiers: the stub tier proves the raw S2 keys `{incident_id, events[{event_kind, occurred_unix_nano}], total, truncated}` in order, an empty `events` reading `total: 0`, and an unknown id landing as a typed `VerifyError::JsonRpc` (`-32603`, `incident not found`), never `Ok` (`conductor-verify/tests/readback.rs`), and a sidecar lacking the tool blocks on the EXISTING `required tool(s) absent` precondition (`preflight.rs`; `preflight_spawn.rs` against the child stub built from `READBACK_TOOLS`); the live read is the operator-gated `p075_round_live` leg; and round-request assertion 7 grades at the harvest tier (`lifecycle_harvest::grade_assertion_7`, its synthetic `round_assertion_7_*` arms, and `p075_reround_assertion_7_incident_events_read_back` over the digest-pinned capture). The resolve call's `std::time` window (`ResolveWindow`, from `probe_resolve_lifecycle_timed`) is unit-proven by two inline `conductor-run` lifecycle tests.

- **Run report envelope** → golden test (insta) of the canonical per-check shape shared by Markdown report + `runs.db` row + JSONL journal; artifact-sanitization assertion (no host paths / struct names).

- **OTLP egress liveness check** → transport-connectability probe; a refused transport surfaces as `Result::Err` (harness fault), NOT a verdict (Vector 5) — optionally exercised deterministically without a live Pulse via turmoil 0.7.2 partition/refusal injection.
- **Pinned MCP contract manifest** → required-tool-set match assertion vs. `contracts/` (mismatch ⇒ `blocked`).

- **Cross-surface parity** → an IN-PROCESS arm calling `conductor_run::{preflight, drive_run}` — the composition `conductor suite` drives in production (`drive_run`'s first production caller since 2026-10-12) — and the assert_cmd CLI subprocess run, both pointed at the same `assert_fs::TempDir` file `runs.db` via a non-default `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`, assert identical envelope verdict/state/seed for the same scenario+seed (Critical Path 7 / test-scope Sec 5 cross-surface-coordination trigger). The leg lives in `crates/conductor-cli/tests/cross_surface_parity.rs` — the package declaring the `conductor` bin, so its CLI arm binds through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_conductor` — a package with no `tauri` dependency in any section, as measured at `2026-09-02-mutation-tier-restored-for-conductor-tauri`.

- **The GUI test-harness leg retired with the window (2026-10-11):** the `Channel`-frame-sequence assertion, the webview render leg and the mock-runtime command-dispatch tier have no surface; the in-process ↔ CLI parity half stands as landed (above).
(See `## 11. Test Anti-Patterns` § Integration for integration-level bans.)

title: 6. E2E Test Strategy

body: _[Included — the cli surface is agent-drivable.]_
**Drivers per surface** (from research Per-Surface Driver category):
| Surface | Driver | Mode | Notes |

| cli (`conductor-cli` / `agent-run`) | assert_cmd 2.1.2 + predicates 3 (`Command::cargo_bin("conductor")`) + assert_fs 1 sandbox | direct subprocess | release gate; asserts exit code + `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[HOLD]`/`[BLOCKED]`/`[MANUAL]`/`[RESIDUAL]` labels — the closed per-P-ID set — plus the run-level non-lamp caption SET — `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` (the SUT-load-envelope caption) and `[PRECONDITION]` (the `conductor preconditions` probe caption), both printed outside the lamp column and neither a `ReportState` — the first where a run breaches the load envelope, the second where the probe reports an unmet subject (both NO_COLOR-stable) + `runs.db` row + JSONL journal; stdin closed proves **no-hang / exit-0 only** — with no live Pulse the preflight blocks and `execute_scenario` returns on the Blocked spine BEFORE the hold, so this leg never reaches an interactive prompt (measured 2026-08-22: a fresh `agent-latest.jsonl` carried ZERO resolution witnesses, ending at `preflight blocked: MCP read-back path unreachable`). The never-blocks property is proven at the UNIT tier (`headless_never_blocks_under_paused_clock`; `resolve_kind_agent_mode_overrides_an_attended_tty`) |

| ipc-internal (MCP read-back) | the hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp` over stdio (CI); live `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar (local gate) | direct IPC client | CI leg fully runnable via stub; live read-back leg gated on `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` (`workflow_dispatch`/local) |

(Skip surfaces flagged "untestable" in test-scope Section 1: live Pulse + its (plaintext) `corpus.db`, `OsKeychainBackend`, `drive+observe` human visual judgment, `static-only` Pulse capabilities — no driver assigned.)

**Selector strategy:** role/text/data-testid + brand anchors (upstream-context Layout Templates Signature Placements + Design System brand anchors) — text-paired status labels `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[HOLD]`/`[MANUAL]`/`[RESIDUAL]`/`[BLOCKED]` (the closed per-P-ID set) plus the run-level non-lamp caption SET — `[ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT]` (the SUT-load-envelope caption) and `[PRECONDITION]` (the `conductor preconditions` probe caption), both printed outside the lamp column and neither a `ReportState` (color never sole signal, so text/role selectors are reliable per the Color-Only a11y rule), `role="alertdialog"` on the operator-pause dialog, `aria-live` HOLD/verdict announcements, signature heading text "HOLD — operator pause", and mono P-ID tokens (the manifest's accepted set) for coverage-matrix/report rows. NO xpath, NO hashed-CSS-class selectors.
**Critical path scenarios** (translated from test-scope Section 4):

title: Scenario: Headless deterministic scenario run with MCP read-back (`error-baseline-spike`)

data.head: #### Scenario: Headless deterministic scenario run with MCP read-back (`error-baseline-spike`)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** cli + ipc-internal (MCP read-back) + persistent-storage

- **Steps:**
  1. Preflight gate returns `ready:true` (the hand-rolled MCP stub in CI; live Pulse on local gate) — reached through `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} boot`, or by invoking `conductor preflight --json` directly (§3).
  2. assert_cmd: `Command::cargo_bin("conductor")` `.arg("run").arg("error-baseline-spike").arg("--seed").arg("<s>")` with `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` → `assert_fs::TempDir`, stdin closed.
  3. Re-run with the same seed.

- **Verification signal:**
  - `.assert().success()` (exit 0); stdout shows `[RESIDUAL]` — the family is DECLARE-ONLY (its read-back token checks retired 2026-08-18: no surface can carry them under deterministic L4 — the degraded report renders fixture constants and no cue kind; the evidence count reads a `span_ids` field no producer populates), so the row is a reported state, never a hard fail.
  - `runs.db` row: `verdict` null, `state="KnownResidual"` (degraded read-back), `latency_ms` recorded against the scenario's declared `slo_tier` (bound-parameter `SELECT`).
  - The live claim grades at the HARVEST tier: Pulse's `triage.cue.emit` lines (kind `error_rate_spike` · priority `suggested` · magnitude/confidence/`suppression_bypassed`) harvested at the `conductor-run` unit tier in `crates/conductor-run/tests/baseline_harvest.rs` — the `storm_harvest.rs` precedent.
  - `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` exists; its envelope LINE parses to the envelope, and any per-check lines parse to the `CheckRecord` shape (`serde_json` / `jq -e`).
  - MCP read-back (`query_incident_list`/`retrieve_report`) confirms Pulse's reaction (live leg) / stub canary (CI leg).
  - Same-seed re-run yields identical stream shape (insta golden on the journal, redacting `run_id`/timestamps).

- **Cleanup:** `TempDir` drop removes journal + report + DB rows. (`connection-lifecycle` is DECLARE-ONLY since 2026-08-19: the family's four read-back checks retired with the measurement recorded in each TOML header — connection state reaches no MCP read-back surface (Pulse's FSM rides the TauRPC resolver, the broadcast topic and tracing lines only) — its rows landing `verdict` null / `state="KnownResidual"`, non-Blocked, `latency_ms` against each declared `slo_tier`; the live walk/conflict claims grade at the HARVEST tier in `crates/conductor-run/tests/connection_harvest.rs`. `pii-scrub` is DECLARE-ONLY since 2026-08-19: all five `[[expected]]` read-back checks retired with the measurement recorded in the scenario TOML header — vacuous `Absent` / structural-fail `Contains` under deterministic L4 — its row landing `verdict` null / `state="KnownResidual"`, non-Blocked, `latency_ms` against its declared `slo_tier`; the live scrub claim grades at the HARVEST tier in `crates/conductor-run/tests/pii_harvest.rs`, the `storm/baseline/restart_harvest.rs` precedent.)

title: Scenario: Fingerprint-storm (fault-injection burst + read-back)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** cli + ipc-internal + persistent-storage; exercises `conductor-faults` fingerprints
- **Steps:** 1. preflight `ready:true` (via `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} boot`, or `conductor preflight --json` directly — §3). 2. `conductor run fingerprint-storm --seed <s>`.

- **Verification signal:** exit 0; per-P-ID `verdict`/`state` rows in `runs.db`; the envelope's `fingerprints` field PRESENT and SUT-populated under deterministic L4 (fed from `fingerprint_refs`: the fixture's `evidence_refs` fill it with a constant `det-*` triple — measured 2026-08-18 at SUT HEAD `efabe8e`, payload-invariant — and at HEAD `83d4060` it also carries each incident's triggering-cue fingerprint, which varies with what Conductor emitted (measured 2026-09-10; arch [Read-Back Dependency Posture]); no shipped check keys on the array, and it is never an empty-literal value pin); the scenario's read-back token checks are DECLARE-ONLY (retired 2026-08-18, when `retrieve_report` read back `degraded_mode` and its markdown carried no scenario token: a `Contains` always failed, an `Absent` passed VACUOUSLY). `degraded_mode` is a per-read-back property, never a mode-wide one: an incident read back `degraded_mode: false` under deterministic L4 at Pulse S `03ec944`, as measured at `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-02-p-075-assert-round-against-pulse/evidence/p075-leg.txt`. Since 2026-10-02 one test-tier check computes the emitted fingerprint's membership in `fingerprint_refs` — `lifecycle_harvest::p075_round_assertion_1_read_back_content_fidelity`, over the P-075 round's digest-pinned capture, which commits only the boolean. The live proof is the test-only harvest of Pulse's own `triage.pattern.storm.detected` line — `cue_kind = "retry_storm"` · `severity_hint` · `occurrence_count` · `fingerprint_hex` — asserted at the `conductor-run` unit tier (`crates/conductor-run/tests/storm_harvest.rs`) on the operator/live gate.

- **Real-model interpretation leg (P-018 · P-031 · P-033 · P-034 · P-044, the scenario's `p_ids`; a sibling leg of this scenario, not an eighth `####` scenario, and no §9 stage-table row — 2026-09-22):** `scenarios/real-model-interpretation.toml` (`l4_posture = "real-model"`, declare-only from birth) runs only through `agent-run run --live real-model` (§3; operator-gated, driven only as the pre-stated series of `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` — and once, on 2026-10-07, as that contract's pre-registered capture run, which states no verdict — never CI). Its interpretation claim grades at the HARVEST tier in `crates/conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs` (default suite) over the drive's scrubbed capture, against the grading rule stated before the drive — the rule's span is recorded into the capture ahead of the leg and asserted to predate it: `Identified → (Pass, Pass)`, `NotIdentified → (CalibrationRegion, ManualCheck)`, and an outcome with nothing to grade (no ranked hypothesis, no attributable incident, a failed read-back) → `(null, Blocked)`. Since 2026-09-29 the rule also grades P-031 `structure`, P-034 `steps`, P-044 `retrieval` and the `canary:` attempts, APPENDED below the recorded 2026-09-23 rule, which the harvest asserts is a byte-exact prefix (P-033's rule provably unedited). Synthetic arms cover every outcome plus the extraction, token-surface and host-path-mask arms and, since 2026-09-30, the workspace-key mask and rendering-witness arms, and since 2026-10-01 the arms pairing Pulse's `interpretation.incident.skipped` line — its `skip_reason` rides each `canary:` line as a trailing field, recorded and never graded (the rule reads the first token). Every committed capture is held by a sha256 digest pin over its LF-normalized content (the test-only `sha2` dev-dependency) and graded from the file only after the digest matches: a one-byte tamper arm shows the pin can fail, naming the file and never the text, and a source arm holds that no committed capture text sits in test source; the graded 2026-09-23 capture is an elided copy (its storm `fingerprint_hex` tokens printed `<fingerprint>`), the frozen 2026-09-22 file since elided in place (2026-10-02, the founder's ruling; a recorded exception to frozen evidence never being edited) and byte-identical to it. Since 2026-10-02 `elide_fingerprints` elides every `fingerprint_hex=` value whatever its class — the 2026-10-01 d3 capture's all-digit prefix re-elided and its pin moved, the 2026-10-01 arm asserting zero for every drive — and a population arm (`every_committed_capture_carries_no_un_elided_fingerprint_value`) holds every committed `rm-capture*.txt` at zero un-elided keyed values and a fixed point of the elision, the population pinned by count, beside its inverse control (`un_elided_keyed_values_counts_a_planted_value`). The 2026-09-23 drive (run `2026-09-23T07-39-39-845`) graded `NoAttributableIncident → Blocked`, model-side, so neither a pickup nor a formation figure was measured; the 2026-09-29 series ran five counted drives and graded one `NotIdentified → (CalibrationRegion, ManualCheck)` (`v3-09` not met; cause in that chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`); the 2026-09-30 series (three drives on one fresh letters-only data dir, Pulse `fcc31b2`) graded none — d1 canary-blocked, d2 and d3 scenario-side dismissals — so `v3-09` stays not met (that chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`); the 2026-10-01 series (three drives on one fresh letters-only data dir, Pulse `a2addb3`, the rule byte-identical) graded two — d1 `Identified`, d3 `NotIdentified`; d2's scenario spans were refused by Pulse (`append_failed`, its span identity replaying d1's inside Pulse's buffer window) — so `v3-09` stays not met, while beside that verdict the real model surfaced 6 of 6 canary digests and the scenario's digest both times it formed (that chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). That replay is repaid since `2026-10-01-per-run-span-identity-in-the-real-model-harness`: the production path re-keys every trace export's span identity under a per-execution `std::time` salt (`execute_scenario`'s `emitted_ms` → `Dispatcher::connect(…, Some(_))` → `conductor_emit::rekey_trace_identity`), content staying a pure function of seed — held at the dispatcher integration tier by `dispatch_wire`'s `two_same_seed_drives_inside_one_window_share_no_span_identity` (RED with the re-key removed) and live by the `span_landing_live` witness (two same-seed drives 253 507 ms apart inside Pulse's 600 s retention, zero refused appends; that chunk's `evidence/witness-ledger.md`). The 2026-10-06 series (three drives in one sitting, Pulse `5f77859`, its shipped model `gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M`, the rule byte-identical; the first series on the Linux dev host) graded all three — d1 `Identified`, d2 `Identified`, d3 `NotIdentified` — so `v3-09` stays not met (`v3_09_is_not_met_by_the_2026_10_06_series`; no ref test, no fourth drive), while beside that verdict the real model surfaced 6 of 6 classified canary digests and the scenario's digest in all three drives, and every rank-1 statement carried a retry token (that chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). The 2026-10-07 series (three drives in one sitting, Pulse `f70be92`, prompt `v2.6`, the same model, the design and the rule byte-identical) graded all three — d1 `Identified`, d2 `Identified`, d3 `NotIdentified` — so `v3-09` stays not met (`v3_09_is_not_met_by_the_2026_10_07_series`; no ref test, no fourth drive): the same split on the same drive as the 2026-10-06 series at prompt `v2.5`, which three drives per series do not separate, while beside that verdict the real model again surfaced 6 of 6 classified canary digests and the scenario's digest in all three drives, and every rank-1 statement carried a retry token (the `2026-10-07-a-fifth-pre-registered-real-model-series-for-v3-09` chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). The 2026-10-07 capture run (three drives in one sitting, the 2026-10-07 series' Pulse, model, prompt and byte-identical rule; pre-registered as a capture, its contract section applying no pass condition) states NO `v3-09` verdict: its three drives each attributed an incident on the read-back route and read `Identified`, recorded as observations and held by the `…2026_10_07_capture_run…` harvest tests, which import no verdict arm and carry no ref test — so `v3-09` stays not met on the 2026-10-07 series' record (the `2026-10-07-a-capture-run-records-the-prompt-the-model-received-in-each-drive` chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). The 2026-10-07 sixth series (three drives in one sitting on 2026-10-08, on one fresh letters-only data dir, Pulse `9bfefb8`, the same model, prompt `v2.6`, the design and the rule byte-identical, pre-registered as the last series with its stop rule fixed before the launch) graded all three — d1 `Identified`, d2 `Identified`, d3 `Identified`, the real-model and launch witnesses holding on each — so `v3-09` is met on those three drives and read no wider (`v3_09_is_met_by_the_2026_10_07_sixth_series`; the ref test `v3_09_ref_identified_with_the_real_model_witnesses_2026_10_07_sixth`; no re-fire, no fourth drive). The pass is not attributed to the Pulse-side change at `9bfefb8`: no prompt was recorded, the capture's corpus-row line counts candidates before the selection, and the 2026-10-07 capture run on the `f70be92` build also read three `Identified`. Beside the verdict, Pulse's own log shows every canary storm surfaced (9 of 9) and the scenario's digest surfaced in all three drives; the captures of d1 and d2 print a third `canary:` line reading `pipeline-fault`, a reading of the capture's own pairing window that Pulse's log does not bear out and that no grade and no re-fire read (as measured at the `2026-10-07-a-sixth-pre-registered-real-model-series-for-v3-09` chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). Since 2026-10-08 (`2026-10-08-capture-canary-pairing-window-corrective`; no drive, and those captures keep the tokens they printed) the capture's canary pairing reads a selected digest's inference across the emission instant: the instant selects the cue-bearing ticks that print — a tick whose own stamp parses and is strictly earlier than it — and no longer drops the lines stamped at or after it. The corrective is pinned at the harvest tier by the default-suite arms of `real_model_grading/canary_pairing.rs`, a child module of the `real_model_harvest` target, over in-test lines built from the sixth series' recorded stamps and line kinds: the d1 and d2 shapes read `surfaced` with `parse=ok created=false deduped=true`, the scenario's own storm digest never prints as a canary, a tick stamped at or after the instant (the d3 shape) or one the instant cannot place gets no line, and `the_pre_fix_window_read_the_same_shapes_as_a_pipeline_fault` keeps the earlier reading reproducible from the same lines; the capture's own call is held by a source literal and by the `--features live-pulse` lint line, never by a run. Limit of the proof: a failing-first reading on those in-test lines (that chunk's `evidence/failing-first.md`); what the capture binary prints on a next real drive is unmeasured until someone drives it. The series set is the posture contract's dated series sections, never a count restated here; its capture-run section is not a series.
- **Cleanup:** `TempDir` drop.

title: Scenario: Restart-suppression incl. one bypass case

data.head: #### Scenario: Restart-suppression incl. one bypass case

body: - **Surfaces involved:** cli + ipc-internal + persistent-storage

- **Steps:** 1. preflight `ready:true` (via `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} boot`, or `conductor preflight --json` directly — §3). 2. `SCENARIO=restart-suppression bash scripts/agent-run.sh run` (no `SEED` — the TOML-declared seed 4317015 governs; fresh data dir per the live-leg recipe).

- **Verification signal:** declare-only row — `verdict` null + `state="KnownResidual"` (non-Blocked, never a hard-fail exit) with `latency_ms` recorded against the declared `slo_tier` (`<90s`); journal + `runs.db` row assert the deterministic stream. The live suppression/bypass claim grades as hard pass/fail at the HARVEST tier in `crates/conductor-run/tests/restart_harvest.rs` at the `conductor-run` unit tier (the `baseline_harvest.rs`/`storm_harvest.rs` precedent), pinning verbatim leg lines: the P-015 restart pair (`triage.pattern.restart_emit`, `gap_seconds` > 20, one per gap/resume cycle), the P-016 drop→keep crossing (an in-window not-bypassed `triage.cue.suppression_check` below the 30-sample cutoff with NO matching `triage.cue.emit`, then the same service's cues plain-kept at ≥ 30), and the P-057 absolute arm (`triage.cue.suppression_bypass` reason `absolute` + the kept young bypassed cue). The relative-magnitude arm is unreachable at shipped SUT constants (α-ratio = the bypass multiplier; recorded, not asserted); `persistence_seconds` is the service's cumulative sample count, not a spike duration; the `triage.cue.tick` counters are redacted live and carry no evidence.
- **Cleanup:** `TempDir` drop.

title: Scenario: Severity-lifecycle full pass (auto-resolve + resolution summary)

data.head: #### Scenario: Severity-lifecycle full pass (auto-resolve + resolution summary)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** cli + persistent-storage (no ipc-internal leg — the lifecycle write is exercised out-of-band by `probe_resolve_lifecycle`, never inside `execute_scenario`; see the `mark_incident_resolved` note in §5)

- **Steps:** 1. preflight `ready:true` (via `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} boot`, or `conductor preflight --json` directly — §3). 2. `SCENARIO=<name> scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} run` for each of the FIVE family scenarios — `incident-auto-resolution` · `severity-tier-autonomous` · `severity-tier-suggested` · `severity-tier-curious` · `ack-cooldown`. There is no scenario named `severity-lifecycle` (the family is five separately-named TOMLs), and `--seed` rides only an explicitly set `SEED` (§3 precedence).

- **Verification signal:** DECLARE-ONLY since 2026-08-21 — all five TOMLs carry zero `[[expected]]`, so each row lands exit 0 / `verdict` null / `state="KnownResidual"` with `latency_ms` against its declared `slo_tier`. The live claims grade at the HARVEST tier (`crates/conductor-run/tests/severity_harvest.rs`, the storm/baseline/restart/pii/connection precedent): auto-resolve is asserted HARD on the instant Pulse's active set EMPTIES (`incidents.list_active.request` `item_count`) against the 120s window + 30s observer tick, plus the same-fingerprint retrigger reading `created=true, deduped=false` — Pulse dedups against the ACTIVE set alone, so that pair is an independent resolution proof. Two witnesses do NOT work and are recorded, not asserted: `triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick`'s `resolved_count`/`evaluated_count`/`duration_ms` render `"<redacted>"` on the wire (so the tick proves the observer RAN, never that it resolved), and P-059's resolution summary is unreachable under deterministic L4. Pairing a creation with the FIRST active-count drop measures the preflight canary's own resolution, so that mis-pairing is pinned as a negative test. Severity *choice* stays CalibrationRegion, graded at the cue tier over Pulse's `priority` labels (report-for-human, NOT a non-zero exit — Creator Brief assertion-policy split).
- **Cleanup:** `TempDir` drop.

title: Scenario: Known-residual classification (P-032)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** cli + ipc-internal (`retrieve_report` with `degraded_mode`) + persistent-storage; runs inside a real git workspace (P-032 environment requirement)

- **Steps:** 1. preflight `ready:true` (via `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} boot`, or `conductor preflight --json` directly — §3) in a real git workspace with known recent commits. 2. `conductor run P-032 --seed <s>`.
