title: Scenario: Coverage-matrix completeness gate (static)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** cli + persistent-storage (`coverage-matrix.md` artifact)
- **Steps:** 1. `conductor` generates/validates `coverage-matrix.md`.

- **Verification signal:** the matrix enumerates every capability in the SUT capability manifest with zero unclassified entries; a missing `P-XXX` fails the gate (non-zero exit) — "A P-XXX missing from the matrix is a defect" (Creator Brief; "0.1.0 done" definition). Asserted (shipped 2026-09-06) by `cargo nextest run -p conductor-report --test coverage_gate --profile ci`, in three arms: `check_sut_drift` over the manifest loaded at runtime from its conventional repo path via `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` (never the CWD-relative `default_path()`, which cannot resolve from a test binary's package-root CWD) returns `Ok`; a negative arm removes each classified row IN TURN from the REAL `coverage_matrix()` and asserts `Err(CoreError::SutDrift)` naming the dropped id; and the committed `coverage-matrix.md` is byte-equal to `CoverageMatrix::render()`. The retired `assert_cmd` exit-code + insta-golden / **static row-count** mechanism is superseded — a row count is the literal-count form this same path's Verification signal forbids.

- **Scenario-backing leg (second axis):** classification completeness is necessary but not sufficient — a capability classified `Auto` claims Conductor asserts its reaction, which is false if no scenario names it. Assert `check_scenario_backing` over the committed classification + catalog against the `UNBACKED_AUTO` pin by **exact-set equality in both directions**, so the gate fails on a new unbacked `Auto` claim, on a pinned id a scenario now covers (pin rot), and on a pinned id that lost its `Auto` classification. Only `Auto` participates. Unit-tier over committed artifacts (no live Pulse), so it runs in CI like its `check_sut_drift` sibling.

- **Scenario-assertion audit leg (the second static gate over committed data, 2026-09-16):** `crates/conductor-core/tests/scenario_audit_gate.rs`, asserted by `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core --test scenario_audit_gate --profile ci` and CI-enforced by the `.github/workflows/ci.yml` step `Scenario-assertion audit gate` (its own named step after `Coverage-completeness gate`, a presence guard on the ledger then the target, `continue-on-error: false`). It grades the committed `contracts/scenario-audit-ledger.toml` against the catalog on two axes — scenarios carrying a live `[[expected]]` block, and scenarios whose summed phase `gap_ms` exceeds their declared tier's `SloTier::deadline_ms()` — by exact-set equality in BOTH directions (`unpinned` / `rotted` / `lost_subject`), with no literal-count predicate anywhere, the same ban this scenario's Verification signal already states. Its can-fail demonstration is in-suite: six negative arms, each mutating the REAL committed ledger and asserting the error names the offending scenario, plus a closed-set arm (an out-of-set tier must fail to deserialize) and a sweep control proving the comment-marker-stripped wrap-tolerant form detects a gloss the plain single-line search misses. A ledger row's `discriminates` flag is RECORDED, never graded — whether a token depends on the scenario's own stimulus is a SUT-behaviour claim §11 routes to the live/operator gate, so a static check must not pretend to measure it. This is a sibling leg of this static-gate scenario, not an eighth `####` scenario, and it takes no §9 stage-table row — the `2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate` operator resolution.

- **Repository-hygiene legs (2026-09-24 — static gates, but not over committed data):** two further sibling legs with the same step shape — each its own `rust`-job step with a presence guard that emits `::error::` and exits 1, no `continue-on-error`, no `if:`. (1) **Secret-scan leg:** `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core --test secret_scan_gate --profile ci`, step `Secret-scan gate`, guarded on a non-empty `git ls-files`. Its subject is `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, so a new file is scanned before it is committed. Where the workspace root holds no `.git` entry at all (a VCS-less copy, such as cargo-mutants' default copy), the gate skips with one path-free stderr line, `secret-scan gate: skipped — no git repository at the workspace root`, and passes; the check is `Path::exists` before any spawn, so a `.git` FILE (a worktree, a submodule) counts as a repository, and a listing failure inside a repository still fails the gate ("the gate has no subject"). Both arms are pinned in-suite over runtime-built scratch dirs (`a_tree_with_no_git_entry_is_skipped_without_a_spawn`, `a_listing_failure_inside_a_repository_still_fails`), and the CI step's presence guard is unchanged. It applies content rules plus a secret-file-name class against an exact-set allowlist graded in both directions (an unallowlisted hit fails, and so does an entry matching nothing). A hit renders as a repo-relative `path:line` with its rule and never the matched text. (2) **Workflow env-context leg:** `cargo nextest run -p conductor-core --test workflow_env_gate --profile ci`, step `Workflow env-context gate`, guarded on `.github/workflows/*.yml`. It checks every `${{ env.X }}` and bare `if: env.X` read against that file's `env:` keys plus its `GITHUB_ENV`-written keys, and fails naming the file, line and key. A `GITHUB_ENV context probe` step pair re-measures that admission on every run. Both legs prove they can fail in-suite on inputs built at test time — runtime-assembled secret samples, in-memory workflow text — with no committed fixture, and both run again inside the Unit stage's `nextest run --workspace --profile ci`, so neither takes a §9 stage-table row.
- **Cleanup:** none (read-only over the committed catalog).

title: Scenario: In-process ↔ headless parity

body: - **Surfaces involved:** cli + in-process core

- **Steps:**
  1. CLI leg: assert_cmd `conductor run <scenario> --seed <s>` → file `runs.db` in `assert_fs::TempDir`.
  2. In-process core leg (CI): `conductor_run::{preflight, drive_run}` for the same scenario+seed, same `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`, driven directly.

- **Verification signal:** the in-process core run's `runs.db` envelope (`verdict`/`state`/`seed`) is identical to the headless `conductor run` envelope for the same deterministic-posture scenario+seed (a real-model-posture scenario is excluded by design — Critical Path 7's scope); emission journal written per run from both paths (Critical Path 7 / cross-surface-coordination trigger). The control-panel-LAUNCHED half retired with the window (2026-10-11).
- **Cleanup:** `TempDir` drop.
(7 scenarios — the test-scope Section 4 maximum.)
(See `## 11. Test Anti-Patterns` § E2E for E2E-level bans.)

title: 7. Test Data & Fixtures

body: _[ALL tiers]_

**Fixture library:** rstest 0.26.1 (`#[fixture]` / `#[rstest]` / `#[case]` / `#[once]` / `#[future]`+`#[awt]`) — the dev-dependency proc-macro layer over cargo-nextest; results surface through the runner exit code + JUnit.
**Seed strategies:**
| Data type | Strategy | Lifecycle |

| Persistent data — `runs.db` rows | rstest `#[once]` schema fixture + rusqlite `open_in_memory()`; `assert_fs::TempDir` file DB for cross-process | per-test fresh (in-memory) / per-cross-process-test (TempDir) |

| Fixture files (scenario config) | checked-in declarative serde+garde config under `scenarios/`, each file naming its P-IDs (a P-ID may be named by several files); valid + invalid matrices | per-suite (committed) |
| Randomized data | proptest 1.9.0 strategies with seed control; counterexamples persisted to `proptest-regressions/` | seeded per test, replayed deterministically |
| Synthetic telemetry stream | seeded `conductor-timeline` generator (`#[fixture]`); same scenario+seed ⇒ same stream shape | seeded per test |
| Time-sensitive data | tokio `start_paused = true` + `tokio::time::advance` (scheduling only); journal stamps from `std::time::SystemTime` | injected per test |

| Golden artifacts | insta snapshots in two families: the **envelope/journal** goldens (Run-report envelope + JSONL journal, redacting `run_id`/`journal_emitted_at`/`read_back_observed_at`) and the **seeded stream** goldens committed per-crate under `<crate>/tests/snapshots/`, one file per test-file family × seed (`replay__*` transitions · `pacing__*` emission stream · `dispatch_wire__*` dispatched-wire projection). Stream goldens carry no wall-clock field to redact — the dispatch-tier projection EXCLUDES every `*_time_unix_nano` rather than masking it, and the `dispatch_wire__*` goldens drive the UNSALTED dispatcher (`identity_salt: None`), the tier where span identity stays seed-pure; production identity is salted per execution, and a salted test passes a fixed salt | committed; CI fail-don't-write (never `cargo insta review`) |
**Self-bootstrapping requirement:**

- Tests MUST seed their own data from the sanctioned provenance SET — the seeded `conductor-timeline` generator, rstest fixtures, and the **committed fixture family** — the SET of committed fixture trees, crate-local `tests/fixtures/` trees plus (since 2026-09-30) `scripts/fixtures/mutation-gate/`, the first member outside a crate (read-only fixture tallies with `roster.toml` · `roster-bad.toml` · `arms.toml`, consumed by `scripts/mutation-gate.py selftest` through the gate's own grading function); today `crates/conductor-core/tests/fixtures/` (read-only, consumed in-test through the production sweep `conductor_core::carries_retired_gloss`, whose MEANING — that it carries the gloss WRAPPED across two comment lines, so the comment-strip-and-join is load-bearing and a plain single-line search misses it — is pinned by the round-trip in `scenario_audit_gate.rs`). Beside that family, the real-model harvest reads committed live-leg capture EVIDENCE under a chunk's `evidence/` tree — read-only, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`-anchored, each file checked against its sha256 digest pin before any grade reads it (since 2026-09-30); a capture is evidence, never a fixture copied elsewhere. NO "developer pre-populates `runs.db`" (test-scope Sec 3: "no developer-seeded DB") — the ban stands: a committed journal is a reviewable declarative artifact read through the production reader, not a hand-populated database.

- A committed fixture carries its MEANING under test, not just its parseability: a round-trip through the production reader/writer — the SET, one per committed fixture; a Rust test for each crate-local tree, and for `scripts/fixtures/mutation-gate/` the gate's `selftest` verb (each `[[arm]]` graded through the production grading function and asserted on verdict, a named finding, the finding count and no absolute path, beside a known-bad control proving the harness can fail; an operator-local Python entry, never a CI step) — `conductor-core`'s `scenario_audit_gate::the_sweep_sees_a_wrapped_gloss_the_plain_form_misses` (`tests/fixtures/wrapped-gloss.toml` through the production sweep `carries_retired_gloss`, asserting BOTH that the stripped form detects the wrapped gloss and that a plain single-line search does not — the second half is what keeps the fixture proving the comment-strip-and-join is load-bearing rather than decorative) — asserts the properties its consumers depend on, so a reader- or sweep-side change that leaves the file parseable but semantically inert fails (at `cargo nextest` for the crate-local tree, at `selftest` for the mutation-gate tallies).
- `boot`/test setup creates the in-memory or `TempDir` `runs.db` schema automatically (`#[once]` fixture); scenario config files are the committed declarative fixtures.
**Test data lifecycle:**
- **Per-test:** isolated state — in-memory `runs.db` per test (parallel-safe under nextest's per-process model); no shared mutable fixtures across parallel tests.
- **Per-session:** `cleanup` / `TempDir` drop removes `runs/` artifacts + `runs.db` rows.
- **CI:** ephemeral GitHub Actions runner per pipeline run; live-Pulse scenarios excluded from CI (operator/local gate).
(See `## 11. Test Anti-Patterns` § Test Data for data bans.)

title: 8. Mocking & Stubbing Discipline

body: _[Included — integration tests present.]_
**What to mock:**

- The `andromeda-pulse-mcp` MCP sidecar / live Pulse — mock with the hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp` binary over the sidecar stdio (in-process duplex transport for verdict-logic unit tests; the same stub spawned as a child for the spawn/`.env()` injection-rejection path). The live sidecar is local-gate-only; CI uses the stub.

- Time — `tokio::time` virtual clock via `#[tokio::test(flavor="current_thread", start_paused=true)]` + `tokio::time::advance` for `conductor-timeline` scheduling determinism. NOT for journal/report stamps (those use `std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant` — security anti-pattern bans virtual-clock stamps).

- Random sources — seeded generators (`conductor-timeline` seed; proptest strategies with `proptest-regressions/` persistence). The per-execution span-identity salt is INJECTED, never read inside the primitive: `Dispatcher::connect`'s required `identity_salt: Option<u64>` takes `None` or a fixed `Some(N)` in tests and only production `execute_scenario` passes its `std::time` `emitted_ms`; the re-key primitive is held at the `conductor-emit` unit tier and the two-drive identity property at the dispatcher integration tier against the loopback `TraceService` stub.

- OTLP/gRPC egress (optional, deterministic) — turmoil 0.7.2 single-threaded seeded network simulation for transport partition/latency/refusal faults (assert refusal ⇒ `Result::Err`, never false Pass); OR a hand-rolled in-process tonic `TraceServiceServer`/`LogsServiceServer` on `127.0.0.1:0` for byte-level egress tests.
**What NOT to mock:**
- Pure functions in seams under test — timeline scheduling, fault generators, garde validation, verdict mapping, envelope serialization (test directly).
- The DB at integration level — use rusqlite `open_in_memory()` / `assert_fs::TempDir` file DB (bundled SQLite needs no external service), NOT a mock.
- Code paths the agent verifies end-to-end — the cli release-gate scenarios go through assert_cmd against the real binary (Section 6).
- Live Pulse's reaction — genuinely out-of-process, local-gate-only; do NOT fake it as a CI verdict (the stub canary proves wiring, not Pulse's behavior).
**Mocking libraries (specific, from research):**
| Concern | Library | Pattern |

| MCP sidecar / process | the hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp` (no `#[tool]` macro exists in it) | in-process duplex transport (fast) + the stub spawned as a child binary (spawn path); DI of transport, no monkey-patch |
| Time mocking | tokio 1.52.3 `test-util` | `start_paused = true` + `tokio::time::advance(Duration)`; DI-free, no monkey-patch |
| gRPC/transport fault server | turmoil 0.7.2 (or in-process tonic server) | seeded deterministic partition/latency/refusal on one thread; OR `TraceServiceServer` on `127.0.0.1:0` |
| HTTP fake server | wiremock-rs 0.6.5 | **NOT applicable** to the gRPC egress (do NOT force-fit onto `tonic`); reserved for any future HTTP smoke surface only |

**Anti-monkey-patching:** prefer dependency injection (stdio-transport injection into the hand-rolled JSON-RPC client; the built-in tokio virtual clock; ephemeral-port tonic server) over runtime patching of production code — matching the research-targets preference.
(See `## 11. Test Anti-Patterns` § Mocking for mocking bans.)

title: 9. CI Integration

body: _[ALL tiers]_
**Platform:** GitHub Actions (upstream-context arch CI/CD Platform).
**Pipeline structure:**
| Stage | Runs | Parallel | Cache |

| Lint | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` + the feature-gated `cargo clippy -p conductor-verify --features stub-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p conductor-run --features live-pulse --all-targets -- -D warnings` (all three in `agent-run run`'s bundled default, reached through the dogfood step) + `cargo fmt --check` | n/a | `~/.cargo` + `target/` keyed on `Cargo.lock` |
| Supply-chain audit | `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check` (advisories/licenses/bans/sources) | yes | RustSec advisory-db cache |
| Unit | `agent-run.{sh,ps1} run --unit` → `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` | yes (nextest per-test process model) | `Cargo.lock`-keyed |
| Doctest | `cargo test --workspace --doc` | yes | `Cargo.lock`-keyed |
| Integration | `agent-run.{sh,ps1} run --integration` → the hand-rolled MCP stub + in-memory/`TempDir` `runs.db` | partial | `Cargo.lock`-keyed |
| Coverage report | `cargo llvm-cov nextest --lcov --output-path lcov.info` (+ `--cobertura`) | n/a | `Cargo.lock`-keyed |
| Quality gates | `--fail-under-lines` threshold + audit-green + zero-retry check | n/a | n/a |

**Live-Pulse scenarios:** the dynamic end-to-end proof (live Pulse, `mcp-server` feature + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` + matching `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`) is an explicit **operator/local gate via `workflow_dispatch`, `scripts/agent-run.sh` — including its composed `run --live` stage (2026-09-06), which drives the feature-gated targets in ONE invocation and is still never a CI gate, and its `run --live real-model` selector (2026-09-22), which drives only the `real_model_live` capture — its `rule_record` before each drive's leg, the capture after: driven only as the pre-stated series of `contracts/pulse-real-model-leg-posture.md` (fixed before its first drive; every drive recorded and never replaced — only a Conductor-side environment or pipeline fault may be re-fired, once) — and once, on 2026-10-07, as that contract's pre-registered capture run, which states no verdict and re-fires only as its own section says — its pickup recorded per attributing drive as a measurement and never budgeted, and no real-model formation figure contracted (the 2026-09-23 drive graded `NoAttributableIncident`, a model-side block, and measured neither; every capture that attributes an incident prints its pickup, as measured at the series chunks' committed captures) — **and whose auto-resolve leg carries a SUT-UPTIME precondition the other legs do not: it needs an EMPTY active set at read-back, which holds only while Pulse is inside the emitting service's one-hour bootstrap window.** Past it, `service_went_silent` cues raise NEW autonomous incidents during the leg's own silent phase, so no window length reaches the arm; inside it, the window must still clear 150 s (120 s idle + up to a full 30 s observer tick) measured from the LAST incident the leg's own preflight formed, which can be more than one. Neither is a source-delta fact — an unchanged tree grades differently by SUT uptime alone, so this leg is not run-stable and must not be read as one **UNDER THE DEFAULT WINDOW**. That default is a boot-time posture, not a constant: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` is resolved once at Pulse's boot (`Thresholds::from_env`) and Conductor never sets or reads it, so the arm's reachability is bounded by the window IN FORCE AT BOOT. The suite now launches Pulse under a stretched boot-wide window, which disarms the silence evaluator for the whole run; confirm which posture actually booted by grepping Pulse's log for the TARGET `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override` (level WARN, `reason="env_override"`, `resolved_seconds`) — never for the emitting function name, which appears nowhere in the log. **The posture removes cause (a) only; the leg is STILL NOT RUN-STABLE under it, because cause (b) is untouched.** As measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven/evidence/hue-verdict.md`, two runs of the identical tree under the identical posture on 2026-09-07 graded differently — the evaluator was disarmed in both (`silence_cues_emitted: 0`, `services_in_bootstrap: 2`, zero silence cues emitted), and what separated them was WHEN the window's last incident formed: +45s into the 200s window it cleared the 120s idle + 30s tick and the arm fired (`KnownResidual`), +137s it was ~62s old at read-back and the arm was missed (`ManualCheck`). Plan a leg that needs this arm on a FRESHLY started Pulse with the posture set, and still record the verdict as conditional. As measured at `pulse-legs/a11y-20260906-110201` on 2026-09-06: reached at 09:17Z (~6 min into that window), failed at 10:07Z INSIDE it on the margin (two preflight incidents, the later ~122 s old at read-back) and at 11:00Z past it on silence cues (incidents created 11:00:33 and 11:02:02; the day's first emitted silence cue 10:11:09.723Z, one hour after the canary service's first span), against `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_SECONDS = 3_600` (`andromeda-pulse crates/triage/src/baseline/activity_floor.rs:36`, HEAD `83d4060`). Observables 2 and 3 are unaffected — they key on the storm incident and reproduced across runs — or a CARGO-FEATURE-GATED test file invoked directly, NOT a CI gate** (arch CI/CD note). CI runs the stub legs only. The third path was added 2026-09-01: `conductor-run/tests/lifecycle_live.rs` behind `[features] live-pulse = []` — an EMPTY feature declaring no dependency, so it adds zero package nodes and leaves `Cargo.lock` byte-unchanged, and it now gates a SET of targets rather than that one (2026-09-06 added `conductor-run/tests/live_suite.rs`, the `--live` suite's capture tool, 2026-09-22 `conductor-run/tests/real_model_live.rs`, the real-model arm's capture, 2026-10-01 `conductor-run/tests/span_landing_live.rs`, the per-run span-identity witness (auto-discovered; its own lint line `cargo clippy -p conductor-run --features live-pulse --all-targets -- -D warnings`), and 2026-10-02 `conductor-run/tests/p075_round_live.rs`, the P-075 assert-round leg (auto-discovered, under the same lint line); the manifest stayed byte-unchanged and the feature added ZERO package nodes — the lock's package total is read from `Cargo.lock`, never pinned in this prose, precisely so a dependency change elsewhere cannot re-stale it), while keeping the leg out of default `nextest`, the workspace `clippy` pass and release builds, and out of both runner-portability runs. Because a gated file is invisible to the workspace lint pass, such a leg OWES its own lint command (`cargo clippy -p <crate> --features <feat> --all-targets -- -D warnings`). Since 2026-10-04 both owed lines run in `agent-run run`'s bundled default in both shells, after the workspace clippy — `-p conductor-verify --features stub-server` (the `stub-server`-gated `preflight_spawn.rs` and the `stub_pulse_mcp` bin) and `-p conductor-run --features live-pulse` (the `live-pulse` target set) — so CI compiles and lints them through the `rust` job's dogfood step, as measured at CI#37201730301; they are still never RUN in CI. A new target under either feature is covered by that feature's line; a new feature owes its own line in the bundle.

**Scoped mutation audit:** the cargo-mutants run (§4) sits on the same footing as the live-Pulse leg — an **operator/local instrument, never a blocking CI stage**. It runs at the epoch-boundary code audit ONLY, never per chunk (founder ruling, 2026-09-30) — since 2026-09-13 through its committed form `python -X utf8 scripts/mutation-gate.py {unit}`, which carries the `-f` full-crate-path and `--test-tool=nextest` discipline §4 states — not workspace-wide, so the stage table above is the complete inventory of gates CI enforces and NOT the complete inventory of checks a chunk may owe. The committed form changes the invocation only: no CI step invokes it and the non-CI footing is unchanged.

**Supply-chain audit form:** the shipped gate is the BARE `cargo audit` beside `cargo deny check`; the `cargo audit --deny warnings` form is never the gate, because it exits 1 by construction against the `deny.toml`-adjudicated allowed-warning set. The tools' version floors (`cargo-audit`, `cargo-deny`) are the security plan's (§Dependency Security), not restated here.
**Matrix builds:**

- OS: the SHIPPED CI arrangement is the job set `.github/workflows/ci.yml` declares, named by job rather than by line coordinate (which move as the workflow grows) — today `rust` alone, on `windows-latest`: the `frontend` and `a11y` jobs left with the window on 2026-10-11 (the gate's job-count read 1). No OS matrix exists. The webview leg's hosted-runner and dev-host capability findings retired with it — removed, not re-measured; their text is last at `321dc8f`. Should a matrix arrive, set the nextest `job_name` per variant so `dorny/test-reporter` distinguishes per-OS results.
- Toolchain: pinned ≥ 1.94.1 via `rust-toolchain.toml` (tar-rs CVE-2026-33056); committed `Cargo.lock` (no drift).

**Test report format:** machine-parseable — cargo-nextest `ci`-profile JUnit XML (via `quick-junit`) parsed by `dorny/test-reporter` into per-test PR annotations; cargo-llvm-cov Cobertura uploaded as a coverage artifact; agent reads via CI artifact API / `agent-run logs`.
**Build failure conditions:**
- Any unit / integration / E2E test fails (nextest `NextestExitCode` 100/101).
- Coverage falls below the Minimal threshold (Section 10).
- Lint / clippy `-D warnings` / fmt error.
- `cargo audit` or `cargo deny check` non-green; `Cargo.lock` drift.

- A repository-hygiene gate red (a secret-shaped string or file name in the workspace; an undeclared `env.X` workflow read), or the `GITHUB_ENV context probe (assert)` step finding the env expression context without a `GITHUB_ENV` key.
(See `## 11. Test Anti-Patterns` § CI for CI bans.)

title: 10. Quality Gates & Coverage Targets

body: _[ALL tiers]_
**Coverage thresholds (per tier):**
| Tier | Line coverage | Branch coverage | Function coverage |
| Comprehensive | ≥ 85% | ≥ 80% | ≥ 95% |

Enforced by cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7 `--fail-under-lines 60` over the workspace (rolls up across `conductor-<seam>` crates). The SHIPPED exclusion is ONE generic path regex, not an enumeration: `--ignore-filename-regex '[\\/]tests[\\/]'` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:`/`:144`/`:147`, as measured 2026-09-13), which covers every crate-local `tests/` tree — so a new shared fixture such as `conductor-emit/tests/common` needs no entry — while generated tonic/prost OTLP codegen is excluded by llvm-cov itself as external-crate code. It is NARROWER than an enumeration in one named direction: the hand-rolled MCP stub lives at `conductor-verify/src/bin/stub_pulse_mcp.rs`, under `src/`, and is therefore NOT excluded by the regex. Branch coverage requires nightly; line/function coverage works on the stable pinned toolchain (≥ 1.94.1) — the line gate is the binding CI gate, branch coverage is informational on stable.

**Performance budgets:** N/A — `test_tier=Minimal` and there is no perf-budget trigger in test-scope Sec 5. Creator Brief anti-pattern explicitly excludes load: "NOT a load-tester ... 50k+ spans/sec saturation regimes are explicitly out" (Pulse's `perf_load_profiles.rs` owns saturation). The bounded fault-injection (P-060 "typical/high" profiles) is a chaos correctness check (Section 8), NOT a perf budget.

**Zero-flakiness budget:** flaky tests are NOT tolerated. If a test flakes once, it gets quarantined immediately and fixed (root cause — not retry-once budget). Do NOT set cargo-nextest `retries` > 0. Agent-driven dev cannot distinguish flake from real bug; retry policies mask actual failures. Determinism is enforced upstream (tokio `start_paused` virtual clock, seeded `conductor-timeline`, proptest `proptest-regressions/` persistence) so flakes indicate a real determinism break. **A runner-dependent result is in this class** — a test green under one runner and red under the other is a shared-state defect to remove at the cause (§11 Integration), never a runner to pin to.

**Mutation-survivor disposition (audit tier, non-blocking):** where the epoch-boundary code audit runs the §4 mutation instrument, every NAMED survivor ends either **killed** or **classified accepted-deliberate against a cited rule** — the second is a real disposition, not a deferral, on either of TWO bases: a standing rule prescribes the untested shape, or the mutant is PROVEN EQUIVALENT — no input in the domain distinguishes it, so no assertion over values can, and the acceptance rests on a measurement rather than on a rule foreclosing the test (`conductor-emit`'s 2026-09-14 member is the first of this second kind, and its scope is the individual mutant, never the comparison class its siblings share) (the accepted-deliberate roster now has TWO joined forms: the accepted-deliberate roster below is the CITATION HOME, holding each member's cited rule and evidence pointer, and `scripts/mutation-roster.toml` is its coordinate-free EXECUTABLE form, which `scripts/mutation-gate.py` grades a run's `missed.txt` and `timeout.txt` against, each row by its required `tally` class (§4); the two join on a `member` key and neither restates the other's content — the citation home carries the reasoning, the roster carries only what a tally comparison needs. Each member is cited against its own rule — `conductor-run`'s `declares` env-read arms, `conductor-tauri`'s 2026-09-03 triple (retired with its crate, 2026-10-11), `conductor-run`'s 2026-09-03 classes B and C, `conductor-verify`'s 2026-09-04 `sidecar_resolves_on_path` pair, `conductor-cli`'s 2026-09-05 tty-gate wrapper pair, and `conductor-emit`'s 2026-09-14 equivalent-mutant single, each enumerated there rather than carried as a count here — so a new accepted disposition EXTENDS the roster rather than contradicting a single-case literal; the `declares` arms cite `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-08-10, which requires env be read at the caller and passed in as a typed value, precisely so the edge stays thin and both branches test without `unsafe` env mutation). This is deliberately NOT a numeric `--fail-under` threshold beside the coverage gate: the score moves as a consequence of dispositioning named survivors, and is never itself the acceptance.

**Accepted-deliberate roster — the citation home.** Each member's set (keyed by mutation DESCRIPTION, §4), its cited rule and its evidence pointer stand here; `scripts/mutation-roster.toml` is the executable form, joined on `member`. Rejected alternatives are part of a disposition. A new accepted disposition extends this list.

- **`member-1` — `conductor-run`'s `declares` env-read arm:** the set is `replace declares -> bool with false` ALONE, in `crates/conductor-run/src/preconditions.rs`. `declares` is a thin env-reading wrapper delegating its value test to `conductor_core::flag_declared`; the operator arms are caught there by the `flag_declared` / `handle_declared` rstest matrix, `declares -> true` by `declares_rejects_a_name_this_environment_does_not_declare`, and the enclosing `observe_run_contract` mutant by `observe_run_contract_names_the_term_this_environment_does_not_declare`. Only the env-gated body replacement survives — indistinguishable from the real code whenever the var is unset. Cited against `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-08-10 (env read at the caller, passed in as a typed value); a kill would need `unsafe set_var` in a shared-process test module, the hazard that rule removed. Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-03-conductor-run-composition-root-survivors-dispositioned/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`, as reduced by `2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence`.

- **`member-2` — retired 2026-10-11 with `conductor-tauri`:** its triple left with the crate; the disposition evidence stays at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-03-conductor-tauri-survivors-dispositioned/evidence/survivor-dispositions.md`.

- **`member-3` — `conductor-run`'s classes B and C:** class B is `delete field degraded from struct Observation expression in execute_scenario` + `replace - with + in execute_scenario` + `replace - with / in execute_scenario` — unreachable past a fixed-endpoint egress gate: they sit past `probe_egress(DEFAULT_OTLP_ENDPOINT)` and `Dispatcher::connect(scenario, DEFAULT_OTLP_ENDPOINT)`, where the endpoint is the fixed `http://127.0.0.1:4317` (`conductor-emit/src/client.rs`), not injectable; reaching them means binding Pulse's own ingest port in a unit test, which architecture.md §Occupied Resources — Ports does not sanction and which contends between `--jobs 2` mutant processes (§10 zero-flakiness); `Preflight`'s fields are crate-private, and making the endpoint injectable is a production signature change. Class C is `delete ! in preflight` — unreachable without the sidecar binary: the guard needs a connected client, and `ReadbackClient::connect` spawns `andromeda-pulse-mcp` as a fixed program NAME through the inherited `PATH`, so a kill needs the sidecar as a host precondition or a new injectable seam. Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-03-conductor-run-composition-root-survivors-dispositioned/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`.

- **`member-4` — `conductor-verify`'s pair:** `replace sidecar_resolves_on_path -> bool with true` and `… with false`, in `spawn.rs` — whole-body replacements of a function whose entire body IS the `PATH`/`PATHEXT` read plus delegation, so the env-at-the-caller mechanism lives in that function itself; its pure half `resolves_on` is tested on both arms. Cited against `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-08-10 (a kill needs `unsafe { std::env::set_var }`). Rejected: an agreement test against the real `PATH`, which kills exactly one arm depending on whether `andromeda-pulse-mcp` is on `PATH`, making the score host-dependent — a roster must mean the same thing on every host (§10 zero-flakiness). The unit's mutant population is read from the run, never restated. Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-sidecar-spawn-without-a-console-window/report.md`.

- **`member-5` — `conductor-cli`'s pair:** `replace stdout_color -> bool with false` and `replace stderr_color -> bool with false` in `render.rs` — wrapper bodies whose surviving arm reads the HOST's own state (a real-terminal stdout or stderr), which every runner captures, so the only kill is host-dependent. The acceptance is scoped to the unobservable DIRECTION, not the function: `stderr_color` → `true` is killed by an assert_cmd subprocess whose piped stderr carries no escape byte, and the three-condition logic is killed through the pure `color_enabled(is_terminal, no_color_set, term)` seam. Rejected: a `CONDUCTOR_COLOR`-class env override — a new `CONDUCTOR_*` handle is a new occupied resource (architecture.md §Occupied Resources), and `unsafe { set_var }` is process-global. Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-05-audit-corrective/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`.

- **`member-emit-1` — `conductor-emit`'s single, the first EQUIVALENT-MUTANT member:** `replace < with <= in quantile` in `latency.rs`, over the population `exception.rs` + `latency.rs` WHOLE (never a `--shard` subset, which is not re-measurable once indices shift). The guard's two branches meet at `u = 0.5` with the same value — `u / 0.5` is exactly `1.0` and `(u - 0.5) / 0.45` exactly `0.0`, both yielding exactly `p50` — and `u = 0.5` is the only input the flip re-routes, so the mutated fn returns a bit-identical `f64` for every input (measured under EXACT `f64` comparison over 5 profiles × 10 008 points: 0 differing). Scoped to THIS mutant, never the comparison class: four siblings of the same shape are killable and killed, because the later branches are one line algebraically but not in IEEE754. Rejected: a tolerance band around the breakpoints (any epsilon wide enough to feel safe re-admits the four siblings — exact equality is what discriminates), and restructuring `quantile` so the boundary becomes observable (a production behaviour change made to satisfy a mutation tool, which §11 forbids). The unit's timeouts have NO roster rows: timeout identity is coordinate-free and collides within a helper, so the rows are seeded by the epoch-boundary code audit from its own measured `timeout.txt` (overseer, founder-delegated); until then `mutation-gate.py conductor-emit` FAILs closed with one `TIMED OUT, not in roster` line per timeout, and that output is the input the rows are written from. Evidence: `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-14-emit-scrubber-and-percentile-math-under-test/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`.
**Build failure conditions:**
- Test failure (any level) — nextest `NextestExitCode` 100/101.
- Coverage below the Minimal threshold (`--fail-under-lines 60`).
- Lint / clippy `-D warnings` / fmt failure.
- Supply-chain: `cargo audit` or `cargo deny check` non-green; `Cargo.lock` drift; toolchain < 1.94.1.
- Repository hygiene: a secret-scan or workflow env-context gate red, or the `GITHUB_ENV context probe (assert)` step red.
_(Compliance Test Coverage subsection omitted — `security_tier=Minimal`, not Hardened; no compliance triggers in test-scope Section 5.)_
(See `## 11. Test Anti-Patterns` § Quality for quality-gate bans.)

title: 11. Test Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)

body: _[ALL tiers — single source of truth for all test bans]_

title: Test Strategy

body: - NEVER violate the test pyramid — heavy E2E with sparse unit tests is slow + brittle; the per-seam `cargo nextest run -p conductor-<seam>` unit layer is the bulk, E2E is the 7 critical paths only.
- NEVER over-mock at integration level (you stop testing the integration — e.g., do not fake the `runs.db` instead of using rusqlite `open_in_memory()`).

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER fake Pulse's *reaction* as a CI verdict — the hand-rolled stub canary proves MCP wiring only; Pulse's actual behavior is a live/local-gate assertion (Creator Brief: validates Pulse "from the outside, as a real workload").
- **(stack-specific)** NEVER escalate to load/saturation testing — bounded P-060 "typical/high" profiles only; 50k+ spans/sec is Pulse's `perf_load_profiles.rs`, explicitly out of Conductor scope.

title: Unit

body: - NEVER test implementation details (private fns / internal struct fields) — test the public seam API + observable behavior (envelope/verdict/state output).
- NEVER write brittle assertions against fixture-internal values — assert on the Run-report envelope contract.

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER assert on a real wall-clock duration in a `conductor-timeline` test — drive `tokio::time::advance` under `start_paused = true` and assert scheduled ordering/shape, not real elapsed time.

title: Integration

body: - NEVER mock the DB at integration level — use rusqlite `open_in_memory()` (in-memory) or `assert_fs::TempDir` (file-backed for cross-process), never a hand-rolled SQL fake.
- NEVER skip cleanup between integration tests — fresh in-memory `runs.db` per test (nextest per-process model); never share a mutable file DB across parallel tests without per-test `TempDir`.

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER build `runs.db` SQL via `format!`/string concatenation — use rusqlite bound parameters even for synthetic data (security anti-pattern); a negative/static test asserts this.

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER rely on nextest's per-test process to isolate a test from a **process-global, first-install-wins singleton** — the `conductor_core::init_observability` subscriber is the shipped case. A per-test `TempDir` sink does NOT isolate it: whichever test installs the subscriber first owns the sink, and every concurrent sibling's events land in that file. The remedy is a SET of two, and the discriminator for both is that the fix holds green under BOTH runners. (a) A test binary of its own — `cargo test` gives each `tests/*.rs` its own process, and nextest is already process-per-test, so one file per such test holds under both; this is the default answer. (b) A shared in-module guard that serializes ONLY the tests touching the singleton — the answer when the singleton's tests are INLINE (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`) over crate-private helpers, where (a) would require `pub` on those helpers and widen the crate's public API for tests alone, which architecture.md §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries] forbids. **As measured 2026-09-10** (`2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle`): the `conductor-core` panic-hook pair took (b) via a `static Mutex<()>` held across each test's take/set/restore window, green under nextest AND `cargo test -p conductor-core`, plus 12/12 under forced contention. What stays banned either way is serializing the FILE with a runner knob (`--test-threads=1` / a profile setting), which hides the shared-state defect rather than removing it (§10) — an in-code guard removes the interleaving at the cause and is not that. The nextest-per-process rationale restated in §3 / §5 / §7 / §9 stays valid for `runs.db` / `TempDir` isolation; it is not a guarantee for process-global state.

title: E2E

body: - NEVER use xpath selectors — use role / data-testid / text + brand anchors (`[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[HOLD]` labels, `role="alertdialog"`, `aria-live`, "HOLD — operator pause" heading text, P-ID tokens).

- NEVER use `sleep(N)` for synchronization — wait for an explicit signal (envelope `state` field, JSONL journal line, element role/`aria-live`, exit code). The ban's subject is SYNCHRONISATION INSIDE A TEST; it is not a ban on wall-clock time as such. A harness-level wait BETWEEN legs that reproduces a documented SUT-side precondition — the `--live` suite's 150 s quiet window, which exists so Pulse's `(kind, scope, scope_id)` dedupe window (120 s idle + a 30 s resolver tick) elapses before the next leg's canary — is part of the leg's firing form (§6), not a substitute for a signal: there is no signal to wait on, because the transition being waited out is the ABSENCE of a Pulse-side event. The same class covers the `span_landing_live` operator pass's 180 s window between its two same-seed drives (120 s idle + a 30 s resolver tick + margin, so drive B's preflight canary does not dedupe against drive A's open incident) — a firing-form wait between drives; the witness itself waits on nothing. Nothing inside a test may sleep to synchronise.
- NEVER use brittle selectors that drift across iterations (hashed Tailwind/CSS class names) — the Color-Only a11y rule guarantees text/role pairing, so use that.

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER treat a `blocked`/`ManualCheck`/`KnownResidual`/`CalibrationRegion` state as a non-zero process exit — those are reported envelope states, not hard `Fail` exits (Creator Brief assertion-policy split); only a hard `Fail` is a non-zero exit.

title: Test Data

body: - NEVER use production data in tests — only self-generated synthetic OTLP from the seeded `conductor-timeline` generator (there is no user data; synthetic-only by classification).
- NEVER share mutable state across parallel tests — in-memory `runs.db` / `TempDir` per test.
- NEVER use non-deterministic generators without seed control — `conductor-timeline` seed + proptest strategies with `proptest-regressions/` persistence.

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER stamp the emission journal/report from tokio's virtual clock — use `std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant`; a paused-clock leak into the ground-truth artifact corrupts SLO checks (security anti-pattern) and must be caught by a golden test.

title: Mocking

body: - NEVER mock what you don't own without an abstraction layer — wrap the live Pulse behind the hand-rolled JSON-RPC stdio client seam; do NOT monkey-patch `andromeda-pulse-mcp`.
- NEVER over-stub (you stop testing real behavior) — the cli release-gate scenarios run the real binary via assert_cmd.
- NEVER monkey-patch production code at runtime — use DI (stdio-transport injection into the hand-rolled client, tokio built-in virtual clock, ephemeral-port tonic server).

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER force-fit wiremock-rs onto the gRPC OTLP egress — `tonic` is gRPC, not HTTP/1; use an in-process tonic test server or turmoil; reserve wiremock for any future HTTP surface only.

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER interpolate `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` (or any operator value) into the sidecar argv/shell — pass strictly via `.env(...)` after rejecting injection metacharacters; spawn `andromeda-pulse-mcp` as a fixed hard-coded program NAME resolved through the inherited `PATH` (rmcp STDIO injection class CVE-2026-30623); a negative test asserts argv-injection rejection.

title: CI

body: - NEVER run sequentially when parallelizable — unit + integration are parallel-safe under nextest's per-test process model with proper `runs.db`/`TempDir` isolation.
- NEVER skip dependency caching (`~/.cargo` + `target/` keyed on `Cargo.lock`) — slows the agent feedback loop.
- NEVER ignore flaky tests — quarantine and fix immediately; do NOT set nextest `retries`.

- **(stack-specific)** NEVER merge / `cargo build --release` without `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check` green and a committed un-drifted `Cargo.lock` (Minimal-tier residual-risk control); NEVER run the live-Pulse scenarios as a CI gate (operator/local only — `workflow_dispatch`, `scripts/agent-run.sh` — including its composed `run --live` stage — or a cargo-feature-gated test invoked directly, per §9).

title: Quality

body: - NEVER add retry-once policies for flaky tests (masks real failures; determinism is enforced upstream).
- NEVER lower the coverage threshold to pass the build (raise quality, not the bar — keep `--fail-under-lines 60`).
- NEVER skip quality gates "just this once" (audit-green + coverage + clippy are binding).

title: Universal (agent-driven specific)

body: - NEVER use Percy / Chromatic / Applitools (visual regression with human review) — assert role/text/`aria-live` only; `drive+observe` visual go/no-go is the flagged-untestable operator step.
- NEVER include a manual smoke step ("developer verifies before deploy") — except the explicitly-flagged `drive+observe` operator checklist, which is a product feature, not a test step.

- NEVER use Selenium IDE / WebdriverIO codegen-recorder / `cargo insta review` interactive accept UI as a test author — use NON-INTERACTIVE runners only (insta CI/assert mode with the `CI` env var flipping it to fail-don't-write).
- NEVER include "human reviews screenshots" in any test step.
- NEVER use real network calls in tests — loopback only (gRPC/MCP stubs, never `:4317`); the live Pulse leg is local-gate-only, never a CI network call.
- NEVER use real time without injection — tokio `start_paused` virtual clock for scheduling; `std::time` only for ground-truth journal stamps.

- **(project-specific)** NEVER add a scenario without a Pulse P-ID, and NEVER introduce an inbound network listener of Conductor's own (the `:4317` port-occupier is the sole deliberate bind, must release on cleanup, and must never become a general-purpose listener) — both violate the architecture's scope law / loopback-client trust boundary.

title: 12. Test Decisions Log

body: History: test-plan-amendments.md (live); the log moved verbatim to test-plan-amendments-archive.md (U35).

title: 5-command implementation
5-command implementation

body: **`boot`** — precondition probe, then preflight readiness gate (no daemon to start):

- Leading arm: `cargo run -p conductor-cli --bin conductor -- preconditions` — non-zero on an unmet subject SHORT-CIRCUITS `boot`, skipping the preflight invocation (and its two derived timeout budgets) rather than paying it; no `ReadyState` JSON is emitted. Identical semantics in `.sh` and `.ps1` — the short-circuit is environment-CONDITIONAL, firing only on an actually-unmet subject (measured 2026-09-04, both shells exit 0 and emit `ReadyState` JSON under a satisfied environment; the 2026-09-03 both-shells-exit-1 witness measured the pre-fix state, when the subject could not be met). The probe mints no `Verdict`, `ReportState` or per-P-ID row, so the envelope / status-read / JSONL shapes are untouched and §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree.

- Command body (**reached through `boot`** — the leading probe's `handles-declared` subject is satisfiable, so `boot` proceeds here and this body plus its two derived timeout budgets are paid; measured in the full shipped shell SET at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence/report.md`: `scripts/agent-run.sh` 2026-09-04T17:07:17→17:08:04Z and `scripts/agent-run.ps1` 17:11:16→17:12:03Z, both exit 0 with `ready: true` / `canary_round_trip: "ok"` and zero `skipped preflight` lines. Invoking it directly remains valid, not required): `cargo run -p conductor-cli --bin conductor -- preflight --json` — runs the MCP `initialize` handshake through the hand-rolled JSON-RPC client over the spawned sidecar's stdio (arch Standard Contracts: asserts the `protocolVersion` read back from that result against the pinned `2024-11-05`, required-tool presence vs. pinned `contracts/` manifest, then round-trips a canary incident via `query_incident_list` to prove data-dir wiring). In CI the live-Pulse leg is unavailable, so `boot` runs against the hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp` child binary (test-research Mocking) which returns a `ready:true` canary; the live-Pulse leg is `workflow_dispatch`/local-only gated on `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`.

- Readiness signal: stdout JSON `{"ready": true}`; `ready:false` ⇒ every dependent scenario reports `state="Blocked"` with the named precondition string (security anti-pattern: never silently downgrade a failed preflight to pass/fail/manual-check).
- Exit code: 0 on `ready:true` within timeout; non-zero on handshake failure (transport refused surfaces as `Result::Err`, a harness fault — security Vector 5).

- Timeout: **two budgets, both derived — never a literal.** (a) The *in-process* canary poll: `CONDUCTOR_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 30) for the MCP `initialize` + canary round-trip, raised to the run contract's effective floor — `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml` `[incident_formation].min_canary_poll_seconds`, which must outlast Pulse's L3 digest cadence — so the live-Pulse leg must allow at least that floor. (b) The *wall-clock wrapper* `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` `boot` applies around `conductor preflight`: both shells derive it per invocation from the same contract as `warmup_ms/1000 + poll + margin`, because the warm-up pre-roll runs BEFORE the poll starts and a wrapper set to the poll alone kills the run mid-poll. A missing contract term is a hard exit 2, never a silent default; a lowered `CONDUCTOR_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT` clamps up to the floor. The stub leg still completes in <1s (it drives `CanaryPoll::immediate()`, so no real clock is involved).
**`run`** — invoke test suites + scenario catalog:

- Command body (CI build+test gate, arch CI/CD): `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` (cargo-nextest 0.9.137 → JUnit XML at `.config/nextest.toml` `[profile.ci.junit]`) then `cargo test --workspace --doc` (nextest does not run doctests — test-research baseline-fallback note) then `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then (since 2026-10-04) the two feature-gated lint lines `cargo clippy -p conductor-verify --features stub-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p conductor-run --features live-pulse --all-targets -- -D warnings` — they compile and lint the `stub-server` and `live-pulse` targets, which the workspace pass never builds, and never run them; identical in both shells, and CI reaches them through the `rust` job's dogfood step. The bundled default stops at its FIRST non-zero cargo line in BOTH shells: `agent-run.sh` by `set -euo pipefail` (as measured at `2026-10-04-second-test-surface-corrective` `evidence/carry-measurement.md`: a planted clippy-only `-D warnings` lint ended `run` at exit 101 on the workspace clippy line, after green nextest and doctest lines), `agent-run.ps1` by an explicit `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }` after each of its five cargo lines (since 2026-10-04), so it no longer depends on its caller setting `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference` — and the script itself never sets it. A caller that DOES set it (CI's dogfood step) still sees the red line throw before the check runs (a `NativeCommandExitException`, the step exit 1 — CI#34689135760); a caller that does not gets that line's own cargo exit. The ps1 green path is proven by CI#37209452847; its red path is read from the script, not measured — no leg has driven it (the Linux dev host has carried `pwsh` 7.6.6 since 2026-10-06, as measured at the `2026-10-08-version-close-on-measured-evidence` chunk's `evidence/version-close.md`, where the script was parsed and never executed; a missing shell is no longer the reason). Scenario invocation: `cargo run -p conductor-cli --bin conductor -- run <scenario|P-ID> [--seed <s>]` for the named dynamic scenarios (`error-baseline-spike`, `fingerprint-storm`, `restart-suppression`, `pii-scrub`, `connection-lifecycle`, `severity-lifecycle`) and per-P-ID scenarios; `conductor suite` for the full catalog. A P-ID target resolves only where ONE scenario names it: `run` (and the harness's `SCENARIO=`, passed straight through) REFUSES a P-ID that several scenarios name, before any scenario load — a harness fault naming the P-ID, the count and the matching scenario stems (never a host path), rendered as `error:` + `hint: pass one of the named scenarios instead of the P-ID` at exit 1 (`cli_smoke::run_refuses_a_p_id_named_by_several_scenarios`) — and several P-IDs are named by more than one scenario (seven at 2026-09-30, P-018 among them), so name the scenario; a single-owner P-ID still resolves. `preconditions --for` refuses a P-ID outright, at argument parsing. The harness scenario leg (`SCENARIO=<name|P-ID> [SEED=<n>] scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} run`) appends `--seed` ONLY when `SEED` is explicitly set — with it unset the TOML-declared seed governs (arch files-over-env-defaults precedence; identical `.sh`/`.ps1` semantics) and the envelope records the effective seed.

- Exit code semantics: 0 = all checks `Pass`; non-zero = at least one hard `Fail` (cargo-nextest `NextestExitCode` 100), or — in the bundled default — a red build, doctest or `-D warnings` lint line, which ends the run at that line (measured: exit 101 on a clippy-only red with every test green); `blocked`/`ManualCheck`/`KnownResidual`/`CalibrationRegion` are reported states in the envelope, NOT process-failure exits (Creator Brief assertion-policy split: model-interpretive claims are "calibration-region checks + report-for-human, never hard-failed").

- Output format: machine-parseable — cargo-nextest `ci` profile JUnit XML (parsed by `dorny/test-reporter` into PR annotations) for the test gate; the Run-report envelope JSONL/`runs.db` row for the scenario leg.

- Test selection (fast iteration): `cargo nextest run -p conductor-<seam>` for a single seam crate; `cargo nextest run -E 'test(<name>)'` for a single test; `conductor run <scenario> --seed <s>` for one scenario (a P-ID target resolves only where a single scenario names it; a P-ID several scenarios name is refused, naming them — see `run` above).

- CI stage selectors: the `run` command takes mutually-exclusive `--unit` / `--integration` flags so the Section 9 pipeline can split it into parallel stages — plus, since 2026-09-06, the operator-gated `--live`, which is NOT a CI stage and is reachable from no default path (a sibling `case` branch on `run`, so the 5-command discipline holds and both shells ship it at identical semantics). `--live` takes an optional third-token SELECTOR (2026-09-22) and composes one of two shapes. **Bare `--live`** is the live-Pulse suite: a leading non-priming `conductor preconditions` probe (an unmet subject refuses at exit 1 with `[PRECONDITION]` lines and no leg fires) → the ordered leg set the shells' own `live_leg_order` owns — at 2026-09-07 that is leg H (`halo-hue-encoding`, budget `live_leg_budget_sec 180`, first because its sustained stream must not sit inside leg A's silence window) → leg B1 → leg B2 → a 150 s quiet window → leg A (read the order from `live_leg_order` in `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`, never from a count restated here), freezing each leg's `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` to `runs/live-suite/{leg}.jsonl` because that sink truncates per invocation. **`--live real-model`** runs the ONE real-model leg instead of the suite: `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation` (the scenario's real-model posture requires the L4 handle absent or falsy under the union truthiness rule; an unmet subject refuses at exit 1 and no leg fires) → a pre-build of the capture binary → the non-recursive removal of `runs/live-suite/{rm.jsonl,rm-capture.txt,rm-capture.err}` → the grading rule's `rule_record` into `rm-capture.txt` BEFORE the leg (a non-zero exit stops the arm, so no counted drive of the series is spent) → `live_leg rm real-model-interpretation` → the `real_model_live` capture (stdout appended, stderr to `rm-capture.err`, `RUST_LOG` removed for both test invocations) → printed reminders. An unknown selector prints `usage: <script> run --live [real-model]` and exits 2 before any probe, in both shells; `boot` keeps the flagless probe. It adds no port, env var or `CONDUCTOR_*` handle, and leaves the envelope, the `status` disk read and the JSONL shapes untouched — so §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree (`--unit` ⇒ the `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` leg only — `cargo test --workspace --doc` and `cargo clippy` are their own separate Section 9 stages (Doctest / Lint), NOT folded into `--unit`; `--integration` ⇒ the hand-rolled MCP stub + in-memory/`TempDir` `runs.db` leg). The `--e2e` webview stage left with the window on 2026-10-11 — with its printed-verdict check, its `runs/a11y/<run_id>.jsonl` violation record and its fixture seeding — and the token now falls to the existing unknown-token `usage:` exit 2 in both shells. With no flag, `run` executes the full aggregate (nextest + doctest + clippy + scenarios); per-stage target mapping is the Section 9 pipeline table.
**`status`** — query product state (disk artifact read; no listener):

- Command body: `jq -e '<predicate>' runs/<run_id>.jsonl` for a shell-level CI smoke gate (jq -e exits 1 on a `false`/`null` last output, 4 on parse error — test-research serde_json+jq), OR an in-process `rusqlite::Connection::open` + bound-parameter `SELECT` of the `runs.db` row for typed assertions. **The journal read targets the NEWEST ENVELOPE line — never the file's last line**: the journal carries two report-seam record shapes (§3 Log format), so a run that graded checks ends on a `CheckRecord` and an unqualified last-line read reports ITS fields as the envelope (measured 2026-09-06: `seed: null`, `slo_tier: null`, exit 0). Both shells select that line by the envelope-only `seed` key (`jq -s` filtering `has("seed")` · `Where-Object { $_.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'seed' }`). No `curl`/HTTP — there is no inbound listener.

- Polled fields: the Run-report envelope (see Status endpoint shape below) — `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `journal_emitted_at`, `read_back_observed_at`, `fingerprints`.
**`cleanup`** — tear down per-run artifacts:

- Command body: `rm -f runs/<run_id>.jsonl runs/<run_id>.md` in the shells, then `conductor cleanup <run_id>` — **the shells issue no SQL** (2026-09-06). The three bound-parameter deletes (`DELETE FROM runs WHERE run_id = ?1`, `DELETE FROM run_check WHERE run_id = ?1`, `DELETE FROM run_envelope WHERE run_id = ?1`) run inside the binary as three LITERAL statements in one transaction (`conductor_report::RunsDb::delete_run`) — teardown covers every table a run writes, or cleanup leaves orphans (rusqlite bound parameters — security anti-pattern bans `format!`-built SQL, which the `sqlite3` CLI could not have honoured: it has no bind facility, and it is present on neither this host nor any CI runner). In tests this reduces to dropping the `assert_fs::TempDir` sandboxing `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`. Conductor must NOT touch Pulse (Creator Brief: "NO Pulse process management"). The `:4317` port-occupier fault (security Vector 6) releases its `TcpListener` bind on cleanup.
- Idempotency: cleanup MUST be idempotent — re-running against a clean state is a no-op (file-absence is not an error; `DELETE` of zero rows succeeds).

- Verification: `assert_fs` `.assert(predicate::path::missing())` on `runs/<run_id>.{jsonl,md}` + `SELECT count(*) FROM runs WHERE run_id = ?1`, `... FROM run_check ...` and `... FROM run_envelope ...` each returning 0 + a `TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:4317")` succeeding (proving the port-occupier released).
**`logs`** — fetch product logs (emission journal is ground truth):

- Command body: read `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` (the per-run emission journal — "the left side of every SLO check", Creator Brief) directly; sanitized stderr from the CLI subprocess captured by `assert_cmd` `.get_output().stderr`. The journal is emitted via `tracing_subscriber::fmt().json().flatten_event(true)` (test-research Structured Log Parsing), one JSON object per line, with wall-clock stamps from `std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant` (NOT tokio's virtual clock — security anti-pattern).
- Format: see Log format below.
- Retention window: per-`run_id`, append-mostly on disk; tests read the whole journal file for the run under assertion (no rotation needed — bounded synthetic runs).

title: Status endpoint shape
Status endpoint shape

body:
```json
{
  "run_id": "string", "seed": 0, "scenario": "string", "p_ids": ["P-001"],
  "verdict": "Pass | Fail | CalibrationRegion",
  "state": "Pass | Fail | ManualCheck | KnownResidual | Blocked",
  "latency_ms": 0, "slo_tier": "string",
  "journal_emitted_at": "ISO-8601", "read_back_observed_at": "ISO-8601",
  "fingerprints": []
}
```

No HTTP/IPC status *endpoint* exists (no listener). This is the Run-report envelope (arch Standard Contracts), serialized identically into the Markdown report, the `runs` row, and the envelope JSONL journal line. Per-check detail is a separate finer grain, never an extension of the envelope (whose eleven fields are unchanged): the `run_check` table keyed `(run_id, scenario, check_index)` (read via `RunsDb::checks_for`) plus its own journal lines and an indented per-check line in the Markdown report. The agent polls it by reading the `runs.db` row (bound-parameter SQL) or the JSONL journal during/after each scenario. Artifacts MUST NOT leak absolute host paths or internal seam-crate struct names (security anti-pattern) — enforced by the insta golden snapshot + a tracing field-allowlist redaction layer.

title: Log format

body: - **Format:** structured JSONL — one JSON object per line (arch Test-Relevant Conventions: "per-run JSONL journals stemmed by `run_id`"), emitted by `tracing-subscriber` 0.3.x `format::Json`.

- **Required fields:** `journal_emitted_at` (ISO-8601 from `std::time::SystemTime` — NOT virtual clock), plus the envelope identity fields (`run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `fingerprints`). NO absolute host paths, NO internal struct names (security anti-pattern; asserted by a negative test on the journal).

- **Agent parsing:** `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` carries TWO report-seam record shapes — the **run envelope line** (the eleven envelope fields, byte-unchanged) and the **per-check `CheckRecord` line** (`run_id` · `scenario` · `check_index` · `kind` · `verdict` · `state` · `latency_ms` · `deadline_ms` · `budget_ms`; `budget_ms` null when the check inherits its tier, and a blocked or declare-only scenario emits none). Every line is parseable with `jq -c`; a typed parse DISCRIMINATES the shape — `serde_json::from_str::<RunReportEnvelope>(line)` targets the envelope line specifically, not every line. Both are report-seam records, so obs-plan §3's self-obs-line vs run-report-envelope split is unaffected. NEVER multi-line — `tracing` JSON flattening serializes everything onto one line.

- **Self-obs stream is a distinct artifact:** the `tracing` self-observation log stream (the cli's: stderr, or `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` under `--agent-mode`) carries per-line base fields — `timestamp_ms`, `level`, `target`, service-identity (`service.name`/`service.version`/`deployment.environment`), `run_id` — per obs-plan §3. It is SEPARATE from this per-run emission journal (`runs/<run_id>.jsonl`, the SLO ground truth + the Run-report envelope above); the two schemas must not be conflated. The stream carries **two line variants over that one base set**: the **event line** (any `tracing` event record — `message` plus its allowlisted fields — at whatever level obs-plan §11's policy assigns that call site, so a hot-path line sits at `debug` where `info` is banned) and the **span-lifecycle line**, which adds `span` (the bounded §4 span name), `span_event` (`new` | `close`), an optional `parent` (the enclosing span's name, absent on a root), and — on the `new` line only — the span's own allowlisted attributes. Both variants are still the self-obs base line, so obs-plan §3's two-record-shapes split (self-obs line vs Run-report envelope) is unchanged, and a span attribute is gated by the same `conductor-core::redact` allowlist as any event field.

PID file

body: - **Location:** N/A — no daemon (security: "no inbound listener of its own"; arch: `conductor-cli` is a one-shot `#[tokio::main(flavor="current_thread")]` binary). Nothing to write or signal.
- **Lifecycle:** N/A — `cleanup` removes on-disk run artifacts and `runs.db` rows instead of signaling a long-lived process.

title: Test data bootstrap

body: - **Strategy:** self-bootstrapping (no developer-seeded data) — deterministic seeded synthetic generation via `conductor-timeline` (same scenario+seed ⇒ same stream shape, Creator Brief).

- **Mechanism:** rstest 0.26.1 `#[fixture]` producing a seeded `conductor-timeline` generator; table-driven `#[rstest]` `#[case]` rows over the catalog (the manifest’s accepted set) and the garde valid/invalid config matrix; `#[once]` fixture for in-memory `runs.db` schema setup; declarative scenario config files (serde + garde) under `scenarios/`, each naming its P-IDs (a P-ID may be named by several). P-032/P-036 require a real git workspace with known recent commits (Creator Brief environment requirement).

- **Per-test isolation:** `rusqlite::Connection::open_in_memory()` per unit/golden test (parallel-safe under nextest's per-test process model); `assert_fs::TempDir` with `.env("CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR", temp.path())` per CLI-subprocess / cross-process test THAT WRITES RUN ARTIFACTS, so the CLI subprocess and the in-process `conductor_run` arm write to the same file `runs.db`. A CLI-edge test of a verb that writes nothing sets the handle NOT AT ALL: `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` is repo-relative by design and `resolve_under` rejects an absolute `temp.path()` at `Paths::resolve()` — before the verb dispatches — so setting it makes every verb fail with empty stdout (measured 2026-09-03 on the `conductor preconditions` edge tests).
- **Cleanup:** test data cleared by the `cleanup` command / `TempDir` drop per session.

title: Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project)

body: _[ALL tiers — explicit derivation hint for downstream consumers per D26 chain.]_

- **test-runner-install:** install cargo-nextest 0.9.137 (via `taiki-e/install-action`) + `cargo test --doc` step + `[dev-dependencies]` assertion/fixture packages: rstest 0.26, assert_cmd 2 + predicates 3, assert_fs 1, insta 1 (`json` feature), proptest 1.9.

- **5-command-discipline-wire:** wire `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` with the 5 commands (boot=precondition probe + preflight gate / run / status / cleanup / logs) per 5-command implementation above. Binding contract — both shell variants must expose identical semantics, a property asserted of the SCRIPTS **together with the invoking environment**: a caller that preempts native-command exits (`$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true`) diverges the `.ps1` leg with zero script delta, measured in CI 2026-09-07 (Windows/Linux dev-OS targets).

- **status-endpoint-implement:** N/A as an endpoint — instead implement the Run-report envelope serializer (shared by `runs.db` row + JSONL journal + Markdown) per Status endpoint shape; polled by reading the `runs.db` row / JSONL journal.

- **log-format-bind-with-obs:** the `tracing-subscriber` JSON journal format is DEFINED here (see Log format above) — this plan is its source of truth and obs derives its product-side log envelope FROM this subsection (binding contract — harness greps the journal for assertions; format break = harness break). The field-allowlist / redaction layer (no host paths, no struct names) is the one piece owned by obs downstream; this plan asserts that boundary via a negative test.
- **pid-file-commitment-wire:** N/A — no daemon. `cleanup` removes run artifacts + `runs.db` rows + releases the `:4317` port-occupier instead.
- **test-data-bootstrap-wire:** wire rstest seeded fixtures + P-ID-keyed scenario config files + in-memory/`TempDir` `runs.db`; cleanup clears between runs.
- **coverage-tooling-install:** install cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7; emit LCOV via `cargo llvm-cov nextest --lcov --output-path lcov.info` (+ `--cobertura coverage.xml` for CI) + `--fail-under-lines` gate.

- **quality-gate-config-emit:** emit GitHub Actions config enforcing coverage threshold (Section 10), zero-retry flakiness budget, `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check`, committed `Cargo.lock`, toolchain ≥ 1.94.1.

route uses this list to plan phase ordering (test-runner-install → 5-command-discipline-wire → status-endpoint-implement → log-format-bind-with-obs → pid-file-commitment-wire → test-data-bootstrap-wire → coverage-tooling-install → quality-gate-config-emit). setup-project materializes each phase's bootstrap script + dependency list + verification command (the log format + envelope shape are defined in this Section 3 and flow downstream to obs; obs derives its envelope from here, not the reverse).

## 2026-09-01-desktop-a11y-sweep — webview E2E registered as two arms; the driven arm's firing form recorded
**Section:** §2 Agent-runnable invariants (determinism) · §3 CI stage selectors · §4 conductor-tauri/ui · §6 Drivers per surface (desktop-webview) · §9 Live-Pulse scenarios · §11 (CI ban, Universal real-network ban)
**Change:**
- §6 records TWO arms over one stack and the driven arm's FULL FIRING FORM as part of the leg — a `PATH` prefix resolving `andromeda-pulse-mcp`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` + `_L4_DETERMINISTIC`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` **equal to the live Pulse's data dir**, and a QUIET WINDOW of ≥120s idle + a 30s resolver tick after any preflight canary.
- §9 admits an npm-script wdio suite as a fourth sanctioned live-leg invocation path; §11's ban parenthetical follows.
- §3 qualifies `--e2e` as the routine suite only, with the `cwd: repoRoot` spawn and the 60s → 15min mocha ceiling.

- §4's ESM-loadability clause widens from `--e2e` to whichever wdio leg loads the member.
**Why:** each precondition has a failure mode that misreads as something else — a bare invocation returns BLOCKED in ~2ms, indistinguishable from a real gate failure (PATH); a default-dir sidecar reads a corpus Pulse never writes, giving `result_count: 0` forever (data dir); and `conductor preflight` fires its own canary, so Pulse's per-`(kind, scope, scope_id)` dedupe means a second canary inside the window forms no fresh incident (quiet window). ## 2026-09-06 0-pending adaptation (subject: `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite`) — the `--live` auto-resolve leg is not run-stable
**Section:** §9 CI Integration — Live-Pulse scenarios (the composed `run --live` stage sentence)
**Change:** The §9 passage recording the composed stage now states the leg's SUT-UPTIME precondition. The auto-resolve leg needs an EMPTY active set at read-back, which holds only while Pulse is inside the emitting service's one-hour bootstrap window. Past that window, `service_went_silent` cues raise new autonomous incidents during the leg's own silent phase, so no window length reaches the arm. Inside it, the window must still clear 150 s from the LAST incident the leg's own preflight formed, and there can be more than one. This is explicitly NOT a source-delta fact: an unchanged tree grades differently by SUT uptime alone, so the leg must not be read as run-stable. Observables 2 and 3 and the driven a11y arm are unaffected.
**Why:** a 0-pending adaptation over a fact this session measured. Three runs of one unchanged scenario graded two ways, and the two failures had DIFFERENT causes. One failed inside the window with no silence cues, because the later of two preflight incidents was only ~122 s old at read-back (the margin). The other failed past the window on silence cues. A retry tuned for only one cause would mis-tune, which is the operator-ratified reason both are stated. The SUT basis was re-verified at HEAD `83d4060`. §9 is the home because it owns the sanctioned live-leg SET and the CI ban that make this leg operator-gated.
**Kept:** the other `run --live` sites register the flag or its exit rule and do not assert the leg's reachability, so they needed no change. The §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 bind is untouched: no envelope, status-read or JSONL shape changed.
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

body:
## 2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven — The auto-resolve leg's not-run-stable verdict is conditioned on the DEFAULT window
**Section:** 9. CI Integration — Live-Pulse scenarios
**Change:** The verdict is now scoped: the leg is not run-stable UNDER THE DEFAULT one-hour window.
- That default is a boot-time posture. `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` is resolved once by `Thresholds::from_env` at Pulse's boot, and Conductor never sets or reads it. The arm's reachability is therefore bounded by the window IN FORCE AT BOOT.
- The suite launches Pulse under a stretched boot-wide window. The stretch removes cause (a) ONLY, and the leg stays not-run-stable under it.

- (B) §10 member enumeration five → six with `conductor-emit`'s 2026-09-14 equivalent mutant; "a new accepted disposition EXTENDS the roster rather than contradicting a single-case literal" unchanged.
- (C) §12 bullet `member-emit-1`, `replace < with <= in quantile` in `latency.rs` (the `u < 0.5` guard): the branches meet at `u = 0.5` with one value (`u / 0.5` exactly `1.0`, `(u - 0.5) / 0.45` exactly `0.0`, both exactly `p50`), the only input the flip re-routes, so every output is a bit-identical `f64` — EXACT `f64` comparison, 5 profiles × 10 008 points, 0 differing. The fifteen timeouts are classified in the citation home and rostered nowhere — `scripts/mutation-gate.py` reads `missed.txt`/`caught.txt`, never `timeout.txt`.

## 2026-10-04-second-test-surface-corrective — the bundled default stops at its first red line in both shells
**Section:** §3 → 5-command implementation (`run` command body; exit code semantics); §1 → 5-command requirements (`run`)
**Change:**
- `run` body: the bundled default stops at its FIRST non-zero cargo line in both shells — `agent-run.sh` by `set -euo pipefail` (as measured: a planted clippy-only `-D warnings` lint ended `run` at exit 101 on the workspace clippy line, after green nextest and doctest lines); `agent-run.ps1` by an explicit `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }` after each of its five cargo lines (since 2026-10-04). It no longer depends on its caller setting `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference`, and the script never sets it. A caller that does set it (CI's dogfood step) still sees the red line throw first (step exit 1, CI#34689135760); one that does not gets that line's own cargo exit. The ps1 green path is proven by CI#37209452847; its red path is read from the script, unmeasured on the Linux dev host (no `pwsh`).
- Exit code semantics (key file and §1): was "non-zero = at least one hard `Fail`"; now also a red build, doctest or `-D warnings` lint line in the bundled default, which ends the run at that line (measured exit 101 with every test green). The reported-states clause is unchanged.
**Why:** before this chunk the ps1 bundled default blocked on a red cargo line only when its caller set the native-command preference; the measured sh behaviour already contradicted the hard-`Fail`-only exit wording.
**Kept:** the `--e2e` capture-then-print caveat (a caller setting the preference preempts the printed verdict) stands — the `--e2e` arm is unchanged.

**Section:** §4 Unit Test Strategy → Mutation instrument
**Change:** Recorded the second half of cargo-mutants' exit-code semantics — the exit code carries no verdict in EITHER direction: `Found 0 mutants to test` is a no-op at exit 0 (already recorded), and a NON-zero exit reflects surviving/timeout CLASSES rather than run failure. **Why:** Measured this chunk: **exit 3** on a scoped run that fully met its acceptance — 51 mutants, 0 missed, all five named survivors killed — with the non-zero owed entirely to two pre-existing timeouts. §4 previously recorded only the exit-0 direction, which implies by omission that a non-zero exit IS a failure; a reader following §4 alone would have inverted this chunk's verdict.
