title: 2026-09-01-webview-self-verify-windows-host — the webview E2E platform verdict, measured
body:
## 2026-09-01-webview-self-verify-windows-host — the webview E2E platform verdict, measured
**Section:** §1 Surfaces under test (:54) · §1 Coverage triggers (:85) · §2 Agent-runnable invariants (:121, :122) · §3 CI stage selectors (:152) · §3 Bootstrap 5-command-discipline-wire (:207) · §4 conductor-tauri/ui (:244) · §5 GUI-leg deferral (:287) · §6 Drivers per surface (:304) · §6 Both-surface parity (:369) · §9 pipeline table (:456) · §9 Matrix builds (:465) · §11 Universal bans (:575, :577) · §12 Decisions Log (:594)
**Change:** The "Linux + `xvfb` only" verdict is retired as a CAPABILITY claim across every site, replaced by the measured platform SET — Linux CI headless under `xvfb`, plus the Windows dev host headful via WebView2 + an operator-supplied `msedgedriver`; macOS alone stays driver-less, which was always the justification's true content. The CI ARRANGEMENT is unchanged (still an `ubuntu-latest` + `xvfb` job; this chunk made no CI edit). `--e2e` now names its measured preconditions (ensure-frontend → release build `--features tauri/custom-protocol` → `wdio run`), "headless only" becomes "non-interactive only" in both bans, the loopback allowlist admits the harness-lifetime WebDriver pair, §85's coverage trigger splits by who READS the handle, §4 records that the build gate does not prove ESM loadability, and §12's dated decision keeps its text with a dated correction appended.
**Why:** The chunk drove a real WebView2 session on Windows, which falsifies the platform verdict but not the driver choice or the macOS clause. The site list ran to EIGHT where the plan's expected-amendments list named six — `:287` and `:369` additionally deferred GUI legs to "Linux+xvfb" — which is why the fix names the set rather than substituting a fresh literal. §4's ESM clause is the sharper finding: `typecheck:e2e` passed for two months over a `wdio.conf.ts` that could not load on any host.

title: 2026-09-01-desktop-a11y-sweep — webview E2E registered as two arms; the driven arm's firing form recorded
body:
## 2026-09-01-desktop-a11y-sweep — webview E2E registered as two arms; the driven arm's firing form recorded
**Section:** §2 Agent-runnable invariants (determinism) · §3 CI stage selectors · §4 conductor-tauri/ui · §6 Drivers per surface (desktop-webview) · §9 Live-Pulse scenarios · §11 (CI ban, Universal real-network ban)
**Change:** (1) §6 records TWO arms over one stack and the driven arm's FULL FIRING FORM as part of the leg — a `PATH` prefix resolving `andromeda-pulse-mcp`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` + `_L4_DETERMINISTIC`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` **equal to the live Pulse's data dir**, and a QUIET WINDOW of ≥120s idle + a 30s resolver tick after any preflight canary. (2) §9 admits an npm-script wdio suite as a fourth sanctioned live-leg invocation path, §11's ban parenthetical follows. (3) §3 qualifies `--e2e` as the routine suite only, with the `cwd: repoRoot` spawn and the 60s → 15min mocha ceiling. (4) §2/§11 name both arms in the loopback allowlist and record the driven arm as a real-clock live-Pulse leg carried only as the operator-local-gate exception. (5) §4's ESM-loadability clause widens from `--e2e` to whichever wdio leg loads the member.
**Why:** each precondition was measured this chunk and each has a failure mode that misreads as something else — a bare invocation returns BLOCKED in ~2ms indistinguishable from a real gate failure (PATH); a default-dir sidecar reads a corpus Pulse never writes, giving `result_count: 0` forever (data dir); and `conductor preflight` fires its own canary, so Pulse's per-`(kind, scope, scope_id)` dedupe means a second canary inside the window forms no fresh incident (quiet window — two 12-minute runs lost to it). The ban on running any live leg as a CI gate is unchanged in force.

Section 6's ROUTINE arm is re-stated from "subject-absent specs context-skip" to fixture-seeded -- it now asserts the verdict lamps for real, and only the load-envelope banner still context-skips, that path carried at the unit + mock-runtime tiers. Section 7 names the committed-journal fixture family in the sanctioned provenance set and requires such a fixture's MEANING be pinned by a production-reader round-trip. Section 5's read-only-command tier now names the source SET rather than `conductor-core` alone.
**Why:** `/runs/` is gitignored, so on a clean tree the coverage rows had no run record to render and the populated-lamp assertion had no subject -- on a dev host it would have passed off local run residue instead. Section 5's `conductor-core` qualifier was falsified outright: `run_envelope` single-sources `conductor-report`'s `RunsDb::get_envelope` via `conductor_run::read_envelope`.

## 2026-09-02-cross-surface-envelope-parity — the rmcp payload retired, the parity deferral discharged, and the seeder re-stated
**Section:** §1 (Entity · Surfaces · Coverage triggers) · §2 (pyramid) · §3 (`boot` · CI stage selectors) · §4 (unit coverage · external services) · §5 (Driver(s) · boundary table · lifecycle · cross-module patterns · the GUI deferral) · §6 (driver table · scenario steps · routine-arm paragraph) · §7 (provenance set · meaning-under-test) · §8 (mocking) · §9 (pipeline) · §10 (coverage exclusions) · §11 (anti-patterns) · §12 (decisions log)
**Change:** (1) Every site describing the CURRENT read-back client or the CURRENT test stub as rmcp was
re-stated to the shipped hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC client (`jsonrpc.rs` + `client.rs`) and the
hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp`. The rmcp token count fell 24 → 5, and each survivor is a deliberate LEAVE:
`:88` / `:558` name the rmcp STDIO injection vulnerability CLASS, `:91` keeps the quoted anti-pattern TITLE
(its mechanism clause amended), `:33` now reads "rmcp removed 2026-06-27" as a historical note, and `:596`
is the decisions-log entry, corrected in place with a dated 2026-09-02 bracket per this doc's own precedent.
(2) The "negotiates DOWN to `2024-11-05`" mechanism was retired at `:91` AND `:278` — the latter carries NO
`rmcp` token, so a token-keyed sweep could not reach it. (3) §5's GUI-parity deferral narrowed: the
mock-runtime ↔ CLI half is DISCHARGED (an equal-envelope test driving both surfaces into one `runs.db`
under a non-default `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`, comparing the two persisted envelopes rather than each against a
literal); the `Channel`-frame-sequence and webview-render halves remain deferred. (4) §3/§6 re-state the
`--e2e` seeder: `seedFixtureRuns()` now invokes the `conductor-run` `envelope_fixture` test target under
`CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` and writes the subject through the production writer, throwing on a non-zero exit.
(5) §6's routine-arm paragraph retires the load-envelope banner's context-skip — the banner now asserts
(label + axe) — while keeping the RULE that an unproducible DOM state context-skips and a skip is never a
pass. (6) §7's provenance SET widened to admit a fixture seeded through the production WRITER, and the
meaning-under-test proof named as a SET (`lamps_fixture.rs` + `envelope_fixture.rs`). (7) §1's Vector-1
trigger gained the third per-reader handle class and its mandated tier.
**Why:** the chunk's Expected-amendments payload plus what the fan-out found beyond it. The site count was
re-derived independently (`grep -c -i rmcp` = 24) rather than taken from an enumeration — the originating
CARRY had named ONE site and the phase distiller claimed 26. (2) and the §6 banner site were found by the
doc-agents' duplicate-occurrence grep, not by the report, whose own enumeration under-ran on both.

title: 2026-09-02-mutation-tier-restored-for-conductor-tauri — the parity leg's first arm was never the mock runtime
body:
## 2026-09-02-mutation-tier-restored-for-conductor-tauri — the parity leg's first arm was never the mock runtime

**Section:** §2 Critical Path 7 (`:80`) · §2 trigger table (`:93`) · §5 Driver(s) (`:264`) · §5 Cross-module
patterns → Cross-surface parity (`:287`) · §5 deferred-leg bullet (`:288`) · §6 Both-surface parity Steps
step 2 (`:370`) + Verification signal (`:371`) — SEVEN sites, all applied.
**Change:** (1) `:287` retired "the Tauri mock-runtime run" as the leg's first arm and names the measured
arm SET — an in-process call to `conductor_run::{preflight, drive_run}` (the composition the Tauri
`start_run` command's thread runs, using no `tauri::*` item) plus the assert_cmd CLI subprocess arm — and
records the leg's new home, `crates/conductor-cli/tests/cross_surface_parity.rs`, a package with no `tauri`
dependency in any section. (2) `:288`'s landed half renamed mock-runtime ↔ CLI → in-process-core ↔ CLI.
(3) `:370`'s step-2 GUI leg restated as the in-process drive, `get_ipc_response()` kept as the driver of the
mock-runtime command-dispatch tier. (4) `:264`'s parity CLI arm now takes its binary path from the declared
build-graph edge `assert_cmd::Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_conductor"))` rather than
`Command::cargo_bin`'s runtime `target/debug` fallback; assert_cmd is unchanged as the assertion library and
`cli_smoke`, inside the owning package, keeps `cargo_bin`. (5) `:80`, `:93` and `:371` — the Critical-Path-7
**Verification signal** and its required-test-type twin — were SPLIT rather than rewritten: the envelope-
equality half is recorded PROVEN by the in-process arm ↔ CLI subprocess pair, and the control-panel-LAUNCHED
half is recorded DEFERRED to the tauri-driver leg (§5) and explicitly still OWED against the Creator Brief.
**Why:** the chunk measured that the parity leg's first arm uses no `tauri::*` item at all — the relocation
to a package with no `tauri` dependency compiles and passes, which makes the mock-runtime attribution
unambiguously false. (1)-(4) are routine spec-illustration → sound-impl alignment (playbook `:28-30`): the
parity invariant is preserved and only the mechanism's description moved. (5) was ESCALATED and resolved
with the operator, because that rule does NOT govern there — its qualifying clause is "contract preserved",
and `:80` sources its signal from the Creator Brief Must-Work ("from the control panel AND headless"), so
rewriting it to the measured mechanism would have retired a brief-sourced requirement to match the evidence.
The operator chose the split. Site count re-derived by a MECHANISM sweep, not a token sweep: the doc-agent's
token grep (`mock-runtime` / `tauri::test` / `get_ipc_response`) found three of the seven; `:80` and `:371`
carry none of those tokens and were found by sweeping what the claim SAYS, and `:93` — "the Tauri-launched
run", under a `cross-surface-coordination` heading — surfaced only in the post-edit verification sweep,
after both earlier passes had missed it.

body:
## 2026-09-03-conductor-run-composition-root-survivors-dispositioned — the `declares` class shrinks, its crate is corrected, and `conductor-run`'s roster member lands

**Section:** §10 Quality Gates — Mutation-survivor disposition (`:500`) · §12 Test Decisions Log — the `declares` bullet (`:607`) and a new `conductor-run` bullet (`:609`)

**Change:** (1) **§12's `declares` bullet no longer carries the `x6` literal** — it names the SET (`lib.rs:358:5` → `false`, `:360:11`, `:360:21`, `:360:26`) and records that the class SHRANK on 2026-09-03 from the six members ratified 2026-08-21, because `observe_run_contract:346` and `declares:358 → true` both proved killable with no env mutation and fell to `observe_run_contract_names_the_term_this_environment_does_not_declare`. (2) **§12 gains a third roster member** — `conductor-run`'s accepted-deliberate classes B (`lib.rs:518:27`, `:559:25` ×2 — unreachable past the fixed `http://127.0.0.1:4317` egress gate) and C (`lib.rs:66:8` — unreachable without the fixed-name `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar on the inherited `PATH`), each with its cited rules and the chunk's `evidence/disposition-ledger.md` as citation home. (3) **§10's inline roster reference is re-attributed and de-counted** — `conductor-verify`'s `declares` env-reading edge ×6 becomes `conductor-run`'s `declares` env-read arms plus the two 2026-09-03 sets, "each enumerated there rather than carried as a count here".

**Why:** The chunk's tier re-run measured the roster wrong on two axes at once. The COUNT: the class was ratified at six, and two members were killed by a single test — the env read lives in `declares` (`crates/conductor-run/src/lib.rs:357`) and not in its caller, so the cited env-at-the-caller rule (`.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-08-10) never covered the enclosing function's mutant nor the always-true arm; only the operator-ratified `:346` attempt was predicted, `declares:358 → true` fell as a side effect. The CRATE: `fn declares` has never been in `conductor-verify` — a workspace-wide `grep -rn 'fn declares' crates/*/src/*.rs` returns the single `conductor-run` hit. And the roster was 4 members short of the 8 accepted-deliberate survivors the tier now reports (118 mutants: 8 missed / 82 caught / 28 unviable / 0 timeout, `missed.txt` matching the accepted set exactly, verified per-site against both tallies). Both §12 bullets follow the D-tests-derived-count discipline of naming the SET rather than substituting a fresh literal that would re-stale.

**Search that establishes the site set:** `grep -n 'declares'` over test-plan (3 hits: `:500`, `:607`, `:608` — the last being `conductor-tauri`'s triple, correct and untouched); `grep -nE '(x|×)6'` (2 hits, `:500` and `:607`, both amended); and a mechanism sweep for the retired attribution across all seven masters plus the three preserve-verbatim curation homes (CLAUDE.md `USER:session-learnings`, `.claude/rules/testing.md` `## Session Additions`, `docs/session-learnings.md`) and the two judgment bases (`playbook.md`, `drift-base.md`) — **zero hits outside test-plan**. `security-plan.md:114` states the attribution correctly already and needed no change. The two cascade leaves (`.claude/rules/testing.md:19`, `.claude/docs/tests-summary.md:12`) carry the rule and the phrase "the accepted roster is a SET recorded in test-plan §12" but no count and no crate attribution, so they were consistent by construction and required no re-derivation. Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-03-conductor-run-composition-root-survivors-dispositioned/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`.

title: 2026-09-04-sidecar-spawn-without-a-console-window — a zone that cannot be unit-asserted, and the roster's fourth member
body:
## 2026-09-04-sidecar-spawn-without-a-console-window — a zone that cannot be unit-asserted, and the roster's fourth member
**Section:** §1 Test Scope Summary — Untestable zones · §12 Test Decisions Log — mutation-instrument roster · §10 Quality Gates — Mutation-survivor disposition (inline sample) · §6 E2E Test Strategy — Drivers per surface (desktop-webview row)
**Change:** (1) §1 gains an untestable zone for the APPLIED Windows creation flag: `std::process::Command` exposes exactly five getters and none for creation flags (measured 2026-09-04, rustc 1.95.0), so `build_command`'s `.creation_flags(...)` is not assertable through `as_std()` — the flag VALUE is unit-covered and its APPLICATION is SR-leg evidence, never a manual smoke step. (2) §12's roster gains its FOURTH member — `conductor-verify`'s accepted-deliberate pair at `spawn.rs:116:5` (`sidecar_resolves_on_path` → `true` / `false`) — recorded as the enumerated SET with its rejection rationale. (3) §10's inline sample of that roster is extended to four so it does not enumerate three against a four-member set. (4) §6's desktop-webview driver row widens the measured msedgedriver/WebView2 working SET to include Runtime 152.0.4191.62.
**Why:** Report §Counts / qualifiers moved ("test-plan §12 mutation-survivor roster: 3 members → 4") and §Coverage of new surfaces (the creation-flag path graded `tests unrunnable-here at unit tier … recorded as a test-plan §1 untestable zone`). The roster entry is written as the SET, never a count, per the standing rule that a count re-stales on the next addition; the same reason drives §6 naming a runtime PAIR rather than substituting `.62` for `.53` — the driver was un-refreshed across the host bump, so the datum is that the pairing widened, not that it moved. Routine under playbook `:127` (set-naming) for §6, and under the doc's own agent-driven invariant for §1. The §12 entry records that an agreement test was CONSIDERED and REJECTED for the pair, because it would kill exactly one arm host-dependently and make the score mean different things on different hosts (§10 zero-flakiness) — the rejection is part of the disposition, not omitted from it. **Search performed:** grep of test-plan.md for the moved counts (`3 members`, `96`, `852`, `34 announced`, `15 findings`, `152.0.4191.53`) and for `roster` / `accepted-deliberate` / `untestable` read for the claim however worded — 4 sites owed an edit, all 4 amended; §1's `14 rows not-run-here` was checked and is unmoved (this chunk's SR record still grades 15 browse-class rows `not-run-here`, and §1 claims no exhaustive findings count). **Deliberately NOT amended (escalation E2, operator-resolved 2026-09-04):** §9 Matrix builds and its Pipeline E2E row, where a detector proposed retiring the stated 3-OS matrix and the separate `ubuntu-latest` + `xvfb` webview job against the measured `ci.yml` (exactly two jobs, both `windows-latest`). Dismissed as an UNIMPLEMENTED PLAN rather than drift: §9 states target state, already distinguishes CI arrangement from capability, and the markerless route entry *A11y CI gate* explicitly owns building it — retiring the claim would delete a plan, not correct a falsehood. The measured two-job reality is recorded in the chunk report's Outcome row and the handoff instead. Also NOT amended: `TokioChildProcess` at `:597`, which sits in this §12 Decisions Log already carrying an inline `[2026-09-02 correction: rmcp was removed 2026-06-27 …]` — a decisions-log record is annotated, never rewritten.

title: 2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite — the `--live` stage flag, and the `sleep(N)` ban's scope
body:
## 2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite — the `--live` stage flag, and the `sleep(N)` ban's scope
**Section:** §2 Test Strategy — Agent-runnable invariants (determinism) · §3 Test Harness Contract — CI stage selectors · §9 CI Integration — Live-Pulse scenarios · §11 Test Anti-Patterns — CI · §11 Test Anti-Patterns — E2E
**Change:** Five edits. (a) §3's stage-selector bullet names `--live` beside `--unit`/`--integration`/`--e2e`, with its composition (leading non-priming `conductor preconditions` → B1 → B2 → 150s quiet window → A → the driven a11y arm), its per-leg freeze to `runs/live-suite/{leg}.jsonl`, and the facts that it is a sibling `case` branch (so the 5-command discipline holds), adds no port/env/`CONDUCTOR_*` handle, and leaves the envelope / `status` read / JSONL shapes untouched so §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree. (b) §9's sanctioned operator/local live-leg SET gains `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} run --live` as the composed invocation, and records that `[features] live-pulse = []` now gates a SET of targets (`lifecycle_live.rs` + the new `live_suite.rs`), each still owing its own per-feature clippy. (c) §11's CI ban repeats the SET, so the four-path enumeration could not survive a single-site apply; the ban itself (never a CI gate) is unchanged. (d) §2's determinism bullet adds the `--live` suite to the enumerated operator-local real-wall-clock exceptions, which previously closed at two members. (e) §11's `sleep(N)` ban gains a SCOPE clarification.
**Why:** `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite` landed the flag in both shells at identical semantics (report §Harness / gate surface); the plan carried §3 and §9 as Expected amendments and the report's dispositions locate the sites (`--e2e` → 5 hits in this plan; `workflow_dispatch` → 1 hit at the §9 SET). (d) is required because a new non-deterministic real-wall-clock leg outside the enumerated exception set reads as a §10 zero-flakiness break. **(e) was NARROWED from what the detector proposed, deliberately.** The proposal asked for a CARVE-OUT permitting a fixed wall-clock wait on the operator-local gate; that was REJECTED. The 150s quiet window is in the harness shell BETWEEN legs, not inside a test, so §11's ban — whose subject is in-test synchronisation — was never violated and needed no permission. What was applied is a scope clarification: the ban's subject is stated, the quiet window is named as a firing-form precondition reproducing a SUT-side dedupe window that emits no signal to wait on, and the closing sentence re-asserts that nothing inside a test may sleep to synchronise. A ban is not weakened to accommodate something outside it. **Search performed:** `--unit`/`--integration`/`--e2e` enumerations across all seven masters → this plan (§3, §9, §11) and layout-templates `:189` (amended in the same pass); `workflow_dispatch` → 1 hit; the retired closed-set wording re-read at each hit rather than pattern-substituted.

title: 2026-09-06 0-pending adaptation (subject: `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite`) — the `--live` auto-resolve leg is not run-stable
body:
## 2026-09-06 0-pending adaptation (subject: `2026-09-06-operator-gated-live-suite`) — the `--live` auto-resolve leg is not run-stable
**Section:** §9 CI Integration — Live-Pulse scenarios (the composed `run --live` stage sentence)
**Change:** The §9 passage that records the composed stage now carries the leg's SUT-UPTIME precondition: the auto-resolve leg needs an EMPTY active set at read-back, which holds only while Pulse is inside the emitting service's one-hour bootstrap window. Past it, `service_went_silent` cues raise new autonomous incidents during the leg's own silent phase, so no window length reaches the arm; inside it, the window must still clear 150 s measured from the LAST incident the leg's own preflight formed, which can be more than one. Stated explicitly as NOT a source-delta fact — an unchanged tree grades differently by SUT uptime alone, so the leg must not be read as run-stable. Observables 2 and 3 and the driven a11y arm are recorded unaffected.
**Why:** A 0-pending adaptation over a fact this session measured (SKILL step 6's self-produced-fact door). Three runs of one unchanged scenario on 2026-09-06 graded two ways, and the two failures had DIFFERENT causes — which is why both are recorded rather than the simpler "the margin model is false": reached 09:17Z (~6 min into the window); failed 10:07Z INSIDE the window with ZERO silence cues in its span (the day's first was 10:11:09.723Z) because two preflight incidents formed at 10:07:18 and 10:07:53 and the later was only ~122 s old at read-back — genuinely the margin; failed 11:00Z past the window on silence cues (incidents 11:00:33, 11:02:02). A re-attempt tuning for only one cause would mis-tune, which is the operator-ratified reason both are stated. SUT basis re-verified at HEAD `83d4060` (`activity_floor.rs:36`, `emitter.rs:186`, test at `:1104`). §9 is the right home because it owns the sanctioned live-leg SET and the CI ban that make this leg operator-gated in the first place. **Search performed:** `run --live` across all seven masters → test-plan (§2, §3, §9, §11) and layout-templates `:189`; each read for whether it asserts the leg's reachability — only §9's passage describes the leg's preconditions, the others register the flag or its exit rule, so no dependent proposal. The lateral §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 bind is untouched: no envelope, status-read or JSONL shape changed.

title: 2026-09-06-run-report-envelope-conformance-gate — cleanup teardown re-homed to the binary; status reads the newest ENVELOPE line
body:
## 2026-09-06-run-report-envelope-conformance-gate — cleanup teardown re-homed to the binary; status reads the newest ENVELOPE line
**Section:** 3. Test Harness Contract - 5-command implementation (`cleanup` body, `status` body) + 1. Test Scope Summary (5-command `status`)
**Change:** THREE sites. (1) SS3 `cleanup` body: the shells keep only `rm -f runs/<run_id>.{jsonl,md}` and then call `conductor cleanup <run_id>` - the shells issue NO SQL; the three bound-parameter deletes run inside the binary as literal statements in one transaction (`RunsDb::delete_run`). The `sqlite3` CLI could not have honoured the prescribed `?1` form at all (no bind facility) and is present on neither this host nor any CI runner. (2) SS3 `status` body: the journal read targets the NEWEST ENVELOPE line, never the file's last line, with both shells selecting it by the envelope-only `seed` key. (3) SS1 5-command `status`: the same qualification on its Mechanism clause.
**Why:** Report expected amendments E2 and E4. The `status` defect was MEASURED, not inferred: on a seeded mixed-shape journal the verb reported a `CheckRecord`'s fields as the envelope (`seed: null`, `slo_tier: null`, exit 0); after the fix both shells print `seed: 424242`, `slo_tier: "<90s"`. The SS1 site is a `dependent-of` the D-tests-obs-harness detector found and the report's own E4 locating grep could NOT see - it carries no `**status**` bolding, so a single-site apply would have left the unqualified-read claim standing. SS3 <-> obs-plan SS3 still agree: obs-plan owns no status mechanism and the envelope/JSONL shapes are untouched.

## 2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate — Path 6 gate surface shipped; CI matrix re-based on measurement

**Section:** §1 Critical Path 6 · §4 Unit Test Strategy (Scenario catalog + coverage-matrix bullet) · §6 E2E → Coverage-matrix completeness gate scenario · §9 CI Integration → Matrix builds
**Change:** (1) §1 Path 6's surface qualifier now names the shipped gate — the crate-local `conductor-report --test coverage_gate` target, CI-enforced by the `ci.yml` "Coverage-completeness gate" step over the COMMITTED `coverage-matrix.md`, LF-pinned by `.gitattributes`. (2) §4's bullet split: per-scenario P-ID keying stays unit-tier, while the zero-unclassified assertion is re-homed to the crate-local `tests/` tier (it must reach both `conductor_core::check_sut_drift` and `conductor_report::CoverageMatrix::render`, which only that side of the dependency edge can do). (3) §6's mechanism replaced: the retired `assert_cmd` exit-code + insta-golden / static row-count form is superseded by the three shipped arms (runtime manifest load via `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; a negative arm removing each classified row IN TURN asserting `Err(CoreError::SutDrift)` naming the dropped id; byte-equality to `CoverageMatrix::render()`), noting that a row count is the literal-count form this path's own Verification signal forbids. (4) §9 Matrix builds: the three-OS matrix and the separate `ubuntu-latest`+`xvfb` webview-E2E job are re-stated as the TARGET arrangement owned by the *A11y CI gate* route entry; the SHIPPED arrangement is measured as two `windows-latest` jobs (`ci.yml:18`, `:178`). The leg's platform CAPABILITY is untouched.
**Why:** (1)-(3) are the operationalization reconciliation (playbook: a chunk first BUILDING a spec'd gate reconciles that spec's own stale description) — report Expected amendments (3), 5 sites located by `grep -n 'coverage-matrix' .andromeda/test-plan.md`. (4) is D-platform-claim, ESCALATED because the gap is pre-existing and the *A11y CI gate* entry owns the CI-job work; operator resolution 2026-09-06 was NARROW — retire only false PRESENT-TENSE claims, leave target-state descriptions standing. NOT applied: the proposed §9 stage-table row for this gate — its rationale quoted §9 as claiming "the stage table above is the complete inventory of gates CI enforces", which does not exist there (verified by `awk` over §9 piped to `grep -nE 'complete inventory|inventory of gates'` → no match), and the prior chunk's equivalent CI gate step took no row either (`grep -nE 'conformance|journal_conformance' .andromeda/test-plan.md` → 0 hits). Operator resolution: no row, follow the precedent. Six further D-platform-claim sites in this master were left standing under the same NARROW ruling.

title: 2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven — The auto-resolve leg's not-run-stable verdict is conditioned on the DEFAULT window
body:
## 2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven — The auto-resolve leg's not-run-stable verdict is conditioned on the DEFAULT window
**Section:** 9. CI Integration — Live-Pulse scenarios
**Change:** The stated verdict is scoped: the leg is not run-stable UNDER THE DEFAULT one-hour window. That default is a boot-time posture — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` resolved once by `Thresholds::from_env` at Pulse's boot, which Conductor never sets or reads — so the arm's reachability is bounded by the window IN FORCE AT BOOT. The suite now launches Pulse under a stretched boot-wide window, and the booted posture is confirmed by grepping Pulse's log for the TARGET `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override` (level WARN, reason="env_override", resolved_seconds) — never for the emitting function name, which appears nowhere in the log.
**Why:** Leg A reached `KnownResidual` via the `ReadBack::AutoResolved` arm on 2026-09-07 under that posture after failing to reproduce on 2026-09-06, discharging the chunk's CARRY. NARROWED at the light gate, before commit: the wrap's own literal re-run graded the SAME tree under the SAME posture `ManualCheck`, with the evaluator provably disarmed in both runs (`silence_cues_emitted: 0`), so the body now states the posture removes cause (a) ONLY and the leg stays not-run-stable under it — what separated the two runs was when the window's last incident formed (+45s vs +137s). The TARGET string is carried per the wrap directive: the prior wording named the emitting function (`warn_bootstrap_window`), which no log line contains, so a light-gate grep could never hit.

title: 2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed — printed-verdict contract conditioned; a11y job measured red; step set opened
body:
## 2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed — printed-verdict contract conditioned; a11y job measured red; step set opened
**Section:** §3 `run` → `--e2e` CI stage selectors · §3 Bootstrap phases → `5-command-discipline-wire` · §6 Drivers per surface (desktop-webview row) · §9 Pipeline structure (E2E webview row) · §9 Matrix builds (OS bullet)
**Change:** Five amendments. (1) §3 `--e2e`: the printed-verdict contract holds only where the INVOKING environment does not preempt the capture-then-print — a caller setting `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true` turns wdio's non-zero into a terminating error before the script prints or asserts, leaving one `NativeCommandExitException` line and none of the verdict; the CI gate step's setting was removed at this chunk, both shells byte-unchanged. (2) §3 `5-command-discipline-wire`: the identical-semantics binding contract is asserted of the SCRIPTS together with the invoking environment, since such a caller diverges the `.ps1` leg with ZERO script delta. (3) §6 desktop-webview row: the baked `10 passing / 2 skipped` sample de-literalized to the SET it evidences (fully green with only the two live-hold subjects skipped), noting the pass tally is a moving count — 12 as of 2026-09-07. (4) §9 E2E row: the a11y job's step set is no longer closed — two `continue-on-error` diagnostic steps and an `if: always()` `a11y-session-diag` upload joined it, with the rule that the GATE step itself never carries `continue-on-error`. (5) §9 Matrix builds: the job's first push-triggered run is still owed, but the job HAS run in CI (four `ci-probe/` runs) and is RED at WebView2 session creation, owner named as the *Hosted-runner WebView2 session* route entry.
**Why:** D-tests-obs-harness (primary + 1 dependent) and D-tests-derived-count ×3, all substantiated by the report. (3) is the one that caught the ORCHESTRATOR: the report's own site search for the moved count used `'10 spec\|ten spec\|12 spec'` — 0 hits — and concluded no master baked it; the doc spells it `10 passing`, which `grep -rn '10 passing' .andromeda/*.md` returns as this single hit. The probe keyed on a proxy for the claim rather than on what the doc says. Applied as a DE-LITERALIZATION per the detector's own `check` text (name the set, never substitute a fresh literal that re-stales), so the sample stops carrying a value that ages every time the arm grows.

title: 2026-09-08-hosted-runner-webview2-session — driver↔runtime pair SET; hosted-runner capability bounded to the measured runtime
body:
## 2026-09-08-hosted-runner-webview2-session — driver↔runtime pair SET; hosted-runner capability bounded to the measured runtime
**Section:** §1 Surfaces under test (desktop-webview Driver) · §2 Agent-runnable invariants · §6 Drivers-per-surface table (desktop-webview Mode cell) · §6 cross-surface parity step 2 · §9 CI Integration Matrix builds
**Change:** Seven amendments across five sections. (1) §6's Mode cell pairing clause now names the measured set of PAIRS split by the dev host's driver refresh at 2026-09-02 14:45 local — passing = {runtime 152.0.4191.53 x driver 151.0.4129.101, the 2026-09-02 MORNING window only} u {runtime 152.0.4191.x x driver 152.0.4191.53, every run since}, failing = {runtime 151.0.4129.101 x driver 151.0.4129.101} on the hosted image — and records that the 2026-09-04 runs were NOT "un-refreshed" as previously stated. (2)-(6) the five sites stating the hosted `windows-2025` runner as a proven headful WebView2 host (§9 OS bullet primary; §1, §2, §6-parity, §6-Mode opening clause as dependents) now name the dev host as the only member measured to DRIVE a session, with the runner wired-but-non-driving.
**Why:** D-tests-derived-count (1 proposal) and D-platform-claim (1 primary + 4 dependents), substantiated by the report's `Counts / qualifiers moved` and `Spec claims disproved by measurement` #1. The driver attribution was measured false at this chunk: the dev-host driver binary carries mtime 2026-09-02 14:45 and today's driver-alone probe returned `msedgedriverVersion 152.0.4191.53` against `browserVersion 152.0.4191.66`. The morning half was VERIFIED true rather than retired, on that chunk's own evidence timestamps (`chunks/2026-09-02-screen-reader-manual-spec/evidence/nvda-pass.json`, subjects 10:41-10:44Z, before the 12:45Z refresh) — so the amendment splits the claim instead of discarding it. **Scope bounded on operator ruling:** the capability retirement names the hosted image AS SHIPPED (WebView2 Runtime 151.0.4129.101) rather than asserting a flat incapacity, because probe (a) measured that image at that runtime and nothing wider; whether a runtime-152 install in-job changes it is recorded OPEN and owned by the follow-up route entry. (7) §6's Mode cell additionally records the MECHANISM behind the driver's long-observed silence about the profile path: msedgedriver creates its own `%TEMP%\scoped_dir<pid>_<rand>\EBWebView` (two siblings per session, one holding the profile), reports `"userDataDir": ""` in a SUCCEEDED session's own capability response, and overrides an inherited `WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER` — so the path exists while the driver's output names it nowhere. Operator-directed at this wrap (builder's judgment on placement). Sweep basis: `grep -cE '151\.0\.4129|152\.0\.4191'` over all seven masters (test-plan 1, a11y-plan 2, other five 0) plus retired-wording sweeps for `un-refreshed`, `under a 151`, `151 msedgedriver`, `cross-major` with `windows-2025` as the known-positive control; the only surviving hits are this master's own new correcting text and a11y-plan:115, which was verified TRUE and deliberately left standing.

title: 2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate — CI arrangement re-based to the measured job set; the runtime × driver PAIR retired as a discriminator
body:
## 2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate — CI arrangement re-based to the measured job set; the runtime × driver PAIR retired as a discriminator
**Section:** §1 Surfaces under test (desktop-webview Driver note) · §6 E2E Test Strategy — Drivers per surface (the Failing entry) · §9 CI Integration — Matrix builds (OS bullet, two distinct claims on one line)
**Change:** FOUR edits on three sections. (1) §9's OS bullet said "the SHIPPED CI arrangement is measured as two jobs, both `windows-latest` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:18`, `:178`, measured 2026-09-06)". Measured false this chunk by parsing the workflow: THREE jobs — `rust` and `frontend` on `windows-latest`, `a11y` on `windows-2025`. Re-based to the measured job set named BY JOB rather than by line coordinate, which the same bullet already forbids two clauses later. (2) The same line's second, distinct claim — "**Whether installing WebView2 Runtime 152+ in-job changes it is OPEN** — owned by the follow-up probe route entry, and untested as of this writing" — is retired as measured: run `34280136892` installed Evergreen 152.0.4191.66 and the bare-app probe still reported `DevToolsActivePort first seen: never within 90s`. (3) §1's desktop-webview Driver note drops "a runtime-152 install in-job is untested" for the measured result. (4) §6's Failing entry is re-keyed from the `{151 × 151}` pair to the hosted IMAGE at both measured runtimes, and now states that **the PAIR is not the discriminator**: a 152 × 151 combination both PASSES on the dev host (152.0.4191.53 × 151.0.4129.101) and FAILS on the hosted image (152.0.4191.66 × 151.0.4129.101) — same runtime major, same driver, opposite outcomes. What differs is the runtime PATCH (53 vs 66, unmeasured as a cause and named as such) and the image; the open variable is the hosted image itself, a policy or session property, owned by the `v2-24` deferral note.
**Why:** D-platform-claim (2 primaries + 2 `dependent-of`), substantiated by the report's *Spec claims disproved by measurement* bullets. Edit (4)'s framing is the operator's correction at the P2 escalation: extending the measured set alone would have left the table implying the pair still discriminates at major granularity, which the dev-host PASS at the same majors falsifies. Edits (2)–(4) had no matching playbook rule, were ESCALATED, and were approved with the accompanying rule minted. Note the intra-line hazard handled here: `:469` carried TWO distinct claims needing two separate edits — a single verbatim apply would have left one standing.

title: 2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle — singleton remedy widened to a SET; tauri-cli joins the tool-floor roster
body:
## 2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle — singleton remedy widened to a SET; tauri-cli joins the tool-floor roster
**Section:** §11 Test Anti-Patterns — Integration (process-global singleton) · §4 Unit Test Strategy — Tool-version policy
**Change:** TWO edits. (1) §11's process-global-singleton remedy was stated exclusively — "The remedy is a test binary of its own" — and is now a SET of two with the discriminator named: (a) an own test binary, the default answer; (b) a shared in-module guard serializing ONLY the tests that touch the singleton, which is the answer when the tests are INLINE over crate-private helpers and (a) would require `pub` on those helpers, widening the crate's public API for tests alone — forbidden by architecture.md §Established Decisions [Module Boundaries]. Both arms carry the same discriminator, green under BOTH runners. The runner-knob ban is byte-unchanged and re-stated explicitly: serializing the FILE with `--test-threads=1` or a profile setting still hides the defect, and an in-code guard is not that. The body marks the evidence `as measured 2026-09-10`. (2) §4's Tool-version policy roster gains `tauri-cli` beside cargo-nextest / cargo-llvm-cov / cargo-mutants, with the note that it is the BUNDLER and that neither it nor `tauri-bundler` appears in any lockfile — the `tauri` CRATE the lock resolves is a different artifact — installed `cargo install tauri-cli --locked`, floor measured 2.11.4.
**Why:** Edit (1) is D-tests-coverage, **escalated and resolved WITH the operator**: two sound specs collided (test-plan's exclusive remedy vs arch's visibility boundary) and this chunk resolved it by measurement — the `conductor-core` panic-hook pair took the guard, green under nextest and `cargo test -p conductor-core` plus 12/12 under forced contention, with `obs.rs:396` citing §11 by name while doing what §11 called not-the-remedy. Leaving the exclusivity would have left the doc contradicting shipped, measured-sound code. Edit (2) is D-tests-framework AND the chunk plan's own `Expected amendments (wrap)` entry, reconciled at Validate check 5; `grep -c 'tauri-cli'` over the seven masters returned **0 hits in all seven** before this pass, so it is an ADDITION with no other occurrence to sweep.

title: 2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed — the same candidate pair retired at both its sites; the a11y diagnostic-step literal de-literalized to a SET
body:
## 2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed — the same candidate pair retired at both its sites; the a11y diagnostic-step literal de-literalized to a SET
**Section:** §9 CI Integration — Matrix builds · §6 E2E Test Strategy — Drivers per surface (desktop-webview row) · §9 CI Integration — Pipeline structure (E2E-webview row)
**Change:** THREE edits on three sections. (1) §9 Matrix builds' clause "with a hosted-image policy or session property the leading unmeasured candidate" is retired on the same measurement as the architecture.md site — CI run `34586959536`: policy keys ABSENT on the hosted runner AND the dev host, runner `SessionId 2` / `UserInteractive: True` — and states no replacement candidate, recording the elevation difference as a difference rather than a cause and the third probe as having returned no reading. (2) §6's desktop-webview driver row restated the SAME claim in different words ("The open variable is therefore the hosted image itself — a policy or session property —"); it now says the image remains the open variable while both named candidates are measured and retired, leaving no named candidate. The "not a runtime × driver pairing" half is unchanged. title: 3. Test Harness Contract
body:
## 3. Test Harness Contract

_[ALL tiers — central agent-driven mechanism; Section consumed by
setup-project to materialize scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}]_

Architecture committed to the harness pattern: **agent-driven — the headless `scripts/agent-run.sh` path is the source of truth and the release gate; the GUI is a thin shell over the same core commands** (upstream-context arch Test Harness Commitment). This section specifies the concrete contract. Conductor has **no daemon and no inbound listener** (security: "zero network exposure ... no inbound listener of its own"), so `boot` is a precondition probe plus a preflight readiness gate and `status` reads disk artifacts — there is no HTTP/IPC status endpoint.

title: 5-command implementation
body:
### 5-command implementation

**`boot`** — precondition probe, then preflight readiness gate (no daemon to start):
- Leading arm: `cargo run -p conductor-cli --bin conductor -- preconditions` — non-zero on an unmet subject SHORT-CIRCUITS `boot`, skipping the preflight invocation (and its two derived timeout budgets) rather than paying it; no `ReadyState` JSON is emitted. Identical semantics in `.sh` and `.ps1` — the short-circuit is environment-CONDITIONAL, firing only on an actually-unmet subject (measured 2026-09-04, both shells exit 0 and emit `ReadyState` JSON under a satisfied environment; the 2026-09-03 both-shells-exit-1 witness measured the pre-fix state, when the subject could not be met). The probe mints no `Verdict`, `ReportState` or per-P-ID row, so the envelope / status-read / JSONL shapes are untouched and §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree.
- Command body (**reached through `boot`** — the leading probe's `handles-declared` subject is satisfiable, so `boot` proceeds here and this body plus its two derived timeout budgets are paid; measured in the full shipped shell SET at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence/report.md`: `scripts/agent-run.sh` 2026-09-04T17:07:17→17:08:04Z and `scripts/agent-run.ps1` 17:11:16→17:12:03Z, both exit 0 with `ready: true` / `canary_round_trip: "ok"` and zero `skipped preflight` lines. Invoking it directly remains valid, not required): `cargo run -p conductor-cli --bin conductor -- preflight --json` — runs the MCP `initialize` handshake through the hand-rolled JSON-RPC client over the spawned sidecar's stdio (arch Standard Contracts: asserts the `protocolVersion` read back from that result against the pinned `2024-11-05`, required-tool presence vs. pinned `contracts/` manifest, then round-trips a canary incident via `query_incident_list` to prove data-dir wiring). In CI the live-Pulse leg is unavailable, so `boot` runs against the hand-rolled `stub_pulse_mcp` child binary (test-research Mocking) which returns a `ready:true` canary; the live-Pulse leg is `workflow_dispatch`/local-only gated on `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`.
- Readiness signal: stdout JSON `{"ready": true}`; `ready:false` ⇒ every dependent scenario reports `state="Blocked"` with the named precondition string (security anti-pattern: never silently downgrade a failed preflight to pass/fail/manual-check).
- Exit code: 0 on `ready:true` within timeout; non-zero on handshake failure (transport refused surfaces as `Result::Err`, a harness fault — security Vector 5).
- Timeout: **two budgets, both derived — never a literal.** (a) The *in-process* canary poll: `CONDUCTOR_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 30) for the MCP `initialize` + canary round-trip, raised to the run contract's effective floor — `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml` `[incident_formation].min_canary_poll_seconds`, which must outlast Pulse's L3 digest cadence — so the live-Pulse leg must allow at least that floor. (b) The *wall-clock wrapper* `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` `boot` applies around `conductor preflight`: both shells derive it per invocation from the same contract as `warmup_ms/1000 + poll + margin`, because the warm-up pre-roll runs BEFORE the poll starts and a wrapper set to the poll alone kills the run mid-poll. A missing contract term is a hard exit 2, never a silent default; a lowered `CONDUCTOR_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT` clamps up to the floor. The stub leg still completes in <1s (it drives `CanaryPoll::immediate()`, so no real clock is involved).

**`run`** — invoke test suites + scenario catalog:
- Command body (CI build+test gate, arch CI/CD): `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` (cargo-nextest 0.9.137 → JUnit XML at `.config/nextest.toml` `[profile.ci.junit]`) then `cargo test --workspace --doc` (nextest does not run doctests — test-research baseline-fallback note) then `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Scenario invocation: `cargo run -p conductor-cli --bin conductor -- run <scenario|P-ID> [--seed <s>]` for the named dynamic scenarios (`error-baseline-spike`, `fingerprint-storm`, `restart-suppression`, `pii-scrub`, `connection-lifecycle`, `severity-lifecycle`) and per-P-ID scenarios; `conductor suite` for the full catalog. A P-ID target resolves only where ONE scenario names it: `run` (and the harness's `SCENARIO=`, passed straight through) REFUSES a P-ID that several scenarios name, before any scenario load — a harness fault naming the P-ID, the count and the matching scenario stems (never a host path), rendered as `error:` + `hint: pass one of the named scenarios instead of the P-ID` at exit 1 (`cli_smoke::run_refuses_a_p_id_named_by_several_scenarios`) — and several P-IDs are named by more than one scenario (seven at 2026-09-30, P-018 among them), so name the scenario; a single-owner P-ID still resolves. `preconditions --for` refuses a P-ID outright, at argument parsing. The harness scenario leg (`SCENARIO=<name|P-ID> [SEED=<n>] scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1} run`) appends `--seed` ONLY when `SEED` is explicitly set — with it unset the TOML-declared seed governs (arch files-over-env-defaults precedence; identical `.sh`/`.ps1` semantics) and the envelope records the effective seed.
- Exit code semantics: 0 = all checks `Pass`; non-zero = at least one hard `Fail` (cargo-nextest `NextestExitCode` 100); `blocked`/`ManualCheck`/`KnownResidual`/`CalibrationRegion` are reported states in the envelope, NOT process-failure exits (Creator Brief assertion-policy split: model-interpretive claims are "calibration-region checks + report-for-human, never hard-failed").
- Output format: machine-parseable — cargo-nextest `ci` profile JUnit XML (parsed by `dorny/test-reporter` into PR annotations) for the test gate; the Run-report envelope JSONL/`runs.db` row for the scenario leg.
- Test selection (fast iteration): `cargo nextest run -p conductor-<seam>` for a single seam crate; `cargo nextest run -E 'test(<name>)'` for a single test; `conductor run <scenario> --seed <s>` for one scenario (a P-ID target resolves only where a single scenario names it; a P-ID several scenarios name is refused, naming them — see `run` above).
- CI stage selectors: the `run` command takes mutually-exclusive `--unit` / `--integration` / `--e2e` flags so the Section 9 pipeline can split it into parallel stages — plus, since 2026-09-06, the operator-gated `--live`, which is NOT a CI stage and is reachable from no default path (a sibling `case` branch on `run`, so the 5-command discipline holds and both shells ship it at identical semantics). `--live` takes an optional third-token SELECTOR (2026-09-22) and composes one of two shapes. **Bare `--live`** is the live-Pulse suite: a leading non-priming `conductor preconditions` probe (an unmet subject refuses at exit 1 with `[PRECONDITION]` lines and no leg fires) → the ordered leg set the shells' own `live_leg_order` owns — at 2026-09-07 that is leg H (`halo-hue-encoding`, budget `live_leg_budget_sec 180`, first because its sustained stream must not sit inside leg A's silence window) → leg B1 → leg B2 → a 150 s quiet window → leg A → the driven a11y arm (read the order from `live_leg_order` in `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`, never from a count restated here) (`ensure_frontend` + the release build with `--features tauri/custom-protocol` → `npm run a11y:driven`), freezing each leg's `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` to `runs/live-suite/{leg}.jsonl` because that sink truncates per invocation. **`--live real-model`** runs the ONE real-model leg instead of the suite: `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation` (the scenario's real-model posture requires the L4 handle absent or falsy under the union truthiness rule; an unmet subject refuses at exit 1 and no leg fires) → a pre-build of the capture binary → the non-recursive removal of `runs/live-suite/{rm.jsonl,rm-capture.txt,rm-capture.err}` → the grading rule's `rule_record` into `rm-capture.txt` BEFORE the leg (a non-zero exit stops the arm, so no counted drive of the series is spent) → `live_leg rm real-model-interpretation` → the `real_model_live` capture (stdout appended, stderr to `rm-capture.err`, `RUST_LOG` removed for both test invocations) → printed reminders. An unknown selector prints `usage: <script> run --live [real-model]` and exits 2 before any probe, in both shells; `boot` keeps the flagless probe. It adds no port, env var or `CONDUCTOR_*` handle, and leaves the envelope, the `status` disk read and the JSONL shapes untouched — so §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree (`--unit` ⇒ the `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` leg only — `cargo test --workspace --doc` and `cargo clippy` are their own separate Section 9 stages (Doctest / Lint), NOT folded into `--unit`; `--integration` ⇒ the hand-rolled MCP stub + `tauri::test` mock-runtime + in-memory/`TempDir` `runs.db` leg; `--e2e` ⇒ ensure-frontend, then a release build with `--features tauri/custom-protocol` (a plain `--release` binary loads `devUrl` and measures nothing — the feature, not the profile, decides bundle embedding), then the tauri-driver `wdio run` leg — the ROUTINE suite only (wdio default `specs` narrowed to `accessibility.e2e.ts` on 2026-09-01; the `driven` suite sits outside the 5-command harness as the operator leg described in §6/§9. **Since 2026-09-07 both shells ASSERT THE PRINTED VERDICT, not the exit code** — the leg's exit cannot separate a full pass from a total skip, because the handle guard is designed to skip at exit 0 — **and that contract holds only where the INVOKING environment does not preempt the capture-then-print: a PowerShell caller setting `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true` turns wdio's non-zero into a terminating error at the `npm run a11y` call, before the script prints the captured output or reaches its assertion, so the caller sees one `NativeCommandExitException` line and none of the verdict (as measured at `2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed`, with a local control both ways; the CI a11y gate step's setting was removed there, both shells byte-unchanged)** — capturing wdio's output to `$RUNS_DIR/a11y-e2e.log`, reading the exit from the BARE command (never through a pipe), then requiring: zero on the `Spec Files:` failed count (a term the line OMITS when nothing failed), a per-spec skip tally within the expected-skip SET (the two live-hold subjects; a third skip is a failure, which is how a fixture-seeding failure surfaces), and the `[webview2 … windows]` driven-session banner. The leg also emits one violation record per run at `runs/a11y/<run_id>.jsonl` — a SEPARATE artifact whose shape is this §3 envelope's eleven fields PLUS the obs §9 resource tags, deliberately outside the harness's non-recursive `"$RUNS_DIR"/*.jsonl` glob so `status` cannot read it as a scenario run. The command count stays five, no stage selector was added, and the `status` disk read and per-run envelope/JSONL shapes are untouched — so §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree), with the tauri-driver child spawned at `cwd` = the workspace root so the app's `resolve_under` can reach `scenarios/` (it rejects absolute paths and `..`, so the launch cwd is the only lever), and the mocha ceiling raised 60s → 15min because wdio enforces `mochaOpts.timeout` itself — headless under `xvfb` on Linux CI, headful on the Windows host). **The leg SEEDS its own subject before the session** (2026-09-02): `wdio.conf.ts`'s `seedFixtureRuns()` clean-re-creates the gitignored `runs/e2e-fixture/` and invokes `cargo test -q -p conductor-run --test envelope_fixture` with `CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` naming that repo-relative dir, so the subject — the committed lamps journal's records PLUS an over-envelope `run_envelope` row — is written through the production writer (`conductor_run::persist`) rather than copied; a non-zero exit or a missing journal THROWS rather than seeding silently. The tauri-driver spawn then carries `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR=runs/e2e-fixture` (repo-relative — `resolve_under` rejects absolute handles), because `/runs/` is gitignored and an unseeded clean tree gives the coverage rows no run record to render; without it the populated-lamp assertions would have no subject on CI and would read host-local run residue on a dev box. The 5-command surface, the `status` disk read and the envelope/JSONL shapes are unchanged, so §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree. With no flag, `run` executes the full aggregate (nextest + doctest + clippy + scenarios); per-stage target mapping is the Section 9 pipeline table.

**`status`** — query product state (disk artifact read; no listener):
- Command body: `jq -e '<predicate>' runs/<run_id>.jsonl` for a shell-level CI smoke gate (jq -e exits 1 on a `false`/`null` last output, 4 on parse error — test-research serde_json+jq), OR an in-process `rusqlite::Connection::open` + bound-parameter `SELECT` of the `runs.db` row for typed assertions. **The journal read targets the NEWEST ENVELOPE line — never the file's last line**: the journal carries two report-seam record shapes (§3 Log format), so a run that graded checks ends on a `CheckRecord` and an unqualified last-line read reports ITS fields as the envelope (measured 2026-09-06: `seed: null`, `slo_tier: null`, exit 0). Both shells select that line by the envelope-only `seed` key (`jq -s` filtering `has("seed")` · `Where-Object { $_.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'seed' }`). No `curl`/HTTP — there is no inbound listener.
- Polled fields: the Run-report envelope (see Status endpoint shape below) — `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `journal_emitted_at`, `read_back_observed_at`, `fingerprints`.

**`cleanup`** — tear down per-run artifacts:
- Command body: `rm -f runs/<run_id>.jsonl runs/<run_id>.md` in the shells, then `conductor cleanup <run_id>` — **the shells issue no SQL** (2026-09-06). The three bound-parameter deletes (`DELETE FROM runs WHERE run_id = ?1`, `DELETE FROM run_check WHERE run_id = ?1`, `DELETE FROM run_envelope WHERE run_id = ?1`) run inside the binary as three LITERAL statements in one transaction (`conductor_report::RunsDb::delete_run`) — teardown covers every table a run writes, or cleanup leaves orphans (rusqlite bound parameters — security anti-pattern bans `format!`-built SQL, which the `sqlite3` CLI could not have honoured: it has no bind facility, and it is present on neither this host nor any CI runner). In tests this reduces to dropping the `assert_fs::TempDir` sandboxing `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`. Conductor must NOT touch Pulse (Creator Brief: "NO Pulse process management"). The `:4317` port-occupier fault (security Vector 6) releases its `TcpListener` bind on cleanup.
- Idempotency: cleanup MUST be idempotent — re-running against a clean state is a no-op (file-absence is not an error; `DELETE` of zero rows succeeds).
- Verification: `assert_fs` `.assert(predicate::path::missing())` on `runs/<run_id>.{jsonl,md}` + `SELECT count(*) FROM runs WHERE run_id = ?1`, `... FROM run_check ...` and `... FROM run_envelope ...` each returning 0 + a `TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:4317")` succeeding (proving the port-occupier released).

**`logs`** — fetch product logs (emission journal is ground truth):
- Command body: read `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` (the per-run emission journal — "the left side of every SLO check", Creator Brief) directly; sanitized stderr from the CLI subprocess captured by `assert_cmd` `.get_output().stderr`. The journal is emitted via `tracing_subscriber::fmt().json().flatten_event(true)` (test-research Structured Log Parsing), one JSON object per line, with wall-clock stamps from `std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant` (NOT tokio's virtual clock — security anti-pattern).
- Format: see Log format below.
- Retention window: per-`run_id`, append-mostly on disk; tests read the whole journal file for the run under assertion (no rotation needed — bounded synthetic runs).

title: Status endpoint shape
body:
### Status endpoint shape

```json
{
  "run_id": "string", "seed": 0, "scenario": "string", "p_ids": ["P-001"],
  "verdict": "Pass | Fail | CalibrationRegion",
  "state": "Pass | Fail | ManualCheck | KnownResidual | Blocked",
  "latency_ms": 0, "slo_tier": "string",
  "journal_emitted_at": "ISO-8601", "read_back_observed_at": "ISO-8601",
  "fingerprints": []
}
```

No HTTP/IPC status *endpoint* exists (no listener). This is the Run-report envelope (arch Standard Contracts), serialized identically into the Markdown report, the `runs` row, and the envelope JSONL journal line. Per-check detail is a separate finer grain, never an extension of the envelope (whose eleven fields are unchanged): the `run_check` table keyed `(run_id, scenario, check_index)` (read via `RunsDb::checks_for`) plus its own journal lines and an indented per-check line in the Markdown report. The agent polls it by reading the `runs.db` row (bound-parameter SQL) or the JSONL journal during/after each scenario. Artifacts MUST NOT leak absolute host paths or internal seam-crate struct names (security anti-pattern) — enforced by the insta golden snapshot + a tracing field-allowlist redaction layer.

title: Log format
body:
### Log format

- **Format:** structured JSONL — one JSON object per line (arch Test-Relevant Conventions: "per-run JSONL journals stemmed by `run_id`"), emitted by `tracing-subscriber` 0.3.x `format::Json`.
- **Required fields:** `journal_emitted_at` (ISO-8601 from `std::time::SystemTime` — NOT virtual clock), plus the envelope identity fields (`run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `fingerprints`). NO absolute host paths, NO internal struct names (security anti-pattern; asserted by a negative test on the journal).
- **Agent parsing:** `runs/<run_id>.jsonl` carries TWO report-seam record shapes — the **run envelope line** (the eleven envelope fields, byte-unchanged) and the **per-check `CheckRecord` line** (`run_id` · `scenario` · `check_index` · `kind` · `verdict` · `state` · `latency_ms` · `deadline_ms` · `budget_ms`; `budget_ms` null when the check inherits its tier, and a blocked or declare-only scenario emits none). Every line is parseable with `jq -c`; a typed parse DISCRIMINATES the shape — `serde_json::from_str::<RunReportEnvelope>(line)` targets the envelope line specifically, not every line. Both are report-seam records, so obs-plan §3's self-obs-line vs run-report-envelope split is unaffected. NEVER multi-line — `tracing` JSON flattening serializes everything onto one line.
- **Self-obs stream is a distinct artifact:** the `tracing` self-observation log stream (cli: stderr / `logs/agent-latest.jsonl`; Tauri backend: `logs/conductor-tauri.jsonl`) carries per-line base fields — `timestamp_ms`, `level`, `target`, service-identity (`service.name`/`service.version`/`deployment.environment`), `run_id` — per obs-plan §3. It is SEPARATE from this per-run emission journal (`runs/<run_id>.jsonl`, the SLO ground truth + the Run-report envelope above); the two schemas must not be conflated. The stream carries **two line variants over that one base set**: the **event line** (any `tracing` event record — `message` plus its allowlisted fields — at whatever level obs-plan §11's policy assigns that call site, so a hot-path line sits at `debug` where `info` is banned) and the **span-lifecycle line**, which adds `span` (the bounded §4 span name), `span_event` (`new` | `close`), an optional `parent` (the enclosing span's name, absent on a root), and — on the `new` line only — the span's own allowlisted attributes. Both variants are still the self-obs base line, so obs-plan §3's two-record-shapes split (self-obs line vs Run-report envelope) is unchanged, and a span attribute is gated by the same `conductor-core::redact` allowlist as any event field.

title: PID file
body:
### PID file

- **Location:** N/A — no daemon (security: "no inbound listener of its own"; arch: `conductor-cli` is a one-shot `#[tokio::main(flavor="current_thread")]` binary). Nothing to write or signal.
- **Lifecycle:** N/A — `cleanup` removes on-disk run artifacts and `runs.db` rows instead of signaling a long-lived process.

title: Test data bootstrap
body:
### Test data bootstrap

- **Strategy:** self-bootstrapping (no developer-seeded data) — deterministic seeded synthetic generation via `conductor-timeline` (same scenario+seed ⇒ same stream shape, Creator Brief).
- **Mechanism:** rstest 0.26.1 `#[fixture]` producing a seeded `conductor-timeline` generator; table-driven `#[rstest]` `#[case]` rows over the catalog (the manifest’s accepted set) and the garde valid/invalid config matrix; `#[once]` fixture for in-memory `runs.db` schema setup; declarative scenario config files (serde + garde) under `scenarios/`, each naming its P-IDs (a P-ID may be named by several). P-032/P-036 require a real git workspace with known recent commits (Creator Brief environment requirement).
- **Per-test isolation:** `rusqlite::Connection::open_in_memory()` per unit/golden test (parallel-safe under nextest's per-test process model); `assert_fs::TempDir` with `.env("CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR", temp.path())` per CLI-subprocess / cross-process test THAT WRITES RUN ARTIFACTS, so the CLI and the Tauri mock-runtime write to the same file `runs.db`. A CLI-edge test of a verb that writes nothing sets the handle NOT AT ALL: `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` is repo-relative by design and `resolve_under` rejects an absolute `temp.path()` at `Paths::resolve()` — before the verb dispatches — so setting it makes every verb fail with empty stdout (measured 2026-09-03 on the `conductor preconditions` edge tests).
- **Cleanup:** test data cleared by the `cleanup` command / `TempDir` drop per session.

title: Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project)
body:
### Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project)

_[ALL tiers — explicit derivation hint for downstream consumers per D26 chain.]_

- **test-runner-install:** install cargo-nextest 0.9.137 (via `taiki-e/install-action`) + `cargo test --doc` step + `[dev-dependencies]` assertion/fixture packages: rstest 0.26, assert_cmd 2 + predicates 3, assert_fs 1, insta 1 (`json` feature), proptest 1.9.
- **5-command-discipline-wire:** wire `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` with the 5 commands (boot=precondition probe + preflight gate / run / status / cleanup / logs) per 5-command implementation above. Binding contract — both shell variants must expose identical semantics, a property asserted of the SCRIPTS **together with the invoking environment**: a caller that preempts native-command exits (`$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true`) diverges the `.ps1` leg with zero script delta, measured in CI 2026-09-07 (Windows/Linux dev-OS targets; the identical `.sh`/`.ps1` semantics include the webview E2E leg, which runs on Linux+`xvfb` AND headfully on the Windows dev host (`CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER`-gated) — only macOS lacks a WebDriver).
- **status-endpoint-implement:** N/A as an endpoint — instead implement the Run-report envelope serializer (shared by `runs.db` row + JSONL journal + Markdown) per Status endpoint shape; polled by reading the `runs.db` row / JSONL journal.
- **log-format-bind-with-obs:** the `tracing-subscriber` JSON journal format is DEFINED here (see Log format above) — this plan is its source of truth and obs derives its product-side log envelope FROM this subsection (binding contract — harness greps the journal for assertions; format break = harness break). The field-allowlist / redaction layer (no host paths, no struct names) is the one piece owned by obs downstream; this plan asserts that boundary via a negative test.
- **pid-file-commitment-wire:** N/A — no daemon. `cleanup` removes run artifacts + `runs.db` rows + releases the `:4317` port-occupier instead.
- **test-data-bootstrap-wire:** wire rstest seeded fixtures + P-ID-keyed scenario config files + in-memory/`TempDir` `runs.db`; cleanup clears between runs.
- **coverage-tooling-install:** install cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7; emit LCOV via `cargo llvm-cov nextest --lcov --output-path lcov.info` (+ `--cobertura coverage.xml` for CI) + `--fail-under-lines` gate.
- **quality-gate-config-emit:** emit GitHub Actions config enforcing coverage threshold (Section 10), zero-retry flakiness budget, `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check`, committed `Cargo.lock`, toolchain ≥ 1.94.1, `tauri` ≥ 2.10.3.

route uses this list to plan phase ordering (test-runner-install → 5-command-discipline-wire → status-endpoint-implement → log-format-bind-with-obs → pid-file-commitment-wire → test-data-bootstrap-wire → coverage-tooling-install → quality-gate-config-emit). setup-project materializes each phase's bootstrap script + dependency list + verification command (the log format + envelope shape are defined in this Section 3 and flow downstream to obs; obs derives its envelope from here, not the reverse).
