title: 12. Test Decisions Log
body:
## 12. Test Decisions Log

_Records key decisions during plan generation + manual additions
between phase loops._

**Initial entry:**

`2026-06-14` — Initial test plan generated by `/andromeda-tests`
- **Tier:** Minimal (0) — justified by: Minimal security tier (single-developer, local-only, no-cloud, no-auth, zero network exposure, synthetic-only data) + a single release-gate surface (cli; webview + Tauri IPC are "convenience only") + no persistent user data. Held at Minimal's upper boundary (9 seam crates, 7 critical paths, "production-grade verification rigor") so the baseline is augmented with Section 5 triggers WITHOUT escalating to Comprehensive (Creator Brief disqualifies load/multi-target/cloud).
- **Key decisions:**
  - **Test framework:** cargo-nextest 0.9.137 (+ `cargo test --doc` fallback for doctests nextest skips) — chosen because: arch Test-Relevant Conventions name cargo-nextest/`cargo test` as the runner; stable `NextestExitCode` enum (100/101/4) + `ci`-profile JUnit XML make it agent-readable; it is the engine the `run` harness command wraps for the CI build+test gate.
  - **E2E driver(s):** cli → assert_cmd 2.1.2 + predicates 3 + assert_fs 1 (exact Section 2 cli driver: subprocess + `Command::cargo_bin`, exit-code + NO_COLOR-stable labels); MCP read-back → rmcp 1.7.0 stub server over stdio (in-process duplex + `TokioChildProcess` test-binary; CI-runnable without live Pulse) [**2026-09-02 correction:** rmcp was removed 2026-06-27 and is absent from `Cargo.lock`; the shipped read-back client AND its stub are hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC over the sidecar's stdio (`conductor-verify/src/jsonrpc.rs` + `client.rs`; `stub_pulse_mcp`)]; Tauri IPC → tauri 2.10.3 `test` mock runtime (`get_ipc_response()`); desktop-webview → @crabnebula/tauri-driver 2.0.9 via `wdio run` headless on Linux/`xvfb` (no macOS WKWebView driver) [**2026-09-01 correction:** the DRIVER choice is unchanged and stands; the "headless on Linux/`xvfb`" qualifier was measured over-narrow — the platform set is Linux CI + the Windows WebView2 host, macOS still driver-less] — chosen because: each is the named per-surface driver in test-research, and the stub/mock legs keep the CI gate fully headless while the live Pulse leg stays local-gate-only per arch.
  - **Coverage tool:** cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7 (`cargo llvm-cov nextest --lcov` + `--fail-under-lines 60`) — chosen because: canonical LLVM source-based coverage for Rust, first-class nextest integration (one pass for coverage + JUnit), machine-parseable LCOV/Cobertura for the agent gate.
  - **Trigger tooling:** proptest 1.9.0 (determinism + garde cross-field property tests, `proptest-regressions/` deterministic replay); insta 1.46.1 CI/assert mode (Run-report envelope + JSONL golden, redacting non-deterministic fields, enforcing artifact-sanitization); tokio `test-util` `start_paused` (virtual-clock determinism); conductor-faults seeded generators + loopback `TcpListener` probe + optional turmoil 0.7.2 (bounded chaos / transport faults, NOT load); cargo-audit 0.22.2 + cargo-deny 0.19.6 (supply-chain gate; the `--deny warnings` form this entry originally named was measured 2026-09-05 to exit 1 by construction against the `deny.toml`-adjudicated allowed set — the shipped gate is the bare `cargo audit`, the tool choice unchanged) — each chosen as the test-research candidate for its Section 5 trigger.
- **Open questions:**
  - **No JS/TS unit-test runner researched for the React 19 SPA's frontend logic** — test-research catalogs tauri-driver (E2E webview) and tauri::test (IPC) but no component/unit runner (e.g., vitest) for in-webview React logic. Acceptable under Minimal because the GUI is "convenience only" and the CLI is the release gate (webview is asserted only at the E2E/parity layer); flagged here rather than inventing a tool not in research. If frontend unit coverage is later required, re-run research.
  - **turmoil is optional, not load-bearing** — the bounded chaos path is satisfied by conductor-faults seeded generators + a loopback port probe; turmoil 0.7.2 is recommended only for deterministic transport-fault (partition/refusal) assertions without a live Pulse. No decision forced; left to phase execution.


`2026-08-20` — Mutation instrument adopted (`2026-08-20-verifier-self-hardening`)
- **cargo-mutants 27.1.0 registered** as a chunk acceptance instrument under the floors-not-pins policy (§4), an operator/local audit instrument rather than a CI stage (§9) and a disposition rule rather than a numeric threshold (§10).
- **Run discipline, each item measured not assumed:** `-f` resolves from the workspace root (a package-relative path under `-p <crate>` matches nothing and reports `Found 0 mutants to test` at **exit 0** — a silent no-op indistinguishable from a clean pass); `--test-tool=nextest` is required; output is gitignored. The exit code is uninformative in BOTH directions — measured **exit 3** on a fully-accepted run (`2026-08-20-read-back-seam-survivors-closed`: 0 missed, all five named survivors killed, non-zero owed to two pre-existing timeouts) — so the tallies, never the exit code, are the signal.
- **`conductor-run`'s `declares` env-read arm classified accepted-deliberate**, not deferred debt — the set is **`replace declares -> bool with false` alone** (roster `member-1`, in `preconditions.rs`; keyed by cargo-mutants' own mutation DESCRIPTION, not by `file:line:col` — see the identity note closing this entry). Its coordinates were re-pointed twice under the retired line:col form — `lib.rs:358:5` → `lib.rs:362:5` (2026-09-04) → `preconditions.rs:50:5` (2026-09-05, after `conductor-run/src/lib.rs` was split 1944 → 36 lines across seven siblings) — and had moved again by 2026-09-13, which is what retired the form; that chain is kept as history for the shrink narrative below, never as the member's identity, citing `.claude/rules/testing.md` (2026-08-10), which prescribes reading env at the caller and passing it in as a typed value so the edge stays thin and both branches test with no `unsafe` env mutation. Killing these would require `unsafe set_var` in a shared-process test module, the exact hazard the chunk that minted the rule removed. **The class SHRANK on 2026-09-03** (`2026-09-03-conductor-run-composition-root-survivors-dispositioned`): it was ratified as six members, and two of them proved killable with no env mutation at all — `observe_run_contract:346` and `declares:358 → true` both fell to `observe_run_contract_names_the_term_this_environment_does_not_declare`, because the env read lives in `declares` and not in its caller, so the cited rule never covered the enclosing function's mutant nor the always-true arm. Name the set, not a count: the ledger enumerating it is the citation home below. **The class SHRANK again on 2026-09-04** (`2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence`): the set was reduced to ONE arm — `lib.rs:362:5` (→ `false`) **ALONE** at that date, re-pointed to `preconditions.rs:50:5` by the 2026-09-05 split above. `declares` was reduced to a thin env-reading wrapper delegating its value test to `conductor_core::flag_declared`, so the three operator arms (the two `==` and the `||`) relocated into value-taking code and are CAUGHT there by the `flag_declared` / `handle_declared` rstest matrix, while `declares -> true` is caught by `declares_rejects_a_name_this_environment_does_not_declare`. Only the env-gated body replacement survives — indistinguishable from the real code whenever the var is unset, which is exactly what the cited rule forecloses.
- **`conductor-tauri`'s accepted-deliberate TRIPLE (2026-09-03)** — the roster's second member, from the crate's first dispositioned score (22 standing survivors → 3). `main:18` is unkillable by construction: no `main` that launches the Tauri event loop can be called from a test, and no refactor changes that — an extraction moves the testable part out and leaves `main` a thinner unkillable shell — cited against architecture.md §Design Philosophy "thin shells", operator-ratified. `replace run_thread with ()` (roster `member-2`, in `commands.rs`; its coordinates moved `:296` → `:307:5` → `:308:5` across the 2026-09-05 `resolve_run_target` hoist and audit, which is why the member is keyed by DESCRIPTION and not by them) — cites `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-06-26 (a command driving the engine on a background thread is not deterministically testable in-process; test `conductor_run::drive_run` instead). `delete ! in start_run` (roster `member-2`, in `commands.rs`; `:263:8` when minted, `:273:8` by 2026-09-13) cites the SAME 2026-08-10 env-at-the-caller rule as `declares`: reaching the inverted guard needs `capabilities()` and `list_scenarios_impl()` to succeed first, and both resolve against the process CWD — the crate dir under `cargo test`, where neither `contracts/` nor `scenarios/` exists. Citation home: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-03-conductor-tauri-survivors-dispositioned/evidence/survivor-dispositions.md`.
- **`conductor-run`'s accepted-deliberate CLASSES B and C (2026-09-03; coordinates re-measured 2026-09-04)** — the roster's third member, from that crate's first dispositioned score (25 standing survivors → 8; **re-derived to 5 on 2026-09-04**, of which ONE — not four — is a `declares` arm, the entry above). **Members are keyed by cargo-mutants' own mutation DESCRIPTION, each unique across the survivor set — NOT by `file:line:col`, a form retired 2026-09-13 (see the identity note closing this entry):** class B is `delete field degraded from struct Observation expression in execute_scenario` + `replace - with + in execute_scenario` + `replace - with / in execute_scenario`, and class C `delete ! in preflight` (roster `member-3`). Their coordinates moved repeatedly under the retired form — **Re-pointed 2026-09-05** (`2026-09-05-audit-corrective`) after `conductor-run/src/lib.rs` was split 1944 → 36 lines across seven siblings; identity was then re-measured by function + COLUMN (the form retired 2026-09-13, when the class-B `degraded` member's column itself moved 27 → 17): class B was `lib.rs:559:27` + `lib.rs:600:25` ×2 (and `:518:27` + `:559:25` ×2 before that), class C `lib.rs:68:8` (was `:66:8`). **Class B — unreachable past a fixed-endpoint egress gate:** `lib.rs:559:27` and `lib.rs:600:25` ×2 sit inside `execute_scenario` past `probe_egress(DEFAULT_OTLP_ENDPOINT)` and `Dispatcher::connect(scenario, DEFAULT_OTLP_ENDPOINT)`, where the endpoint is the fixed `http://127.0.0.1:4317` (`conductor-emit/src/client.rs:23`), not an injectable parameter; reaching them means binding Pulse's own ingest port in a unit test, which architecture.md §Occupied Resources — Ports does not sanction, and which is flaky by construction because the tier contends that fixed port between `--jobs 2` parallel mutant processes (§10 zero-flakiness). No integration test can drive it either — `Preflight`'s fields are crate-private — and making the endpoint injectable is a production signature change. **Class C — unreachable without the sidecar binary:** `lib.rs:68:8` needs `preflight()` to hold a connected client, and `ReadbackClient::connect` spawns `andromeda-pulse-mcp` as a fixed program NAME through the inherited `PATH` (architecture.md §Occupied Resources — Service / process names); absent on a hermetic host the function returns before the guard, so a kill would need the sidecar as a host precondition (§10 zero-flakiness) or a new injectable seam. Citation home: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-03-conductor-run-composition-root-survivors-dispositioned/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`.
- **`conductor-verify`'s accepted-deliberate PAIR (2026-09-04)** — the roster's FOURTH member, from `spawn.rs`'s first dispositioned score (16 mutants: 13 caught, 1 unviable, 2 accepted; both `console_suppressing_flags` mutants CAUGHT by the new `#[cfg(windows)]` value test). The set is **the two whole-body replacements of `sidecar_resolves_on_path` in `spawn.rs` — `replace sidecar_resolves_on_path -> bool with true` and `… with false`** (roster `member-4`; identified by cargo-mutants' own mutation DESCRIPTION, which is unique across the survivor set, NOT by `file:line:col` — see the identity note at the end of this entry), whose entire body IS the `std::env::var_os("PATH")`/`PATHEXT` read plus delegation, so the env-at-the-caller rule's mechanism lives in that function itself rather than one level down (the 2026-09-03 scoping test applied: the mutants ARE the mechanism's home, not an inheritance up to an enclosing fn). Its pure half `resolves_on` is tested on both arms and its own mutants were caught. Accepted against `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-08-10 (env read at the caller; killing these needs `unsafe { std::env::set_var }`, which edition 2024 makes unsafe precisely because it races). An agreement test against the real `PATH` was CONSIDERED and rejected: it kills exactly ONE of the two arms depending on whether `andromeda-pulse-mcp` happens to be on `PATH`, making the score host-dependent, and a roster is an enumerated set that must mean the same thing on every host (§10 zero-flakiness). Citation home: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-04-sidecar-spawn-without-a-console-window/report.md`. **2026-09-13:** the unit's mutant POPULATION dropped by one when `ContractManifest::default_path` was removed rather than pinned — a `pub` fn with zero call sites workspace-wide that could not acquire one, since `conductor-cli` does not depend on `conductor-verify` and resolves that default from a literal at `crates/conductor-cli/src/paths.rs`. Its mutant left the population rather than moving to `caught.txt`; the population is read from the run, never restated here.
- **`conductor-cli`'s accepted-deliberate PAIR (2026-09-05)** — the roster's FIFTH member, from that crate's first dispositioned score (`2026-09-05-audit-corrective`: 41 standing survivors → 2; the unit's mutant population moved 117 → 111 because one `color_enabled` seam replaced two copies of the three-condition tty rule). The set is **`replace stdout_color -> bool with false` and `replace stderr_color -> bool with false` in `render.rs`** (roster `member-5`; keyed by mutation DESCRIPTION, not `file:line:col`) — the two wrapper bodies whose surviving arm is a read of the HOST's own state (a process whose stdout, or stderr, is a real terminal). Every runner captures those handles, so the only kill available is host-dependent, and a roster is an enumerated set that must mean the same thing on every host — the same reasoning the `sidecar_resolves_on_path` pair above was accepted under (§10 zero-flakiness). The acceptance is scoped to the unobservable DIRECTION, not to the function: `stderr_color` → `true` IS killed, by an assert_cmd subprocess whose piped stderr must carry no escape byte, and the three-condition LOGIC is killed through the pure `color_enabled(is_terminal, no_color_set, term)` seam. **The rejected alternative is part of the disposition** (the 2026-09-04 precedent): a `CONDUCTOR_COLOR`-class env override would make both arms reachable and was refused — a new `CONDUCTOR_*` handle is a new occupied resource (architecture.md §Occupied Resources), and `unsafe { set_var }` is process-global. Citation home: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-05-audit-corrective/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`.
- **`conductor-emit`'s accepted-deliberate SINGLE (2026-09-14)** — the roster's SIXTH member, from that crate's first dispositioned score (`2026-09-14-emit-scrubber-and-percentile-math-under-test`: 221 mutants over `exception.rs` + `latency.rs` WHOLE — 1 missed, 202 caught, 15 timeouts, 3 unviable, as measured at `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-14-emit-scrubber-and-percentile-math-under-test/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`). The population is deliberately the two files whole rather than the 2026-09-14 audit's `--shard 1/4`, which read 115 of their 227 mutants and is not re-measurable once retiring the three `LatencyProfile` accessors shifts every later index — so the audit's 57 survivors are a reading of a strict subset, never a baseline this run differences against. The set is **`replace < with <= in quantile` in `latency.rs`** (roster `member-emit-1`; keyed by mutation DESCRIPTION, not `file:line:col`). It is the first member accepted as an **EQUIVALENT MUTANT** rather than as an untested shape a standing rule forecloses: the guard's two branches meet at `u = 0.5` with the same value — `u / 0.5` is exactly `1.0` and `(u - 0.5) / 0.45` exactly `0.0` there, both yielding exactly `p50` — and `u = 0.5` is the only input the flip re-routes, so the mutated fn returns a bit-identical `f64` for every input in the domain; measured under EXACT `f64` comparison across 5 profiles × 10 008 sample points, **0 differing points**. **The acceptance is scoped to THIS mutant, never the comparison class:** four siblings of the same shape ARE killable and are killed, because the later branches are one line algebraically but not in IEEE754 (`(0.95 - 0.5) / 0.45` is not exactly `1.0`, and the two tail divisors round differently); an earlier prediction that five were equivalent rested on a model comparing with a `1e-9` epsilon that swallows those ~7e-15 differences, and was corrected by exact re-measurement at the P5 review before implementation — accepting the class rather than the member would have silently re-admitted four killable mutants. **The rejected alternatives are part of the disposition:** a tolerance band around the breakpoints (rejected — it is precisely why the four siblings survived the audit at all, since the existing convergence test grades within ±12 % and any epsilon wide enough to feel safe re-creates every one of them; exact equality is what discriminates), and restructuring `quantile` so the boundary becomes observable (rejected — a production behaviour change made to satisfy a mutation tool, which §11 forbids). **The run's fifteen timeouts are classified by class in the citation home and have NO roster rows yet.** Until 2026-09-30 no gate could hold them — `scripts/mutation-gate.py` then read `missed.txt` alone and never `timeout.txt` (measured 2026-09-15), so a caught→timeout regression passed silently. Since 2026-09-30 the gate grades `timeout.txt` against the roster's `tally = "timeout"` rows (§4), but the fifteen cannot be keyed from the ledger: timeout identity is coordinate-free and COLLIDES within a helper, and the raw `timeout.txt` of that run is gone. The epoch-boundary code audit owns seeding them from its own measured `timeout.txt` (overseer, founder-delegated, 2026-09-30); until then `mutation-gate.py conductor-emit` FAILs closed with one `TIMED OUT, not in roster` line per timeout, and that output is the measured input the rows are written from. Citation home: `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-14-emit-scrubber-and-percentile-math-under-test/evidence/disposition-ledger.md`.
- **Runner portability became a standing gate** (§4): the suite must be green under `cargo test -p <crate>` as well as nextest, because only the shared-process runner can expose a test relying on per-test-process isolation from a process-global singleton (§11 Integration).
- **Roster member IDENTITY — `file:line:col` RETIRED 2026-09-13** (`2026-09-13-audit-debt-retired-before-epoch-1-closes`). A member is identified by cargo-mutants' own mutation DESCRIPTION (the text after the coordinates on a `missed.txt` line, `{path}:{line}:{col}: {mutation}`), joined to `scripts/mutation-roster.toml` by its `member` key. The prior rule — "identity re-measured by function + COLUMN, never by line arithmetic" — was itself insufficient and re-staled three times: coordinates were re-pointed on 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05, and by 2026-09-13 the class-B `degraded` member's COLUMN had moved 27 → 17 while its description stayed unique across all 25 survivors, so function + column no longer identified it. The coordinate chains above are kept as dated HISTORY of each re-pointing, never as a member's identity; the executable roster carries no line and no column at all, and matches a run's `missed.txt` or `timeout.txt` — per the row's required, never-defaulted `tally` key (since 2026-09-30) — on `(file, mutation)` as a MULTISET — two members may legitimately share that pair, as the two `replace == with != in stub_result` entries do. The roster is populated PER GATED UNIT, not for the whole ledger: as of 2026-09-14 it carries rows for `conductor-cli` (`member-5`), `conductor-verify` (`member-4`) and `conductor-emit` (`member-emit-1`) — the units a chunk has re-run — so `member-1` (`declares`), `member-2` (the `conductor-tauri` triple) and `member-3` (classes B and C) are §12 numbering with no roster row yet, and gain one when the epoch-boundary code audit re-runs the tier over their crate (mutation runs happen there only, never per chunk — founder ruling, 2026-09-30) (`.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-09-03: a roster is a ledger of owed work and only a re-run can shrink it). **REGISTRATION is the `[[unit]]` declaration, never the row count** (2026-09-14): a unit is declared by a `[[unit]]` table — optionally carrying a `files` list that scopes the tier to those paths via `-f`, workspace-root-relative — so a registered unit whose survivors are ALL killed legitimately carries zero `[[entry]]` rows and PASSES when every graded tally agrees — empty `missed` and `timeout` multisets, each tally's count equal to `outcomes.json`'s, conservation holding — where the prior rule read "no roster rows" as "not a gated unit" and failed it. Rows alone still register, so a roster predating the `[[unit]]` block keeps working; and because a scoped tier can now generate nothing at all, a run producing 0 mutants is an explicit FAIL rather than the clean sweep `cargo mutants` reports it as at exit 0.

title: Obs Plan — Conductor

body:
_Generated by `/andromeda-obs`. This file is the single source of truth
for all observability strategy + harness contracts + SLO invariants.
Read by downstream skills (a11y / route / setup-project per D26
cross-cutting), obs-pass per-phase, combine + `/implement` (via phase
loop)._

_Do not edit during phase loop runs (obs-pass / combine / `/implement`).
Manual edits between runs are fine._

_**Agent-driven invariant:** every telemetry signal described in this
plan must be readable by an agent from a snapshot or pasted log
excerpt. No human-only dashboards, no proprietary APM lock-in, no
human-review-gated log analysis. If a surface cannot be agent-readable,
it is flagged "not-instrumentable" in obs-scope.md Section 1 and
handled via boundary instrumentation only._

title: 1. Obs Scope Summary

body: **Obs tier:** Minimal (0)

**Justification:** The workspace's crate-per-seam members (`Cargo.toml [workspace] members`) + one surface (CLI headless) place Conductor at the lower end of the module-count spectrum. Security tier is Minimal (single-developer, local-only, no cloud, zero network exposure beyond loopback MCP/gRPC client). 7 critical paths identified (Sections 4) — all tightly scoped to single-scenario execution. Creator Brief mandates "production-grade verification rigor" for determinism and assertion-policy split but achieves this via property/golden/contract tests, not comprehensive instrumentation. Tests tier is Minimal (0). Complexity facts: (a) no OTel SDK or exporter for self-observation (creator-explicit anti-pattern §6); (b) self-observation is structured tracing logs only (JSONL via `tracing-subscriber`); (c) paste-to-AI workflow via agent-parseable JSON (no proprietary APM). Telemetry triggers: 5 total (chaos-instrumentation, perf-budget-instruments, cross-surface-trace-propagation, error-budget-SLO, creator-explicit-telemetry) — all addressable within Minimal scope.
**Instrumentation scope (entities needing instrumentation):**
| Entity | Source | Instrumentability | Reason if not fully instrumentable |

| **conductor-core** | Workspace / Modules | Instrumentable | Runtime-agnostic library for scenario execution; produces emission journal and report state; all telemetry sinks controlled by the caller (the CLI) |

| **conductor-timeline** | Workspace / Modules + Stack (tokio 1.52.3 `current_thread` flavor) | Instrumentable | Deterministic seeded phase scheduler; tokio `current_thread` runtime ensures emission ordering is seed-deterministic; instrumentation spans must use wall-clock (`std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant`) not tokio's virtual clock |

| **conductor-emit** | Workspace / Modules + Stack (opentelemetry-proto 0.32.0, tonic 0.14.6) | Instrumentable | Raw OTLP message construction and gRPC egress to `127.0.0.1:4317`; byte-level fault control for fingerprint identity; instrumentation of outbound gRPC call only (the boundary is the emission itself, not Pulse-side receipt) |

| **conductor-faults** | Workspace / Modules | Instrumentable | Fault-injection helpers (ramps, silence, port-occupier, fingerprint generation); telemetry surfaces as `fault.port_occupier` around this crate's own RAII hold. The declarative silence/ramp faults are instrumented from `conductor-run`'s per-phase hook, not here — see §4 Fault-injection spans |

| **conductor-verify** | Workspace / Modules + Standard Contracts (MCP preflight readiness gate + OTLP egress check) | Boundary-only | MCP client over the hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC transport (`jsonrpc.rs` + `client.rs`; rmcp removed 2026-06-27); version negotiation and tool presence check are boundary calls to Pulse's MCP server. The seam carries a WRITE as well as read-back — `ReadbackClient::resolve_incident(i64)` over `mark_incident_resolved` — instrumented by the same bounded `verify.readback.call_tool` span with the allowlisted `mcp_tool` field; Pulse-side state stays untraced (Conductor observes the response, not Pulse's internals) |

| **conductor-report** | Workspace / Modules + Standard Contracts (Run report envelope) | Instrumentable | JSONL journal per-run emission stream; Markdown run report generation; rusqlite synchronous embedded SQLite (`runs.db`) for run-metadata; instrumentation of journal write, report render, DB insert operations |

| **conductor-cli** | Workspace / Modules + Design System (cli surface) | Instrumentable | `agent-run` binary entry point; `#[tokio::main(flavor="current_thread")]` CLI bootstrap with anyhow error bridging; CLI argument parsing (clap) and structured output to stdout/stderr |

| **tokio 1.52.3 `current_thread` runtime** | Stack | Instrumentable | Deterministic single-threaded async runtime; zero work-stealing preserves emission ordering as function of seed; instrumentation must respect the runtime's invariant (no background batch tasks in exporters that would break determinism) |

| **Pulse MCP server** | Standard Contracts (MCP preflight readiness gate + OTLP egress check) | Boundary-only | Third-party observability backend; Conductor acts as MCP client calling `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved`, `retrieve_incident_events` (a by-id read of an incident's lifecycle events, present at Pulse S2 `cdb6c1e`) against pinned `2024-11-05` protocol version; Pulse-side behavior is not instrumentable, and Conductor observes read-back responses and SLO timing — and additionally MUTATES Pulse state at this boundary through `mark_incident_resolved`, whose effect is graded on runtime-state read-back (active-set membership) rather than on any Pulse internal |

| **rusqlite + libsqlite3-sys (`runs.db`)** | Stack | Boundary-only | Synchronous embedded SQLite with bundled C bindings; raw SQL (no ORM); append-mostly run-metadata storage; instrumentation at the rusqlite call boundary — the run-persist WRITE carries the `db.insert_run` span, the TEARDOWN write (`RunsDb::delete_run`) carries no span and no boundary log (deliberate: off the must-trace paths, sole caller has no `tracing` dep), and the READ path a §6 boundary-call `info!` inside the caller's span where the caller holds one (a `conductor-cli` caller such as `conductor report` holds none, and the line is matched by `run_id`; no `db.*` read span); SQLite internal state is not instrumented (C library, outside Rust control) |

| **cargo build / CI/CD pipeline** | CI/CD Platform | Not-instrumentable | GitHub Actions workflow; build-time verification (`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo build`, cargo-nextest, cargo clippy, the static gates incl. the repository-hygiene secret-scan and workflow env-context gates); does not run at runtime; observability focus is on the deployed harness binary and headless `scripts/agent-run.sh` execution |
**Telemetry surfaces:**
| Surface | Backend instrumentation hooks | Frontend instrumentation hooks | Exporter | Service identity | Notes |

| **cli** (headless `conductor-cli` + `scripts/agent-run.sh`) | `tracing` 0.1.x crate + `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter; structured stderr sink (file under `--agent-mode`) for operator or piped consumer; no HTTP/gRPC framework auto-instrumentation (CLI is not an HTTP service) | N/A (no browser frontend) | Stderr JSONL + file sink in agent mode (`logs/agent-latest.jsonl`); no network OTLP (Minimal tier, determinism preservation); paste-to-AI workflow via structured JSON export | Runtime env var `SERVICE_NAME` or hardcoded `conductor`; version via `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")` + cargo manifest; `deployment.environment` from `CONDUCTOR_ENV` env var (default `local`) | Agent-driven mode: no OTel SDK for self-observation (determinism constraint); emission journal format is binding contract from tests excerpt § 5 (JSONL with `journal_emitted_at` ISO-8601, `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `fingerprints` fields); all output agent-parseable via `jq` / `serde_json` |
**Observability harness specification:**

**OTel SDK init:** No OTel SDK for Conductor self-observation (creator-explicit anti-pattern from upstream §6 Obs Anti-Patterns). OTLP is the PRODUCT (fault telemetry emitted AT Pulse via `opentelemetry-proto` raw types + tonic), not the obs mechanism. Self-observation is **structured tracing logs only** — `tracing` spans render as JSON log events (span open/close with fields), NOT exported OTel traces; no W3C `trace_id`/`traceparent`, no metrics, no dashboards. Correlation within a run is the `run_id` field; there is no distributed trace.
**Service identity:**

- **CLI:** `service.name` = hardcoded `"conductor"` or runtime `$CONDUCTOR_SERVICE_NAME`; `service.version` = `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` from `Cargo.toml`; `deployment.environment` = `$CONDUCTOR_ENV` (default `"local"`)
**Logging stack:**
- Library: `tracing` 0.1.x (Rust async tracing facade) + `tracing-subscriber` JSON layer
- Format: JSONL (one JSON object per line) with schema binding contract from tests excerpt §5:

```jsonl
  {
    "journal_emitted_at": "ISO-8601 from std::time::SystemTime",
    "read_back_observed_at": "ISO-8601 (null until read-back; null for blocked rows)",
    "run_id": "string",
    "seed": 0,
    "scenario": "string",
    "p_ids": ["P-001"],
    "verdict": "Pass | Fail | CalibrationRegion",
    "state": "Pass | Fail | ManualCheck | KnownResidual | Blocked",
    "latency_ms": 0,
    "slo_tier": "string",
    "fingerprints": []
  }
  ```

- Sink (CLI): JSON to stderr in dev / non-agent mode, JSON to file `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` in agent mode (one writer at a time, never pretty-printed); no TTY detection for piped output (ANSI 256-color gating per design excerpt)

- Agent mode flag: `--agent-mode` CLI flag (or the `CONDUCTOR_AGENT_MODE` env the harness exports — a read-only trigger Conductor READS as `flag || env-set`, never writes); redirects the JSON stream from stderr to the file (a WRITER switch — the format is JSON either way)
**Log format JSON schema:** (Binding contract from tests excerpt §5 — obs aligns to tests, not vice versa)

```jsonl
{
  "journal_emitted_at": "ISO-8601 from std::time::SystemTime",
  "read_back_observed_at": "ISO-8601 from std::time::SystemTime (null until read-back; null for blocked rows)",
  "run_id": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-<suffix> (filesystem-safe hyphen-delimited)",
  "seed": "u64",
  "scenario": "string",
  "p_ids": ["P-001", "P-002", ...],
  "verdict": "Pass | Fail | CalibrationRegion",
  "state": "Pass | Fail | ManualCheck | KnownResidual | Blocked",
  "latency_ms": "integer or null (null for blocked rows)",
  "slo_tier": "<5s | <20s | <90s",
  "fingerprints": ["fingerprint1", "fingerprint2", ...] or empty array
}
```
- No absolute host paths, no internal struct names (security plan §2 anti-pattern: "Leaking absolute host paths in run-report artifacts")
- Agent-parseable via `jq` and `serde_json`
**Log file location:**
- CLI: `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` (project root, relative to `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`) in agent mode; stderr in dev / non-agent mode
- Paste-to-AI workflow: user pipes CLI output or copies console JSON to Claude Code / Claude web
**Snapshot / paste-to-AI integration:**
- No Pulse-class OTLP receiver in Conductor's own stack (Pulse is external)
- Snapshot path: N/A (Minimal tier, no persistent snapshot API)
- Paste-to-AI surface: structured JSONL logs + sanitized stderr + run report Markdown (per creator brief §6 "Control surface, not a dashboard")
**Correlation (NOT distributed tracing):**

- **No W3C trace context anywhere** — no OTel SDK to generate `trace_id`/`traceparent`, and a local single-process test harness does not need distributed tracing. Within one run, the `tracing` span hierarchy + the `run_id` field on every JSON line are the correlation.
- HTTP: N/A (no HTTP server).
- gRPC outbound (conductor-emit → Pulse): no trace context propagated (Conductor is a stateless injector; the only OTLP it speaks is the PRODUCT fault stream).

- Cross-surface parity (the headless CLI vs the in-process `conductor_run` composition `conductor suite` drives) is asserted by comparing the `runs.db` envelope (same seed ⇒ same verdict/state), NOT by correlating traces.
**Heartbeat ticks:**
- CLI (`conductor-cli`): N/A (short-lived per-scenario execution; 5-120s typical run duration; no long-running server)
**Critical paths (must-trace):** (verbatim from obs-scope Section 4)
| Path | Surfaces involved | Must-trace spans | Required log fields | Source |

| **Headless deterministic scenario run with MCP read-back verification** | CLI (`conductor-cli`) + persistent-storage (`runs.db` / JSONL journal) + boundary-only (MCP client to Pulse) | `scenario.run` (root) → `timeline.execute` → `emit.batch` (per emission) → `verify.readback` (MCP call) → `report.generate` → `db.insert_run` (final verdict write) | `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms` (computed: `read_back_observed_at - journal_emitted_at`), `slo_tier`, `fingerprints` (array), `journal_emitted_at` (ISO-8601, wall-clock), `read_back_observed_at` (ISO-8601) | Tests excerpt §5 Critical Path 1 + Creator Brief §6 "Emission journal as ground truth" + "MCP read-back as the observability surface" |

| **Fingerprint-storm scenario (high-cardinality emission)** | CLI + core + persistent-storage + boundary-only (MCP) | `scenario.run` → `timeline.execute_fingerprint_storm` → `emit.batch` (per P-ID cohort, multiple batches) → `verify.readback_fingerprints` → `report.generate` | `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario` (= "fingerprint-storm"), `p_ids` (array of all touched P-IDs), `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `fingerprints` (array, populated under deterministic L4 from `fingerprint_refs` — the `evidence_refs` fixture constants plus, at Pulse HEAD `83d4060`, each incident's triggering-cue fingerprint, which varies with the emitted payload; see §4), `journal_emitted_at` | Tests excerpt §5 Critical Path 2 |

| **Restart-suppression scenario incl. bypass case** | CLI + core + persistent-storage + boundary-only (MCP) | `scenario.run` → `timeline.execute` (+ two `fault.silence` children, one per gap phase, created-not-entered) → `emit.batch` → `verify.readback*` → `report.generate` | the standard eleven-field envelope — `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario` (= "restart-suppression"), `p_ids`, `verdict` (null — declare-only), `state` (= "KnownResidual" under the degraded read-back), `latency_ms`, `slo_tier` (`<90s`), `fingerprints`, `journal_emitted_at`, `read_back_observed_at`; NO `bypass_triggered` extra — suppression/bypass evidence grades at the harvest tier over Pulse's own tracing lines (`restart_harvest.rs`) | Tests excerpt §5 Critical Path 3 + Creator Brief §6 "one bypass case"; re-based 2026-08-18 (declare-only landing) |

| **Severity-lifecycle full pass observing auto-resolve** (re-based 2026-08-21, live proof) | CLI + core + persistent-storage + boundary-only (MCP) | `scenario.run` → `timeline.execute` → `emit.batch` → `verify.readback*` → `report.generate` (the family-specific chain was never built — see §4) | the standard eleven-field envelope with `verdict` null (declare-only) and `state` "KnownResidual"; NO `lifecycle_phase` / `severity_choice_calibrated` extras. Lifecycle timing grades HARD at the harvest tier on Pulse's own `incidents.list_active.request` `item_count` transition; severity choice stays CalibrationRegion at the cue tier | Tests excerpt §5 Critical Path 4 + Creator Brief §6 "Assertion-policy split" ("lifecycle timing = hard pass/fail; severity choice = CalibrationRegion") |

| **Known-residual classification path** | CLI + core + persistent-storage + boundary-only (MCP) | `scenario.run` → `timeline.execute` → `verify.readback.observe` (the read-back pass whose `retrieve_report` result REPORTS `degraded_mode`) → `report.classify_known_residual` → `db.insert_run` | `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario` (e.g., P-032), `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state` (should be "KnownResidual", NOT "Fail"), `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `fingerprints`, `journal_emitted_at` | Tests excerpt §5 Critical Path 5 + Creator Brief §6 "Known-residual classification" |

| **Coverage-matrix completeness gate** | CLI (coverage render) + the committed `coverage-matrix.md` artifact — no `runs.db` query (the classification is a code-native static, not an aggregation over runs) | none — no span is minted; ONE boundary `info!` from `conductor_report::coverage_rollup` (§4) | none beyond the §3 base set — the derived counts ride the allowlisted `message` value | Tests excerpt §5 Critical Path 6 |

| **In-process ↔ headless parity (same verdict for same seed)** | CLI + in-process core + persistent-storage + boundary-only (MCP) | CLI path: `scenario.run` (as in Path 1) | in-process path: `conductor_run::{preflight, drive_run}` (the composition `conductor suite` drives) → `scenario.run` (same instrumentation) | `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier` | Tests excerpt §5 Critical Path 7 + Creator Brief §6 "Both surfaces emit a journal" |
**Telemetry triggers:** (verbatim from obs-scope Section 5)
| Trigger type | Source | Required telemetry signal |

| **logging-sensitive** (none enumerated in security plan §2) | Security Plan Excerpt §2 "No logging-sensitive vectors enumerated" | N/A (Minimal tier: no PII, no credentials, no payment data in Conductor's domain; only self-generated synthetic telemetry classified Low) |
| **compliance-audit-trail** (not applicable) | Security Tier = Minimal (single-developer, local-only, no compliance requirements) | N/A |

| **perf-budget-instruments** | Creator Brief §6 "SLOs are Pulse's, measured journal-relative" + Tests excerpt §5 SLO tiers ("<5s / <20s / <90s") | OTel histogram for `scenario.latency_ms` bucketed per `slo_tier` ("P-XXX < 5s", "< 20s", "< 90s"); per-run `latency_ms` field in JSONL log (computed: `read_back_observed_at - journal_emitted_at` in wall-clock milliseconds); no metrics backend (Minimal tier) — histogram bucketing is optional; SLO enforcement is JSON field assertion at report-generation time |

| **chaos-instrumentation** | Tests excerpt §5 Coverage Triggers "chaos-test / fault-injection" + Stack (conductor-faults module) | Fault-injection span per fault application: `fault.silence` (network silence window), `fault.ramp` (emission rate ramp), `fault.port_occupier` (port occupation for gRPC connectivity check); span attributes: `fault_type` on all three, plus `fault_duration_ms` + `fault_start_offset_ms` (journal offset) on the run-path silence/ramp spans, `ramp_factor` on the ramp, and `port` on the occupier (which carries neither duration nor offset at open) — per-span sets in §4 Fault-injection spans |

| **cross-surface-parity (NOT trace propagation)** | Tests excerpt §5 Critical Path 7 ("Both-surface parity") | parity is the `runs.db` envelope comparison (same seed ⇒ same verdict/state/seed across the two arms (headless CLI, the in-process composition `conductor suite` drives)) — NOT a W3C trace correlation; no OTel SDK, no `traceparent`; each arm tags its JSON lines with `run_id`, and the two runs are matched by `(scenario, seed)` |

| **multi-platform-exporter-compat** | Design System Excerpt §3 surfaces (Windows/macOS/Linux, cli) | CLI exporter: stderr + file `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` (platform-agnostic POSIX path, relative to `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`); no platform-specific crash reporter (Minimal tier; Sentry/Crashlytics integration deferred to Phase 3 if escalated) |

| **error-budget-SLO** (Minimal tier: zero-unlogged-panics only) | Tests excerpt §5 Quality Gates "Zero-flakiness statement" + Creator Brief §6 Rigor Hints "determinism hard quality bar" | `std::panic::set_hook()` capture: if panic occurs, emit structured error log with backtrace (if available) and context; convert panic to `anyhow::Error` at binary edge (CLI: exit code 1 + sanitized error to stderr) |

| **creator-explicit-telemetry** | Creator Brief §6 Obs Anti-Patterns "The emission-journal format is owned upstream — obs DERIVES, does not re-author" + "the field-allowlist / redaction layer (no absolute host paths, no internal struct names in artifacts)" | Span for `redaction.apply_field_allowlist()` on journal write + report generation; scrub log fields: remove any `path::` (absolute filesystem paths), `module::` (internal crate names), `backtrace` (if present, sanitize file paths); preserve verdict/state/identity/count fields only |

title: 2. Telemetry Strategy

body: **Telemetry signal pyramid (Minimal tier):**
| Signal | Coverage focus | Tier-specific depth |
| Spans / Traces | Critical paths (7 scenarios) + module boundaries (emit, verify, report, timeline) | Present; focused on must-trace paths only (no background task instrumentation) |

| Structured Logs | Boundary calls (MCP readback, DB insert, emit batch) + state transitions (run start, verdict classification) + redaction on output | JSONL-per-line via `tracing-subscriber`; fields match tests' binding schema (Section 6); no absolute paths or internal names |

| Errors | Captured panics + module-boundary `Result::Err` at seams (MCP client, rusqlite, tonic) | `std::panic::set_hook()` + `tracing::error!` + anyhow edge bridging; no external error-reporting platform at Minimal |
| Metrics | Counters / histograms per critical path | Skipped for backend (no metrics backend); SLO perf-budget is a JSON field assertion (latency_ms + slo_tier), not a histogram instrument |
| Audit Logs | Compliance trail | N/A (Minimal tier: no compliance requirement) |
**Agent-readable invariants:**
- Every signal produces machine-parseable output (JSONL for logs; structured span fields for `tracing` calls; plain JSON exit codes / message summary for errors)
- No human-only dashboards (no Grafana, Kibana, or Datadog UI required)
- No proprietary APM SDKs as primary exporter (no Datadog agent, NewRelic SDK, AppDynamics)
- No human-review-gated log analysis
- Every panic captured with structured context via `std::panic::set_hook()`
- Cross-surface parity verified by `runs.db` envelope comparison (same seed ⇒ same verdict/state), not by W3C trace propagation
**Naming conventions:**
- **Span naming:** `{module}.{operation}` pattern (e.g., `scenario.run`, `timeline.execute`, `emit.batch`, `verify.readback`, `report.generate`, `db.insert_run`)
- **Metric naming:** N/A (Minimal tier, no metrics backend); performance budget is JSON field assertion only
- **Log fields:** structured JSONL matching tests' binding schema (journal_emitted_at, run_id, seed, scenario, p_ids, verdict, state, latency_ms, slo_tier, fingerprints)
- **Resource attributes:** `service.name`, `service.version`, `deployment.environment` (via `env!("CARGO_PKG_*")` + env var override)

title: 3. Observability Harness Contract

body: This section specifies the concrete harness pattern for Conductor's deterministic, emission-journal-driven architecture.
Contracts: .andromeda/registries/obs-plan-contracts.toml — ask registry.py contracts; read one contracts/obs-plan/{key}.md; never whole.

title: 4. Span / Trace Coverage

body: **Span naming convention:** `{module}.{operation}` pattern (e.g., `scenario.run`, `timeline.execute`, `emit.batch`, `verify.readback`, `report.generate`, `db.insert_run`). Avoid high-cardinality span names (no per-user-ID, per-trace-ID, or per-path-with-user-input).
**Span kinds:**
- **Internal:** internal operations (scenario execution, phase scheduling, report generation)
- **Client:** outbound calls (MCP readback over the hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC client, rusqlite DB queries, gRPC emit)
**Auto-instrumentation per surface:**
| Surface | Auto-instrumentation | Manual instrumentation |

| **cli** | None (CLI is not an HTTP service) | `#[tracing::instrument]` on the core scenario handlers the CLI drives (`conductor-run` / `conductor-core` / `conductor-report`). NOT on `fn main()`: the `conductor-cli` crate declares no `tracing` dependency and carries no `tracing::` call site, so it raises no spans of its own — every span and log on the CLI path comes from the libraries it drives, and a CLI-side boundary log would first require adding that dependency edge (as measured 2026-09-06 at `2026-09-06-run-report-envelope-conformance-gate`) |
| **conductor-emit** | None (gRPC client is a seam, not auto-instrumented) | Manual span around tonic client call |
| **conductor-verify** | None (the hand-rolled line-delimited JSON-RPC MCP client is a seam) | Manual span around MCP read-back call |

| **conductor-report** | None (rusqlite is synchronous, off async runtime) | Manual span around the run-persist WRITE (`db.insert_run`). The TEARDOWN write — `RunsDb::delete_run`, three literal `DELETE … WHERE run_id = ?1` statements in one transaction, sole caller the `conductor cleanup <run_id>` verb — mints NO span and no boundary log, deliberately: it is off the §4 must-trace paths and its sole caller declares no `tracing` dependency, so the bounded §11 span-name set stays `db.insert_run` alone with no `db.*` widening (as measured 2026-09-06 at `2026-09-06-run-report-envelope-conformance-gate`). READ queries are witnessed by a §6 boundary-call `info!` inside the caller's span where the caller holds one (a `conductor-cli` caller, e.g. `conductor report` over `read_envelope`, holds none; the line is matched by `run_id`), since the bounded §11 span-name set has no `db.*` read name |
**Must-trace path scenarios** (translated from obs-scope Section 4):

title: Scenario: Headless deterministic scenario run with MCP read-back verification

data.head: #### Scenario: Headless deterministic scenario run with MCP read-back verification

body: - **Surfaces involved:** CLI (`conductor-cli`) + core (conductor-core, conductor-timeline, conductor-emit, conductor-verify, conductor-report) + persistent-storage (runs.db, JSONL journal) + boundary-only (MCP client to Pulse)

- **Must-trace spans:** `scenario.run` (root) → `timeline.execute` → `emit.batch` (per emission, multiple) → `verify.readback` (MCP `query_incident_list`/`retrieve_report` call) → `report.generate` → `db.insert_run` (final verdict write)

- **Required span attributes:** 
  - `scenario.run`: `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids` (array)
  - `timeline.execute`: `phase_count`, `emission_count`
  - `emit.batch`: `emission_count`, `p_id_count`
  - `verify.readback`: `mcp_tool` (string: "query_incident_list" / "retrieve_report"), `latency_ms`
  - `report.generate`: `verdict`, `state`
  - `db.insert_run`: `row_count` (1)
- **Required log fields:** `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state`, `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `fingerprints`, `journal_emitted_at`, `read_back_observed_at`

- **Cleanup:** Root `scenario.run` opens per-scenario at the composition root (`conductor-run::execute_scenario`) and closes when that scenario returns; child spans close at each phase boundary (timeline exit, emit batch flush, verify response receipt). **`report.generate` and `db.insert_run` are run-scoped SIBLINGS of the root, not descendants** — `persist` is called alongside `execute_scenario` at every production site, and under a suite ONE `persist` serves N scenarios whose roots have already closed, so the two report-seam spans correlate to the run by `run_id` rather than by nesting

- **Real-model posture (2026-09-22):** the declare-only `real-model-interpretation` scenario (`l4_posture = "real-model"`) adds NO critical path, span name or span attribute — it rides this chain with the standard eleven-field envelope, `verdict` null, and a non-degraded read-back lands `ManualCheck` rather than `KnownResidual`; its interpretation is graded at the harvest tier (`conductor-run/tests/real_model_harvest.rs`, over the scrubbed capture), never through the envelope. Inside `scenario.run` and BEFORE the ready check, `execute_scenario` records a scenario-level `Blocked` when the scenario's declared posture differs from the posture its run's gate evaluated (a real-model scenario reached from the suite, which keeps the deterministic gate), with one `info` line on the allowlisted `message` field (`scenario blocked: declared L4 posture {a} is not the posture this run's gate evaluated ({b})`) — never a sixth gate precondition. The 2026-09-23 drive was blocked at the preflight; the 2026-09-29 series observed this chain live under the real-model posture — both Stage B preflights reached ready, the graded drive's envelope landed `ManualCheck` with `verdict` null and the eleven keys, and canary-blocked drives' envelopes landed `Blocked` (as measured at that chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`) — and its three-storm real-model canary adds no span or field (each storm logs only the existing message-borne `canary fingerprint computed` line). The 2026-10-06 series (Pulse `5f77859`; Pulse's own log read `model_identity` `gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M` and `prompt_version` `v2.5`) observed the chain live again: all three drives' envelopes landed `ManualCheck` with `verdict` null and the eleven keys, and the chunk added no span, log line or field. The capture's `canary:` count is not the storm count — the canary fires three storms per drive and the capture prints one `canary:` line per retry-storm digest ticked before the scenario's emission instant, the third storm landing within milliseconds of that instant: two lines where its digest's tick falls after the instant (as measured at that chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`), three where the tick falls just before it, the third then reading `pipeline-fault` because its prompt assembly lies outside the capture's pairing window, whatever Pulse did with the storm (d1 and d2 of the 2026-10-07 sixth series, 4 ms and 2 ms before the instant, where Pulse's own log shows the storm parsed `ok` and deduped; as measured at the `2026-10-07-a-sixth-pre-registered-real-model-series-for-v3-09` chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). [2026-10-08, `2026-10-08-capture-canary-pairing-window-corrective`: the `pipeline-fault` reading above is the capture as it stood through the 2026-10-07 sixth series and stays as that series' measured record — its committed captures keep the tokens they printed. From this chunk the pairing reads a selected digest's inference across the emission instant: the instant selects which cue-bearing ticks print — a tick whose own stamp parses and is strictly earlier than it — and no longer drops the lines stamped at or after it, so a canary digest ticked just before the instant prints its log-borne outcome (on the sixth series' d1 and d2 shapes, `surfaced` with `parse=ok created=false deduped=true`). The two-line case stands: a canary tick stamped at or after the instant still gets no line. Limit of the proof: as measured on in-test lines built from the sixth series' recorded stamps and line kinds, with a failing-first reading (the `2026-10-08-capture-canary-pairing-window-corrective` chunk's `evidence/failing-first.md`); what the capture binary prints on a next real drive is unmeasured until someone drives it. The chunk added no span name, span attribute, log line, allowlist entry or envelope key.] A canary's outcome is read from Pulse's own log, never from that printed token. The 2026-10-07 series (Pulse `f70be92`; Pulse's own log read `model_identity` `gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M` and `prompt_version` `v2.6`) observed the chain live once more: all three drives' envelopes landed `ManualCheck` with `verdict` null and the eleven keys, and the chunk added no span, log line or field (as measured at the `2026-10-07-a-fifth-pre-registered-real-model-series-for-v3-09` chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). The 2026-10-07 capture run, a pre-registered run that is not a series (Pulse `f70be92`; Pulse's own log again read `model_identity` `gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M` and `prompt_version` `v2.6`), observed the chain live once more: all three drives' envelopes landed `ManualCheck` with `verdict` null and the eleven keys, and the chunk added no span name, span attribute, log line or allowlist entry (as measured at the `2026-10-07-a-capture-run-records-the-prompt-the-model-received-in-each-drive` chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`). The 2026-10-07 sixth series (driven 2026-10-08; Pulse `9bfefb8`; Pulse's own log read `model_identity` `gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M` and `prompt_version` `v2.6`) observed the chain live once more: all three drives' envelopes landed `ManualCheck` with `verdict` null and the eleven keys, and the chunk added no span name, span attribute, log line or allowlist entry (as measured at the `2026-10-07-a-sixth-pre-registered-real-model-series-for-v3-09` chunk's `evidence/attempt-ledger.md`).

- **Must-trace spans:** `scenario.run` → `timeline.execute_fingerprint_storm` → `emit.batch` (per P-ID cohort, multiple batches) → `verify.readback_fingerprints` → `report.generate`

At SUT HEAD `efabe8e` no read-back surface carried Pulse's computed fingerprint (`fingerprint_refs` was fed from the L4 model's `evidence_refs` alone — a constant `det-*` triple under deterministic L4, measured 2026-08-18; `span_events.fingerprint` has zero reads in `mcp-server`). At HEAD `83d4060` `fingerprint_refs` also carries each incident's triggering-cue fingerprint (the grounded union — measured 2026-09-10, arch §Established Decisions [Read-Back Dependency Posture]), so an emitted-vs-read-back match IS now computable. No span attribute computes it; one test-tier check does (2026-10-02): `lifecycle_harvest::p075_round_assertion_1_read_back_content_fidelity` grades the emitted fingerprint's membership in `fingerprint_refs` at Pulse S `03ec944` over the P-075 round's digest-pinned capture — computed in-process by the `live-pulse`-gated `p075_round_live` leg, never through a span or the envelope, so `fingerprints_read_back_count` stays a count

title: Scenario: Severity-lifecycle full pass observing auto-resolve + resolution summary

data.head: #### Scenario: Severity-lifecycle full pass observing auto-resolve + resolution summary

body: - **Surfaces involved:** CLI + core + persistent-storage + boundary-only (MCP)

- **Must-trace spans:** `scenario.run` → `timeline.execute` → `emit.batch` → `verify.readback*` → `report.generate`. The family-specific chain previously mandated here (`timeline.execute_severity_lifecycle` / per-transition `emit.batch` `severity_level`+`phase` / `verify.readback_auto_resolve` / `verify.readback_resolution_summary`) was never built and is RETIRED — measured 2026-08-21, all four names plus `auto_resolve_triggered` / `summary_received` have ZERO occurrences in `crates/`, the family landed declare-only, and read-back is one `verify.readback.observe` pass, not a per-claim call (the restart-suppression precedent).

- **Required log fields:** the standard eleven-field envelope — `verdict` null (declare-only), `state` "KnownResidual"; NO `lifecycle_phase` / `severity_choice_calibrated` extras. The lifecycle evidence lives in PULSE's own tracing lines, graded at the harvest tier (`conductor-run/tests/severity_harvest.rs`): the auto-resolve witness is the unredacted `incidents.list_active.request` `item_count` transition to empty (the `triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick` counters `resolved_count`/`evaluated_count`/`duration_ms` read `"<redacted>"` live — Pulse's default-deny allowlist predates them — so the tick proves only that the observer RAN), corroborated through read-back only where the list actually empties (leg E `result_count: 0`; on leg A the sidecar returned 2 against pulse-app's 1, a corpus/in-app divergence recorded as SUT intake). The tier ladder grades on Pulse's `triage.cue.emit` `priority`, attributed by `persistence_seconds` because that line carries no service identity.

title: Scenario: Known-residual classification path

body: - **Surfaces involved:** CLI + core + persistent-storage + boundary-only (MCP)

- **Must-trace spans:** `scenario.run` → `timeline.execute` → `verify.readback.observe` (the read-back pass whose `retrieve_report` result REPORTS `degraded_mode`) → `report.classify_known_residual` → `db.insert_run`

- **Required span attributes** (a span attribute must be a name in `conductor-core::redact::ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS` — the processor stage drops any other field, so an attribute outside the allowlist emits nothing):
  - `scenario.run`: `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`
  - `timeline.execute`: standard phase count
  - `verify.readback.observe`: `count` (incidents read); the degraded signal is OBSERVED, not requested — Pulse computes `degraded_mode` (`parsed_l4.is_none()`) and returns it in the `retrieve_report` result, so there is no request-side attribute to record. It rides a `warn`-level line on the allowlisted `message` field
  - `report.classify_known_residual`: `classification_result` (string: "KnownResidual")
  - `db.insert_run`: `state_written` (= "KnownResidual")

- **Required log fields:** `run_id`, `seed`, `scenario`, `p_ids`, `verdict`, `state` ("KnownResidual"), `latency_ms`, `slo_tier`, `fingerprints`, `journal_emitted_at`, `read_back_observed_at` — the same eleven-field envelope every other critical path carries (test-plan §3 owns it) — and NOTHING more: the scenario extra `degraded_mode_response` this path once named is retired, never implemented (measured 2026-09-06, zero occurrences under `crates/`), so the known-residual path carries the eleven-field envelope alone. Note the two record shapes differ in what governs them: an envelope extra is written by the report seam, whereas a SPAN attribute must be allowlisted (above)

- **Cleanup:** Root `scenario.run` closes when the scenario returns (`db.insert_run` is a run-scoped sibling reached through `persist`, correlated by `run_id` — see Critical Path 1 Cleanup); the read-back pass closes on MCP response; classification span closes on state determination

- **Delegated-timing family (added 2026-08-21, live proof).** The four declare-only delegated-timing scenarios (`halo-hue-encoding` · `service-constellation-discovery` · `report-render-surface`, joined by `findings-counter-refresh` on 2026-09-15) reach this classification by this path and add NO critical path of their own — their graded quantity is not Conductor's. Their budgets grade at the harvest tier over PULSE's own tracing lines (`conductor-run/tests/delegated_timing_harvest.rs`), each read from its OWN exact allowlist leaf, and NEVER through `budget_ms`/`effective_deadline_ms`, which bound `read_back_observed_at - journal_emitted_at` (Conductor's journal-relative span — it covers the scenario's WHOLE emission window, not the MCP call: as measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round/evidence/live-round-verdict.md`, three legs of 18s / 35s / 30s of declared phases recorded `latency_ms` 18169 / 35120 / 30212 while the sidecar's own tool calls logged `duration_ms` 0–22) rather than a Pulse-internal duration — confirmed live on leg D, whose envelope recorded `latency_ms: 6139` while `metric.findings.counter_refresh_ms` in the same leg measured 1.9ms median. FIELD NAMES ARE NOT UNIFORM: `duration_ms` on `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms` / `.discovery_ms` / `metric.findings.counter_refresh_ms`, but **`value`** on `metric.report.render_ms`. `findings-counter-refresh` IS declare-only as of 2026-09-15 — its single `[[expected]]` `CountAtLeast` floor was retired as structurally dead, because that floor graded `evidence_count` summed from a `span_refs` vector Pulse's only non-test writer sets empty — and it reaches KnownResidual by the same degraded read-back, now with the declare-only envelope shape this section already specifies (`verdict` null, no `CalibrationRegion` grade from that floor). Its harvest-tier leaf `metric.findings.counter_refresh_ms` is unchanged. **P-025's ≤2s bound grades HARD at the harvest tier through `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms`, as measured at `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-29-hue-shift-budget-graded-hard/evidence/hue-verdict.md`: PASS, worst 684.98ms — one graded leg against a Pulse checkout (`4502d5d`) carrying the P-025 fix `e98d838`, whose in-window samples were a rise (684.98ms, anchored to its incident's `interpretation.incident.created` line at 29.98ms) and a fall to `none` (430.79ms).** Since `e98d838` the leaf's `duration_ms` is the paint instant minus `ServiceListItem.tier_effective_at_unix_nano`, the instant the service's maximum incident tier last changed: the raising incident's `opened_at_unix_nano` on a rise, the last max-holder's `resolved_at_unix_nano` on a fall (acknowledgement does NOT lower the tier), one sample per changed service and only for a change the canvas witnessed. The grade is `grade_in_window` (`delegated_timing_harvest.rs::p025_the_graded_leg_meets_its_two_second_budget_at_its_real_value`) under the rule `contracts/pulse-p025-measurement-contract.md` §The grading rule states before the drive: every sample in [phase-2 start, `scenario.run` close], worst observation, inclusive, absence UNGRADED, a breach a hard Fail relayed to Pulse — so all four delegated-timing bounds now grade hard. **Re-graded 2026-10-02 at Pulse S `03ec944` (the P-075 assert round), all four PASS from each leaf's own field under the same rule: P-025 worst 478.56ms in window (the rise anchored 38.24ms), P-027 worst 605.26ms, P-037 0ms (one sample, fired with no desktop input), P-045 worst 5.0ms of 163 — as measured at `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-02-p-075-assert-round-against-pulse/evidence/round-ledger.md`, held by `delegated_timing_harvest::tests::p075_round_assertion_{3..6}_*`.** **Re-graded 2026-10-03 at Pulse S2 `cdb6c1e` (the P-075 re-round, on a Linux dev host under WebKitGTK on Wayland), all four PASS under the same rule: P-025 one in-window sample, a 128.45ms rise anchored 0.55ms (the leg's 930.82ms fall stamped after `scenario.run` closed, so outside the window), P-027 worst 715.54ms of 2, P-037 0ms (one sample, no desktop input), P-045 worst 1.0ms of 118 — as measured at `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-03-p-075-re-round-on-incident-events/evidence/round-ledger.md`, held by `delegated_timing_harvest::tests::p075_reround_assertion_{3..6}_*`.** SCOPE: deterministic L4, the compact widget visible, the rise in the poll-bounded case (the dot listed before the flip). The RETIRED instrument at Pulse HEAD `83d4060` could not grade the bound, as measured at `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-06-halo-hue-budget-re-driven/evidence/hue-verdict.md`: its leaf reported `t_sample − t_last_refreshing_tick` (TICK QUANTIZATION, U(0, 15s) at a randomly-timed flip, independent of the dispatch rate — 14525.9ms matching its offset to the preceding tick to 1.1ms), under slowest-wins aggregation and a staleness start instant; that reading stays pinned as the retired instrument's record (`p025_the_re_driven_leg_measures_tick_quantization_not_update_latency`). Neither SUT-side candidate once named as lifting that bound (stamping `last_seen` from span arrival; copying the activity floor's `last_observed_unix_nanos`) would have done so — each addressed the staleness term alone, as measured at `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-13-p-025-measurement-contract-for-pulse/research.md` — and the shipped fix is neither: it exposes the tier-effective instant. The bound is never bound to a journal-relative term (`latency_ms` / `budget_ms` / `effective_deadline_ms`). Pulse coordinates here are read at HEAD `226554a` on 2026-09-29 unless dated `83d4060`, and expire when that HEAD moves.

title: Scenario: Coverage-matrix completeness gate

body: - **Surfaces involved:** CLI (report output) + persistent-storage (runs.db query aggregating all runs)

- **Must-trace spans:** none — the gate mints NO span (re-based 2026-09-06, when `2026-09-06-coverage-completeness-gate` first operationalized this path). Its observable is ONE boundary `info!` line raised by `conductor_report::coverage_rollup`, the function every surface reaches (the CLI's no-`--write` render path and the artifact write alike; it was deliberately not placed in `CoverageMatrix::render`, which is pure/no-IO and unreached without `--write`). The retired `report.coverage_matrix_generate` → `db.query_all_p_ids` → `report.validate_coverage` chain was never built, and could not have been as written: none of the three names is in §11's bounded span-name set, and this section's own `conductor-report` row keeps that set at `db.insert_run` "with no `db.*` widening", which its own `db.query_all_p_ids` contradicted.

- **Required span attributes:** none. The counts ride the already-allowlisted `message` field (§6 Boundary-call wrappers, the same escape hatch the MCP key-set witness uses), so `conductor-core::redact::ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS` gains nothing. The retired attribute names `p_id_count_found` / `p_id_count_expected` / `coverage_percent` / `missing_count` are absent from that allowlist and would have been dropped at the processor stage — the `degraded_mode_requested` disqualifier, applied here before shipping rather than after.

- **Denominator semantics (load-bearing — the two counts are NOT the same set):** `p_id_count_expected` is the full manifest capability count, whereas `coverage_percent` is computed over the **in-scope** count — the manifest set minus the rows classified out-of-Conductor's-remit. The shipped coverage roll-up already renders this split on all three surfaces (`conductor_report::coverage::summary_line` / `conductor_cli::render::coverage_summary`), so the gate must adopt the same denominator or the two silently disagree. Both counts stay manifest-derived; neither is ever a literal. The roll-up's **auto term additionally carries a derived `(N unbacked)` qualifier** — `Auto`-classified capabilities no scenario names, read from `conductor_core::UNBACKED_AUTO` (which `check_scenario_backing` holds to the committed catalog). It qualifies the auto count rather than joining the breakdown, so the per-mode summands still sum to the row count; a gate reading these fields must not treat it as a fifth mode.

- **Required log fields:** none beyond the §3 self-obs base set. The roll-up's derived counts (row total, in-scope subtotal, the four per-mode counts with the `(N unbacked)` auto qualifier, the out-of-remit count) are rendered INTO the allowlisted `message` value; `missing_p_ids` / `coverage_percent` / `journal_emitted_at` are retired here — the roll-up emits a self-obs line, not a run-report envelope record, and only `p_ids` was ever allowlisted. The completeness ASSERTION is not a log field at all: it is the CI-wired `conductor-report --test coverage_gate` target over the committed `coverage-matrix.md`.
- **Cleanup:** Report generation span closes on validation completion; DB query closes on result return; coverage validation span closes on assertion

title: Fault-injection spans (chaos-instrumentation trigger, obs-scope §5)

body: Bounded "typical/high" profiles ONLY (P-060 SLO checks); explicitly NOT saturation (50k+ spans/sec).

- **Fault.silence span** (network silence window)
  - Attributes: `fault_type` = "silence", `fault_duration_ms` (integer — the phase's effective jittered gap, known at span open), `fault_start_offset_ms` (journal offset)
  - Timing: gated by `tokio::time` under `current_thread` runtime for seed-reproducibility

- **Fault.ramp span** (emission rate ramp)
  - Attributes: `fault_type` = "ramp", `fault_duration_ms`, `fault_start_offset_ms`, `ramp_factor` (float, **−1.0..1.0**) — the normalized SIGNED slope `(to_rate − from_rate) / max(from_rate, to_rate)` over `EmissionShape::Ramp`'s integer `from_rate`/`to_rate`, so direction rides in the value (a rise and a fall of equal steepness are distinguishable). The shape carries no 0.0–1.0 quantity for this attribute to have been.
  - Timing: gated by `tokio::time`

- **Fault.port_occupier span** (port occupation for gRPC connectivity check)
  - Attributes: `fault_type` = "port_occupier", `port` (integer: 4317 for loopback) — **these two only**. Neither `fault_duration_ms` nor `fault_start_offset_ms` is knowable when the bind is taken (the hold has no declared window and there is no journal basis at that site), and the layer records span attributes on the `new` record alone, so the realized hold is witnessed on the allowlisted `message` field at `debug` when the RAII guard releases.
  - Timing: RAII — the span opens at `occupy()` and closes at `release()`/`Drop`.

**Where each span opens** (measured 2026-08-16): the run-path faults are DECLARATIVE phase data, not calls into `conductor-faults` — silence is `EmissionSpec { occurrences: 0 }` and ramp is `EmissionShape::Ramp`. So `fault.silence` and `fault.ramp` open from a caller-supplied per-phase hook (`conductor-timeline`'s `run_timeline_observed` / `PhaseWindow`, with `conductor-run` supplying the fault semantics and the `std::time` journal basis), and they are **created but not entered** — entering would re-parent every `emit.batch` raised in that phase onto the fault span, which Critical Path 1 nests beneath `timeline.execute`. Both are children of `timeline.execute` and close at the phase boundary. `fault.port_occupier` is the one span that opens inside `conductor-faults`, at its RAII bind site, and **it IS a child of `timeline.execute`** — measured live 2026-08-19 on the connection-lifecycle conflict leg (span_event `new`+`close`, `parent: "timeline.execute"`, attributes exactly `fault_type` + `port`): `conductor-run`'s `phase_guard`/`PhaseGuard` drives the occupier for a fault-declared phase's window (the `verification-matrix.json#v2-15` driver, shipped), and the RAII release is the scheduler's boundary drop, so it closes at the phase boundary like the other two fault spans.

title: 5. Metric Coverage

body: _[Minimal tier with perf-budget-instruments trigger — rendered as JSON field assertion, NOT an OTel histogram backend]_

**Naming conventions:** N/A (no instruments).

```
latency_ms <= SLO_threshold_for_slo_tier ? Pass : Fail
```
| Operation | SLO tier | Budget threshold | Measurement |
| scenario.run (all P-IDs) | `<5s` | 5000 ms | `read_back_observed_at - journal_emitted_at` (wall-clock) |
| scenario.run (all P-IDs) | `<20s` | 20000 ms | same |
| scenario.run (all P-IDs) | `<90s` | 90000 ms | same |
**Metric label cardinality discipline:** N/A (no instruments).
